concepts.name: Instructions executed in sequence
concepts.summary: Explain that a program is an ordered list of instructions the computer carries out one at a time, top to bottom.

concepts.name: Variables as named storage
concepts.summary: Describe a variable as a named place holding a value that can be read and changed.

concepts.name: Basic data types
concepts.summary: Recognise integers, decimals, text strings and booleans and say what kind of value each holds.

concepts.name: Assignment versus equality
concepts.summary: Distinguish storing a value in a variable from testing whether two values are equal.

concepts.name: Input and output
concepts.summary: Recall how a program receives data from a user and displays results.

concepts.name: Expressions and operators
concepts.summary: Understand how arithmetic and comparison operators combine values into a new value.

misconceptions.text: A variable remembers the formula used to compute it and updates automatically when other variables change.
The = sign in code means the two sides are equal, as in mathematics.
The text "5" and the number 5 are the same thing and behave identically.

concepts.name: Conditional branching
concepts.summary: Use if, else if and else to run different code depending on a condition.

concepts.name: Boolean logic and comparisons
concepts.summary: Combine comparisons with and, or and not to write correct conditions.

concepts.name: Loops for repetition
concepts.summary: Write for and while loops to repeat actions a set number of times or until a condition changes.

concepts.name: Functions and parameters
concepts.summary: Define a function with parameters, call it with arguments and use its return value.

concepts.name: Lists and indexing
concepts.summary: Store several values in a list and access or loop over them by position.

concepts.name: Reading error messages
concepts.summary: Interpret an error message to find the kind of error and the line where it occurred.

concepts.name: Tracing code with print statements
concepts.summary: Insert output statements to observe variable values and find where a program departs from expectations.

misconceptions.text: A loop condition is checked continuously, so a while loop stops the instant the condition becomes false mid-body.
Lists start counting at 1, so the first item is at index 1.
A function that prints a value and a function that returns a value are the same.

concepts.name: Problem decomposition
concepts.summary: Break a problem into smaller subproblems and map each to a function or code block.

concepts.name: Variable scope and lifetime
concepts.summary: Predict where a variable is visible and how long its value persists, including local versus global.

concepts.name: Nested control flow
concepts.summary: Analyse and write combinations of loops and conditions, tracking state across iterations.

concepts.name: Off-by-one and boundary errors
concepts.summary: Identify boundary conditions in loops and indexing and test them deliberately.

concepts.name: Systematic debugging
concepts.summary: Reproduce a bug, form hypotheses, isolate the cause with a debugger or tests, and verify the fix.

concepts.name: Dictionaries and key lookup
concepts.summary: Choose and use key-value structures to associate and retrieve data.

concepts.name: Pass by value versus reference
concepts.summary: Analyse how assigning or passing mutable and immutable values affects whether changes are shared.

concepts.name: Writing simple tests
concepts.summary: Write small checks with expected outputs to confirm a function behaves correctly.

misconceptions.text: Using global variables everywhere is simpler and has no downside.
Copying a list with assignment creates an independent copy.
If a program works on a few typical inputs, it is correct.

concepts.name: Recursion and base cases
concepts.summary: Analyse and write functions that call themselves, identifying base and recursive cases and the call stack.

concepts.name: Algorithmic efficiency comparison
concepts.summary: Evaluate alternative approaches by how running time and memory grow with input size.

concepts.name: Error handling strategies
concepts.summary: Judge when to validate input, raise, catch or propagate errors to keep programs robust.

concepts.name: Abstraction and modular design
concepts.summary: Evaluate how code is split into cohesive, loosely coupled functions and modules.

concepts.name: Choosing data structures
concepts.summary: Select among lists, sets, dictionaries and similar structures based on the operations a task needs.

concepts.name: Refactoring for readability
concepts.summary: Restructure working code and improve naming to reduce duplication without changing behaviour.

concepts.name: Designing test cases
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a test set covers normal, boundary and failure cases.

misconceptions.text: Recursion is always more elegant and efficient than iteration.
Catching and silently ignoring errors makes a program more reliable.
Shorter code is always better code.

concepts.name: Paradigm trade-off evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate procedural, object-oriented and functional styles against a problem's needs.

concepts.name: Designing for change
concepts.summary: Design program structure so likely future requirements can be added with minimal rework.

concepts.name: Invariants and correctness reasoning
concepts.summary: Use invariants, preconditions and postconditions to argue that code is correct.

concepts.name: Designing debugging strategies
concepts.summary: Create strategies such as bisecting history or inputs and instrumentation to isolate faults in unfamiliar code.

concepts.name: Side effects and state management
concepts.summary: Evaluate how shared mutable state and side effects affect predictability and testing.

concepts.name: Teaching and critiquing code
concepts.summary: Review others' code and give reasoned, actionable feedback on correctness, clarity and design.

concepts.name: Creating reusable abstractions
concepts.summary: Create functions or modules with clear interfaces that solve a class of problems rather than one case.

misconceptions.text: One programming paradigm is objectively best for all problems.
Designing for every possible future need up front is good practice.
Passing tests proves a program is correct.

concepts.name: Indentation-based block syntax
concepts.summary: Explain that consistent indentation, not braces, defines blocks and recognise an IndentationError.

concepts.name: Variables and dynamic typing
concepts.summary: Understand that names are bound to objects of built-in types such as int, float, str and bool, and that types belong to values rather than names.

concepts.name: Lists and tuples
concepts.summary: Describe ordered sequences, indexing and slicing, and the difference between mutable lists and immutable tuples.

concepts.name: Dicts and sets
concepts.summary: Explain that dicts map unique keys to values and sets hold unique unordered items, and recall their literal syntax.

concepts.name: Conditionals and loops
concepts.summary: Understand how if statements, for loops over iterables and while loops control the flow of a program.

concepts.name: Defining and calling functions
concepts.summary: Understand how def creates a function with parameters and a return value, and how calling it runs the body.

concepts.name: Running scripts and printing
concepts.summary: Recall how to run a .py file or the interactive interpreter and use print and input.

misconceptions.text: Indentation in Python is only for readability and can be changed freely without affecting behaviour.
A tuple can be changed in place just like a list.
A variable must be declared with a fixed type before it is used.

concepts.name: List comprehensions
concepts.summary: Write list, dict and set comprehensions with conditions to build collections from iterables.

concepts.name: Function arguments and defaults
concepts.summary: Use positional, keyword and default parameters plus *args and **kwargs when writing and calling functions.

concepts.name: Exception handling with try/except
concepts.summary: Catch specific exceptions with try/except/else/finally and raise errors deliberately.

concepts.name: Reading and writing files
concepts.summary: Open, read and write text files using the with statement so they are closed automatically.

concepts.name: Importing modules
concepts.summary: Import standard library modules and names and call their functions, and structure code across your own module files.

concepts.name: Basic standard library usage
concepts.summary: Use os and sys for paths and arguments, json to serialise data and datetime to handle dates.

concepts.name: Virtual environments and pip
concepts.summary: Create a venv, activate it and install third-party packages with pip.

concepts.name: String methods and formatting
concepts.summary: Use common string methods and f-strings to transform and format text.

misconceptions.text: A bare except clause is the best way to make code robust because it catches everything.
A default argument such as an empty list is created fresh on every call.
Files do not need to be closed because Python always writes data immediately.

concepts.name: Object identity and mutability
concepts.summary: Analyse how aliasing, shallow and deep copies, and mutable versus immutable objects affect program behaviour.

concepts.name: Classes and instances
concepts.summary: Define classes with attributes and methods and distinguish instance from class attributes.

concepts.name: Inheritance and special methods
concepts.summary: Analyse when to use inheritance with super() and implement dunder methods such as __repr__, __eq__ and __len__.

concepts.name: Generators and iterators
concepts.summary: Explain the iterator protocol and use yield and generator expressions to process data lazily.

concepts.name: Decorators
concepts.summary: Analyse how a decorator wraps a function, and write one that preserves metadata with functools.wraps.

concepts.name: Scope and closures
concepts.summary: Trace name resolution through local, enclosing, global and built-in scopes and explain how closures capture variables.

concepts.name: Collections module and containers
concepts.summary: Choose among defaultdict, Counter, deque and namedtuple for counting, grouping and queue tasks.

concepts.name: Packages and module layout
concepts.summary: Organise code into packages, understand how Python finds modules via sys.path, and use the main guard.

misconceptions.text: Assigning one list to another variable makes an independent copy.
A generator stores all its values in memory like a list.
Attributes defined at class level are always separate per instance.

concepts.name: Context managers
concepts.summary: Implement context managers via dunder methods or contextlib to guarantee resource cleanup and judge when to use them.

concepts.name: Dataclasses and typing hints
concepts.summary: Evaluate when annotations and dataclasses improve clarity and how static type checkers use them, given hints are not enforced at runtime.

concepts.name: Custom exception design
concepts.summary: Design exception hierarchies and use chaining to produce meaningful error handling across layers.

concepts.name: Descriptors and properties
concepts.summary: Analyse how properties and the descriptor protocol control attribute access and validation.

concepts.name: Concurrency models and the GIL
concepts.summary: Evaluate threads, processes and asyncio for I/O-bound versus CPU-bound work given the GIL.

concepts.name: Testing with pytest and unittest
concepts.summary: Write and structure unit tests with fixtures and mocks and analyse what they do and do not verify.

concepts.name: Profiling and performance tuning
concepts.summary: Measure with timeit and cProfile and judge optimisations by evidence rather than intuition.

concepts.name: Dependency and packaging management
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches to pinning dependencies and packaging a project for reproducible installs.

misconceptions.text: Python threads give true parallel speed-up for CPU-bound code.
Type hints are checked and enforced by the interpreter at runtime.
Optimising code without measuring is the quickest way to make it faster.

concepts.name: Metaclasses and class creation
concepts.summary: Design class-construction hooks using metaclasses, __init_subclass__ or class decorators and judge when simpler tools suffice.

concepts.name: Data model protocol design
concepts.summary: Create APIs that integrate with Python's data model through dunder methods, ABCs and structural protocols.

concepts.name: CPython memory and execution internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how reference counting, cyclic garbage collection and bytecode execution affect behaviour and performance.

concepts.name: Advanced asynchronous architecture
concepts.summary: Design robust asynchronous systems with correct cancellation, backpressure and mixing of blocking code.

concepts.name: Extending Python with native code
concepts.summary: Evaluate options for native extensions against pure Python and decide when the integration cost is justified.

concepts.name: Library API and compatibility design
concepts.summary: Create stable, well-documented library interfaces with deliberate deprecation and compatibility strategies.

concepts.name: Import system customisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how finders, loaders and import hooks work and when customising imports is appropriate.

misconceptions.text: Metaclasses are the standard way to customise classes and should be used often.
Reference counting alone frees all unused objects, so garbage collection never matters.
Using async and await makes any code faster, including blocking or CPU-heavy code.

concepts.name: Variable declarations let const
concepts.summary: Explain how let, const and var declare variables and choose const by default and let when reassignment is needed.

concepts.name: Primitive and object types
concepts.summary: Recall JavaScript's primitive types, objects, arrays and the typeof operator.

concepts.name: Strict versus loose equality
concepts.summary: Explain why === avoids type coercion and what truthy and falsy values are.

concepts.name: Function declarations and expressions
concepts.summary: Write and call functions with parameters and return values, including function expressions.

concepts.name: Template literals
concepts.summary: Build strings with interpolated expressions and multiline text using backticks.

concepts.name: Object and array literals
concepts.summary: Create objects and arrays and access their members with dot and bracket notation.

concepts.name: Console output and debugging
concepts.summary: Use console methods to inspect values and read basic error messages.

misconceptions.text: const makes the value completely immutable, even for objects and arrays.
== and === behave the same way.
typeof null returns 'null' and arrays have the type 'array'.

concepts.name: Arrow function syntax
concepts.summary: Write arrow functions with implicit returns and recognise when they are appropriate.

concepts.name: Destructuring and spread
concepts.summary: Extract values from arrays and objects and copy or merge them using spread and rest syntax.

concepts.name: Map filter reduce
concepts.summary: Transform, select and aggregate arrays with map, filter and reduce instead of manual loops.

concepts.name: JSON parsing and serialising
concepts.summary: Convert between objects and JSON strings and know what values JSON cannot represent.

concepts.name: Block scope and hoisting
concepts.summary: Predict how var, let and const are scoped and hoisted, including the temporal dead zone.

concepts.name: DOM selection and modification
concepts.summary: Select elements and change their text, attributes, classes and styles.

concepts.name: Event listeners
concepts.summary: Attach handlers to elements and use the event object to respond to user actions.

misconceptions.text: map modifies the original array in place.
let and const variables are not hoisted at all.
Spread creates a deep copy of nested objects.

concepts.name: Lexical scope and closures
concepts.summary: Analyse how functions retain access to variables of their defining scope and use this for private state.

concepts.name: this binding rules
concepts.summary: Determine the value of this from call-site, call/apply/bind, and arrow function lexical binding.

concepts.name: Prototype chain lookup
concepts.summary: Trace property lookup along the prototype chain and distinguish own from inherited properties.

concepts.name: ES6 class syntax
concepts.summary: Define classes with constructors, methods, static members and inheritance via extends and super.

concepts.name: ES module import export
concepts.summary: Organise code with named and default exports and imports and understand module scope.

concepts.name: Event propagation and delegation
concepts.summary: Analyse capture and bubble phases and use delegation to handle events on dynamic elements.

concepts.name: Shallow versus deep copying
concepts.summary: Distinguish reference sharing, shallow copies and deep copies and pick a suitable cloning approach.

misconceptions.text: Closures capture the value of a variable at creation time rather than the variable itself.
JavaScript classes work like classes in Java, copying methods into instances.
this refers to the function itself or the lexical scope where it is defined, in every function type.

concepts.name: Prototype-based design tradeoffs
concepts.summary: Evaluate classes, factory functions, and Object.create composition for a given design.

concepts.name: Module design and dependencies
concepts.summary: Assess module structure, circular imports, live bindings and side effects at import time.

concepts.name: Functional composition patterns
concepts.summary: Compose pure functions, currying and higher-order utilities and judge when they improve clarity.

concepts.name: Immutability strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches such as spread updates, Object.freeze and non-mutating array methods for avoiding shared-state bugs.

concepts.name: Property descriptors and getters
concepts.summary: Use property descriptors, getters, setters and enumerability to control object behaviour.

concepts.name: Symbols and iteration protocols
concepts.summary: Analyse how iterables and iterators power for...of, spread and destructuring, and implement custom ones.

concepts.name: DOM performance and reflow
concepts.summary: Evaluate DOM update strategies such as batching, fragments and avoiding forced layout.

misconceptions.text: Object.freeze makes nested objects deeply immutable.
Functional style with map and reduce is always faster and clearer than loops.
Imported bindings are copies of the exported values.

concepts.name: Language semantics critique
concepts.summary: Judge the impact of coercion, hoisting and this quirks on code style and enforce safer conventions.

concepts.name: Metaprogramming with Proxy
concepts.summary: Design objects with Proxy and Reflect traps for validation or observation while weighing costs.

concepts.name: Library API architecture
concepts.summary: Create a coherent, extensible, module-based API using appropriate patterns for inheritance, composition and configuration.

concepts.name: Memory leaks and garbage collection
concepts.summary: Diagnose leaks from closures, detached DOM nodes and lingering listeners and evaluate fixes.

concepts.name: Engine optimisation awareness
concepts.summary: Evaluate how object shape stability and type consistency affect engine optimisation without premature tuning.

concepts.name: Custom event architectures
concepts.summary: Design decoupled component communication using custom events and a clear listener lifecycle.

concepts.name: Conventions and style standards
concepts.summary: Create team conventions and lint configurations that prevent known language pitfalls.

misconceptions.text: Garbage collection means JavaScript programs cannot leak memory.
Micro-optimising code by hand is the best way to speed up JavaScript.
Proxies are a free abstraction with no performance or semantic cost.

concepts.name: Psychology as behavioral science
concepts.summary: Recall that psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, distinct from common sense or opinion.

concepts.name: Major subfields of psychology
concepts.summary: Name the main subfields such as clinical, cognitive, developmental, social and biological psychology and what each studies.

concepts.name: Classical conditioning
concepts.summary: Explain how a neutral stimulus paired with an unconditioned stimulus comes to trigger a conditioned response.

concepts.name: Operant conditioning
concepts.summary: Explain how consequences such as reinforcement and punishment change the likelihood of a behavior.

concepts.name: Memory stages
concepts.summary: Describe memory as encoding, storage and retrieval and distinguish sensory, short-term and long-term memory.

concepts.name: Nature and nurture
concepts.summary: Understand that behavior arises from the interplay of genetic and environmental influences.

concepts.name: Basic emotions and motives
concepts.summary: Recall that motives such as hunger and belonging drive behavior and that emotions involve feelings, body responses and expression.

misconceptions.text: Psychology is just common sense or only about treating mental illness.
Punishment and negative reinforcement are the same thing.
Memory works like a video recording that stores events exactly as they happened.

concepts.name: Research methods in psychology
concepts.summary: Distinguish experimental, correlational, survey and case-study methods and what each can show.

concepts.name: Correlation versus causation
concepts.summary: Apply the rule that correlation does not show causation by spotting third variables and reverse direction in examples.

concepts.name: Developmental stage theories
concepts.summary: Describe Piaget's cognitive stages and Erikson's psychosocial stages and how each frames development.

concepts.name: Trait models of personality
concepts.summary: Use the Big Five dimensions to describe and compare people's personality profiles.

concepts.name: Maslow's hierarchy and motivation theories
concepts.summary: Apply hierarchy-of-needs and intrinsic versus extrinsic motivation ideas to everyday situations.

concepts.name: Social influence and conformity
concepts.summary: Use classic findings on conformity and obedience to explain how others shape individual behavior.

concepts.name: Psychological disorder categories
concepts.summary: Describe major categories such as anxiety, mood, psychotic and personality disorders and the idea of diagnostic criteria.

misconceptions.text: If two things are strongly correlated, one must cause the other.
Everyone passes through developmental stages at exactly the same ages in the same way.
Personality traits are fixed labels that predict behavior identically in every situation.

concepts.name: Experimental design and validity
concepts.summary: Analyse a study's design for random assignment, control, confounds and threats to internal and external validity.

concepts.name: Statistical significance and effect size
concepts.summary: Interpret significance and effect size and explain why a significant result may be small or unimportant.

concepts.name: Reconstructive memory and forgetting
concepts.summary: Analyse how schemas, suggestion and interference produce distortion and forgetting, as in eyewitness testimony.

concepts.name: Cognitive biases and heuristics
concepts.summary: Identify heuristics like availability and biases like confirmation in real examples and show how they distort judgment.

concepts.name: Attribution and attitudes
concepts.summary: Analyse how people explain behavior and reduce inconsistency between attitudes and actions.

concepts.name: Biological bases of behavior
concepts.summary: Apply knowledge of neurons, neurotransmitters and major brain regions to explain behavior and drug effects.

concepts.name: Theoretical approaches to disorders
concepts.summary: Compare biological, cognitive, behavioral and sociocultural explanations of mental disorders and their treatments.

misconceptions.text: A statistically significant result means the effect is large and important.
Confident, vivid eyewitness memories are reliably accurate.
People use only 10 percent of their brains, or are either left-brained or right-brained.

concepts.name: Evaluating evidence quality
concepts.summary: Judge whether a study's sample, measures, design and replication support its conclusion.

concepts.name: Replication crisis and research bias
concepts.summary: Evaluate how questionable research practices and publication bias undermine findings and how preregistration helps.

concepts.name: Cultural limits of generalization
concepts.summary: Analyse how WEIRD samples and cultural context limit the reach of psychological theories.

concepts.name: Competing theories of emotion
concepts.summary: Compare major emotion theories and weigh the evidence supporting each.

concepts.name: Situation versus disposition debate
concepts.summary: Evaluate how well situational and trait explanations account for behavior, including critiques of classic social experiments.

concepts.name: Treatment effectiveness evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for psychotherapies and medications, including placebo effects and common factors.

concepts.name: Gene-environment interaction
concepts.summary: Analyse what heritability estimates do and do not say and how genes and environments interact.

misconceptions.text: A finding published in a peer-reviewed journal is established fact.
A heritability of 50 percent means half of an individual's trait comes from genes.
Findings from American college students apply equally to all humans.

concepts.name: Integrating levels of explanation
concepts.summary: Judge when biological, psychological and social explanations of the same behavior are complementary or competing.

concepts.name: Assessing everyday behavioral claims
concepts.summary: Evaluate popular claims such as learning styles or subliminal persuasion against the evidence and explain why they persist.

concepts.name: Designing a rigorous study
concepts.summary: Create a study plan with a testable hypothesis, valid measures, controls, power consideration and ethical safeguards.

concepts.name: Ethics in psychological research
concepts.summary: Evaluate research designs against ethical principles such as consent, harm minimization and debriefing.

concepts.name: Theory comparison and falsifiability
concepts.summary: Assess competing psychological theories for falsifiability, explanatory scope and predictive success.

concepts.name: Applying psychology to interventions
concepts.summary: Create an evidence-based plan to change behavior in a setting such as school, health or work using learning, motivation and social principles.

misconceptions.text: A theory that can explain any outcome is the strongest theory.
Ethical approval is only a formality after the design is finished.
Only one level of explanation, such as the brain, can be the real explanation of behavior.

concepts.name: Monolith versus microservices
concepts.summary: Explain how a single deployable application differs from a set of small services that are deployed and scaled independently.

concepts.name: Independent deployability
concepts.summary: Understand that each service can be built, released and scaled without redeploying the others.

concepts.name: Database per service
concepts.summary: Understand that each service owns its data and other services access it only through the service's API.

concepts.name: Service responsibility and size
concepts.summary: Describe a service as focused on one business capability rather than a technical layer or arbitrary line count.

concepts.name: Synchronous service calls
concepts.summary: Recall that services can call each other over the network with request-response protocols such as REST.

concepts.name: Benefits and costs trade-off
concepts.summary: Explain the main benefits (independent scaling, team autonomy, fault isolation) and costs (network latency, operational complexity, distributed failures).

misconceptions.text: Microservices are always better than a monolith.
A service is a microservice simply because it is small in lines of code.
Several services can safely share one database as long as each uses its own tables.

concepts.name: Bounded context decomposition
concepts.summary: Apply domain-driven design to draw service boundaries around bounded contexts in a simple business domain.

concepts.name: API gateway routing
concepts.summary: Configure a gateway to route client requests to services and handle cross-cutting concerns such as authentication and rate limiting.

concepts.name: Service discovery
concepts.summary: Use a registry or platform DNS so that services find each other when instances change address.

concepts.name: Asynchronous messaging basics
concepts.summary: Use a message broker with queues or topics so that services communicate without waiting for each other.

concepts.name: Contract-based service APIs
concepts.summary: Define and version service interfaces so that changes do not break consumers.

concepts.name: Containerised service deployment
concepts.summary: Package and run each service as its own container with its own configuration and dependencies.

concepts.name: Distributed logging and tracing
concepts.summary: Understand how correlation IDs and centralised logs let you follow a request across services.

misconceptions.text: Services should be split by technical layer, such as one for the UI, one for business logic and one for data.
The API gateway is the place to put all business logic shared between services.
Asynchronous messaging is just a faster version of synchronous calls.

concepts.name: Context mapping and ownership
concepts.summary: Analyse relationships between contexts and teams, including upstream/downstream dependencies and anti-corruption layers, to refine boundaries.

concepts.name: REST versus gRPC trade-offs
concepts.summary: Compare REST, gRPC and messaging for a given interaction in terms of coupling, performance, typing and client needs.

concepts.name: Eventual consistency handling
concepts.summary: Analyse where data across services may be temporarily stale and design workflows and user experience to tolerate it.

concepts.name: Saga pattern
concepts.summary: Implement multi-service business transactions as a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions, using choreography or orchestration.

concepts.name: Circuit breaker and timeouts
concepts.summary: Apply timeouts, retries with backoff and circuit breakers to stop failures from cascading between services.

concepts.name: Idempotent message handling
concepts.summary: Analyse delivery guarantees and make consumers idempotent so that duplicates and redelivery do not corrupt state.

concepts.name: Event-driven data propagation
concepts.summary: Analyse how services publish domain events and maintain local read copies of data owned by others.

misconceptions.text: Retrying failed calls always improves reliability.
A saga gives the same isolation and atomicity guarantees as a database transaction.
A message broker guarantees each message is delivered exactly once, so consumers need no duplicate handling.

concepts.name: Strangler fig migration
concepts.summary: Evaluate and sequence the incremental extraction of capabilities from a monolith behind a routing facade, deciding what to extract first.

concepts.name: Data separation during migration
concepts.summary: Analyse approaches such as shared-schema stages, synchronisation and change data capture for pulling data out of a monolith database.

concepts.name: Transactional outbox pattern
concepts.summary: Analyse how writing events to an outbox in the same local transaction avoids losing or inventing events when updating state and publishing.

concepts.name: CQRS and read models
concepts.summary: Evaluate when separate read models or API composition are justified for queries spanning multiple services.

concepts.name: Observability and SLO design
concepts.summary: Analyse metrics, traces and logs to find bottlenecks and failure sources, and set service-level objectives.

concepts.name: Consumer-driven contract testing
concepts.summary: Evaluate a testing strategy that balances unit, contract, integration and end-to-end tests across services.

concepts.name: Service-to-service security
concepts.summary: Analyse how authentication, authorisation and token propagation work between services behind a gateway.

misconceptions.text: Migrating to microservices should start with a full rewrite of the monolith.
Publishing an event right after committing to the database is reliable enough without an outbox.
End-to-end tests alone are sufficient to verify that services work together.

concepts.name: Architecture fitness evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge whether microservices, a modular monolith or a hybrid best fits an organisation's scale, team structure and domain volatility.

concepts.name: Boundary evolution and refactoring
concepts.summary: Critique existing boundaries and decide when to merge, split or re-draw services to remove coupling and chatty communication.

concepts.name: Resilience and chaos strategy
concepts.summary: Design a resilience programme with graceful degradation, load shedding and failure-injection experiments across a service landscape.

concepts.name: Consistency model design
concepts.summary: Design how business invariants are enforced across services, choosing between sagas, reservation patterns, and relaxed or redefined rules.

concepts.name: Platform and governance design
concepts.summary: Create shared platform capabilities and governance, such as templates, standards and deployment pipelines, that keep many teams autonomous yet consistent.

concepts.name: Event schema evolution strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate compatibility rules, schema registries and versioning approaches so that producers and consumers evolve independently.

concepts.name: Cost and organisational impact
concepts.summary: Evaluate the operational cost and team-topology effects of a service architecture, including Conway's law and cognitive load.

misconceptions.text: If services are deployed separately, the architecture is automatically loosely coupled.
Every cross-service business rule must be enforced with strong consistency to be correct.
Team structure has little effect on service architecture, which is purely a technical choice.

concepts.name: Strategy versus operations
concepts.summary: Explain that strategy is about choosing where to compete and how to win, distinct from running day-to-day activities efficiently.

concepts.name: Mission, vision and goals
concepts.summary: Define mission, vision and strategic objectives and recall how they guide strategic choices.

concepts.name: Competitive advantage
concepts.summary: Explain competitive advantage as performing better than rivals in a way that yields higher returns than the industry average.

concepts.name: Cost leadership and differentiation
concepts.summary: Describe how a firm can win by lower cost or by offering distinctive value customers will pay more for.

concepts.name: Target customers and value proposition
concepts.summary: Describe how a firm chooses which customers to serve and what value it offers them.

concepts.name: SWOT analysis
concepts.summary: Classify internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats for a company.

concepts.name: Internal versus external environment
concepts.summary: Distinguish factors a firm controls from industry and macro forces it must respond to.

misconceptions.text: Strategy is just a detailed plan or budget for the next year.
Being the best at operational efficiency is the same as having a strategy.
A SWOT list on its own tells a firm what strategy to pursue.

concepts.name: PESTEL macro-environment scan
concepts.summary: Apply the political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal framework to identify external trends affecting a firm.

concepts.name: Porter's Five Forces
concepts.summary: Apply the five forces to assess how rivalry, entry, substitutes and supplier and buyer power shape industry profitability.

concepts.name: Value chain activities
concepts.summary: Map a firm's primary and support activities to locate where it creates cost or differentiation advantages.

concepts.name: Resources and capabilities
concepts.summary: Distinguish tangible and intangible resources from capabilities and relate them to advantage.

concepts.name: Competitor profiling
concepts.summary: Build a profile of rivals' offerings, strategies, strengths and likely moves.

concepts.name: Growth matrix options
concepts.summary: Use market penetration, market development, product development and diversification to classify growth options.

concepts.name: Market segmentation and positioning
concepts.summary: Segment a market and position an offering distinctively for chosen segments.

misconceptions.text: The most attractive industries are simply those growing fastest.
Five Forces analyses a single company rather than an industry's structure.
Any valuable resource gives a lasting advantage.

concepts.name: VRIO resource assessment
concepts.summary: Analyse whether resources are valuable, rare, costly to imitate and organized to be exploited, to judge advantage durability.

concepts.name: Strategic groups and mobility barriers
concepts.summary: Analyse how firms cluster by strategy within an industry and what keeps them from moving between groups.

concepts.name: Business model analysis
concepts.summary: Break down how a firm creates, delivers and captures value, including revenue and cost structure.

concepts.name: Portfolio analysis
concepts.summary: Use portfolio tools to assess business units and allocate resources across them.

concepts.name: Corporate versus business strategy
concepts.summary: Differentiate the choice of which businesses to be in from how each business competes.

concepts.name: Vertical integration decisions
concepts.summary: Analyse when owning upstream or downstream activities creates value versus using the market, using transaction costs.

concepts.name: Industry life cycle implications
concepts.summary: Analyse how competitive dynamics and strategic priorities shift across introduction, growth, maturity and decline.

concepts.name: Strategy and financial performance
concepts.summary: Link strategic position to profitability using margins, capital turnover and returns on invested capital.

misconceptions.text: A resource that is valuable and rare is automatically a sustained advantage.
The BCG matrix tells managers which units to keep or sell without further analysis.
Vertical integration always increases control and profit.

concepts.name: Game theory and competitive dynamics
concepts.summary: Analyse competitor moves and responses, such as price wars, signaling and commitment, as strategic games.

concepts.name: Dynamic capabilities
concepts.summary: Evaluate a firm's ability to sense change, seize opportunities and reconfigure resources in shifting markets.

concepts.name: Platforms and network effects
concepts.summary: Analyse how platform businesses gain advantage through network effects, multi-homing and switching costs.

concepts.name: Diversification and synergy evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether diversification creates value through shared resources, or destroys it through complexity and overpayment.

concepts.name: Mergers, alliances and acquisitions
concepts.summary: Evaluate build, buy and ally choices and the risks of integration and value capture.

concepts.name: Disruptive innovation dynamics
concepts.summary: Analyse how entrants with lower-end or new-market offerings displace incumbents and why incumbents struggle to respond.

concepts.name: International strategy choices
concepts.summary: Evaluate entry modes and the trade-off between global efficiency and local adaptation.

concepts.name: Strategic fit and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a firm's activities reinforce one another and make deliberate trade-offs that rivals cannot easily copy.

misconceptions.text: Synergies in acquisitions reliably materialize once the deal closes.
Disruptors win because their products are better than incumbents' from the start.
Network effects guarantee a winner-take-all outcome in any platform market.

concepts.name: Strategy formulation under uncertainty
concepts.summary: Design strategies that stay robust across plausible futures using scenarios and staged commitments.

concepts.name: Reshaping industry structure
concepts.summary: Create strategies that change industry boundaries or forces rather than just position within them.

concepts.name: Critiquing strategic frameworks
concepts.summary: Judge when frameworks such as Five Forces or the resource-based view mislead and which fits a given context.

concepts.name: Strategy execution and organization design
concepts.summary: Design structure, governance, metrics and incentives that turn strategic intent into consistent action.

concepts.name: Ecosystem and coopetition strategy
concepts.summary: Design positions within ecosystems and partnerships with rivals that capture value while sustaining partners.

concepts.name: Strategic renewal and turnaround
concepts.summary: Create plans to reinvent a firm's strategy or recover from decline while managing inertia and core rigidities.

concepts.name: Strategic decision biases
concepts.summary: Evaluate how overconfidence, anchoring and escalation distort strategic decisions and design safeguards.

misconceptions.text: Better analysis and forecasting remove the need to place strategic bets under uncertainty.
A sound strategy executes itself once it is announced.
Standard frameworks apply equally well to every industry and context.

concepts.name: Intuitive idea of a limit
concepts.summary: Explain that a limit describes the value a function approaches as the input nears a point, regardless of the value at the point itself.

concepts.name: Reading limits from graphs
concepts.summary: Estimate limits and one-sided limits from graphs and numerical tables and recognise when a limit fails to exist.

concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.summary: State the three conditions for continuity at a point and identify removable, jump and infinite discontinuities.

concepts.name: Average versus instantaneous rate
concepts.summary: Distinguish the average rate of change over an interval from the instantaneous rate at a point as the interval shrinks.

concepts.name: Derivative as tangent slope
concepts.summary: Interpret the derivative at a point as the slope of the tangent line and as an instantaneous rate of change.

concepts.name: Integral as accumulated area
concepts.summary: Describe the definite integral as signed area under a curve and as accumulated change of a rate.

concepts.name: Derivative and integral notation
concepts.summary: Recognise and read f'(x), dy/dx, the integral sign with limits, and limit notation.

misconceptions.text: The limit of a function at a point is always equal to the function's value at that point.
A limit that approaches a value means the function actually reaches and never passes that value.
A function that is defined at a point must be continuous there.

concepts.name: Limit laws and algebraic evaluation
concepts.summary: Compute limits using limit laws, factoring, rationalising and simplifying indeterminate 0/0 forms.

concepts.name: Limits at infinity
concepts.summary: Evaluate limits as x goes to infinity and infinite limits to find horizontal and vertical asymptotes.

concepts.name: Limit definition of the derivative
concepts.summary: Compute derivatives of simple functions directly from the limit of the difference quotient.

concepts.name: Power, sum and constant rules
concepts.summary: Differentiate polynomials and power functions and the derivatives of sine, cosine and exponential functions with the basic rules.

concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
concepts.summary: Apply the product and quotient rules to differentiate combinations of functions.

concepts.name: Chain rule for composites
concepts.summary: Differentiate composite functions by multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

concepts.name: Basic antiderivatives
concepts.summary: Find antiderivatives of power, trigonometric and exponential functions and include the constant of integration.

concepts.name: Riemann sums
concepts.summary: Approximate area under a curve with left, right and midpoint sums and connect finer partitions to the definite integral.

misconceptions.text: The derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.
In the chain rule you only need to differentiate the outer function.
A limit of the form 0/0 is always 0 or always undefined.

concepts.name: Implicit differentiation
concepts.summary: Differentiate relations not solved for y by applying the chain rule to y and solving for dy/dx.

concepts.name: Derivatives of inverse functions
concepts.summary: Differentiate logarithmic, inverse trigonometric and general exponential functions, using logarithmic differentiation where helpful.

concepts.name: Related rates modelling
concepts.summary: Build an equation relating changing quantities, differentiate with respect to time, and solve for an unknown rate.

concepts.name: Curve analysis with derivatives
concepts.summary: Use critical points, monotonicity, concavity and inflection points to analyse and sketch function behaviour.

concepts.name: Optimization problems
concepts.summary: Formulate an objective function with constraints and justify the absolute extremum on a closed or open interval.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.summary: Use both parts of the theorem to differentiate accumulation functions and evaluate definite integrals via antiderivatives.

concepts.name: Substitution for integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate indefinite and definite integrals by substitution, changing limits correctly.

concepts.name: Area and volume by integration
concepts.summary: Set up integrals for area between curves and for volumes of solids of revolution by disks, washers or shells.

misconceptions.text: In related rates, you can substitute the instantaneous values of changing quantities before differentiating.
A point where the derivative is zero is always a local maximum or minimum.
After u-substitution in a definite integral, you keep the original x limits.

concepts.name: Formal epsilon-delta limits
concepts.summary: Analyse and construct epsilon-delta arguments to verify limits of simple functions.

concepts.name: Mean Value and Intermediate Value Theorems
concepts.summary: Analyse the hypotheses and conclusions of the IVT, Rolle's theorem and MVT and apply them to prove properties of functions.

concepts.name: L'Hôpital's rule and indeterminate forms
concepts.summary: Recognise indeterminate forms, transform them to 0/0 or ∞/∞, and justify when L'Hôpital's rule applies.

concepts.name: Integration by parts and partial fractions
concepts.summary: Choose among integration by parts, partial fractions and trigonometric substitution to evaluate integrals.

concepts.name: Improper integrals convergence
concepts.summary: Evaluate and judge convergence of integrals with infinite limits or unbounded integrands, including comparison arguments.

concepts.name: Sequence and series convergence
concepts.summary: Analyse convergence of sequences and series via partial sums, geometric and p-series, and the divergence test.

concepts.name: Convergence tests for series
concepts.summary: Select and justify the appropriate test among comparison, ratio, root, integral and alternating series tests, including absolute versus conditional convergence.

concepts.name: Power series and radius of convergence
concepts.summary: Find the radius and interval of convergence of a power series and differentiate or integrate it termwise.

misconceptions.text: If the terms of a series approach zero, the series must converge.
L'Hôpital's rule can be applied to any limit by differentiating the quotient.
The ratio test being inconclusive (limit equal to 1) means the series diverges.

concepts.name: Taylor polynomials and remainder
concepts.summary: Construct Taylor polynomials and evaluate approximation accuracy using remainder bounds.

concepts.name: Taylor series representation
concepts.summary: Judge when a function equals its Taylor series and derive series for standard functions by manipulation.

concepts.name: Uniform convergence and termwise operations
concepts.summary: Evaluate when limits, derivatives and integrals may be interchanged with infinite sums using uniform convergence.

concepts.name: Riemann integrability criteria
concepts.summary: Assess integrability using upper and lower sums and relate continuity and discontinuity sets to integrability.

concepts.name: Proof of the Fundamental Theorem
concepts.summary: Construct a proof of both parts of the Fundamental Theorem using the Mean Value Theorem and the definition of the integral.

concepts.name: Numerical approximation methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate error and convergence of trapezoid and Simpson rules and Newton's method, and choose among them.

concepts.name: Differential equation modelling
concepts.summary: Create models using separable differential equations and interpret solutions, including exponential and logistic growth.

concepts.name: Pathological functions and counterexamples
concepts.summary: Evaluate the limits of intuition using counterexamples such as continuous nowhere differentiable functions and smooth non-analytic functions.

misconceptions.text: Every infinitely differentiable function equals its Taylor series near the point.
A power series can always be differentiated and integrated termwise anywhere, including at the endpoints of its interval.
Every continuous function is differentiable except at isolated points.

concepts.name: Cells, rows, columns, ranges
concepts.summary: Identify cells by column-row address and describe ranges, rows, columns and worksheets in a workbook.

concepts.name: Entering and editing data
concepts.summary: Enter text, numbers and dates into cells and understand how the spreadsheet interprets and displays each type.

concepts.name: Basic number and text formatting
concepts.summary: Apply number, currency, percent, date and alignment formats and explain that formatting changes display rather than the stored value.

concepts.name: Simple formulas with operators
concepts.summary: Write formulas starting with an equals sign using +, -, *, / and cell references so results update when inputs change.

concepts.name: Core summary functions
concepts.summary: Use SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT on a range and explain what each returns.

concepts.name: Row and column layout adjustments
concepts.summary: Insert, delete, resize, hide and freeze rows and columns to make a sheet readable.

misconceptions.text: Typing a calculated result into a cell is the same as using a formula.
Formatting a cell as a percent or currency changes the underlying number.
A cell's displayed text is always exactly what is stored in it.

concepts.name: Relative and absolute references
concepts.summary: Copy formulas using relative, absolute and mixed references and predict how addresses change.

concepts.name: Sorting data
concepts.summary: Sort a data table by one or more columns while keeping rows intact.

concepts.name: Filtering data
concepts.summary: Filter a table by text, number or date criteria to show only matching rows without deleting others.

concepts.name: Conditional logic with IF
concepts.summary: Write IF formulas with comparison operators to return different results depending on a condition.

concepts.name: Conditional aggregation functions
concepts.summary: Use SUMIF, COUNTIF and AVERAGEIF to total or count only cells meeting a criterion.

concepts.name: Basic chart creation
concepts.summary: Create column, line and pie charts from a range and add titles, axis labels and legends.

concepts.name: Conditional formatting rules
concepts.summary: Apply rules that highlight cells by value, threshold or duplicate status.

misconceptions.text: Sorting a single column on its own is safe even when neighboring columns hold related data.
Filtering a table deletes the rows that are hidden.
Copying a formula always keeps pointing at the same cells it originally referenced.

concepts.name: Lookup functions
concepts.summary: Retrieve values from a table by key using lookup functions, choosing exact match and handling missing keys.

concepts.name: Nested and combined logic
concepts.summary: Combine IF with AND, OR and other functions to model multi-condition rules and analyse where they fail.

concepts.name: Text and date functions
concepts.summary: Clean, split and combine text and calculate with dates using text and date functions.

concepts.name: Pivot table construction
concepts.summary: Build pivot tables with row, column, value and filter fields to summarize a dataset by category.

concepts.name: Structured data preparation
concepts.summary: Organize data as a flat table with one header row, consistent types and no blanks or merged cells, and diagnose issues that break analysis.

concepts.name: Data validation controls
concepts.summary: Restrict cell entries with lists and rules to prevent invalid input.

concepts.name: Formula error diagnosis
concepts.summary: Interpret error values and use auditing tools to locate and fix formula problems.

concepts.name: Chart selection and design
concepts.summary: Choose chart types suited to the comparison being made and remove misleading or cluttered design.

misconceptions.text: Pivot tables update automatically the moment source data changes.
Merging cells and leaving blank rows makes data tables cleaner for analysis.
Approximate-match lookup is fine as a default on unsorted data.

concepts.name: Dynamic array formulas
concepts.summary: Use array-returning functions that spill results and analyse when they outperform copied formulas.

concepts.name: Named ranges and structured tables
concepts.summary: Use tables and named ranges so formulas stay readable and expand automatically as data grows.

concepts.name: Pivot calculations and slicers
concepts.summary: Extend pivot tables with grouping, calculated fields, percent-of measures and slicers for interactive analysis.

concepts.name: Model structure and assumptions
concepts.summary: Evaluate and design workbooks that separate inputs, calculations and outputs and document assumptions.

concepts.name: What-if and sensitivity analysis
concepts.summary: Use Goal Seek and scenario tools to test how changing inputs affects results and judge reliability.

concepts.name: Cross-sheet and external data
concepts.summary: Combine data from multiple sheets, files or imports and manage refresh and link risks.

concepts.name: Dashboard design
concepts.summary: Assess and assemble charts, pivots and key figures into a clear dashboard that answers specific questions.

misconceptions.text: A workbook that produces the right number today is a sound model.
Goal Seek proves the answer is realistic, not just mathematically achievable.
Linked external data is always current and safe from broken links.

concepts.name: Reusable formula patterns
concepts.summary: Design reusable calculations with LET, LAMBDA or named functions that reduce duplication and error.

concepts.name: Automation with macros and scripts
concepts.summary: Create macros or scripts to automate repetitive workbook tasks and judge when automation is warranted.

concepts.name: Workbook performance optimization
concepts.summary: Evaluate causes of slow workbooks, such as volatile functions and whole-column array calculations, and redesign for speed.

concepts.name: Spreadsheet risk and auditing
concepts.summary: Evaluate workbooks for hidden errors, hard-coded values and logic flaws using systematic review and checks.

concepts.name: Collaboration and access governance
concepts.summary: Judge and set protection, permissions and versioning practices for shared workbooks.

concepts.name: Choosing the right tool
concepts.summary: Decide when a spreadsheet is the right tool versus a database, BI tool or code, based on scale, integrity and repeatability.

concepts.name: Designing templates for others
concepts.summary: Build self-explanatory templates with validation, guidance and protection so non-experts can use them correctly.

misconceptions.text: Any spreadsheet problem is best solved by adding more formulas or macros.
Formulas that return no errors are correct.
Sheet protection or hiding is a secure way to guard sensitive data.

concepts.name: Chronology and periodization
concepts.summary: Place major events and eras such as prehistory, antiquity, medieval, early modern and modern in correct order using BCE/CE dating.

concepts.name: Neolithic agricultural revolution
concepts.summary: Explain how the shift from foraging to farming enabled settled communities and population growth.

concepts.name: River valley civilizations
concepts.summary: Describe how Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus Valley and the Yellow River developed cities, irrigation and writing.

concepts.name: Classical Greece and Rome
concepts.summary: Outline key features of Greek city-states, Athenian democracy, the Roman Republic and Empire.

concepts.name: Early Chinese and Indian states
concepts.summary: Recall major dynasties and empires such as Qin, Han, Maurya and Gupta and their main achievements.

concepts.name: World religions' origins
concepts.summary: Explain where and when Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity and Islam arose and their central ideas.

concepts.name: Primary and secondary sources
concepts.summary: Distinguish evidence created in the period from later accounts written about it.

misconceptions.text: Ancient peoples were primitive and less intelligent than modern people.
Civilizations developed in isolation without contact or exchange.
Farming made life clearly better for everyone who adopted it.

concepts.name: Fall of Rome and successor states
concepts.summary: Describe the causes of Western Roman decline and the Byzantine, Islamic and Germanic kingdoms that followed.

concepts.name: Islamic caliphates and learning
concepts.summary: Explain the expansion of Islamic rule and its contributions in science, mathematics and trade.

concepts.name: Feudalism and medieval Europe
concepts.summary: Apply the ideas of lordship, vassalage and manorial economy to explain medieval European society.

concepts.name: Silk Road exchange networks
concepts.summary: Use examples of goods, ideas and diseases to show how trade routes linked Afro-Eurasia.

concepts.name: Mongol Empire and its effects
concepts.summary: Explain the Mongol conquests and their consequences for trade, politics and the spread of the Black Death.

concepts.name: Pre-Columbian Americas and Africa
concepts.summary: Describe major states such as Aztec, Inca, Mali and Songhai and their economies.

concepts.name: Cause and effect in history
concepts.summary: Apply short-term versus long-term cause and consequence to a given event.

misconceptions.text: The Middle Ages were a uniformly backward 'Dark Age' with no progress.
Rome fell suddenly in 476 CE and the whole empire ended then.
The Mongols were only destructive and contributed nothing to connections between regions.

concepts.name: Renaissance and Reformation
concepts.summary: Analyse how humanism, printing and religious conflict reshaped European thought and politics.

concepts.name: Early modern gunpowder empires
concepts.summary: Compare how the Ottoman, Safavid, Mughal and Chinese empires built and legitimized power.

concepts.name: Columbian Exchange and Atlantic world
concepts.summary: Analyse the biological, economic and demographic impacts of European contact with the Americas and the Atlantic slave system.

concepts.name: Scientific Revolution and Enlightenment
concepts.summary: Apply Enlightenment ideas of reason, rights and natural law to explain political change.

concepts.name: Age of revolutions
concepts.summary: Compare the causes, ideologies and outcomes of the American, French, Haitian and Latin American revolutions.

concepts.name: Industrialization and its consequences
concepts.summary: Analyse why industrialization began in Britain and how it changed economies, cities and class relations.

concepts.name: Source analysis and corroboration
concepts.summary: Analyse a primary source's origin, purpose and audience and cross-check it against other evidence.

misconceptions.text: The Renaissance was a sudden break with the medieval period.
Revolutions always achieved liberty and equality for all people.
Industrialization was an inevitable result of European superiority.

concepts.name: Imperialism and colonial economies
concepts.summary: Analyse economic, ideological and strategic drivers of 19th-century imperialism and its extractive systems.

concepts.name: Responses to Western dominance
concepts.summary: Evaluate reform, resistance and adaptation strategies in Japan, China, India and the Ottoman Empire.

concepts.name: Origins of the world wars
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing explanations for the outbreak of World War I and the failures of the interwar settlement leading to World War II.

concepts.name: Totalitarianism and genocide
concepts.summary: Analyse how totalitarian regimes arose and enabled mass violence including the Holocaust.

concepts.name: Cold War global conflict
concepts.summary: Evaluate the Cold War's ideological and strategic dynamics and its effects on the decolonizing world.

concepts.name: Decolonization movements
concepts.summary: Analyse the varied paths to independence in India, Africa and Southeast Asia and their legacies.

concepts.name: Historiographical schools
concepts.summary: Evaluate how different schools of interpretation shape explanations of the same historical events.

misconceptions.text: World War I was caused solely by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
Colonized peoples were passive recipients of imperial rule.
The Cold War was only a US-Soviet conflict with little effect on the rest of the world.

concepts.name: Global and comparative history methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate comparative, connected and world-systems frameworks for their strengths and blind spots across regions.

concepts.name: Debating the Great Divergence
concepts.summary: Assess rival explanations for why industrial growth diverged between Europe and Asia.

concepts.name: Eurocentrism and periodization critique
concepts.summary: Critique how conventional periodization and narratives embed Eurocentric assumptions.

concepts.name: Memory, politics and commemoration
concepts.summary: Evaluate how states and societies use history in national narratives, memorials and education.

concepts.name: Environmental and big history
concepts.summary: Judge how climate, disease and ecological change act as long-run historical forces.

concepts.name: Designing an original historical argument
concepts.summary: Construct an original, evidence-based thesis using multilingual or varied archival sources and engaging prior scholarship.

concepts.name: Counterfactual and causal reasoning
concepts.summary: Create disciplined counterfactual arguments to weigh contingency against structural causes.

misconceptions.text: A single global narrative can be neutral and free of perspective.
Counterfactuals are idle speculation with no scholarly value.
Using more sources automatically makes a historical argument stronger.

concepts.name: Antiderivative as reverse differentiation
concepts.summary: Recognise that an antiderivative of f is a function F whose derivative is f, and recall that it is not unique.

concepts.name: Indefinite integral and constant
concepts.summary: Explain that the indefinite integral represents a whole family of antiderivatives differing by a constant C.

concepts.name: Basic power rule for integrals
concepts.summary: Understand and state that the integral of x^n is x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C for n not equal to -1, and why n = -1 is excluded.

concepts.name: Standard integral formulas
concepts.summary: Recall antiderivatives of sin x, cos x, e^x, 1/x and sec^2 x by reversing known derivative rules.

concepts.name: Area under a curve idea
concepts.summary: Explain that a definite integral measures signed area between a curve and the x-axis, with area below the axis counting negative.

concepts.name: Linearity of integration
concepts.summary: Understand that integrals split over sums and pull out constant factors, so terms can be integrated one at a time.

misconceptions.text: The integral of 1/x is x^0/0 by the power rule, or is simply ln x with no absolute value needed.
The constant C can be dropped because it does not affect the answer.
A definite integral always gives a positive area.

concepts.name: Riemann sums
concepts.summary: Compute left, right and midpoint sums over a partition to approximate the area under a curve.

concepts.name: Definite integral as limit
concepts.summary: Interpret the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums as the partition width goes to zero.

concepts.name: Properties of definite integrals
concepts.summary: Apply rules such as reversing limits, splitting intervals and comparison to evaluate and simplify definite integrals.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a definite integral as F(b) - F(a) using an antiderivative.

concepts.name: Accumulation function derivative
concepts.summary: Apply the fact that d/dx of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt equals f(x), including with a variable upper limit via the chain rule.

concepts.name: Basic u-substitution
concepts.summary: Choose u so that an inner function and its derivative appear, and integrate in terms of u.

concepts.name: Net change interpretation
concepts.summary: Use the integral of a rate of change to find net change such as displacement from velocity.

misconceptions.text: A Riemann sum gives the exact area for any number of rectangles.
When using u-substitution on a definite integral, the original x-limits can be kept after changing to u.
The integral of velocity gives total distance travelled rather than net displacement.

concepts.name: Integration by parts
concepts.summary: Apply the formula integral u dv = uv - integral v du, choosing u and dv sensibly, including repeated use and cyclic cases.

concepts.name: Trigonometric integrals
concepts.summary: Integrate products and powers of trig functions using identities and substitution.

concepts.name: Partial fraction decomposition
concepts.summary: Decompose a rational function into simpler fractions with linear and repeated factors and integrate each term.

concepts.name: Trigonometric substitution
concepts.summary: Select a sine, tangent or secant substitution based on the radical form and convert back to x using a reference triangle.

concepts.name: Area between curves
concepts.summary: Set up integrals for regions between curves by identifying intersections, upper and lower functions, and when to integrate in y.

concepts.name: Volumes by disks and washers
concepts.summary: Analyse a region and axis of rotation to build a disk or washer integral for the volume.

concepts.name: Method selection for integrals
concepts.summary: Analyse an integrand's form to decide among substitution, parts, partial fractions and trig substitution.

misconceptions.text: The integral of a product is the product of the integrals.
Partial fractions can be applied directly to any rational function, even when the numerator degree is at least the denominator degree.
Area between curves is always the integral of the right-hand function minus the left-hand function, regardless of which is on top.

concepts.name: Shell method
concepts.summary: Derive and apply shell integrals for volumes of revolution and compare when shells or washers give a simpler setup.

concepts.name: Arc length and surface area
concepts.summary: Set up arc length integrals using the square root of 1 + (f')^2 and extend to surface area of revolution.

concepts.name: Improper integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate integrals with infinite limits or discontinuities by taking limits and decide convergence or divergence.

concepts.name: Comparison tests for improper integrals
concepts.summary: Judge convergence of an integral without computing it by comparing with p-integrals and other known cases.

concepts.name: Sequences and series convergence
concepts.summary: Distinguish convergence of a sequence from convergence of a series through its partial sums, using geometric and p-series as benchmarks.

concepts.name: Divergence and integral tests
concepts.summary: Apply the nth-term test and the integral test, checking its positivity, continuity and decreasing conditions.

concepts.name: Comparison and ratio tests
concepts.summary: Evaluate which of comparison, limit comparison, ratio or root tests suits a series and justify the conclusion.

concepts.name: Alternating series and absolute convergence
concepts.summary: Assess alternating series with the alternating series test and classify them as absolutely or conditionally convergent.

misconceptions.text: If the terms of a series tend to zero, the series must converge.
An integral from -infinity to infinity of an odd function is automatically zero.
The ratio test being inconclusive (limit equal to 1) means the series diverges.

concepts.name: Rigour of Riemann integrability
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a function is Riemann integrable using upper and lower sums, and recognise that continuous or bounded functions with finitely many discontinuities qualify.

concepts.name: Proof of the Fundamental Theorem
concepts.summary: Critique and reconstruct the proof linking differentiation and integration via the mean value theorem for integrals.

concepts.name: Numerical integration error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate trapezoidal and Simpson's rules by deriving or applying error bounds and choosing step size for a target accuracy.

concepts.name: Integrals without elementary antiderivatives
concepts.summary: Judge when an integral such as e^(-x^2) has no closed form and select series or numerical approaches instead.

concepts.name: Power series integration
concepts.summary: Construct power series for integrands and integrate term by term within the radius of convergence to obtain series for functions and values.

concepts.name: Taylor remainder and error bounds
concepts.summary: Evaluate approximation accuracy using Taylor remainder and alternating series bounds to justify a truncation.

concepts.name: Modelling with integrals
concepts.summary: Design integral models for quantities such as work, mass, probability, centroids or fluid force by slicing and accumulating.

misconceptions.text: Every continuous function has an antiderivative expressible in elementary functions.
Term-by-term integration of a power series is valid on any interval, even outside the radius of convergence.
Simpson's rule is always more accurate than the trapezoid rule regardless of the function's smoothness.

concepts.name: Null and alternative hypotheses
concepts.summary: State a research question as a null hypothesis of no effect and an alternative hypothesis describing the effect being looked for.

concepts.name: Sample versus population claims
concepts.summary: Explain that a test uses a sample to judge a claim about a population, so the result carries uncertainty.

concepts.name: Test statistic
concepts.summary: Describe a test statistic as a number summarising how far the sample result lies from what the null hypothesis predicts.

concepts.name: P-value meaning
concepts.summary: Interpret a p-value as how probable data at least this extreme would be if the null hypothesis were true.

concepts.name: Significance level alpha
concepts.summary: Recall that alpha is a threshold chosen in advance, often 0.05, against which the p-value is compared.

concepts.name: Reject or fail to reject
concepts.summary: Turn a p-value and alpha into a decision to reject or not reject the null hypothesis, worded correctly.

misconceptions.text: The p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
Failing to reject the null hypothesis proves the null hypothesis is true.
A result with p below 0.05 proves the effect is real and important.

concepts.name: One-tailed versus two-tailed tests
concepts.summary: Choose a one- or two-sided alternative from the question asked and compute the matching p-value.

concepts.name: Type I and Type II errors
concepts.summary: Distinguish rejecting a true null from missing a false null and relate each to alpha and beta.

concepts.name: One-sample z-test
concepts.summary: Run a z-test for a mean with known standard deviation, computing the z statistic and its p-value.

concepts.name: One-sample t-test
concepts.summary: Test a mean against a hypothesised value using the t statistic, degrees of freedom and the t distribution.

concepts.name: Critical values and rejection regions
concepts.summary: Find the cutoff for a given alpha and decide by checking whether the test statistic falls in the rejection region.

concepts.name: Test for a proportion
concepts.summary: Test a sample proportion against a claimed population proportion using the normal approximation.

concepts.name: Confidence interval link
concepts.summary: Explain that a two-sided test at alpha agrees with whether the hypothesised value lies inside the (1-alpha) confidence interval.

misconceptions.text: A one-tailed test can be chosen after seeing which direction the data went.
Alpha is the probability that the null hypothesis is true when we reject it.
Use a z-test whenever the sample is large or the standard deviation is estimated, regardless of other conditions.

concepts.name: Two-sample t-tests
concepts.summary: Compare the means of two independent groups, choosing pooled or Welch variants and computing the statistic correctly.

concepts.name: Paired t-test
concepts.summary: Analyse before-after or matched data by testing the mean of the within-pair differences.

concepts.name: Chi-square test of independence
concepts.summary: Compute expected counts from a contingency table and test whether two categorical variables are associated.

concepts.name: Chi-square goodness of fit
concepts.summary: Compare observed category counts with those expected under a specified distribution.

concepts.name: Test assumptions and diagnostics
concepts.summary: Check independence, normality, equal variance and expected-count conditions and judge when they are violated.

concepts.name: Statistical power
concepts.summary: Analyse how sample size, effect size, alpha and variability determine the chance of detecting a real effect.

concepts.name: Effect size measures
concepts.summary: Separate statistical from practical significance by quantifying the magnitude of an effect.

concepts.name: Choosing the appropriate test
concepts.summary: Select a test from the data type, number of groups, pairing and the question asked.

misconceptions.text: An independent two-sample t-test is fine for before-and-after measurements on the same subjects.
A significant chi-square test shows that one variable causes the other.
A tiny p-value means the effect is large.

concepts.name: ANOVA and F-test
concepts.summary: Compare more than two group means by partitioning variance and interpreting the F statistic.

concepts.name: Multiple comparisons correction
concepts.summary: Evaluate how many tests inflate false positives and choose a correction such as Bonferroni or FDR control.

concepts.name: Post-hoc pairwise testing
concepts.summary: Follow a significant ANOVA with controlled pairwise comparisons to locate which groups differ.

concepts.name: Nonparametric alternatives
concepts.summary: Judge when rank-based tests are preferable to t-tests given outliers, skew or ordinal data.

concepts.name: Permutation and bootstrap tests
concepts.summary: Build a null distribution by resampling to test hypotheses without relying on parametric assumptions.

concepts.name: Power analysis and sample size
concepts.summary: Plan a study by determining the sample size needed for a target power given an expected effect size.

concepts.name: P-hacking and researcher degrees of freedom
concepts.summary: Evaluate how flexible analysis choices and selective reporting invalidate p-values.

concepts.name: Equivalence and non-inferiority testing
concepts.summary: Test whether an effect is small enough to be negligible rather than merely not significant.

misconceptions.text: Running several t-tests between all pairs of groups is equivalent to a single ANOVA.
Nonparametric tests make no assumptions at all and are always safer than t-tests.
A non-significant result shows two treatments are equivalent.

concepts.name: Neyman-Pearson versus Fisher frameworks
concepts.summary: Critique the hybrid null hypothesis significance testing practice by contrasting Fisher's evidential p-values with Neyman-Pearson error-rate decisions.

concepts.name: Bayesian alternatives to testing
concepts.summary: Evaluate Bayes factors and posterior inference against frequentist tests for answering what the data say about a hypothesis.

concepts.name: Sequential and adaptive testing
concepts.summary: Design experiments with interim looks that keep error rates valid, using alpha-spending or sequential methods.

concepts.name: Replication and meta-analytic evidence
concepts.summary: Assess how publication bias, low power and replication results affect the credibility of significant findings.

concepts.name: Likelihood ratio, Wald and score tests
concepts.summary: Compare the large-sample tests derived from the likelihood and decide which suits a given model.

concepts.name: Robust testing under violated assumptions
concepts.summary: Design analyses that keep valid error rates under dependence, unequal variance or non-normality, verified by simulation.

concepts.name: Pre-registration and analysis planning
concepts.summary: Create a pre-specified analysis and testing protocol that separates confirmatory from exploratory inference.

misconceptions.text: Peeking at interim results and stopping once p drops below 0.05 is harmless as long as the final p-value is reported.
A Bayes factor and a p-value measure the same thing and always lead to the same conclusion.
Pre-registration forbids any exploratory analysis.

issues: adb-3 (z-test) and adb-4 (t-test) are near-duplicate one-sample mean tests; the z-test with known sigma is a rare special case and adb-4 depends on it only loosely.
adb-3 depends on adb-1 and nov-3 but the proportion test adb-6 and the t-test should be separate branches; chain adb-3 -> adb-4 is weak.
adb-7 depends on adb-5 but should depend on the t-test or z-test and confidence intervals, not critical values specifically.
nov-5 is C1 though the stage band is C1-C2, which is fine, but nov-6 summary Bloom C2 is more an application; acceptable.
cmp-5 'Test assumptions and diagnostics' is vague and cmp-5 depends on chi-square but not on two-sample tests.

cmp-6 and prf-6 overlap: power concept at competent and sample size planning at proficient is fine, but cmp-7 effect size should precede power planning; cmp-6 -> cmp-7 order is reversed (power depends on effect size).
