concepts.summary: Assess how JavaScript rendering affects indexing and choose between server-side, static and client-side approaches.

concepts.name: Site architecture and link equity
concepts.summary: Judge and redesign site structure, depth and internal linking to distribute authority to priority pages.

concepts.name: Link building strategy evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate link acquisition tactics for effectiveness and risk, distinguishing earned links from manipulative schemes.

concepts.name: Migration planning and risk
concepts.summary: Assess a domain or platform migration plan, with redirect mapping, pre and post benchmarks and rollback checks.

concepts.name: Content quality and E-E-A-T
concepts.summary: Evaluate content against quality guidelines for experience, expertise, authority and trust and decide what to improve or prune.

concepts.name: International and multilingual SEO
concepts.summary: Analyse hreflang, domain structure and localisation choices for sites serving multiple languages or regions.

concepts.name: SEO measurement and attribution
concepts.summary: Judge organic performance with rankings, traffic, conversions and Search Console data while accounting for seasonality and updates.

misconceptions.text: Google renders all JavaScript content instantly and perfectly, so rendering strategy is irrelevant.
Crawl budget is a concern for every website.
Deleting or disavowing links is routine maintenance for any site.

concepts.name: Algorithm update diagnosis
concepts.summary: Critically assess traffic changes around algorithm updates to separate causes from coincidence and decide on a response.

concepts.name: Enterprise SEO governance
concepts.summary: Evaluate processes, templates and team responsibilities that keep SEO quality across large sites and many contributors.

concepts.name: Programmatic SEO design
concepts.summary: Design templated page systems with unique value, safeguards against thin content and scalable internal linking.

concepts.name: SEO experimentation framework
concepts.summary: Create controlled tests using page groups and statistical modelling to measure the effect of SEO changes.

concepts.name: Search in AI-driven results
concepts.summary: Evaluate how generative answers, SERP features and zero-click results change visibility strategy and measurement.

concepts.name: Entity and topical authority strategy
concepts.summary: Build a strategy that establishes a brand and topics as recognised entities through content, markup and off-site signals.

concepts.name: SEO business case and prioritisation
concepts.summary: Create forecasts and prioritisation models that size opportunities and justify investment against other channels.

misconceptions.text: Every ranking drop after an update means the site was penalised and needs fixing.
Publishing thousands of templated pages reliably scales organic traffic.
SEO changes can be tested like A/B tests by splitting users between versions.

concepts.name: Scarcity and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Explain that unlimited wants meet limited resources, so every choice requires giving something up.

concepts.name: Opportunity cost
concepts.summary: Identify the value of the best forgone alternative in a simple everyday or business choice.

concepts.name: Demand and law of demand
concepts.summary: Describe how quantity demanded falls as price rises, other things equal, and read a demand schedule or curve.

concepts.name: Supply and law of supply
concepts.summary: Describe how quantity supplied rises with price and read a supply schedule or curve.

concepts.name: Market equilibrium price
concepts.summary: Locate the price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded and explain why surpluses and shortages push prices toward it.

concepts.name: Marginal thinking
concepts.summary: Recognise that rational choices compare the extra benefit and extra cost of one more unit.

concepts.name: Positive versus normative statements
concepts.summary: Distinguish testable statements about what is from value judgements about what ought to be.

misconceptions.text: Scarcity only affects poor people or poor countries.
Opportunity cost is the total of all money spent on a choice.
A shortage means a good has completely run out.

concepts.name: Shifts versus movements
aliases: change in demand vs quantity demanded
concepts.summary: Apply the distinction between a price-driven movement along a curve and a non-price shift of the curve.

concepts.name: Determinants of demand and supply
concepts.summary: Use income, related goods, tastes, input costs and technology to predict which curve shifts and in which direction.

concepts.name: Comparative statics of equilibrium
concepts.summary: Predict the new equilibrium price and quantity after a shift in one curve or both.

concepts.name: Price elasticity of demand
concepts.summary: Calculate and interpret elasticity from price and quantity changes, classifying demand as elastic, inelastic or unit elastic.

concepts.name: Elasticity and total revenue
concepts.summary: Apply elasticity to predict how a price change alters a seller's revenue.

concepts.name: Price ceilings and floors
concepts.summary: Show how binding price controls create shortages or surpluses in a supply and demand diagram.

concepts.name: Consumer and producer surplus
concepts.summary: Measure the benefit buyers and sellers receive as areas under demand and above supply.

misconceptions.text: A higher price shifts the demand curve to the left.
Elasticity is the same as the slope of the demand curve.
Raising price always increases a firm's revenue.

concepts.name: Utility maximisation and budget constraint
concepts.summary: Derive a consumer's optimal bundle by equating marginal utility per dollar across goods given income and prices.

concepts.name: Short-run production and diminishing returns
concepts.summary: Analyse how output responds to additional variable input when some inputs are fixed.

concepts.name: Cost curves
concepts.summary: Derive and relate fixed, variable, average and marginal costs, including why MC crosses average curves at their minima.

concepts.name: Profit maximisation rule
concepts.summary: Determine the profit-maximising output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost and when a firm should shut down.

concepts.name: Perfect competition outcomes
concepts.summary: Analyse how price-taking firms, entry and exit drive long-run price to minimum average cost.

concepts.name: Monopoly pricing and deadweight loss
concepts.summary: Explain why a monopolist sets MR = MC, charges above marginal cost and causes deadweight loss.

concepts.name: Other elasticities
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret income, cross-price and supply elasticities to classify goods and predict responses.

concepts.name: Tax incidence
concepts.summary: Analyse how the burden of a tax splits between buyers and sellers according to relative elasticities.

misconceptions.text: A firm should produce where average cost is lowest to maximise profit.
Monopolists can charge any price they like and still sell the same quantity.
The party legally required to pay a tax is the one who bears its burden.

concepts.name: Long-run costs and scale
concepts.summary: Analyse how returns to scale and the long-run average cost curve determine efficient firm size and market structure.

concepts.name: Price discrimination
concepts.summary: Evaluate when and how firms with market power charge different prices to different customers and the welfare effects.

concepts.name: Monopolistic competition
concepts.summary: Analyse firms with differentiated products, free entry, excess capacity and zero long-run profit.

concepts.name: Oligopoly and game theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate strategic interaction among few firms using Nash equilibrium and why collusion is unstable.

concepts.name: Externalities and Pigouvian remedies
concepts.summary: Evaluate how divergence between private and social cost or benefit causes inefficiency and compare taxes, subsidies and regulation.

concepts.name: Public goods and common resources
concepts.summary: Analyse non-rivalry and non-excludability and why markets under-provide public goods and over-use common resources.

concepts.name: Asymmetric information
concepts.summary: Analyse how hidden information or action distorts markets such as insurance and used goods.

concepts.name: Factor markets and wages
concepts.summary: Analyse how firms hire inputs where marginal revenue product equals factor price and how wages are set.

misconceptions.text: Oligopoly firms always collude because it maximises joint profit.
Any externality should be eliminated entirely.
Price discrimination always harms consumers and lowers total welfare.

concepts.name: Comparing remedies for market failure
concepts.summary: Evaluate corrective taxes, tradable permits, regulation and bargaining under uncertainty and transaction costs.

concepts.name: Coase theorem and property rights
concepts.summary: Judge when private negotiation can resolve externalities and why transaction costs and unclear rights limit it.

concepts.name: Government failure and second best
concepts.summary: Assess when intervention worsens outcomes because of information limits, incentives or other existing distortions.

concepts.name: Mechanism design and auctions
concepts.summary: Design rules or auction formats that elicit truthful information and achieve a stated objective.

concepts.name: Contracts and principal-agent incentives
concepts.summary: Design contracts or signals that align incentives under hidden information or hidden action.

concepts.name: Welfare analysis and distribution
concepts.summary: Critique policies using Pareto and compensation criteria while weighing efficiency against equity.

concepts.name: Competition policy and market definition
concepts.summary: Evaluate mergers and conduct using concentration, substitutes, entry barriers and consumer welfare effects.

concepts.name: Behavioural departures from rationality
concepts.summary: Evaluate where systematic biases undermine standard choice models and how this changes market and policy design.

misconceptions.text: The Coase theorem shows markets always solve externalities without government.
Fixing one market distortion always moves the economy closer to efficiency.
A Pareto-efficient outcome is necessarily fair.

concepts.name: Gross domestic product definition
concepts.summary: State that GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a period and recognise what it counts and excludes.

concepts.name: Real versus nominal values
concepts.summary: Explain why nominal values must be adjusted for price changes to show real changes in output or income.

concepts.name: Inflation and price indices
concepts.summary: Describe inflation as a sustained rise in the general price level and how a basket-based index measures it.

concepts.name: Unemployment rate measurement
concepts.summary: Explain how the unemployment rate is computed from the labour force and why people outside the labour force are not counted.

concepts.name: Economic growth and recessions
concepts.summary: Distinguish long-run growth from short-run fluctuations and recognise expansions, peaks, recessions and troughs.

concepts.name: Central bank and interest rates
concepts.summary: Recall that a central bank sets a policy interest rate that influences borrowing costs across the economy.

concepts.name: Government budget, deficit and debt
concepts.summary: Distinguish a deficit (an annual flow) from debt (an accumulated stock) and identify main taxes and spending.

misconceptions.text: A government deficit and the national debt are the same thing.
A rise in nominal GDP always means the economy produced more.
Falling inflation means prices are falling.

concepts.name: Expenditure approach to GDP
concepts.summary: Compute GDP from consumption, investment, government purchases and net exports and classify transactions into those components.

concepts.name: Types of unemployment
concepts.summary: Classify cases of unemployment as frictional, structural or cyclical and relate them to the natural rate.

concepts.name: Causes of inflation
concepts.summary: Apply demand-pull and cost-push explanations to scenarios and distinguish them.

concepts.name: Aggregate demand and supply
concepts.summary: Use the AD-AS diagram to show how demand and supply shifts change output and the price level.

concepts.name: Fiscal policy tools
concepts.summary: Predict the direction of effect on aggregate demand from changes in taxes and government spending.

concepts.name: Monetary policy tools
concepts.summary: Trace how interest rate changes and open market operations affect borrowing, spending and output.

concepts.name: Exchange rates and trade balance
concepts.summary: Explain how currency appreciation or depreciation affects exports, imports and the trade balance.

misconceptions.text: Zero unemployment is the goal of a healthy economy.
Buying stocks or used goods counts as investment in GDP.
A trade deficit always signals a weak economy.

concepts.name: Fiscal multiplier
concepts.summary: Calculate and interpret the multiplier from the marginal propensity to consume and note why real multipliers vary.

concepts.name: Short-run Phillips curve
concepts.summary: Analyse the inverse inflation-unemployment relation and why it shifts with expectations and supply shocks.

concepts.name: Money market and loanable funds
concepts.summary: Analyse how money supply, money demand and saving-investment balance determine interest rates.

concepts.name: Crowding out
concepts.summary: Analyse how government borrowing can raise interest rates and reduce private investment.

concepts.name: Long-run growth determinants
concepts.summary: Decompose growth into capital, labour and productivity contributions and explain diminishing returns to capital.

concepts.name: Balance of payments accounts
concepts.summary: Interpret current and financial account entries and why they offset each other.

concepts.name: Automatic stabilisers and lags
concepts.summary: Analyse how built-in stabilisers work and how recognition, decision and impact lags limit discretionary policy.

misconceptions.text: Policymakers can permanently lower unemployment by accepting higher inflation.
Government spending always raises GDP by the full multiplier amount.
Printing money is how central banks normally change interest rates.

concepts.name: Expectations and long-run neutrality
concepts.summary: Analyse how expectations make the long-run Phillips curve vertical and money neutral in the long run.

concepts.name: Monetary policy rules
concepts.summary: Evaluate rule-based versus discretionary policy and judge inflation targeting against alternatives.

concepts.name: Open-economy policy effects
concepts.summary: Evaluate how fiscal and monetary policy work under floating and fixed exchange rates with capital mobility.

concepts.name: Debt sustainability
concepts.summary: Assess whether a debt ratio is sustainable using interest rate, growth and primary balance.

concepts.name: Supply shocks and stagflation
concepts.summary: Analyse why supply shocks raise prices while lowering output and constrain policy responses.

concepts.name: Financial crises and balance sheets
concepts.summary: Analyse how leverage and asset price falls propagate into recessions.

concepts.name: Zero lower bound and unconventional policy
concepts.summary: Evaluate tools used when policy rates cannot fall further and their limits.

misconceptions.text: A government's debt is like a household's and must eventually be fully repaid.
Central banks can fix any recession by cutting rates.
Fiscal stimulus works the same way under every exchange rate regime.

concepts.name: DSGE and model assumptions
concepts.summary: Critique the assumptions, strengths and failures of microfounded macro models for policy analysis.

concepts.name: Empirical identification of shocks
concepts.summary: Evaluate methods for isolating causal effects of policy and shocks and their limits.

concepts.name: Policy regime design
concepts.summary: Design monetary and fiscal frameworks that balance credibility, flexibility and accountability.

concepts.name: Time inconsistency and credibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate how incentives to deviate from announced plans undermine policy and why behaviour shifts with regimes.

concepts.name: Crisis response synthesis
concepts.summary: Construct a coherent combination of monetary, fiscal and financial measures for a given crisis.

concepts.name: Global imbalances and currency unions
concepts.summary: Evaluate the costs and benefits of currency unions and persistent external imbalances.

concepts.name: Long-run secular trends
concepts.summary: Assess evidence on falling natural interest rates, productivity and demographics shaping policy room.

misconceptions.text: A well-fitted macro model can be used unchanged to predict the effects of a new policy regime.
Central bank independence guarantees low inflation regardless of fiscal conditions.
Correlations between policy changes and outcomes directly reveal causal policy effects.

concepts.name: Purpose of three statements
concepts.summary: Recall what the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement each report and the question each answers about a company.

concepts.name: Income statement structure
concepts.summary: Explain how revenue flows down through costs and expenses to gross profit, operating profit and net income.

concepts.name: Balance sheet structure
concepts.summary: Describe how assets, liabilities and equity are grouped into current and non-current items at a point in time.

concepts.name: Cash flow statement sections
concepts.summary: Distinguish operating, investing and financing cash flows and what kinds of transactions fall in each.

concepts.name: Profit versus cash
concepts.summary: Explain why net income and cash generated in a period differ because of accrual accounting.

concepts.name: Ratio as a comparison
concepts.summary: State that a ratio divides one statement figure by another to make companies and periods comparable regardless of size.

misconceptions.text: Net income is the same as the cash a company has received during the period.
A large profit means the company has a large cash balance.
The balance sheet shows performance over a year just like the income statement.

concepts.name: Profit margin ratios
concepts.summary: Calculate gross, operating and net margins and interpret what each says about pricing and cost control.

concepts.name: Liquidity ratios
concepts.summary: Compute current and quick ratios and interpret a firm's ability to meet short-term obligations.

concepts.name: Return on assets and equity
concepts.summary: Calculate ROA and ROE and explain what they show about how efficiently capital generates profit.

concepts.name: Leverage ratios
concepts.summary: Compute debt-to-equity and interest coverage and interpret how much a firm relies on borrowing.

concepts.name: Activity turnover ratios
concepts.summary: Calculate inventory, receivables and asset turnover and read them as measures of operating efficiency.

concepts.name: Horizontal and vertical analysis
concepts.summary: Apply year-over-year change and common-size percentages to spot trends and changes in statement composition.

concepts.name: Free cash flow basics
concepts.summary: Calculate operating cash flow less capital expenditure and explain it as cash available after maintaining the asset base.

misconceptions.text: A higher current ratio is always better.
A single ratio for one year is enough to judge a company.
Debt is always bad, so a lower debt-to-equity ratio always signals a better company.

concepts.name: DuPont decomposition
concepts.summary: Break ROE into net margin, asset turnover and financial leverage to diagnose what drives returns.

concepts.name: Cash conversion cycle
concepts.summary: Combine days inventory, receivables and payables to analyse how efficiently working capital turns into cash.

concepts.name: Earnings quality assessment
concepts.summary: Compare operating cash flow with net income and examine accruals to judge how sustainable and reliable reported earnings are.

concepts.name: Peer and industry benchmarking
concepts.summary: Select appropriate peers and adjust for industry norms and accounting differences before comparing ratios.

concepts.name: Non-recurring item adjustment
concepts.summary: Identify one-off gains, write-downs and restructuring charges and adjust earnings to reflect recurring performance.

concepts.name: Debt capacity and solvency
concepts.summary: Analyse net debt, EBITDA-based leverage and coverage together with maturities to assess ability to service debt.

concepts.name: Footnote and disclosure reading
concepts.summary: Use notes on accounting policies, debt, leases and segments to explain and qualify the face-statement numbers.

misconceptions.text: A high ROE always means a highly profitable and healthy business.
Ratios can be compared directly between any two companies regardless of industry or accounting policy.
EBITDA is equivalent to cash flow.

concepts.name: Accounting policy comparability
concepts.summary: Evaluate how choices such as inventory method, depreciation and revenue recognition distort comparisons and restate to a common basis.

concepts.name: Lease and off-balance-sheet adjustments
concepts.summary: Adjust debt, assets and coverage ratios for leases and other obligations to reflect true leverage.

concepts.name: Red flags for manipulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate warning signs such as receivables outpacing sales, aggressive capitalisation and persistent gaps between profit and cash.

concepts.name: Return on invested capital analysis
concepts.summary: Assess ROIC against cost of capital to judge whether growth creates or destroys value.

concepts.name: Segment and geographic analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse segment margins, growth and capital use to see which parts drive consolidated results.

concepts.name: Sustainable growth and funding
concepts.summary: Judge whether growth can be funded from retained earnings and operating cash or depends on external capital.

concepts.name: Forecast-based ratio stress testing
concepts.summary: Project statements under downside scenarios and evaluate effects on liquidity, covenants and coverage.

misconceptions.text: If statements are audited and comply with standards, accounting-policy differences do not affect comparability.
Positive net income and growing revenue show that growth is creating value.
Manipulation shows up only as outright fraud, so compliant statements need no scepticism.

concepts.name: Integrated firm assessment
concepts.summary: Synthesise profitability, liquidity, leverage, cash generation and earnings quality into a defensible overall judgement and know which evidence outweighs the rest.

concepts.name: Sector-specific analytical frameworks
concepts.summary: Evaluate when standard ratios fail, as in banks or asset-light and cyclical firms, and choose sector-appropriate metrics.

concepts.name: Analytical model design
concepts.summary: Design a repeatable framework or scorecard that combines adjusted metrics and trends for screening or credit decisions.

concepts.name: Linking statements to valuation
concepts.summary: Translate normalised earnings, reinvestment and returns into forecast assumptions that feed a valuation or credit view.

concepts.name: Standards and regime differences
concepts.summary: Evaluate how differing accounting standards and regulatory regimes change reported figures and conclusions in cross-border comparison.

concepts.name: Communicating analytical conclusions
concepts.summary: Construct a clear, evidence-based, caveated recommendation that reconciles conflicting signals for decision-makers.

misconceptions.text: A single well-chosen model or ratio set works for every industry.
Sophisticated statement analysis removes the need for judgement about uncertain forecasts.
Moving between IFRS and US GAAP only changes presentation, not the numbers.

concepts.name: Italian vowel and consonant pronunciation
concepts.summary: Pronounce the five pure vowels and consonants consistently, since Italian spelling is largely phonetic.

concepts.name: Hard and soft c and g
concepts.summary: Explain that c and g are soft before e and i (cena, gelato) and hard before a, o, u or with h (chi, ghetto).

concepts.name: Gn and gli sounds
concepts.summary: Recognise and produce gn as in lasagna and gli as in figlio.

concepts.name: Double consonant length
concepts.summary: Hold doubled consonants longer and understand that this changes meaning, as in pala/palla and caro/carro.

concepts.name: Greetings and politeness phrases
concepts.summary: Recall and use buongiorno, buonasera, ciao, grazie, prego, per favore and scusi in the right situations.

concepts.name: Café and restaurant ordering phrases
concepts.summary: Understand and use set phrases such as vorrei un caffè, il conto, per favore and un tavolo per due.

concepts.name: Noun gender and number
concepts.summary: Identify nouns as masculine or feminine and form regular plurals from the endings -o/-i, -a/-e and -e/-i.

misconceptions.text: Double consonants are spelled twice but pronounced like single ones.
The letter c is always pronounced like k.
Gli is pronounced like English gl in glue.

concepts.name: Definite articles il, lo, gli
concepts.summary: Choose il, lo, l', la, i, gli or le according to the gender, number and initial sound of the following word.

concepts.name: Indefinite articles un, uno, una
concepts.summary: Select un, uno, una or un' correctly depending on the following noun.

concepts.name: Essere in the present
concepts.summary: Conjugate essere and use it for identity, origin, state and description.

concepts.name: Avere in the present
concepts.summary: Conjugate avere and use it for possession and idioms such as avere fame and avere vent'anni.

concepts.name: Regular present tense verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate regular -are, -ere and -ire verbs in the present and use them in simple sentences.

concepts.name: Adjective agreement and placement
concepts.summary: Make adjectives agree in gender and number with nouns and place them correctly, usually after the noun.

concepts.name: Articulated prepositions
concepts.summary: Combine di, a, da, in and su with definite articles, as in al bar and nel ristorante.

misconceptions.text: Il is the masculine article for every masculine noun.
Subject pronouns must always be stated, as in English.
Adjectives always come before the noun, as in English.

concepts.name: Passato prossimo formation
concepts.summary: Form the passato prossimo with the present of avere or essere plus the past participle, including irregular participles.

concepts.name: Choosing avere or essere auxiliary
concepts.summary: Decide between avere and essere as auxiliary, and apply participle agreement with essere.

concepts.name: Imperfetto formation and use
concepts.summary: Form the imperfetto and use it for habits, descriptions and ongoing past actions.

concepts.name: Contrasting passato prossimo and imperfetto
concepts.summary: Analyse a narrative to decide which past tense fits completed events versus background or repeated actions.

concepts.name: Direct and indirect object pronouns
concepts.summary: Use lo, la, li, le, mi, ti, gli and le correctly, including agreement with the participle in compound tenses.

concepts.name: Reflexive verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate reflexive verbs and recognise that they take essere in compound tenses.

concepts.name: Future and conditional
concepts.summary: Form and use the simple future and present conditional, including polite requests such as vorrei.

misconceptions.text: Passato prossimo always takes avere as its auxiliary.
Imperfetto and passato prossimo are interchangeable and differ only in style.
The past participle never changes form.

concepts.name: Congiuntivo presente forms
concepts.summary: Form the present subjunctive of regular and common irregular verbs and recognise its endings in context.

concepts.name: Triggers for the congiuntivo
concepts.summary: Identify expressions of opinion, doubt, desire and emotion, and conjunctions like benché, that require the subjunctive.

concepts.name: Congiuntivo imperfetto and past
concepts.summary: Form and apply the imperfect and past subjunctive with correct sequence of tenses.

concepts.name: Hypothetical if-clauses
concepts.summary: Choose the right mood and tense in real, possible and unreal conditions, such as se avessi tempo, verrei.

concepts.name: Passato remoto
concepts.summary: Recognise and interpret the passato remoto in narrative and understand regional differences in its use.

concepts.name: Combined and double pronouns
concepts.summary: Combine pronouns such as glielo, me lo and ce ne and order them correctly with verbs.

concepts.name: Formal and informal register
concepts.summary: Judge when to use tu or Lei and adjust vocabulary and verb forms to the social situation.

misconceptions.text: The congiuntivo is optional and only literary, so the indicative can always replace it.
The subjunctive is used after every che clause.
The passato remoto is used everywhere in Italy instead of the passato prossimo.

concepts.name: Stylistic choice of mood and tense
concepts.summary: Evaluate when indicative or subjunctive, and which past tense, gives the intended nuance in writing and speech.

concepts.name: Regional variation and dialect influence
concepts.summary: Assess how regional Italian, dialects and standard Italian differ in pronunciation, lexicon and tense usage.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and pragmatic expression
concepts.summary: Judge the appropriateness of idioms, discourse markers and politeness strategies across contexts.

concepts.name: Complex sentence construction
concepts.summary: Compose fluent, well-structured texts that use subordination, relative clauses, and implicit forms like gerundio and infinito.

concepts.name: Register-adapted text production
concepts.summary: Create texts such as formal emails, narratives and reviews tuned to audience and purpose.

concepts.name: Error diagnosis and L1 interference
concepts.summary: Diagnose typical learner errors, including those caused by the first language, and design corrective practice.

misconceptions.text: Standard Italian is spoken uniformly across Italy.
Grammatical correctness alone guarantees natural and appropriate Italian.
Literal translation of idioms from one's own language usually yields natural Italian.

concepts.name: Beginning, middle and end
concepts.summary: Recall that a story moves through a setup, a developing middle and a conclusion, and identify these parts in a simple tale.

concepts.name: Character and desire
concepts.summary: Explain that a story centers on a character who wants something, and that this desire drives what happens.

concepts.name: Conflict as obstacle
concepts.summary: Understand that conflict is whatever stands between the character and their goal, and that without it there is no story.

concepts.name: Stakes
concepts.summary: Explain that stakes are what the character stands to gain or lose, and that they give the audience a reason to care.

concepts.name: Climax and resolution
concepts.summary: Identify the climax as the peak moment of confrontation and the resolution as the outcome that settles the story.

concepts.name: Story versus list of events
concepts.summary: Distinguish a story, where events cause one another, from a mere sequence of things that happened.

misconceptions.text: A story is just a series of events told in order.
Conflict means a fight or violence between characters.
Stakes only matter in life-or-death stories.

concepts.name: Three-act structure
concepts.summary: Apply the setup, confrontation and resolution framework to outline a short story with turning points between acts.

concepts.name: Inciting incident
concepts.summary: Place an event early in a story that disrupts the status quo and sets the protagonist on a path toward a goal.

concepts.name: Rising action and escalation
concepts.summary: Sequence complications so each raises difficulty or stakes and builds toward the climax.

concepts.name: Show, don't tell
concepts.summary: Rewrite abstract statements of emotion or trait into concrete actions, details and dialogue.

concepts.name: Story hooks
concepts.summary: Write an opening that raises a question or tension so the audience wants to hear more.

concepts.name: Basic character arc
concepts.summary: Describe how a character begins with a flaw or belief and changes by the end because of what they experience.

concepts.name: Sensory and specific detail
concepts.summary: Use specific sensory details in place of generalities to make scenes tangible.

misconceptions.text: The inciting incident is the same as the climax.
Showing means adding more description and adjectives.
Three-act structure is a rigid formula where each act has the same length.

concepts.name: Hero's journey stages
concepts.summary: Map a story onto the stages of departure, initiation and return, such as the call, ordeal and return with the elixir.

concepts.name: Internal versus external conflict
concepts.summary: Analyse how a character's external goal and inner flaw interact, and how the want diverges from the need.

concepts.name: Pacing and tension control
concepts.summary: Analyse how scene length, reveals and withheld information raise or release tension across a story.

concepts.name: Business story structure
concepts.summary: Build a short business story with a relatable protagonist, a clear challenge, a turning point and a point tied to the message.

concepts.name: Audience-centered framing
concepts.summary: Analyse what an audience cares about and choose the story, details and emphasis that connect to it.

concepts.name: Turning points and reversals
concepts.summary: Identify and design moments where circumstances or understanding shift and change the story's direction.

concepts.name: Emotional beats
concepts.summary: Plan the sequence of emotions the audience should feel and attach each to a specific moment.

misconceptions.text: The hero's journey must be followed step by step for every story to work.
A business story just needs facts and results; emotion is unprofessional.
What the character wants and what they need are the same thing.

concepts.name: Subtext and implication
concepts.summary: Analyse how meaning conveyed through gaps, gestures and omissions engages the audience more than explicit statement.

concepts.name: Evaluating structural fit
concepts.summary: Judge which structure, such as three acts, journey, in medias res or nested stories, best suits a given purpose and context.

concepts.name: Character arc variants
concepts.summary: Distinguish positive, negative and flat arcs and analyse how each shapes theme and audience response.

concepts.name: Theme and controlling idea
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether every scene and detail serves a single underlying idea the story proves through its outcome.

concepts.name: Persuasive narrative design
concepts.summary: Evaluate how stories shift beliefs or decisions, including transportation, identification and the risk of manipulation.

concepts.name: Critique and revision
concepts.summary: Diagnose weaknesses such as flat stakes or unearned endings and revise by cutting, reordering and sharpening.

concepts.name: Oral delivery and presence
concepts.summary: Analyse how voice, pause, pacing and gesture shape the impact of a story told live.

misconceptions.text: Characters should always change positively by the end of a story.
Subtext means hiding the point so the audience has to guess it.
A moving story persuades on its own, so supporting evidence is unnecessary.

concepts.name: Original structure design
concepts.summary: Create new or hybrid narrative structures, such as nonlinear, braided or fragmented forms, that serve a specific emotional effect.

concepts.name: Subverting conventions deliberately
concepts.summary: Evaluate when breaking an expected convention strengthens a story and when it merely confuses the audience.

concepts.name: Narrative strategy for organizations
concepts.summary: Design a body of stories that carries an organization's purpose, values and change agenda across audiences and channels.

concepts.name: Ethics of storytelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate questions of truthfulness, consent, representation and emotional manipulation in using real people's stories.

concepts.name: Adapting across media
concepts.summary: Redesign one story for speech, page, screen, slides or interactive formats, using each medium's strengths.

concepts.name: Unreliable narration and perspective
concepts.summary: Evaluate how narrator choice, reliability and withheld perspective shape audience trust and interpretation.

concepts.name: Coaching others' stories
concepts.summary: Develop methods to elicit, shape and give feedback on others' stories while preserving their authentic voice.

misconceptions.text: Expert storytellers simply ignore structure and rely on instinct.
A story that is emotionally true can be freely embellished for effect.
A story that works in one medium will work unchanged in another.

concepts.name: Carbon bonding and hybridisation
concepts.summary: Explain how carbon forms four bonds and how sp3, sp2 and sp hybridisation determine geometry.

concepts.name: Structural representations
concepts.summary: Read and draw Lewis, condensed and skeletal structures and interpret implied carbons and hydrogens.

concepts.name: Common functional groups
concepts.summary: Recognise alcohols, ethers, amines, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amides and alkenes/alkynes in structures.

concepts.name: IUPAC alkane nomenclature
concepts.summary: Name branched alkanes and simple substituted compounds by finding the parent chain and numbering substituents.

concepts.name: Isomerism types
concepts.summary: Distinguish constitutional isomers from stereoisomers and draw isomers of a given formula.

concepts.name: Polarity and intermolecular forces
concepts.summary: Relate bond polarity and intermolecular forces to boiling point and solubility of organic compounds.

misconceptions.text: Each vertex and line end in a skeletal structure is a carbon with no hydrogens attached.
Molecules with the same molecular formula are the same compound.
Larger molecules always have higher boiling points regardless of functional groups or branching.

concepts.name: Conformations of alkanes and cyclohexane
concepts.summary: Draw Newman projections and chair cyclohexanes and identify axial and equatorial positions and the more stable conformer.

concepts.name: Chirality and R/S assignment
concepts.summary: Identify stereocentres and assign R/S configuration using Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priorities.

concepts.name: Enantiomers, diastereomers and meso compounds
concepts.summary: Classify pairs of stereoisomers and recognise meso compounds from their symmetry.

concepts.name: Acid-base reactions of organic compounds
concepts.summary: Use pKa values and structural effects to predict acid strength and the direction of proton transfer.

concepts.name: Curved-arrow notation
concepts.summary: Draw curved arrows showing electron-pair movement for simple steps and resonance structures.

concepts.name: Nucleophiles, electrophiles and leaving groups
concepts.summary: Identify nucleophilic and electrophilic sites and judge what makes a good leaving group.

concepts.name: Alkene addition reactions
concepts.summary: Predict products of HX addition, hydration and halogenation of alkenes using Markovnikov's rule.

misconceptions.text: R and S configuration tells you whether a compound rotates light clockwise or counterclockwise.
Any molecule with a stereocentre is chiral.
In a chair cyclohexane, substituents prefer the axial position.

concepts.name: SN2 and SN1 mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse substrate, nucleophile, leaving group and solvent to decide between SN1 and SN2 and predict stereochemical outcome.

concepts.name: E1 and E2 eliminations
concepts.summary: Predict elimination products and regiochemistry and distinguish elimination from substitution competition.

concepts.name: Carbocation stability and rearrangements
concepts.summary: Rank carbocation stability and recognise when shifts give more stable intermediates.

concepts.name: Alcohol and ether reactions
concepts.summary: Predict outcomes of alcohol oxidation, conversion to halides and sulfonates, and ether cleavage and epoxide opening.

concepts.name: Carbonyl nucleophilic addition
concepts.summary: Explain and predict additions of Grignard reagents, hydrides and cyanide to aldehydes and ketones.

concepts.name: Spectroscopic structure determination
concepts.summary: Combine IR, 1H and 13C NMR and mass spectra to deduce the structure of an unknown.

concepts.name: Aromaticity and electrophilic substitution
concepts.summary: Apply Hückel's rule and analyse how substituents direct electrophilic aromatic substitution.

misconceptions.text: SN2 reactions proceed with retention of configuration, or racemise the stereocentre.
Substitution and elimination are separate reactions that never compete.
All substituents on a benzene ring direct incoming electrophiles to the ortho and para positions.

concepts.name: Enolate chemistry
concepts.summary: Analyse enolate formation and its use in alkylation, aldol and Claisen reactions including kinetic versus thermodynamic control.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acid derivative interconversion
concepts.summary: Use relative reactivity to predict nucleophilic acyl substitution among acid chlorides, anhydrides, esters and amides.

concepts.name: Retrosynthetic analysis
concepts.summary: Work backward from a target by disconnections and evaluate alternative routes.

concepts.name: Chemoselectivity and protecting groups
concepts.summary: Judge when protecting groups are needed and choose ones compatible with the reaction conditions.

concepts.name: Pericyclic reactions
concepts.summary: Predict Diels-Alder outcomes including regiochemistry and endo stereochemistry using orbital symmetry ideas.

concepts.name: Conjugate addition and amine chemistry
concepts.summary: Distinguish 1,2- from 1,4-addition and design routes to amines via reductive amination and related methods.

concepts.name: Stereochemical control in reactions
concepts.summary: Evaluate stereospecific and stereoselective reactions and predict the stereochemistry of products.

misconceptions.text: A synthesis route is good if each step works in isolation, regardless of other functional groups present.
Aldol reactions always give a single product regardless of which carbonyl compounds are mixed.
Any carboxylic acid derivative can be converted into any other by simple nucleophile addition.

concepts.name: Transition metal cross-coupling
concepts.summary: Evaluate palladium-catalysed coupling mechanisms and choose coupling strategies for carbon-carbon bond construction.

concepts.name: Asymmetric synthesis strategies
concepts.summary: Design enantioselective routes using chiral pool, auxiliaries or catalysts and justify the choice.

concepts.name: Frontier orbital and physical organic analysis
concepts.summary: Use orbital theory, kinetics, linear free-energy relationships and isotope effects to evaluate proposed mechanisms.

concepts.name: Multistep total synthesis planning
concepts.summary: Devise efficient convergent syntheses for complex molecules balancing step count, selectivity and protecting-group economy.

concepts.name: Radical and photochemical reactions
concepts.summary: Evaluate radical chain processes and photochemical pathways and their selectivity relative to polar chemistry.

concepts.name: Conformational and stereoelectronic control
concepts.summary: Assess how conformation and orbital alignment dictate diastereoselectivity and reactivity in acyclic and cyclic systems.

misconceptions.text: A reaction that gives the expected product proves the proposed mechanism is correct.
Cross-coupling works equally well with any halide, organometallic partner and ligand.
Enantioselective catalysis simply makes only the favoured product by blocking the other enantiomer entirely.

concepts.name: Hangul consonant letters
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce the basic consonant letters and know how their shapes relate to place of articulation.

concepts.name: Hangul vowel letters
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce basic vowels, including vertical and horizontal vowel shapes and the contrast of ㅓ/ㅗ and ㅡ/ㅜ.

concepts.name: Syllable block construction
concepts.summary: Explain how consonants and vowels combine into square syllable blocks and read blocks left-to-right and top-to-bottom.

concepts.name: Batchim final consonants
concepts.summary: Understand that a consonant at the bottom of a block is pronounced as one of seven representative sounds.

concepts.name: Aspirated and tense consonants
concepts.summary: Distinguish plain, aspirated and tense consonant triplets such as ㄱ/ㅋ/ㄲ in sound and spelling.

concepts.name: Basic greetings and polite phrases
concepts.summary: Remember common expressions like 안녕하세요, 감사합니다 and 네/아니요 and when they are used.

concepts.name: SOV word order
concepts.summary: Understand that Korean sentences place the verb at the end, with other elements before it.

misconceptions.text: Hangul letters are written in a line like the Latin alphabet rather than grouped into blocks.
Every batchim consonant is pronounced exactly as its letter name suggests.
ㅇ at the start of a block is pronounced like the 'ng' sound.

concepts.name: Topic and subject particles
concepts.summary: Choose 은/는 and 이/가 by final-sound form and apply them to mark topic versus subject.

concepts.name: Object and location particles
concepts.summary: Use 을/를 for objects and 에 and 에서 for destinations, existence locations and action locations.

concepts.name: Present-tense 해요 style
concepts.summary: Conjugate verbs and adjectives into the polite 해요 form including 하다 verbs and vowel harmony.

concepts.name: Formal 합니다 style
concepts.summary: Form the formal polite ending by checking whether the stem ends in a vowel or consonant.

concepts.name: Native Korean numbers
concepts.summary: Count and state age and hours with native numbers and their counter-form changes.

concepts.name: Sino-Korean numbers
concepts.summary: Use Sino-Korean numbers for dates, money, minutes and phone numbers, and pick the right set by context.

concepts.name: Copula 이다 and 있다/없다
concepts.summary: Express identity with 이에요/예요 and existence or possession with 있어요/없어요.

concepts.name: Liaison and nasalisation sound changes
concepts.summary: Apply linking of batchim to a following vowel and nasalisation to predict actual pronunciation.

misconceptions.text: 은/는 and 이/가 are interchangeable and both simply mean 'is'.
Native and Sino-Korean numbers can be used freely in any context.
Korean needs an explicit subject in every sentence.

concepts.name: Irregular verb conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate ㅂ, ㄷ, ㅅ, ㅡ, 르 and ㅎ irregular stems correctly before vowel endings.

concepts.name: Past and future tense endings
concepts.summary: Form past with -았/었- and future or conjecture with -(으)ㄹ 거예요 and use them appropriately.

concepts.name: Subject honorific -(으)시-
concepts.summary: Add -(으)시- to the verb and swap honorific vocabulary such as 드시다 and 계시다 for respected subjects.

concepts.name: Connective endings
concepts.summary: Distinguish sequence, cause and contrast connectives and choose the ending that fits the logical relation.

concepts.name: Counters and quantity expressions
concepts.summary: Combine numbers with counters like 명, 개, 권 and 시 using the correct number set.

concepts.name: Negation patterns
concepts.summary: Differentiate 안 (will not) from 못 (cannot) and short from long negation.

concepts.name: Tensification and aspiration rules
concepts.summary: Analyse when stops are tensed or ㅎ merges with neighbours to produce aspiration and predict pronunciation.

concepts.name: Modifier forms of verbs
concepts.summary: Build noun-modifying clauses with tense-sensitive endings and distinguish verb from adjective forms.

misconceptions.text: Irregular verbs follow no pattern and must be memorised one by one.
-아서/어서 and -(으)니까 are fully interchangeable for giving reasons.
안 and 못 both simply mean 'not' with no difference in meaning.

concepts.name: Speech level selection
concepts.summary: Judge which of the speech levels, from 합쇼체 to 반말, suits relationship, setting and intent.

concepts.name: Object honorifics and humble forms
concepts.summary: Analyse humble verbs such as 드리다 and 뵙다 and decide when lowering oneself is appropriate versus raising the subject.

concepts.name: Nuance of sentence-final endings
concepts.summary: Differentiate endings expressing confirmation, surprise, discovery and softening and select by speaker stance.

concepts.name: Reported speech
concepts.summary: Convert direct statements, questions, commands and suggestions into indirect quotations with correct endings.

concepts.name: Passive and causative constructions
concepts.summary: Analyse how suffixes and periphrastic forms create passive and causative meanings and when each is natural.

concepts.name: Auxiliary verb constructions
concepts.summary: Interpret aspect and attempt meanings from auxiliary verbs attached to main verbs.

concepts.name: Sino-Korean and native vocabulary
concepts.summary: Use Sino-Korean word roots to infer meaning and judge when native or Sino-Korean synonyms fit better.

concepts.name: Evaluating natural phrasing
concepts.summary: Critique learner sentences for unnatural particle, subject and politeness choices and justify corrections.

misconceptions.text: Dropping to 반말 is fine with anyone once you have met a few times.
Honorific -시- can be used for oneself to be polite.
Passive suffixes work like English passives and can be applied to any transitive verb.

concepts.name: Pragmatic register shifting
concepts.summary: Evaluate and manage shifts between registers to signal distance, intimacy, authority or irony.

concepts.name: Discourse topic and information structure
concepts.summary: Evaluate how 은/는, 이/가, ellipsis and word scrambling organise given and new information.

concepts.name: Written and spoken style variation
concepts.summary: Judge differences among news, academic, literary and conversational Korean, including the 한다체.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and sino-compound expression
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply idioms, proverbs and four-character compounds with appropriate nuance.

concepts.name: Dialect and sociolinguistic variation
concepts.summary: Assess how dialects, generational slang and North-South differences affect comprehension and usage.

concepts.name: Composing culturally apt texts
concepts.summary: Create emails, essays and speeches in Korean with register, vocabulary and rhetoric suited to audience.

concepts.name: Translation between Korean and English
concepts.summary: Produce translations that handle dropped subjects, honorific information and word-order differences faithfully.

misconceptions.text: Standard Seoul Korean is the only form that matters, and dialects are just mistakes.
Translating means preserving every particle and honorific literally.
The 한다체 plain style is rude and never appropriate in writing.

concepts.name: Pinyin initials and finals
concepts.summary: Read and pronounce pinyin syllables by combining initials and finals, including distinctive sounds such as zh/ch/sh, q, x, ü.

concepts.name: Four tones and neutral tone
concepts.summary: Distinguish and produce the high-level, rising, dipping and falling tones plus the unstressed neutral tone, and recognise that tone changes word meaning.

concepts.name: Stroke order rules
concepts.summary: Write simple characters using the standard rules such as top to bottom, left to right, and horizontal before vertical.

concepts.name: Radicals as character components
concepts.summary: Recognise common radicals like 氵, 亻, 口 and 木 and know they often hint at meaning.

concepts.name: Basic SVO word order
concepts.summary: Build simple statements with subject-verb-object order and no verb conjugation, e.g. 我喝茶.

concepts.name: Core greetings and numbers
concepts.summary: Recall greetings, pronouns, numbers 1–99 and the first set of HSK 1 words in simplified characters.

concepts.name: Yes-no questions with ma and ne
concepts.summary: Form basic questions by adding 吗 to statements or 呢 for follow-up questions.

misconceptions.text: Tones are optional extras that native speakers will ignore if the word is clear from context.
Pinyin letters are pronounced like the same English letters, so q is like English q and x like English x.
The order in which you draw strokes does not matter as long as the finished character looks right.

concepts.name: Tone sandhi for third tone
concepts.summary: Apply the rule that a third tone before another third tone is pronounced as second tone, as well as 不 and 一 tone changes.

concepts.name: Measure words with numbers
concepts.summary: Use common measure words like 个, 本, 杯 and 张 between a number or demonstrative and a noun.

concepts.name: Completed action le
concepts.summary: Use 了 after a verb to mark completed actions and distinguish it from sentence-final 了 marking change of state.

concepts.name: Experiential guo
concepts.summary: Use 过 after a verb to say one has had an experience, and negate it with 没.

concepts.name: Time words and word position
concepts.summary: Place time and location phrases before the verb and order them correctly in a sentence.

concepts.name: Negation with bu and mei
concepts.summary: Choose 不 for habitual, future or stative negation and 没(有) for past events and possession.

concepts.name: Radical-based character lookup
concepts.summary: Use radicals and phonetic components to guess meaning or sound and find characters in a dictionary, across HSK 1–2 vocabulary.

concepts.name: Question words in place
concepts.summary: Form questions with 什么, 谁, 哪, 几 and 怎么 in the position of the answer, without fronting.

misconceptions.text: The particle 了 is the past tense marker and goes on every past-time sentence.
Measure words can be dropped, so 三书 is as correct as 三本书.
不 and 没 are interchangeable ways of saying 'not'.

concepts.name: Ba construction structure
concepts.summary: Build 把 sentences with subject + 把 + definite object + verb + complement, showing what is done to the object.

concepts.name: Bei passive construction
concepts.summary: Form passives with 被 (and 叫/让) plus an agent and a verb with a complement, often with adverse or notable results.

concepts.name: Durative zhe
concepts.summary: Use 着 to express ongoing states or manner, and contrast it with 在 for progressive actions.

concepts.name: Resultative and directional complements
concepts.summary: Attach complements such as 完, 到, 好, 上来 to verbs to express result or direction.

concepts.name: Aspect particle contrast
concepts.summary: Analyse a context to choose between 了, 过, 着 and 在, explaining the difference in meaning.

concepts.name: Degree and potential complements
concepts.summary: Use 得 to describe manner or degree and 得/不 potential forms like 听得懂 and 看不见.

concepts.name: HSK 3–4 vocabulary by word formation
concepts.summary: Learn HSK 3–4 vocabulary by analysing how compounds are built from known characters and morphemes.

misconceptions.text: The 把 construction can be used with any verb and any object.
The 被 passive is used wherever English uses a passive, so it is neutral and very common.
着 is just the Chinese equivalent of the English -ing ending.

concepts.name: Sentence-final le versus verb le
concepts.summary: Analyse sentences with both verbal and sentence-final 了 and explain how they differ in meaning and implication.

concepts.name: Ba and bei semantic constraints
concepts.summary: Judge when 把 or 被 is required, optional or unacceptable based on definiteness, affectedness and complement type.

concepts.name: Topic-comment structure
concepts.summary: Analyse how topics are fronted and how subjects can be omitted when recoverable from context.

concepts.name: Conjunctions and connective pairs
concepts.summary: Use paired connectors such as 虽然…但是, 不但…而且 and 即使…也 to structure complex arguments.

concepts.name: Register and spoken versus written
concepts.summary: Evaluate word choice between colloquial and formal equivalents such as 吃 and 食用 or 因此 and 所以.

concepts.name: HSK 5–6 vocabulary and chengyu
concepts.summary: Interpret and use common four-character idioms and HSK 5–6 vocabulary in context.

concepts.name: Reading unseen characters
concepts.summary: Infer meaning and approximate sound of unfamiliar characters from phonetic and semantic components, knowing the limits of such inference.

misconceptions.text: Sentence-final 了 and verb 了 are the same particle with the same meaning in any position.
Every sentence must have an explicit subject, and dropping it is sloppy.
A character's phonetic component always gives its exact pronunciation and tone.

concepts.name: Evaluating aspect usage in discourse
aliases: discourse use of le guo zhe
concepts.summary: Evaluate native and learner texts for how aspect particles organise narrative sequence, background and foregrounding.

concepts.name: Prosody and intonation across tones
concepts.summary: Judge how tones interact with stress, rhythm and sentence intonation in connected speech and correct nonnative patterns.

concepts.name: Stylistic composition across registers
concepts.summary: Compose texts such as emails, essays and speeches in suitable registers using appropriate syntax and idiom.

concepts.name: Regional variation and Mandarin norms
concepts.summary: Evaluate differences between putonghua, regional accents and Taiwan Mandarin in vocabulary, pronunciation and script.

concepts.name: Classical Chinese in modern usage
concepts.summary: Assess how classical grammar and vocabulary persist in idioms, formal writing and set phrases.

concepts.name: Designing teaching and study materials
concepts.summary: Create graded materials and explanations that sequence grammar, characters and vocabulary for specific learner groups.

concepts.name: Translation and nuance equivalence
concepts.summary: Produce translations that preserve nuance, deciding on how to render aspect, measure words and omitted subjects.

misconceptions.text: Mandarin has no grammar to speak of, so fluency is mostly a matter of memorising vocabulary.
Taiwan and mainland Mandarin differ only in script, not in vocabulary or pronunciation.
Faithful translation means matching each Chinese particle with an English tense or word.

concepts.name: Series as labeled array
concepts.summary: Recall that a Series is a one-dimensional array of values paired with an index of labels and a single dtype.

concepts.name: DataFrame as table
concepts.summary: Explain that a DataFrame is a two-dimensional table of rows and columns where each column is a Series sharing a common index.

concepts.name: Reading files into DataFrames
concepts.summary: Load a CSV or similar file into a DataFrame and understand what the resulting object represents.

concepts.name: Inspecting a DataFrame
concepts.summary: Use head, shape, info, dtypes and describe to understand a dataset's size, columns, types and basic statistics.

concepts.name: Column selection
concepts.summary: Understand that selecting one column gives a Series while selecting a list of columns gives a DataFrame.

concepts.name: Index and column labels
concepts.summary: Recall that rows are identified by index labels and columns by names, and that both are accessible as attributes.

concepts.name: Column dtypes
concepts.summary: Understand that each column has a dtype such as int64, float64, object or datetime64 that determines which operations work.

misconceptions.text: A DataFrame is just a Python list of lists with no extra structure.
Selecting a single column with brackets returns a DataFrame.
Reading a CSV file keeps the file open and edits to the DataFrame change the file on disk.

concepts.name: Label versus position indexing
concepts.summary: Select rows and columns with loc by label and iloc by integer position, and know when each is appropriate.

concepts.name: Boolean mask filtering
concepts.summary: Filter rows with boolean conditions combined using &, | and ~ with parentheses, and with isin.

concepts.name: Creating and modifying columns
concepts.summary: Add or transform columns using vectorized arithmetic, assignment and rename or drop.

concepts.name: Missing value handling
concepts.summary: Detect missing values with isna and treat them with dropna or fillna depending on context.

concepts.name: Sorting and ranking
concepts.summary: Order rows by one or more columns and index labels, ascending or descending.

concepts.name: Summary statistics and counts
concepts.summary: Compute column aggregates and frequency counts, such as mean, sum, nunique and value_counts, to summarize data.

concepts.name: Writing data out
concepts.summary: Save a DataFrame to a file with control over the index and chosen columns.

concepts.name: Type conversion and string methods
concepts.summary: Convert column dtypes with astype and clean text columns using the str accessor.

misconceptions.text: Use and and or to combine multiple filter conditions on a DataFrame.
iloc slices include the end position just like loc label slices.
Methods like sort_values or dropna change the original DataFrame in place by default.

concepts.name: Split-apply-combine with groupby
concepts.summary: Group rows by one or more keys and apply aggregations to produce per-group summaries.

concepts.name: Multiple and named aggregations
concepts.summary: Apply several functions to different columns in one groupby with agg and name the outputs.

concepts.name: Merging and joining tables
concepts.summary: Combine DataFrames on keys with inner, left, right and outer joins and analyze how each affects the row count.

concepts.name: Concatenation of frames
concepts.summary: Stack DataFrames vertically or side by side and handle index alignment and mismatched columns.

concepts.name: Pivoting and reshaping
concepts.summary: Convert between wide and long layouts with pivot_table, melt, stack and unstack to suit an analysis.

concepts.name: Datetime handling
concepts.summary: Parse dates, extract components with the dt accessor, and compute time differences.

concepts.name: Index alignment in operations
concepts.summary: Predict how arithmetic between Series or DataFrames aligns on index labels and produces NaN for mismatches.

concepts.name: Data cleaning workflow
concepts.summary: Detect and resolve duplicates, inconsistent categories and outliers, and validate results systematically.

misconceptions.text: A merge always returns the same number of rows as the left table.
Groupby computes results immediately when called, before any aggregation is specified.
Arithmetic between two Series matches values by position, not by index label.

concepts.name: Transform and filter on groups
concepts.summary: Use transform, filter and apply on groups to add group-level features without collapsing rows, and choose among them.

concepts.name: Copy versus view semantics
concepts.summary: Diagnose when assignments modify the original or a copy, and avoid chained assignment by using loc or explicit copies.

concepts.name: Vectorization versus apply
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to use vectorized operations instead of apply or loops based on clarity and speed.

concepts.name: Memory-efficient dtypes
concepts.summary: Judge and apply categorical, nullable and downcast numeric dtypes to reduce memory use with correct semantics.

concepts.name: MultiIndex data manipulation
concepts.summary: Select, slice, reshape and reset hierarchical indexes produced by grouping and pivoting.

concepts.name: Time series resampling and windows
concepts.summary: Resample time series to other frequencies and compute rolling, expanding and shifted calculations.

concepts.name: Method chaining pipelines
concepts.summary: Structure readable, reproducible transformations as method chains using assign, query and pipe.

concepts.name: Merge validation and diagnostics
concepts.summary: Check key uniqueness and unmatched rows during merges to detect silent row duplication or loss.

misconceptions.text: Using apply with a row-wise function is just as fast as a vectorized operation.
Chained indexing such as df[mask]['col'] = value reliably updates the original DataFrame.
Converting every string column to category is always beneficial regardless of cardinality.

concepts.name: Scaling beyond memory
concepts.summary: Evaluate chunked reading, column selection, columnar formats and alternative engines when data exceeds memory.

concepts.name: Performance profiling and optimization
concepts.summary: Profile pipelines to find bottlenecks and choose between vectorization, indexing, dtype changes and algorithmic restructuring.

concepts.name: Designing reusable data pipelines
concepts.summary: Design modular, tested and idempotent transformation functions with explicit schemas for production use.

concepts.name: Data validation and schema contracts
concepts.summary: Create automated checks for types, ranges, uniqueness and referential integrity that fail loudly on bad data.

concepts.name: Custom extensions and accessors
concepts.summary: Extend pandas with custom accessors or extension types where built-in behavior does not fit a domain.

concepts.name: Choosing pandas versus alternatives
concepts.summary: Judge when pandas, SQL, NumPy or other dataframe engines best suit a task based on scale, semantics and team context.

concepts.name: Reproducible statistical analysis workflows
concepts.summary: Build analyses that are deterministic and auditable, handling missing data, bias and sampling choices explicitly.

misconceptions.text: If a dataset fits in memory, pandas performance is never a concern.
Pandas is always the best tool for any tabular task, so alternatives are unnecessary.
Passing a few visual spot checks is enough to validate a data pipeline's output.

concepts.name: Sources of business law
concepts.summary: Recall that business obligations come from statutes, regulations, court decisions and contracts, and that rules vary by jurisdiction.

concepts.name: Types of business structure
concepts.summary: Name the main structures (sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation) and describe how they differ in broad terms.

concepts.name: Legal personality
concepts.summary: Explain that some entities are legally separate from their owners and can own property, sign contracts and be sued in their own name.

concepts.name: Contract elements
concepts.summary: Explain that a contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration, intent to be bound and capacity, and recognise each in a simple example.

concepts.name: Business liability
concepts.summary: Understand that a business can be held responsible for harm, debts or breaches, and that owners may or may not be personally exposed.

concepts.name: Types of intellectual property
concepts.summary: Recall the main IP forms (trademarks, copyright, patents, trade secrets) and the kind of thing each protects.

concepts.name: Employee versus contractor
concepts.summary: Understand that people working for a business are classed as employees or independent contractors, with different legal rights and obligations.

concepts.name: Licences, permits and registration
concepts.summary: Recall that businesses often must register, hold licences and file returns to operate lawfully.

misconceptions.text: A verbal agreement is never a legally binding contract.
Registering a company name automatically gives full trademark protection.
Any business structure fully protects the owner's personal assets.

concepts.name: Offer, acceptance and written terms
concepts.summary: Apply formation rules to emails, quotes and signed documents to decide whether and when a binding agreement exists.

concepts.name: Common contract clauses
concepts.summary: Read and apply clauses on payment, termination, warranties, confidentiality and governing law to a given agreement.

concepts.name: Breach and remedies
concepts.summary: Identify a breach and match it to likely remedies such as damages, termination or specific performance.

concepts.name: Limited liability protection
concepts.summary: Explain how limited liability structures shield owners from business debts and why personal guarantees limit that shield.

concepts.name: Choosing a structure
concepts.summary: Apply criteria such as liability, tax treatment, cost and funding needs to pick a suitable structure for a small business scenario.

concepts.name: Trademark and copyright ownership
concepts.summary: Determine who owns a logo, brand name or creative work, including work made by employees or freelancers.

concepts.name: Employment basics
concepts.summary: Apply core employer duties such as written terms, minimum pay, working time, non-discrimination and workplace safety to simple cases.

concepts.name: Data privacy obligations
concepts.summary: Understand that collecting customer or staff data brings duties on notice, consent, security and retention.

misconceptions.text: If a contract is signed, every clause in it is automatically enforceable.
Whoever pays for a logo or website design automatically owns the copyright.
Forming an LLC or corporation means the owner can never be personally liable.

concepts.name: Contract risk allocation
concepts.summary: Analyse how indemnities, limitation of liability and warranty clauses shift risk between parties and spot one-sided terms.

concepts.name: Contract defects and defences
concepts.summary: Analyse whether misrepresentation, mistake, duress or illegality undermines an agreement.

concepts.name: Piercing the corporate veil
concepts.summary: Analyse facts such as commingled funds, undercapitalisation and fraud that lead courts to hold owners personally liable.

concepts.name: Directors' and partners' duties
concepts.summary: Apply duties of care, loyalty and good faith to decisions by directors, officers or partners.

concepts.name: Vicarious and product liability
concepts.summary: Analyse when a business is liable for employee conduct, negligence or defective products.

concepts.name: IP protection and infringement
concepts.summary: Analyse whether a use infringes IP and which registration, licensing or confidentiality steps best protect an asset.

concepts.name: Worker classification and termination
concepts.summary: Analyse classification tests and dismissal, redundancy and restrictive covenant risks in employment relationships.

concepts.name: Compliance programme design
concepts.summary: Apply a risk-based approach to map applicable regulations (tax, consumer, data, sector rules) to policies, records and deadlines.

misconceptions.text: A limitation of liability clause always protects a party regardless of how it behaved.
Calling someone a contractor in the agreement settles their legal status.
Separate legal personality means a court will never look behind the company to its owners.

concepts.name: Negotiation strategy for contracts
concepts.summary: Evaluate which terms matter most in a deal given leverage, risk and commercial goals, and decide where to concede or insist.

concepts.name: Dispute resolution options
concepts.summary: Evaluate negotiation, mediation, arbitration and litigation by cost, speed, confidentiality and enforceability.

concepts.name: Structuring for growth and exit
concepts.summary: Evaluate how structure, shareholder agreements, vesting and investor terms affect control, liability and exit.

concepts.name: IP strategy and licensing
concepts.summary: Evaluate licensing, assignment and registration choices across jurisdictions to balance protection, revenue and cost.

concepts.name: Cross-border legal issues
concepts.summary: Analyse how choice of law, jurisdiction, export rules and local employment or tax rules affect cross-border operations.

concepts.name: Legal risk assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate the likelihood and impact of legal risks and judge which to avoid, insure, mitigate or accept.

concepts.name: Instructing and managing lawyers
aliases: knowing when to seek legal advice
concepts.summary: Judge when a matter needs a lawyer, what kind, and how to brief and control scope and cost.

misconceptions.text: Arbitration is always cheaper and faster than court.
Using a template contract removes the need to check it against the specific deal and jurisdiction.
Legal advice is only needed once a dispute has already started.

concepts.name: Bespoke contract architecture
concepts.summary: Design contract frameworks that align incentives, allocate uncertainty and stay workable over a long relationship.

concepts.name: Enterprise legal risk framework
concepts.summary: Create a governance framework linking board oversight, policies, controls and escalation to the organisation's legal risks.

concepts.name: Evaluating regulatory change
concepts.summary: Evaluate how new or conflicting regulation affects the business model and decide when to adapt, lobby or restructure.

concepts.name: Transaction and restructuring design
concepts.summary: Design acquisitions, financings or reorganisations that manage liability, diligence findings, tax and stakeholder interests.

concepts.name: Crisis and insolvency decisions
concepts.summary: Evaluate legal duties and options during financial distress, investigations or major incidents, including directors' exposure.

concepts.name: Global IP and data strategy
concepts.summary: Create integrated strategies for IP ownership, data transfers and enforcement that hold across several legal systems.

concepts.name: Legal ethics and culture
concepts.summary: Evaluate how incentives, whistleblowing channels and tone from leadership shape real compliance beyond the letter of the law.

misconceptions.text: Full compliance with the written rules is enough to eliminate legal and reputational risk.
A more detailed contract always reduces risk more than a simpler one.
Directors are protected from personal exposure once a company is in distress, because the entity bears the losses.

concepts.name: Product manager role
concepts.summary: Can describe what a product manager or product owner is responsible for and how the role differs from engineering, design and project management.

concepts.name: Product lifecycle stages
concepts.summary: Can explain the stages of introduction, growth, maturity and decline and how product priorities shift across them.

concepts.name: Product vision statement
concepts.summary: Can explain that a vision describes the long-term change a product aims to create for its users and why it guides decisions.

concepts.name: Product backlog
concepts.summary: Can define the backlog as an ordered list of work items and state who owns and maintains it.

concepts.name: User story format
aliases: As a, I want, so that
concepts.summary: Can explain a user story as a short statement of who needs what and why, written from the user's perspective.

concepts.name: Product roadmap purpose
concepts.summary: Can explain a roadmap as a communication of direction and planned outcomes over time, and who it is for.

concepts.name: Outputs versus outcomes
concepts.summary: Can distinguish features shipped (outputs) from changes in user behaviour or business results (outcomes).

misconceptions.text: The product manager is the boss of the engineering and design team who tells them what to build.
A roadmap is a fixed schedule of features with committed delivery dates.
Shipping more features means the product is succeeding.

concepts.name: Writing acceptance criteria
concepts.summary: Can write testable acceptance criteria for a user story so that the team knows when it is complete.

concepts.name: MoSCoW prioritisation
concepts.summary: Can sort backlog items into Must, Should, Could and Won't have for a defined release scope.

concepts.name: RICE scoring
concepts.summary: Can calculate RICE scores as reach times impact times confidence divided by effort and rank items by them.

concepts.name: Kano model categories
concepts.summary: Can classify features as basic expectations, performance features or delighters and explain how satisfaction responds to each.

concepts.name: Product requirements document
concepts.summary: Can draft a PRD covering problem, goals, target users, scope, requirements and open questions.

concepts.name: Now-Next-Later roadmap
concepts.summary: Can build a roadmap organised by time horizons and themes rather than dated feature lists.

concepts.name: Basic product metrics
concepts.summary: Can define common metrics such as active users, conversion, retention and churn and say what each tells you.

concepts.name: Story splitting
concepts.summary: Can split large stories into small, independent, valuable slices that fit within a sprint.

misconceptions.text: Everything in a MoSCoW list can be labelled Must have, because stakeholders consider it all important.
A RICE score is an objective answer, so the highest score must be built first.
A PRD must be a long, complete document that is finished before development starts.

concepts.name: Product strategy formulation
concepts.summary: Can analyse market, users and company goals to choose a coherent set of bets that connect vision to roadmap.

concepts.name: Outcome-based OKRs
concepts.summary: Can write objectives with measurable key results that express outcomes rather than tasks, and cascade them from company goals.

concepts.name: North Star and input metrics
concepts.summary: Can break a north star metric into driver metrics and analyse which levers the team can influence.

concepts.name: Product-market fit assessment
concepts.summary: Can analyse retention curves, survey signals and growth patterns to judge whether a product has achieved fit.

concepts.name: Discovery and validation experiments
concepts.summary: Can identify risky assumptions and choose prototypes, interviews or tests to validate value, usability and feasibility cheaply.

concepts.name: Stakeholder alignment and trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can analyse competing stakeholder demands and negotiate scope trade-offs using evidence and strategy.

concepts.name: Go-to-market plan
concepts.summary: Can build a launch plan covering target segment, positioning, pricing, channels and success measures.

concepts.name: A/B test interpretation
concepts.summary: Can analyse experiment results including sample size, significance and guardrail metrics before deciding to ship.

misconceptions.text: Key results are a list of deliverables to be completed by the end of the quarter.
Product-market fit is a single moment that, once reached, never needs to be revisited.
An A/B test that shows a lift in the primary metric should always be shipped.

concepts.name: Portfolio and investment allocation
concepts.summary: Can evaluate how to split capacity across core improvements, growth bets and technical health against strategic goals.

concepts.name: Evaluating prioritisation frameworks
concepts.summary: Can judge when RICE, MoSCoW, Kano or cost of delay fits a decision and where each distorts it.

concepts.name: Pricing and packaging decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate pricing models and tiers against value delivered, willingness to pay and segment behaviour.

concepts.name: Launch readiness and rollout strategy
