concepts.summary: Can assess launch risk and choose between beta, staged rollout or full launch with go and no-go criteria.

concepts.name: Unit economics and growth loops
concepts.summary: Can analyse customer lifetime value, acquisition cost, payback and loops to find sustainable growth levers.

concepts.name: Segmentation and positioning choices
concepts.summary: Can evaluate which customer segments to prioritise and defend a positioning against competitors.

concepts.name: Roadmap communication and governance
concepts.summary: Can judge how to tailor roadmap commitments and uncertainty for executives, sales and engineering and revise them as evidence changes.

misconceptions.text: Pricing can be set after launch by adding a margin to cost.
A prioritisation framework removes the need for judgement.
A launch is complete when the feature ships, with no further ownership needed.

concepts.name: Designing the product operating model
concepts.summary: Can design team structures, decision rights and planning cadences that let product teams deliver outcomes at scale.

concepts.name: Creating multi-year product strategy
concepts.summary: Can create a differentiated multi-year strategy with explicit bets, moats and kill criteria.

concepts.name: New product and market entry
concepts.summary: Can design a staged approach to establish a new product or enter a market, including investment gates.

concepts.name: Platform and ecosystem strategy
concepts.summary: Can evaluate when to build a platform, the role of partners and network effects, and the trade-offs for internal and external users.

concepts.name: Metric system and incentive design
concepts.summary: Can design a coherent system of metrics, OKRs and incentives that avoids gaming and misaligned optimisation.

concepts.name: Portfolio sunsetting and pivot decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate evidence to pivot, persevere, merge or retire products, handling sunk cost and customer migration.

concepts.name: Coaching product leaders
concepts.summary: Can build product management capability by creating coaching practices, hiring standards and decision-quality reviews.

misconceptions.text: A pivot means the product has failed and the team should have avoided it.
Good strategy is a detailed plan that predicts the market for several years.
Tying incentives directly to a single metric reliably produces the desired behaviour.

concepts.name: Wave-particle duality
concepts.summary: Explain that light and matter show both wave-like and particle-like behaviour depending on the experiment, such as the double-slit experiment.

concepts.name: Energy quantization
concepts.summary: Understand that bound systems have only certain allowed energies and that energy exchange occurs in discrete amounts like E = hf.

concepts.name: Wavefunction and probability
concepts.summary: Understand that the wavefunction encodes probability amplitudes and that |ψ|² gives probability density for finding a particle.

concepts.name: Superposition of states
concepts.summary: Describe a system as a combination of several possible states until measured.

concepts.name: Measurement and collapse
concepts.summary: Explain that measurement yields one definite outcome with probabilities given by the state, and changes the state afterwards.

concepts.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
concepts.summary: State that position and momentum cannot both be sharply defined, with Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2, as a property of quantum states.

concepts.name: Planck constant and scales
concepts.summary: Recall the role of Planck's constant in setting the scale at which quantum effects matter.

misconceptions.text: An electron is a tiny ball orbiting the nucleus like a planet.
Uncertainty arises only because measuring instruments disturb the system clumsily.
A superposed particle is really in one definite state that we just do not know.

concepts.name: Time-independent Schrödinger equation
concepts.summary: Write and use Hψ = Eψ for a given potential to find stationary states and energies.

concepts.name: Normalization of wavefunctions
concepts.summary: Compute the constant that makes the integral of |ψ|² equal one and use it to get probabilities.

concepts.name: Particle in an infinite well
concepts.summary: Solve for the sinusoidal states and energies Eₙ ∝ n²/L² and compute probabilities in regions of the box.

concepts.name: Boundary conditions and quantization
concepts.summary: Apply continuity and vanishing conditions on ψ to show how allowed energies arise.

concepts.name: Expectation values
concepts.summary: Calculate ⟨x⟩ and ⟨p⟩ by integrating ψ* with the relevant operator.

concepts.name: Position and momentum operators
concepts.summary: Represent position as multiplication and momentum as −iħ d/dx and use them to build observables.

concepts.name: Free particle and plane waves
concepts.summary: Describe free-particle solutions e^{i(kx−ωt)} with p = ħk and E = ħ²k²/2m.

misconceptions.text: The wavefunction ψ itself is the probability of finding the particle at x.
The particle in a box has a zero-energy lowest state.
The particle in a box spends equal time everywhere in every state.

concepts.name: Hermitian operators and eigenvalues
concepts.summary: Show that observables are Hermitian operators whose eigenvalues are real measurement outcomes and eigenfunctions are orthogonal.

concepts.name: Expansion in eigenstates
concepts.summary: Expand a state in an orthonormal eigenbasis and read off outcome probabilities as |cₙ|².

concepts.name: Time-dependent Schrödinger equation
concepts.summary: Evolve a superposition of stationary states using phase factors e^{-iEₙt/ħ} and identify which quantities change in time.

concepts.name: Dirac bra-ket notation
concepts.summary: Express states, inner products, projectors and operators in bra-ket form and translate to wavefunctions.

concepts.name: Quantum harmonic oscillator
concepts.summary: Derive the evenly spaced levels (n+½)ħω and analyse states using ladder operators and Hermite-Gaussian forms.

concepts.name: Finite wells and barrier tunneling
concepts.summary: Analyse the classically forbidden decay of ψ and how transmission depends on barrier width and height.

concepts.name: Commutators and compatibility
concepts.summary: Use commutators to decide whether observables can be sharply defined together and to derive uncertainty relations.

concepts.name: Spin-1/2 and Pauli matrices
concepts.summary: Represent spin-½ states as two-component spinors and compute measurement outcomes with Pauli matrices.

misconceptions.text: A particle with energy below the barrier height cannot appear on the other side because it lacks the energy.
A superposition of energy eigenstates has a definite energy that changes over time.
Spin is the literal rotation of a small spinning ball.

concepts.name: Hydrogen atom solutions
concepts.summary: Analyse separation of variables in a Coulomb potential, the quantum numbers n, l, m and the resulting orbitals and energies.

concepts.name: Angular momentum algebra
concepts.summary: Use commutation relations to derive angular momentum eigenvalues and the allowed l and m values.

concepts.name: Angular momentum addition
concepts.summary: Combine angular momenta to find total j states and decide when a coupled or uncoupled basis is appropriate.

concepts.name: Time-independent perturbation theory
concepts.summary: Compute and assess first- and second-order energy corrections and decide when degeneracy requires special treatment.

concepts.name: Variational method
concepts.summary: Choose trial wavefunctions to bound ground-state energy and evaluate the quality of the approximation.

concepts.name: Identical particles and exclusion
concepts.summary: Analyse symmetric and antisymmetric many-particle states and their consequences for atomic structure.

concepts.name: Density matrices and mixed states
concepts.summary: Distinguish pure superpositions from classical mixtures using the density operator and compute expectation values.

concepts.name: WKB approximation
concepts.summary: Apply semiclassical methods to estimate energy levels and tunneling rates and judge where they fail.

misconceptions.text: Orbitals are literal paths electrons follow around the nucleus.
A statistical mixture of states is the same thing as a quantum superposition.
Perturbation theory works whenever the perturbation is small in absolute terms, even with degenerate levels.

concepts.name: Measurement problem interpretations
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing interpretations by what they predict, assume and leave unexplained.

concepts.name: Entanglement and Bell inequalities
concepts.summary: Assess how violations of Bell inequalities rule out local hidden-variable models without allowing signalling.

concepts.name: Decoherence and classical limit
concepts.summary: Evaluate how environmental coupling suppresses interference and what it does and does not explain about collapse.

concepts.name: Time-dependent perturbation and transitions
concepts.summary: Judge the validity of transition-rate calculations and derive selection rules for driven systems.

concepts.name: Path integral formulation
concepts.summary: Construct propagators as sums over paths and relate them to the Schrödinger picture and the classical limit.

concepts.name: Second quantization
concepts.summary: Build many-body models using creation and annihilation operators for bosons and fermions.

concepts.name: Scattering theory
concepts.summary: Choose between Born and partial-wave methods to compute cross sections and judge their regimes of validity.

concepts.name: Quantum information modelling
concepts.summary: Design models of qubit systems including unitary gates, measurement and noise channels, and justify approximations.

misconceptions.text: Decoherence fully solves the measurement problem by itself.
Entanglement lets distant parties send information faster than light.
Observation by a conscious observer is required for collapse in all standard formulations.

issues: adb-1 and cmp-3 are flagged as near-duplicates: the names differ only by 'time-independent' vs 'time-dependent', so they look duplicated even though the content is distinct; cmp-3 should be renamed to make the time-evolution focus explicit.

nov-7 (Planck constant and scales) is C1 recall of a constant, close to a prerequisite fact rather than a concept; the prerequisite nov-7 to nov-2 is fine, but the concept is thin. Replace it with a more specific concept (photoelectric effect / photon energy).

adb-6 (position and momentum operators) is a prerequisite for adb-1 and adb-5; its Bloom level C2 is at the band edge but acceptable. adb-2 normalization is also needed before adb-3 probabilities (missing dependency).

cmp-5 depends on cmp-3 in the map, but the harmonic oscillator does not need time-dependent evolution; it needs the TISE (adb-1) and ladder operators/commutators (cmp-7). Missing prerequisite cmp-7 to cmp-5.
cmp-8 spin-1/2 depends on cmp-7 and cmp-4 but not cmp-1's matrix eigenproblem directly; acceptable. The map has 8 concepts in competent, which is within limits.

prf-5 (variational method) is made to depend on prf-4 (perturbation theory), which is not a genuine dependency; the variational method needs only the TISE/expectation values and the eigenstate expansion. prf-8 (WKB) depends on prf-5, which is not genuine; WKB depends on tunneling and the TISE (cmp-6).
prf-7 density matrices is listed as a prerequisite to prf-6 identical particles, which is not a real dependency.

exp-7 scattering theory depends on exp-4 in the map, which is not a genuine requirement for scattering (Born approximation is time-independent in common treatments; partial waves require angular momentum, prf-2). Missing: prf-2 to exp-7.
exp-8 depends on exp-3 and exp-2, fine; exp-6 should depend on prf-6 (identical particles), which is missing.
prf-3 and exp-4 are fine in stage, but exp-4 is a direct extension of prf-4 so a prerequisite prf-4 to exp-4 is missing.

concepts.name: Wave-particle duality
concepts.summary: Explain that light and matter show both wave-like and particle-like behaviour depending on the experiment, such as the double-slit experiment.

concepts.name: Energy quantization
concepts.summary: Understand that bound systems have only certain allowed energies and that energy exchange occurs in discrete amounts like E = hf.

concepts.name: Wavefunction and probability
concepts.summary: Understand that the wavefunction encodes probability amplitudes and that |ψ|² gives probability density for finding a particle.

concepts.name: Superposition of states
concepts.summary: Describe a system as a combination of several possible states until measured.

concepts.name: Measurement and collapse
concepts.summary: Explain that measurement yields one definite outcome with probabilities given by the state, and changes the state afterwards.

concepts.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
concepts.summary: State that position and momentum cannot both be sharply defined, with Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2, as a property of quantum states.

concepts.name: Photoelectric effect and photon energy
concepts.summary: Recall that light comes in photons of energy E = hf, which explains the photoelectric threshold, and that Planck's constant sets the scale of quantum effects.

misconceptions.text: An electron is a tiny ball orbiting the nucleus like a planet.
Uncertainty arises only because measuring instruments disturb the system clumsily.
A superposed particle is really in one definite state that we just do not know.

concepts.name: Time-independent Schrödinger equation
concepts.summary: Write and use Hψ = Eψ for a given potential to find stationary states and energies.

concepts.name: Normalization of wavefunctions
concepts.summary: Compute the constant that makes the integral of |ψ|² equal one and use it to get probabilities.

concepts.name: Particle in an infinite well
concepts.summary: Solve for the sinusoidal states and energies Eₙ ∝ n²/L² and compute probabilities in regions of the box.

concepts.name: Boundary conditions and quantization
concepts.summary: Apply continuity and vanishing conditions on ψ to show how allowed energies arise.

concepts.name: Expectation values
concepts.summary: Calculate ⟨x⟩ and ⟨p⟩ by integrating ψ* with the relevant operator.

concepts.name: Position and momentum operators
concepts.summary: Represent position as multiplication and momentum as −iħ d/dx and use them to build observables.

concepts.name: Free particle and plane waves
concepts.summary: Describe free-particle solutions e^{i(kx−ωt)} with p = ħk and E = ħ²k²/2m.

misconceptions.text: The wavefunction ψ itself is the probability of finding the particle at x.
The particle in a box has a zero-energy lowest state.
The particle in a box spends equal time everywhere in every state.

concepts.name: Hermitian operators and eigenvalues
concepts.summary: Show that observables are Hermitian operators whose eigenvalues are real measurement outcomes and eigenfunctions are orthogonal.

concepts.name: Expansion in eigenstates
concepts.summary: Expand a state in an orthonormal eigenbasis and read off outcome probabilities as |cₙ|².

concepts.name: Time evolution of superpositions
concepts.summary: Solve iħ∂ψ/∂t = Hψ by evolving a superposition of stationary states with phase factors e^{-iEₙt/ħ} and identify which quantities change in time.

concepts.name: Dirac bra-ket notation
concepts.summary: Express states, inner products, projectors and operators in bra-ket form and translate to wavefunctions.

concepts.name: Quantum harmonic oscillator
concepts.summary: Derive the evenly spaced levels (n+½)ħω and analyse states using ladder operators and Hermite-Gaussian forms.

concepts.name: Finite wells and barrier tunneling
concepts.summary: Analyse the classically forbidden decay of ψ and how transmission depends on barrier width and height.

concepts.name: Commutators and compatibility
concepts.summary: Use commutators to decide whether observables can be sharply defined together and to derive uncertainty relations.

concepts.name: Spin-1/2 and Pauli matrices
concepts.summary: Represent spin-½ states as two-component spinors and compute measurement outcomes with Pauli matrices.

misconceptions.text: A particle with energy below the barrier height cannot appear on the other side because it lacks the energy.
A superposition of energy eigenstates has a definite energy that changes over time.
Spin is the literal rotation of a small spinning ball.

concepts.name: Hydrogen atom solutions
concepts.summary: Analyse separation of variables in a Coulomb potential, the quantum numbers n, l, m and the resulting orbitals and energies.

concepts.name: Angular momentum algebra
concepts.summary: Use commutation relations to derive angular momentum eigenvalues and the allowed l and m values.

concepts.name: Angular momentum addition
concepts.summary: Combine angular momenta to find total j states and decide when a coupled or uncoupled basis is appropriate.

concepts.name: Time-independent perturbation theory
concepts.summary: Compute and assess first- and second-order energy corrections and decide when degeneracy requires special treatment.

concepts.name: Variational method
concepts.summary: Choose trial wavefunctions to bound ground-state energy and evaluate the quality of the approximation.

concepts.name: Identical particles and exclusion
concepts.summary: Analyse symmetric and antisymmetric many-particle states and their consequences for atomic structure.

concepts.name: Density matrices and mixed states
concepts.summary: Distinguish pure superpositions from classical mixtures using the density operator and compute expectation values.

concepts.name: WKB approximation
concepts.summary: Apply semiclassical methods to estimate energy levels and tunneling rates and judge where they fail.

misconceptions.text: Orbitals are literal paths electrons follow around the nucleus.
A statistical mixture of states is the same thing as a quantum superposition.
Perturbation theory works whenever the perturbation is small in absolute terms, even with degenerate levels.

concepts.name: Measurement problem interpretations
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing interpretations by what they predict, assume and leave unexplained.

concepts.name: Entanglement and Bell inequalities
concepts.summary: Assess how violations of Bell inequalities rule out local hidden-variable models without allowing signalling.

concepts.name: Decoherence and classical limit
concepts.summary: Evaluate how environmental coupling suppresses interference and what it does and does not explain about collapse.

concepts.name: Time-dependent perturbation and transitions
concepts.summary: Judge the validity of transition-rate calculations and derive selection rules for driven systems.

concepts.name: Path integral formulation
concepts.summary: Construct propagators as sums over paths and relate them to the Schrödinger picture and the classical limit.

concepts.name: Second quantization
concepts.summary: Build many-body models using creation and annihilation operators for bosons and fermions.

concepts.name: Scattering theory
concepts.summary: Choose between Born and partial-wave methods to compute cross sections and judge their regimes of validity.

concepts.name: Quantum information modelling
concepts.summary: Design models of qubit systems including unitary gates, measurement and noise channels, and justify approximations.

misconceptions.text: Decoherence fully solves the measurement problem by itself.
Entanglement lets distant parties send information faster than light.
Observation by a conscious observer is required for collapse in all standard formulations.

concepts.name: Capturing tasks in a list
concepts.summary: Recall that writing every task in one trusted place frees working memory and prevents forgotten commitments.

concepts.name: Deadlines versus importance
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between a task being urgent (time-pressured) and important (valuable to your goals).

concepts.name: Estimating task duration
concepts.summary: Understand that tasks take time and that giving each a rough duration makes planning realistic.

concepts.name: Calendar as commitment record
concepts.summary: Recall that a calendar holds fixed-time commitments such as appointments and deadlines.

concepts.name: Common distractions
concepts.summary: Identify typical distractions such as notifications and social media and explain how they break focus.

concepts.name: Procrastination as avoidance
concepts.summary: Understand that procrastination is usually avoidance of discomfort rather than laziness.

misconceptions.text: Time management means filling every minute of the day with tasks.
Procrastination is simply laziness or a character flaw.
Keeping tasks in your head is enough if you are paying attention.

concepts.name: Prioritising with Eisenhower matrix
concepts.summary: Sort tasks into do, schedule, delegate and eliminate quadrants and act on each accordingly.

concepts.name: Time blocking
concepts.summary: Assign specific tasks to dedicated calendar blocks of time for the day.

concepts.name: Pomodoro technique
concepts.summary: Work in timed focus intervals separated by short breaks and longer breaks after several rounds.

concepts.name: Breaking tasks into steps
concepts.summary: Split vague large tasks into small concrete next actions that can be started immediately.

concepts.name: Daily planning routine
concepts.summary: Choose a few key priorities each day and plan them against the calendar.

concepts.name: Reducing distractions
concepts.summary: Apply tactics like muting notifications and clearing the workspace to protect focus.

concepts.name: Starting tactics against procrastination
concepts.summary: Use small starting commitments to overcome the resistance of beginning a task.

misconceptions.text: Everything urgent is important, so urgent tasks should always be done first.
A time-blocked schedule must be followed perfectly or it has failed.
Pomodoro breaks are wasted time that should be skipped when you feel productive.

concepts.name: Weekly planning and review
concepts.summary: Review the past week, clear inboxes and plan the next week's priorities against goals and calendar.

concepts.name: Batching similar tasks
concepts.summary: Group similar low-focus tasks like email or errands into set sessions to cut context-switching costs.

concepts.name: Context switching costs
concepts.summary: Analyse how switching between tasks reduces efficiency and arrange work to limit it.

concepts.name: Saying no and negotiating
concepts.summary: Decline, defer or renegotiate requests politely when they conflict with existing priorities.

concepts.name: Energy-aware scheduling
concepts.summary: Match demanding tasks to high-energy periods and routine tasks to low-energy ones.

concepts.name: Buffers and planning fallacy
concepts.summary: Explain why estimates run short and add buffers to absorb overruns and interruptions.

concepts.name: Diagnosing procrastination causes
concepts.summary: Identify whether a delayed task stems from unclear next steps, fear, boredom or low value, and choose a fix accordingly.

misconceptions.text: Multitasking lets you get more done than doing one thing at a time.
Saying no makes you unhelpful and damages relationships.
A weekly review is wasted time that could be spent on actual work.

concepts.name: Aligning time with goals
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether your calendar reflects long-term goals and reallocate time accordingly.

concepts.name: Auditing time use
concepts.summary: Track how time is actually spent and analyse gaps between plan and reality to find leaks.

concepts.name: Selecting system fit
concepts.summary: Judge which techniques suit a given role, workload and personality and adapt or drop those that do not.

concepts.name: Managing interruptions and availability
concepts.summary: Design norms for email, chat and meetings that balance responsiveness with deep work.

concepts.name: Delegation and elimination decisions
concepts.summary: Decide which tasks to delegate, automate or abandon based on value and cost.

concepts.name: Handling overload and replanning
concepts.summary: Triage and replan when workload exceeds capacity, renegotiating scope and deadlines.

concepts.name: Sustainable pace and recovery
concepts.summary: Analyse how rest, sleep and breaks affect output and plan them as part of the system.

misconceptions.text: Working longer hours always yields proportionally more output.
A productivity system that works for someone else will work for you unchanged.
Being instantly responsive to every message demonstrates good time management.

concepts.name: Designing a personal system
concepts.summary: Create an integrated system of capture, planning, review and focus practices tailored to your context.

concepts.name: Evaluating system effectiveness
concepts.summary: Assess a system by outcomes and wellbeing rather than activity and refine it using evidence.

concepts.name: Opportunity cost and strategic choice
concepts.summary: Evaluate commitments by what they displace and choose deliberately among competing good options.

concepts.name: Team and shared time design
concepts.summary: Create meeting, handoff and availability norms that protect focus time across a group.

concepts.name: Coaching others on time
concepts.summary: Diagnose another person's time problems and design tailored, realistic changes for them.

concepts.name: Adapting across life changes
concepts.summary: Judge when role, workload or life changes demand rebuilding routines rather than patching them.

misconceptions.text: The goal of time management is maximum efficiency and throughput at all times.
Once a system is built, it should be kept fixed for consistency.
Advice that helped you will work for anyone you coach.

concepts.name: Kitchen hygiene and food safety
concepts.summary: Explain and follow handwashing, separating raw and cooked foods, safe storage temperatures and safe internal cooking temperatures to prevent illness.

concepts.name: Mise en place
concepts.summary: Understand why reading the whole recipe and prepping and measuring ingredients before heating anything makes cooking calmer and more reliable.

concepts.name: Basic knife grip and safety
concepts.summary: Hold a chef's knife with a pinch grip, guide food with a claw hand, and keep the board stable and the blade sharp and safely handled.

concepts.name: Core kitchen tools and measures
concepts.summary: Name common pans, knives, utensils and measuring tools and recall standard units such as teaspoons, tablespoons, cups and grams.

concepts.name: Stovetop heat levels
concepts.summary: Describe what low, medium and high heat look and sound like and how pan and burner settings change how food cooks.

concepts.name: Salt and tasting
concepts.summary: Understand that salt enhances flavour and that tasting during cooking guides seasoning adjustments.

concepts.name: Boiling and simmering
concepts.summary: Tell a rolling boil from a simmer and explain how each is used to cook foods like pasta, rice and eggs.

misconceptions.text: Washing raw chicken before cooking makes it safe to eat.
A dull knife is safer than a sharp one because it cuts less.
Higher heat always cooks food faster and better.

concepts.name: Basic knife cuts
concepts.summary: Produce slices, dices and chopped pieces of consistent size so that ingredients cook evenly.

concepts.name: Sautéing and pan-frying
concepts.summary: Preheat a pan, add fat, avoid overcrowding and move food appropriately to brown and cook it through.

concepts.name: Roasting vegetables and meats
concepts.summary: Set oven temperature, use a suitable tray and cut size, and judge doneness for roasted vegetables and simple meats.

concepts.name: Following a recipe accurately
concepts.summary: Carry out recipe steps in order using correct quantities, timings and cues such as colour and texture.

concepts.name: Cooking pasta rice and grains
concepts.summary: Cook pasta, rice and grains with suitable water ratios and times to a good texture.

concepts.name: Doneness checks and thermometer use
concepts.summary: Use a thermometer and visual or touch cues to confirm food is cooked safely and to the desired level.

concepts.name: Basic pantry and fat choices
concepts.summary: Choose appropriate oils, butter, acids and staples for different tasks and keep a workable pantry.

misconceptions.text: Piling all the food into the pan at once saves time without affecting results.
Meat is done when the outside is browned.
Pieces of any size cook in the same time if the heat is the same.

concepts.name: Maillard browning and caramelisation
concepts.summary: Analyse how dry surfaces, heat and time create browned flavour and adjust technique to achieve or avoid it.

concepts.name: Balancing flavour
concepts.summary: Diagnose a dish as lacking salt, acidity, sweetness, bitterness or richness and correct it with targeted additions.

concepts.name: Moist-heat methods
concepts.summary: Choose and carry out braising, poaching and steaming according to the food's structure and desired result.

concepts.name: Pan sauces and emulsions
concepts.summary: Build a pan sauce by deglazing and reducing, and make a stable vinaigrette or simple emulsion.

concepts.name: Recipe substitution and scaling
concepts.summary: Analyse a recipe's functional ingredients to swap items and scale quantities and cooking times sensibly.

concepts.name: Timing a multi-dish meal
concepts.summary: Plan prep and cooking order so several dishes finish together and hot food is served hot.

concepts.name: Resting and carryover cooking
concepts.summary: Explain how residual heat keeps cooking food and juices redistribute, and pull food early accordingly.

concepts.name: Balanced everyday meal planning
concepts.summary: Compose meals with vegetables, protein and carbohydrate and plan shopping and leftovers across a week.

misconceptions.text: Searing meat seals in the juices.
Wet food browns just as well as dry food if the pan is hot enough.
Any ingredient can be swapped one-for-one in baking and sauces with no effect.

concepts.name: Diagnosing and fixing failed dishes
concepts.summary: Trace a flawed result such as toughness, blandness or a split sauce to its cause and choose a corrective step.

concepts.name: Selecting method by ingredient structure
concepts.summary: Judge the best cooking method for a cut or vegetable based on its connective tissue, fat, moisture and thickness.

concepts.name: Intuitive heat management
concepts.summary: Read sound, smell and visual cues to adjust heat, pan choice and oven position during cooking.

concepts.name: Building dishes from principles
concepts.summary: Evaluate available ingredients and apply flexible templates such as stir-fries, soups and roasts to improvise a coherent dish.

concepts.name: Layering flavour through the cook
concepts.summary: Decide when to add aromatics, salt, spices and acid to build depth and judge the effect of each stage.

concepts.name: Efficient kitchen workflow
concepts.summary: Analyse workflow, batch prep and storage to cut waste and time while keeping food safe and fresh.

concepts.name: Evaluating recipe quality
concepts.summary: Assess whether a recipe's ratios, times and instructions are sound before cooking it and justify changes.

misconceptions.text: Great cooks never need to measure or follow ratios.
A published recipe is always tested and correct as written.
All tough cuts of meat just need more time at high heat to become tender.

concepts.name: Designing original dishes
concepts.summary: Create a new dish with coherent flavour, texture and balance and refine it through iterative testing.

concepts.name: Writing reliable recipes
concepts.summary: Produce clear, tested recipes with accurate quantities, cues and troubleshooting that others can reproduce.

concepts.name: Cross-cuisine technique adaptation
concepts.summary: Evaluate techniques and flavour systems from different cuisines and adapt them respectfully to new ingredients.

concepts.name: Menu design for diets and constraints
concepts.summary: Design menus that meet allergy, dietary, budget and seasonal constraints without losing flavour or nutritional balance.

concepts.name: Evidence-based technique evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge cooking claims and techniques using food science and controlled comparison rather than tradition alone.

concepts.name: Teaching and coaching cooks
concepts.summary: Create lessons and feedback that diagnose a learner's gaps and build their skill and confidence.

concepts.name: Sustainable and economical kitchen systems
concepts.summary: Design routines for sourcing, using whole ingredients and repurposing leftovers to reduce cost and waste.

misconceptions.text: Authentic technique means never adapting a dish to different ingredients or needs.
Traditional kitchen rules are proven and need no testing.
A new dish is finished once it tastes good once.

concepts.name: User flow diagrams
concepts.summary: Explain how a user flow maps the steps and decisions a person takes from entry point to goal across screens.

concepts.name: Wireframe fidelity levels
concepts.summary: Describe how low-fidelity wireframes, mockups and prototypes differ in purpose and detail.

concepts.name: Visual hierarchy cues
concepts.summary: Recognise how size, contrast, colour, spacing and position direct attention to the most important elements.

concepts.name: Common UI components
concepts.summary: Name and recognise buttons, form fields, menus, cards, modals and tabs and state what each is for.

concepts.name: Alignment and spacing
concepts.summary: Understand how alignment, consistent spacing and grouping make related items read as a unit and screens feel orderly.

concepts.name: Figma frames and layers
concepts.summary: Remember how frames, shapes, text and layers are organised on a Figma canvas.

concepts.name: Core accessibility needs
concepts.summary: Explain why text contrast, readable size and non-colour cues matter for users with visual, motor and cognitive differences.

misconceptions.text: UX design is just making screens look attractive.
Wireframes should show final colours, images and polished styling.
Accessibility only matters for a small group of users with disabilities.

concepts.name: Information architecture structure
concepts.summary: Organise content into sensible groups and hierarchies using labels, categories and sitemaps.

concepts.name: Navigation pattern selection
concepts.summary: Apply patterns such as top nav, tab bar, hamburger menu and breadcrumbs appropriately to a product's size and platform.

concepts.name: Grid and layout systems
concepts.summary: Lay out screens on a column grid and adapt the layout across mobile, tablet and desktop breakpoints.

concepts.name: Typography and colour usage
concepts.summary: Apply a limited type scale and palette that support readability and convey hierarchy and state.

concepts.name: Clickable prototype building
concepts.summary: Link frames with interactions and transitions in Figma to simulate a flow for testing.

concepts.name: Contrast and WCAG checks
concepts.summary: Check text and UI contrast against WCAG ratios and fix failing combinations.

concepts.name: Reusable components and variants
concepts.summary: Build Figma components with variants and states so repeated elements stay consistent and editable.

concepts.name: Giving design feedback
concepts.summary: Describe feedback on a design in terms of user goals and observable features rather than personal taste.

misconceptions.text: A hamburger menu is a good default for any product's navigation.
Information architecture is the same as the visual menu design.
Meeting the minimum contrast ratio makes a design fully accessible.

concepts.name: Task-driven flow design
concepts.summary: Derive flows from research findings, analysing steps for friction, dead ends and unnecessary decisions.

concepts.name: Interaction states and feedback
concepts.summary: Design hover, focus, disabled, loading, empty and error states so the system always communicates its status.

concepts.name: Form and input design
concepts.summary: Analyse and structure forms with sensible field order, inline validation and helpful error messages to reduce abandonment.

concepts.name: Design token foundations
concepts.summary: Define colour, type and spacing variables so styles are applied consistently and changed centrally.

concepts.name: Keyboard and screen reader support
concepts.summary: Specify focus order, labels, headings and alt text so a screen can be used without a mouse or sight.

concepts.name: Responsive adaptation decisions
concepts.summary: Decide what to reprioritise, collapse or reflow across screen sizes rather than just scaling layouts.

concepts.name: Structured design critique
concepts.summary: Run and take part in critiques that tie each decision to goals and constraints and lead to concrete revisions.

concepts.name: Usability heuristic evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate screens against established heuristics to find and rank usability problems.

misconceptions.text: Designing only the happy path is enough for a complete flow.
Accessibility can be added at the end by running an automated checker.
Responsive design means shrinking the desktop layout to fit a phone.

concepts.name: Design system architecture
concepts.summary: Analyse how tokens, components, patterns and documentation layer together and where a system should or should not constrain designers.

concepts.name: Trade-off evaluation in design
concepts.summary: Weigh competing options such as simplicity versus flexibility or consistency versus context fit using evidence and constraints.

concepts.name: Cognitive load management
concepts.summary: Analyse screens for load and apply progressive disclosure, chunking and defaults to reduce it.

concepts.name: Usability test-informed iteration
concepts.summary: Judge which usability findings justify design changes and prioritise revisions by severity and impact.

concepts.name: Complex navigation and IA
concepts.summary: Evaluate and restructure the IA and navigation of large products using card sort, tree test and analytics evidence.

concepts.name: Accessibility conformance review
concepts.summary: Audit designs against WCAG criteria, judge severity and recommend fixes beyond automated checks.

concepts.name: Developer handoff specification
concepts.summary: Analyse what engineers need, such as states, responsive rules, tokens and edge cases, and document them so the build matches intent.

misconceptions.text: A design system guarantees good UX because everything is consistent.
Fewer options and fewer clicks always make an interface easier to use.
Every usability test finding should be fixed before release.

concepts.name: Design system strategy
concepts.summary: Judge the value, cost and governance of a design system and decide how it should evolve with product and team scale.

concepts.name: Cross-product experience coherence
concepts.summary: Create patterns and principles that keep flows and interfaces coherent across multiple products and platforms.

concepts.name: Design principles authoring
concepts.summary: Craft specific, usable principles that resolve disagreements and guide decisions for a team.

concepts.name: Design quality measurement
concepts.summary: Evaluate and select metrics such as task success, time on task and satisfaction to judge whether design changes improved the experience.

concepts.name: Critique culture leadership
concepts.summary: Evaluate and shape critique and review practices so teams produce better decisions and grow designers' judgment.

concepts.name: Inclusive design at scale
concepts.summary: Build accessibility into systems, process and tooling so inclusive outcomes are the default rather than a late fix.

concepts.name: Ethical and manipulative patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs for deceptive or harmful patterns and argue for alternatives balancing business goals and user wellbeing.

misconceptions.text: Design quality can be judged by a single metric such as conversion rate.
A mature design system removes the need for design judgment on individual screens.
Critique is for senior designers to approve work.

concepts.name: Line manager role and responsibilities
concepts.summary: Can state what a line manager is accountable for: team results, direct reports' performance, wellbeing and development, and day-to-day people decisions.

concepts.name: One-on-one meeting purpose
concepts.summary: Can explain why regular one-on-ones exist, whose meeting they are, and what they cover such as progress, obstacles, feedback and wellbeing.

concepts.name: Clear expectations
concepts.summary: Can explain why people need to know what is expected of them in outcomes, behaviours and standards, and how unclear expectations cause problems.

concepts.name: Basic goal setting
concepts.summary: Can describe what makes a goal specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound, and why goals link to team priorities.

concepts.name: Delegation versus task assignment
concepts.summary: Understands that delegation transfers responsibility for an outcome with authority to act, while the manager remains accountable.

concepts.name: Feedback types
concepts.summary: Can distinguish recognition of good work from corrective feedback and recall why both are needed and timely.

concepts.name: Onboarding stages
concepts.summary: Can list what a new hire needs: pre-start preparation, first-day logistics, introductions, role goals and early check-ins.

concepts.name: Manager's HR boundaries
concepts.summary: Understands that absence, discipline and grievances are governed by policy and law, and that a manager must know when to consult HR.

misconceptions.text: A manager's job is to be the best doer on the team and to do the hardest work personally.
One-on-ones are the manager's status-update meeting and can be cancelled when things are busy.
Good people don't need expectations spelled out because they will work it out themselves.

concepts.name: Running an effective one-on-one
concepts.summary: Can run a regular one-on-one with a shared agenda, listening more than talking, and recording and following up on actions.

concepts.name: Writing goals with measures
concepts.summary: Can draft goals for a direct report that state outcomes, success measures and deadlines and link to team objectives.

concepts.name: Giving behaviour-based feedback
concepts.summary: Can give specific feedback describing the situation, observable behaviour and impact, without judging character.

concepts.name: Matching tasks to people
concepts.summary: Can choose what to delegate and to whom based on skill, will, development value and risk, with a clear brief.

concepts.name: Structured onboarding plan
concepts.summary: Can build a plan for a new hire's first weeks with milestones, a buddy, training and scheduled check-ins.

concepts.name: Performance review cycle
concepts.summary: Understands the stages of a review cycle, from goal setting through evidence gathering to rating and discussion, and the manager's role in each.

concepts.name: Recording absence and return conversations
concepts.summary: Can follow the absence reporting procedure, hold a supportive return-to-work conversation and keep accurate confidential records.

concepts.name: Spotting early conflict signs
concepts.summary: Can recognise early signs of friction such as withdrawal, sniping or avoidance and understand why prompt, neutral action matters.

misconceptions.text: Feedback should be saved for the annual review so it can be given with all the evidence.

Onboarding is finished after the first day or week.

concepts.name: Evidence-based performance assessment
concepts.summary: Can gather examples across the period, compare them against expectations, and write a balanced assessment that avoids rating biases.

concepts.name: Coaching conversation model
concepts.summary: Can use open questions in a structure such as goal, reality, options and way forward to help a report find their own solutions.

concepts.name: Career development planning
concepts.summary: Can hold a career conversation and agree a development plan with stretch assignments, learning and sponsors matched to aspirations and business needs.

concepts.name: Underperformance diagnosis
concepts.summary: Can analyse whether poor performance stems from unclear expectations, skill gaps, motivation, resources, health or personal circumstances before choosing a response.

concepts.name: Performance improvement plan
concepts.summary: Can set out specific shortfalls, support, measures, timescales and review points in a fair improvement plan, following policy.

concepts.name: Mediating team conflict
concepts.summary: Can analyse the interests behind a dispute and facilitate a conversation toward agreed behaviours, escalating when needed.

concepts.name: Managing long-term absence
concepts.summary: Can keep in contact, agree adjustments and a phased return, and work with HR and occupational health on prolonged absence.

concepts.name: Calibrating delegation level
concepts.summary: Can analyse a person's readiness and the task's risk to choose how much autonomy to give and how closely to follow up.

misconceptions.text: Coaching means telling people the answer more patiently.
Underperformance is nearly always a motivation or attitude problem.
A performance improvement plan is a formality to document a dismissal.

concepts.name: Tailoring management to individuals
concepts.summary: Can analyse each report's competence, confidence and motivation and adapt directive and supportive behaviours accordingly.

concepts.name: Calibrating ratings across teams
concepts.summary: Can evaluate ratings against peers' and defend them in calibration, detecting bias such as recency, halo and leniency.

concepts.name: Talent and succession development
concepts.summary: Can judge potential and readiness within the team and design development to build bench strength and reduce key-person risk.

concepts.name: Managing difficult cases legally
concepts.summary: Can assess a complex case such as repeated underperformance or misconduct, weigh evidence and fairness, and choose proportionate action with HR and legal input.

concepts.name: Team dynamics and psychological safety
concepts.summary: Can diagnose team norms, trust and voice issues and take actions that make it safe to raise problems and disagree.

concepts.name: Workload and wellbeing management
concepts.summary: Can evaluate individual and team workload, spot burnout risk and rebalance priorities or resourcing.

concepts.name: Managing remote and hybrid reports
concepts.summary: Can adapt communication, visibility, fairness and onboarding to distributed working while managing outcomes rather than presence.

concepts.name: Inclusive and fair people decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate allocation, development and discipline decisions for fairness and unequal impact across team members.

misconceptions.text: Treating everyone identically is what fairness means in management.
A strong team is one without disagreement.
Remote reports can be managed fairly by how visible and responsive they are.

concepts.name: Designing people management practices
concepts.summary: Can design rhythms, templates and norms for one-on-ones, goals, feedback and reviews that suit the team and organisation.

concepts.name: Evaluating performance systems
concepts.summary: Can critique goal frameworks, rating scales and review methods for validity, motivation effects and fairness, and recommend improvements.

concepts.name: Developing other managers
concepts.summary: Can create ways to coach new and experienced managers in people practices, such as case discussions and shadowing.

concepts.name: Managing through organisational change
concepts.summary: Can evaluate the people impact of reorganisation, role changes or redundancy and lead teams through it ethically and lawfully.

concepts.name: Building team capability strategically
concepts.summary: Can create a plan for hiring, onboarding, development and retention that closes future skill gaps.

concepts.name: Resolving entrenched dysfunction
concepts.summary: Can design an intervention for a team with chronic conflict, low trust or poor performance, combining individual and structural action.

concepts.name: Ethical judgement in people decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate dilemmas such as confidentiality versus duty, loyalty versus fairness or business need versus wellbeing and justify a decision.

misconceptions.text: A standard process applied identically across all teams yields consistent good management.
A manager can fix a dysfunctional team by replacing its most difficult person.
Being transparent about organisational change means sharing everything immediately.

concepts.name: Position, displacement and distance
concepts.summary: Distinguish position, displacement and distance travelled and describe motion along a line with a coordinate axis.

concepts.name: Speed and velocity
concepts.summary: Explain velocity as the rate of change of position with direction and compute average speed and velocity.

concepts.name: Acceleration as rate of change
concepts.summary: Explain acceleration as the rate of change of velocity and interpret its sign relative to motion.

concepts.name: Force as push or pull
concepts.summary: Describe forces as vector interactions and identify common ones such as weight, normal force, friction and tension.

concepts.name: Newton's three laws
concepts.summary: State and explain inertia, F=ma and action-reaction pairs in everyday situations.

concepts.name: Free fall near Earth
concepts.summary: Explain that all objects fall with the same acceleration g of about 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is negligible.

concepts.name: Mass versus weight
concepts.summary: Distinguish mass as amount of inertia from weight as gravitational force W=mg.

misconceptions.text: A moving object needs a continuing net force to keep moving at constant velocity.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones in the absence of air resistance.
Negative acceleration always means the object is slowing down.

concepts.name: Constant-acceleration kinematic equations
concepts.summary: Select and apply the equations relating displacement, velocity, acceleration and time to one-dimensional problems.

concepts.name: Motion graphs
concepts.summary: Read slopes and areas of position, velocity and acceleration graphs to find velocity, acceleration and displacement.

concepts.name: Vector components and resolution
concepts.summary: Resolve forces and velocities into perpendicular components using trigonometry and recombine them.

concepts.name: Projectile motion
concepts.summary: Treat horizontal and vertical motion independently to find range, flight time and maximum height.

concepts.name: Free-body diagrams
concepts.summary: Draw all forces acting on a single body and write Newton's second law along chosen axes.

concepts.name: Friction and inclined planes
concepts.summary: Apply friction coefficients and weight components to find acceleration on level and inclined surfaces.

concepts.name: Work and kinetic energy
concepts.summary: Compute work as force times displacement along the force and kinetic energy as ½mv².

misconceptions.text: A projectile at its peak has zero acceleration.
Friction always opposes the motion of an object, even when it is what accelerates it, such as a car's wheels or a box on a belt.
The normal force always equals the weight of the object.

concepts.name: Work-energy theorem
aliases: net work equals change in kinetic energy
concepts.summary: Use net work equals change in kinetic energy to solve speed and distance problems without time.

concepts.name: Conservative forces and potential energy
concepts.summary: Define potential energy for conservative forces and apply conservation of mechanical energy, accounting for non-conservative work.

concepts.name: Power
concepts.summary: Compute power as rate of energy transfer, including P=Fv.

concepts.name: Momentum and impulse
concepts.summary: Relate impulse, force over time, to change in momentum.

concepts.name: Conservation of linear momentum
concepts.summary: Identify when a system is isolated in a direction and use momentum conservation to analyse interactions.

concepts.name: Elastic and inelastic collisions
concepts.summary: Classify collisions by kinetic energy conservation and solve one- and two-dimensional cases.

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion of springs
concepts.summary: Apply Hooke's law and find period, frequency and energy of a mass on a spring.

concepts.name: Uniform circular motion
concepts.summary: Explain that circular motion requires a net inward force and compute v²/r and the required force.

misconceptions.text: Kinetic energy is conserved in all collisions.
Centrifugal force is a real outward force acting on an object in circular motion.
The period of a mass on a spring depends on the amplitude of oscillation.

concepts.name: Rotational kinematics and dynamics
concepts.summary: Map linear quantities onto angular ones and relate angular acceleration to net torque.

concepts.name: Torque and static equilibrium
concepts.summary: Compute torque as r×F and apply zero net force and torque conditions to structures.

concepts.name: Moment of inertia
concepts.summary: Analyse how mass distribution and axis choice determine rotational inertia, using standard shapes and the parallel-axis theorem.

concepts.name: Angular momentum conservation
concepts.summary: Apply conservation of angular momentum when net external torque is zero, as in a spinning skater.

concepts.name: Rolling motion and energy
concepts.summary: Combine translational and rotational kinetic energy to analyse rolling bodies on inclines.

concepts.name: Newtonian gravitation and orbits
concepts.summary: Use the inverse-square law to derive circular orbital speed and period and apply Kepler's laws.

concepts.name: Gravitational potential energy and escape
concepts.summary: Evaluate orbital energies and escape speed using the potential -GMm/r.

concepts.name: Pendulum and damped oscillations
concepts.summary: Judge when the simple pendulum is harmonic and analyse damping, driving and resonance.

misconceptions.text: Astronauts in orbit float because there is no gravity there.
A heavier object always has a larger moment of inertia regardless of how its mass is distributed or about which axis.
The pendulum period depends on the bob's mass and is independent of the length.

concepts.name: Lagrangian formulation
concepts.summary: Derive equations of motion from L=T-V with generalised coordinates and judge when this beats Newtonian force analysis.

concepts.name: Symmetries and conservation laws
concepts.summary: Link translation, rotation and time invariance to conservation of momentum, angular momentum and energy.

concepts.name: Central-force problem
concepts.summary: Reduce the two-body problem to an effective one-dimensional potential and classify orbits by energy and angular momentum.

concepts.name: Rigid body rotation in 3D
concepts.summary: Use the inertia tensor and principal axes to explain torque-free rotation, precession and gyroscopic effects.

concepts.name: Non-inertial reference frames
concepts.summary: Formulate dynamics in accelerating and rotating frames and evaluate centrifugal and Coriolis effects.

concepts.name: Small oscillations and normal modes
concepts.summary: Linearise about equilibrium and construct normal modes of coupled systems.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian mechanics and phase space
concepts.summary: Use Hamilton's equations and phase-space portraits to analyse dynamics and stability.

concepts.name: Limits of Newtonian models
concepts.summary: Evaluate where classical models fail or lose predictability, including chaos and relativistic or quantum regimes.

misconceptions.text: The Lagrangian approach gives different physics from Newton's laws rather than an equivalent reformulation.
Fictitious forces like Coriolis are not real, so they can be ignored when analysing motion in a rotating frame.
Deterministic equations of motion always allow long-term prediction.

concepts.name: Speech purpose and audience
concepts.summary: Explain that every talk has a specific purpose (inform, persuade, inspire) and must be shaped around who the listeners are and what they need.

concepts.name: Three-part speech structure
concepts.summary: Describe how a speech is organised into an opening, a body and a closing, each with its own job.

concepts.name: Single core message
concepts.summary: State the one key message you want the audience to remember and understand why limiting the number of main points helps.

concepts.name: Basic vocal delivery
concepts.summary: Recall that speaking loudly enough, clearly and at a steady pace lets the whole room hear and follow you.

concepts.name: Eye contact with audience
concepts.summary: Remember that looking at people in the room rather than at notes, the floor or the screen builds connection and trust.

concepts.name: Nerves as normal
concepts.summary: Explain that nervousness before speaking is common and that physical symptoms like a fast heartbeat are energy, not signs of failure.

concepts.name: Value of rehearsal
concepts.summary: Understand why practising a speech aloud, rather than only reading it silently, improves delivery and timing.

misconceptions.text: Good speakers are born confident and never feel nervous.
Reading the speech word for word from a script is the safest way to deliver it well.
The more points and facts a speech contains, the better it will be.

concepts.name: Speech outline construction
concepts.summary: Build a working outline with a main point hierarchy, supporting evidence and transitions between sections.

concepts.name: Attention-grabbing openings
concepts.summary: Craft an opening using a story, question, striking fact or scenario that earns attention and previews the topic.

concepts.name: Memorable closings
concepts.summary: Write a closing that recaps the core message and ends with a clear final thought or call to action.

concepts.name: Readable slide design
concepts.summary: Apply principles of few words, large fonts, high contrast and one idea per slide to support rather than replace the speaker.

concepts.name: Pacing and pausing
concepts.summary: Control speaking speed and use deliberate pauses to emphasise points and let listeners absorb them.

concepts.name: Purposeful gestures and posture
concepts.summary: Use open posture and natural gestures that reinforce meaning while avoiding distracting habits like pacing or fidgeting.

concepts.name: Timed rehearsal practice
concepts.summary: Rehearse with a timer and adjust content so the talk fits its allotted time.

concepts.name: Basic relaxation techniques
concepts.summary: Use controlled breathing and physical warm-ups to reduce tension before and during a talk.

misconceptions.text: Slides should contain the full text of the talk so the audience can follow along.
Silence during a talk means you have lost your place and should be filled with words like 'um'.
Gestures should be planned and performed identically at set moments.

concepts.name: Audience-tailored message design
concepts.summary: Analyse audience knowledge, attitudes and expectations to select content, depth, examples and tone.

concepts.name: Storytelling for persuasion
concepts.summary: Use stories with a clear arc and relevance to the message to make points emotionally and mentally sticky.

concepts.name: Organisational pattern selection
concepts.summary: Choose among patterns such as chronological, problem-solution, and cause-effect based on purpose and audience.

concepts.name: Voice modulation and projection
concepts.summary: Vary pitch, volume and tempo, and project from the diaphragm, to maintain energy and convey emphasis in different room sizes.

concepts.name: Q&A handling technique
concepts.summary: Listen, restate, answer concisely and redirect hostile, off-topic or unknown questions without losing control.

concepts.name: Slide-speaker integration
concepts.summary: Analyse how each slide's content and timing relate to spoken narration, and cut or restructure what duplicates or distracts.

concepts.name: Feedback-driven rehearsal
concepts.summary: Use video recordings and peer feedback to diagnose delivery weaknesses and target revisions.

concepts.name: Webinar delivery adaptation
concepts.summary: Adjust camera framing, vocal energy, interaction and slide pacing for remote audiences without room cues.

misconceptions.text: A talk that works for one audience will work for any audience if the delivery is good.
Projecting your voice means shouting.
In Q&A you must have an answer to every question, and admitting you don't know damages credibility.

concepts.name: Rhetorical appeals balancing
concepts.summary: Analyse how credibility, emotion and logic work together in a speech and balance them for the context.

concepts.name: Reading and adapting to the room
concepts.summary: Interpret audience cues such as attention, confusion and energy and decide how to adjust pace, depth or content on the spot.

concepts.name: Managing difficult audiences
concepts.summary: Judge how to respond to hostility, interruptions and technical failures while protecting the message and the relationship.

concepts.name: Cognitive load in slide design
concepts.summary: Evaluate slide decks against how people process words, visuals and speech simultaneously and revise to reduce overload.

concepts.name: Presence and stage command
concepts.summary: Analyse how movement, positioning, stillness and use of the stage or camera frame signal confidence and direct attention.

concepts.name: Speaking anxiety reframing
concepts.summary: Analyse personal anxiety triggers and apply cognitive reframing, exposure and preparation routines to channel arousal.

concepts.name: Flexible improvised delivery
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to use full notes, key-point cues or no notes and deliver fluidly from structure rather than memorised text.

misconceptions.text: Memorising a speech word for word makes delivery more polished and reduces risk.
Appealing to emotion is manipulative and weakens a rational argument.
Eliminating all nervousness is the goal of managing speaking anxiety.

concepts.name: Signature speaking style development
concepts.summary: Create a distinctive, authentic delivery style that integrates a speaker's strengths, values and stories.

concepts.name: Original keynote architecture
concepts.summary: Design an original talk with a central idea, emotional arc, recurring motifs and tailored structure for a major event.

concepts.name: Evaluating speeches critically
concepts.summary: Assess speeches by others against purpose, context and rhetorical effect, and justify the judgements with evidence.

concepts.name: Ethical persuasion judgement
concepts.summary: Judge when persuasive techniques cross into manipulation or misrepresentation and set principles for honest influence.

concepts.name: Mixed-format event design
concepts.summary: Design talks that engage in-room and remote audiences simultaneously, including interaction, staging and production coordination.

concepts.name: Coaching other speakers
concepts.summary: Create development plans and give targeted feedback that improve another speaker's structure, delivery and confidence.

concepts.name: High-stakes performance strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate and plan for high-pressure contexts such as investor pitches, crisis briefings and live-broadcast talks, including contingencies.

misconceptions.text: Expert speakers follow one universal formula that can be copied to produce great talks.
Coaching means correcting every flaw so the speaker imitates your own style.
A hybrid event can be run by delivering the in-room talk and simply streaming it.

concepts.name: Points, lines, and planes
concepts.summary: Recall and describe points, lines, rays, segments and planes and name them with correct notation.

concepts.name: Angle types and measurement
concepts.summary: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight and measure them in degrees with a protractor.

concepts.name: Parallel and perpendicular lines
concepts.summary: Explain what makes two lines parallel or perpendicular and recognise them in figures.

concepts.name: Triangle and quadrilateral classification
concepts.summary: Name triangles by sides and angles and quadrilaterals by their defining properties.

concepts.name: Perimeter and area formulas
concepts.summary: Recall perimeter and area formulas for rectangles, squares and triangles and state units.

concepts.name: Circle parts and vocabulary
concepts.summary: Identify radius, diameter, chord, circumference and center of a circle.

misconceptions.text: A square is not a rectangle because rectangles must have unequal sides.
Area and perimeter measure the same thing and use the same units.
A triangle's height is always one of its sides.

concepts.name: Angle pair relationships
concepts.summary: Use complementary, supplementary, linear pair and vertical angle relationships to find unknown angles.

concepts.name: Transversal angle relationships
concepts.summary: Apply corresponding, alternate interior and same-side interior angle facts to parallel lines cut by a transversal.

concepts.name: Triangle angle sum
concepts.summary: Use the 180° angle sum and exterior angle theorem to find missing triangle angles.

concepts.name: Pythagorean theorem application
concepts.summary: Compute a missing side of a right triangle and test whether side lengths form a right triangle.

concepts.name: Polygon angle sums
concepts.summary: Find interior and exterior angle sums and individual angles of regular polygons.

concepts.name: Area of composite figures
concepts.summary: Compute areas of parallelograms, trapezoids, circles and composite shapes by decomposition.

concepts.name: Volume of prisms and cylinders
concepts.summary: Calculate volume as base area times height for prisms and cylinders.

misconceptions.text: Alternate interior angles are equal whether or not the lines are parallel.
The Pythagorean theorem a²+b²=c² works for any triangle.
Volume is found by multiplying all the side lengths of any solid.

concepts.name: Triangle congruence criteria
concepts.summary: Choose and apply SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL to establish that two triangles are congruent.

concepts.name: Two-column proof construction
concepts.summary: Build a logically ordered proof with statements justified by givens, definitions, postulates and theorems.

concepts.name: CPCTC use in proofs
concepts.summary: Use congruent triangles to deduce equality of corresponding segments and angles.

concepts.name: Similar triangles and proportions
concepts.summary: Establish similarity by AA, SAS or SSS similarity and set up proportions for missing lengths.

concepts.name: Scale factor effects
concepts.summary: Predict how scale factor k changes lengths, areas (k²) and volumes (k³).

concepts.name: Circle arcs and central angles
concepts.summary: Relate central and inscribed angles to arcs and compute arc length and sector area.

concepts.name: Surface area of solids
concepts.summary: Compute surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres using nets and formulas.

concepts.name: Special right triangles
concepts.summary: Use the side ratios of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles to find lengths without the full theorem.

misconceptions.text: SSA is a valid triangle congruence criterion.
Doubling a figure's side lengths doubles its area.
CPCTC can be used to prove the triangles congruent in the first place.

concepts.name: Circle chord and tangent theorems
concepts.summary: Analyse relationships among chords, tangents and secants, including tangent-radius perpendicularity and segment product rules.

concepts.name: Strategy selection in proofs
concepts.summary: Analyse a problem to choose between congruence, similarity, angle chasing or auxiliary lines and plan a proof.

concepts.name: Auxiliary constructions
concepts.summary: Judge which added segments, parallels or altitudes will expose usable relationships in a figure.

concepts.name: Similarity in right triangles
concepts.summary: Derive and apply geometric mean relationships created by the altitude to the hypotenuse.

concepts.name: Cyclic quadrilateral properties
concepts.summary: Use opposite-angle supplementarity and inscribed angle results to analyse figures within circles.

concepts.name: Multi-step solid measurement
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches to volume and surface area of composite solids, including slant heights and cross sections.

concepts.name: Proof validity assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate proofs for gaps, unjustified assumptions, circular reasoning and diagram-based conclusions.

misconceptions.text: A conclusion that looks true in an accurate diagram needs no justification.
A tangent line to a circle can intersect the circle at two points.
Any quadrilateral can be inscribed in a circle.

concepts.name: Axiomatic structure of Euclid
concepts.summary: Evaluate how theorems depend on postulates, especially the parallel postulate, and judge the logical order of results.

concepts.name: Non-Euclidean contrasts
concepts.summary: Assess which Euclidean results fail on spheres or hyperbolic planes, such as the triangle angle sum.

concepts.name: Original proof design
concepts.summary: Create proofs for unfamiliar statements and compare multiple proofs, such as synthetic, coordinate and transformational, for efficiency.

concepts.name: Coordinate and transformation methods
concepts.summary: Design coordinate or rigid-motion arguments that prove congruence and similarity results.

concepts.name: Geometric construction design
concepts.summary: Devise and justify compass-and-straightedge constructions and recognise impossible ones such as trisecting an arbitrary angle.

concepts.name: Modeling with geometric measures
concepts.summary: Build and critique geometric models of real situations, choosing approximations and judging error in area and volume estimates.

concepts.name: Teaching geometric reasoning
concepts.summary: Evaluate learner arguments and sequence tasks to diagnose and repair reasoning errors in geometry.

misconceptions.text: Euclidean geometry is the only consistent geometry and describes physical space exactly.
Any angle can be trisected with compass and straightedge given enough ingenuity.
A proof that works for one drawn example is sufficient to establish a general theorem.

concepts.name: Non-relational data store idea
concepts.summary: Can state that NoSQL stores hold data in models other than fixed-schema relational tables and name why they emerged.

concepts.name: Key-value model
concepts.summary: Can explain that data is stored and retrieved as opaque values looked up by a unique key.

concepts.name: Document model
concepts.summary: Can explain that records are self-contained, nested documents (such as JSON) grouped into collections.

concepts.name: Wide-column model
concepts.summary: Can describe rows identified by keys holding sparse, flexible sets of columns grouped into column families.

concepts.name: Graph model
concepts.summary: Can describe data as nodes and relationships with properties, suited to highly connected data.

concepts.name: Flexible schema
concepts.summary: Can explain that records in one collection may have different fields and the structure is enforced by the application rather than the database.

concepts.name: Matching model to use case
concepts.summary: Can match typical examples (caching, catalogues, time series, social networks) to the NoSQL family that fits them.

misconceptions.text: NoSQL means the database can never use SQL-like query languages or has no structure at all.
All NoSQL databases work the same way and are interchangeable.
A flexible schema means the data has no schema at all.

concepts.name: CRUD operations on documents
concepts.summary: Can insert, read, update and delete documents and key-value entries using a store's basic API or shell.

concepts.name: Query filters and projections
concepts.summary: Can write queries with conditions, sorting, limits and field projections against a document collection.

concepts.name: Primary keys and partition keys
concepts.summary: Can explain that the key determines how records are located and distributed, and choose a sensible key for simple cases.

concepts.name: Embedding versus referencing
concepts.summary: Can model a one-to-many relationship either by embedding child data in a parent document or by storing references.

concepts.name: Secondary indexes
concepts.summary: Can create an index on a non-key field to speed up a query and recognise its write and storage cost.

concepts.name: Basic graph traversal queries
concepts.summary: Can write a simple query that matches nodes and follows relationships to find connected items.

concepts.name: Replication and sharding terms
concepts.summary: Can explain that replication copies data for availability and sharding splits data across nodes for scale.

misconceptions.text: Queries in a document database are fast on any field without any indexing.
Embedding is always better than referencing because there are no joins.
Replication and sharding are the same thing.

concepts.name: Query-driven data modelling
concepts.summary: Can derive a data model from the application's list of queries rather than from entity normalisation.

concepts.name: Denormalisation and duplication trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can analyse where duplicating data speeds reads and what update-consistency burden it creates.

concepts.name: CAP theorem
concepts.summary: Can analyse what a system must give up between consistency and availability during a network partition.

concepts.name: Eventual versus strong consistency
concepts.summary: Can explain and compare eventual and strong consistency and predict what reads may return after writes.

concepts.name: Partition key selection
concepts.summary: Can analyse a candidate partition key for even distribution, query locality and hot-spot risk.

concepts.name: Aggregation pipelines
concepts.summary: Can build multi-stage aggregations that filter, group and transform documents.

concepts.name: Single-document atomicity and transactions
concepts.summary: Can analyse which operations are atomic by default and when multi-record transactions are needed or costly.

concepts.name: Relational versus NoSQL selection
concepts.summary: Can compare relational and NoSQL options for a scenario on structure, queries, consistency and scale.

misconceptions.text: You should model NoSQL data by normalising entities first, exactly as in a relational design.
CAP means a system permanently picks only two of consistency, availability and partition tolerance.
NoSQL databases do not support transactions or atomic operations at all.

concepts.name: Tunable consistency and quorums
concepts.summary: Can reason about replica counts and read/write quorum settings to tune consistency against latency and availability.

concepts.name: Consistent hashing and rebalancing
concepts.summary: Can analyse how consistent hashing places data and limits movement when nodes join or leave.

concepts.name: Storage engines and LSM trees
concepts.summary: Can analyse how LSM-based and B-tree storage engines trade write throughput, read cost and compaction.

concepts.name: Conflict resolution strategies
concepts.summary: Can evaluate approaches to resolving concurrent writes and their risk of data loss or complexity.

concepts.name: PACELC and latency trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can evaluate how a system trades latency against consistency even when there is no partition.

concepts.name: Index and query performance diagnosis
concepts.summary: Can use query plans and metrics to diagnose slow queries and fix indexing or model problems.

concepts.name: Polyglot persistence design
concepts.summary: Can evaluate combining several data stores in one system and the cost of keeping them in sync.

concepts.name: Schema evolution and migration
concepts.summary: Can evaluate strategies for changing document structure in live systems without downtime or inconsistency.

misconceptions.text: Setting quorums to majority always guarantees linearizable reads.
Last-write-wins is a safe default because it never loses data.
Consistency trade-offs only matter during network partitions.

concepts.name: Architecture selection under constraints
concepts.summary: Can judge and defend a data store choice against workload, consistency, cost, operational and team constraints.

concepts.name: Distributed correctness reasoning
concepts.summary: Can evaluate a system's guarantees against anomalies such as stale reads, lost updates and write skew.

concepts.name: Multi-region replication design
concepts.summary: Can design a multi-region topology balancing latency, failover, data residency and conflict handling.

concepts.name: Capacity and scaling strategy
concepts.summary: Can create a plan for growth covering sharding, rebalancing, hot-key mitigation and cost.

concepts.name: Event-driven derived data pipelines
concepts.summary: Can design pipelines that propagate changes into search, cache and analytic views with defined consistency.

concepts.name: Failure and resilience testing
concepts.summary: Can evaluate durability and recovery behaviour through failure scenarios, backups and restore drills.

concepts.name: Custom data model frameworks
concepts.summary: Can create reusable modelling patterns and governance guidelines for teams working with NoSQL stores.

misconceptions.text: Horizontal scaling a NoSQL database is automatic and needs no data model or key design effort.
Multi-region replication improves availability without any consistency or latency cost.
Derived stores populated from change streams are always immediately consistent with the source.

concepts.name: Voltage, current and resistance
concepts.summary: Define voltage as energy per charge, current as charge flow rate and resistance as opposition to current, with their units.

concepts.name: Closed circuit loop
concepts.summary: Explain why current flows only in a complete conducting loop containing a source and how open and short circuits differ.

concepts.name: Ohm's law
concepts.summary: Relate voltage, current and resistance with V=IR and rearrange it to find any one of the three.

concepts.name: Circuit symbols and schematics
concepts.summary: Recognise standard symbols for sources, resistors, capacitors, inductors, switches and ground and read a simple schematic.

concepts.name: Series and parallel connections
concepts.summary: Distinguish series (same current) from parallel (same voltage) arrangements and say what each does to current and voltage.

concepts.name: Electrical power
concepts.summary: Explain power as the rate of energy transfer and compute it with P=VI, I²R or V²/R.

misconceptions.text: Current is used up as it flows through a resistor, so less current leaves than enters.
A battery supplies a fixed current regardless of what is connected to it.
Ohm's law means every component has constant resistance whatever the voltage across it.

concepts.name: Equivalent resistance
concepts.summary: Reduce series and parallel resistor combinations step by step to a single equivalent resistance.

concepts.name: Voltage and current dividers
