concepts.name: Formative and summative assessment
concepts.summary: Distinguish assessment used during learning to guide improvement from assessment used at the end to judge achievement.

misconceptions.text: Objectives that say learners will understand or appreciate a topic are measurable enough.
Higher Bloom levels are always better, so every objective should target creating or evaluating.
A needs assessment just means asking learners what they want to learn.

concepts.name: Task and content analysis
concepts.summary: Break a target performance into its component tasks, knowledge and skills to determine what must be taught.

concepts.name: Cognitive load management
concepts.summary: Apply principles like reducing extraneous load and managing element interactivity to material and activity design.

concepts.name: Gagné's events of instruction
concepts.summary: Structure a lesson using events such as gaining attention, stating objectives, presenting content, eliciting practice and giving feedback.

concepts.name: Practice and retrieval design
concepts.summary: Design practice that requires recall and application, distributed over time and with increasing difficulty.

concepts.name: Instructional strategy selection
concepts.summary: Analyse an objective and learner context to choose between strategies such as direct instruction, case study, simulation or collaborative work.

concepts.name: Rubrics and assessment validity
concepts.summary: Build rubrics and judge whether an assessment validly and reliably measures the intended objective.

concepts.name: Kirkpatrick evaluation levels
concepts.summary: Plan evaluation across reaction, learning, behavior and results and apply it to a program.

misconceptions.text: Learners have fixed learning styles, and teaching to each person's preferred style improves learning.
Adding more visuals, animation and audio always improves learning.
Positive learner satisfaction ratings show that the training worked.

concepts.name: Performance problem diagnosis
concepts.summary: Judge whether a performance gap stems from knowledge and skill, or from motivation, tools, incentives or environment, and decide if training is the right solution.

concepts.name: Instructional design models comparison
concepts.summary: Evaluate process models such as ADDIE, SAM and Dick and Carey and choose one based on project constraints and uncertainty.

concepts.name: Learning transfer design
concepts.summary: Design pre-, during- and post-training supports such as job aids, manager involvement and application tasks so skills transfer to work.

concepts.name: Modality and blended design
concepts.summary: Analyse trade-offs between delivery modes and combine them so each part of the objective is served by the best fit.

concepts.name: Motivation and engagement design
concepts.summary: Analyse sources of learner motivation and design attention, relevance, confidence and satisfaction supports accordingly.

concepts.name: Learning analytics and item analysis
concepts.summary: Interpret assessment and usage data to find weak items, content or activities and revise the design.

concepts.name: Accessibility and inclusive design
concepts.summary: Evaluate a design against accessibility and UDL principles and revise it to reduce barriers for diverse learners.

misconceptions.text: Training is the right answer to any performance problem.
Learners who pass the end-of-course test will automatically apply the skills at work.
Moving a face-to-face course online unchanged gives an equivalent learning experience.

concepts.name: Evidence-based design synthesis
concepts.summary: Critically evaluate research claims and weigh learning science evidence against context when making design decisions.

concepts.name: Complex skill design models
concepts.summary: Create learning programs for complex skills using whole-task sequences, scaffolding and fading of support.

concepts.name: Program-level evaluation strategy
concepts.summary: Design evaluation plans that isolate the training effect, link to business or organizational outcomes and inform decisions about continuing the program.

concepts.name: Adaptive and personalized pathways
concepts.summary: Create learning pathways that adapt content, pacing or support to learner diagnostics while preserving objective alignment.

concepts.name: Learning ecosystem architecture
concepts.summary: Design coherent curricula and ecosystems that combine formal training, performance support and social learning to meet organizational goals.

concepts.name: Design trade-off judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs among rigor, cost, time and stakeholder demands, and defend which design compromises are acceptable.

concepts.name: Stakeholder and SME leadership
concepts.summary: Evaluate and manage stakeholder expectations and subject matter expert input, including expert blind spots, to keep the design focused on outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Following a single proven model or framework rigorously guarantees an effective course.
ROI calculations can fully and cleanly prove the value of training.
Subject matter experts know best how the content should be taught.

concepts.name: Copy's single action goal
concepts.summary: Explain that copy exists to move a reader toward one specific action such as clicking, buying or signing up, not just to inform or entertain.

concepts.name: Target reader identification
concepts.summary: Describe who the copy is for and what that reader wants, fears and already knows.

concepts.name: Features versus benefits
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a product has (feature) from what it does for the reader (benefit) and recognise which a line states.

concepts.name: Headline's role
concepts.summary: Recall that the headline must earn attention and promise something that makes the reader continue.

concepts.name: Call to action basics
concepts.summary: Identify a call to action as the explicit instruction telling the reader what to do next.

concepts.name: Clear plain-language writing
concepts.summary: Understand why short sentences, concrete words and the reader's own vocabulary beat jargon and vague claims.

concepts.name: Copy formats and channels
aliases: ad, email, landing page, product page
concepts.summary: Name the main copy formats (ads, landing pages, emails, product pages) and what each is typically used for.

misconceptions.text: Good copy is mainly clever, creative wording that shows off the writer's style.
Listing everything the product can do is the same as persuading the reader.
A call to action is optional if the text is good enough.

concepts.name: Turning features into benefits
concepts.summary: Convert a feature list into reader-focused benefits by repeatedly asking 'so what?' until an outcome the reader values appears.

concepts.name: Headline formulas
concepts.summary: Write headlines using proven patterns such as benefit, how-to, number, question and curiosity, and choose one that fits the goal.

concepts.name: You-focused voice
concepts.summary: Rewrite company-centred sentences ('we offer') into reader-centred ones ('you get') without losing accuracy.

concepts.name: Writing effective CTAs
concepts.summary: Write specific, action-and-outcome CTAs such as 'Get my free guide' in place of generic ones like 'Submit'.

concepts.name: Scannable layout
concepts.summary: Structure copy with subheads, short paragraphs and bullets so a skimming reader grasps the offer.

concepts.name: Social proof elements
concepts.summary: Explain how testimonials, ratings and usage figures reduce doubt and apply them in appropriate places.

concepts.name: Email subject lines
concepts.summary: Write subject lines that are clear, relevant and honest enough to earn an open and match the email's content.

misconceptions.text: A benefit is just a feature described with more enthusiastic adjectives.
The more curiosity a headline creates, the better, even if it hides what the page offers.
Readers read all the copy carefully, so formatting does not matter.

concepts.name: Audience research and voice-of-customer
concepts.summary: Analyse reviews, interviews and support tickets to extract the pains, desires and exact phrases customers use, and build copy from them.

concepts.name: Awareness-level matching
concepts.summary: Diagnose how aware a reader is of the problem and solution and choose the opening angle accordingly.

concepts.name: Persuasion structures
concepts.summary: Apply frameworks such as AIDA and Problem-Agitate-Solve to organise copy and judge when each suits the goal.

concepts.name: Objection handling
concepts.summary: Identify likely reader objections about price, trust or effort and answer them with proof, guarantees or FAQs.

concepts.name: Unique value proposition
concepts.summary: Distinguish what makes an offer different from competitors and express it as a clear, specific claim.

concepts.name: Landing page copy architecture
concepts.summary: Arrange hero, benefits, proof, objections and CTA on a landing page so the message flows toward one action.

concepts.name: Tone and voice adaptation
concepts.summary: Adjust tone and formality to fit brand, audience and channel while keeping the message consistent.

concepts.name: Message-match across touchpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse whether an ad, email or link promise is carried through to the destination page, and fix mismatches.

misconceptions.text: Writers should invent the messaging from their own imagination rather than from customers' own words.
Using a framework like AIDA guarantees persuasive copy regardless of the audience.
Mentioning objections in copy plants doubts, so it is better to leave them out.

concepts.name: Copy testing design
concepts.summary: Design and evaluate copy tests with a single variable, a clear metric and enough sample to judge whether a variant truly won.

concepts.name: Psychological levers in persuasion
concepts.summary: Analyse how scarcity, social proof, authority, loss aversion and anchoring work in copy and where they backfire.

concepts.name: Ethical persuasion limits
concepts.summary: Judge whether a claim or urgency device is truthful and legally and ethically defensible, and rewrite it if not.

concepts.name: Funnel-stage copy strategy
concepts.summary: Plan how copy differs across awareness, consideration, purchase and retention stages and how pieces connect.

concepts.name: Email sequence design
concepts.summary: Evaluate and shape multi-email sequences by pacing, purpose per message and segmentation.

concepts.name: Copy critique and editing
concepts.summary: Assess a draft against goal, audience and clarity, and cut or restructure it to raise its effectiveness.

concepts.name: Interpreting performance data
concepts.summary: Read click-through, conversion and engagement metrics to diagnose which part of the copy is failing.

misconceptions.text: A test variant that has a higher conversion rate after a few days has proven it is better.
Fake urgency and scarcity are harmless because they reliably raise conversions.
The same message works at every funnel stage if it is written well enough.

concepts.name: Messaging strategy architecture
concepts.summary: Create a coherent messaging system of positioning, pillars and proof that guides all copy across channels and teams.

concepts.name: Evidence-based optimisation programme
concepts.summary: Design a continuous programme that turns research and test results into prioritised hypotheses and compounding learnings.

concepts.name: Evaluating persuasion trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge when aggressive response tactics harm trust, retention or brand and choose approaches that balance both.

concepts.name: Market sophistication and differentiation
concepts.summary: Assess how saturated a market's claims are and craft angles that stand out when audiences have heard every promise.

concepts.name: Cross-cultural and localised copy
concepts.summary: Evaluate and adapt messaging for different cultures and languages beyond literal translation.

concepts.name: Briefing and directing writers
concepts.summary: Produce briefs and feedback standards that let other writers deliver on-strategy copy and develop a consistent house style.

concepts.name: Original concept and angle creation
concepts.summary: Generate and select original campaign ideas and angles grounded in customer insight that hold across formats.

misconceptions.text: Test results from one page or audience can be applied unchanged to every other context.
Maximising immediate conversion rate is always the right goal for copy.
Translating copy word for word is enough to localise it for a new market.

concepts.name: Disability types and web barriers
concepts.summary: Explain how visual, auditory, motor and cognitive disabilities, whether permanent, temporary or situational, lead to different barriers on web pages.

concepts.name: Assistive technology types
concepts.summary: Recall the main assistive technologies such as screen readers, magnifiers, switch devices and voice control, and what each does.

concepts.name: POUR principles
concepts.summary: Explain the four WCAG principles of Perceivable, Operable, Understandable and Robust with an example of each.

concepts.name: Text alternatives for images
concepts.summary: Understand why images need an alt attribute and what makes alt text useful versus redundant.

concepts.name: Headings and page structure
concepts.summary: Understand how heading levels give a page a navigable outline for screen reader users.

concepts.name: Keyboard-only operation
concepts.summary: Understand that all functionality must be usable with the keyboard alone, using Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys.

concepts.name: Colour contrast basics
concepts.summary: Remember that text needs sufficient contrast with its background and that colour alone should not convey meaning.

misconceptions.text: Accessibility only matters for blind users.
Every image needs a long descriptive alt text.
Accessible pages must be plain, text-only versions of the site.

concepts.name: Semantic landmark elements
concepts.summary: Apply header, nav, main, aside and footer elements so assistive tech users can jump between page regions.

concepts.name: Decorative versus informative images
concepts.summary: Choose between descriptive alt text, empty alt and alternatives for functional images such as linked icons.

concepts.name: Accessible form labels
concepts.summary: Associate every form control with a visible label using label elements and group related controls with fieldset and legend.

concepts.name: Meaningful link text
concepts.summary: Write link text that makes sense out of context instead of phrases like click here.

concepts.name: Visible focus indication
concepts.summary: Keep or restyle the focus indicator so keyboard users can see where they are.

concepts.name: Native interactive elements
concepts.summary: Use button and a elements instead of clickable divs to get keyboard and role behaviour for free.

concepts.name: WCAG contrast ratios
concepts.summary: Check text and UI colours against WCAG ratio thresholds using a contrast tool.

concepts.name: Page language and title
concepts.summary: Understand why lang and a unique descriptive title help screen readers and navigation.

misconceptions.text: A placeholder can replace a visible label.
Removing the focus outline is fine because it looks cleaner.
A div with a click handler is as accessible as a button.

concepts.name: Accessible name computation
concepts.summary: Analyse how browsers derive an element's accessible name from content, labels and ARIA attributes.

concepts.name: ARIA roles and properties
concepts.summary: Apply ARIA roles, states and properties only where native HTML cannot express the semantics.

concepts.name: Focus order and management
concepts.summary: Keep DOM order logical, use tabindex 0 and -1 correctly and move focus programmatically for dialogs and route changes.

concepts.name: Accessible form errors
concepts.summary: Identify errors in text, link them to fields with aria-describedby and announce them to assistive tech.

concepts.name: Live regions for dynamic updates
concepts.summary: Use aria-live regions and status roles to announce content changes without moving focus.

concepts.name: Responsive and zoom support
concepts.summary: Analyse layouts for reflow at 400% zoom, text resizing and touch target size.

concepts.name: Motion and media alternatives
concepts.summary: Provide captions, transcripts and pause controls, and respect reduced-motion preferences.

concepts.name: WCAG conformance levels
concepts.summary: Distinguish levels A, AA and AAA and map success criteria to defects found on a page.

misconceptions.text: Adding ARIA always improves accessibility.
Positive tabindex values are a good way to set tab order.
Colour-only red borders are enough to signal form errors.

concepts.name: Custom widget keyboard patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse and implement expected keyboard interaction and ARIA states for tabs, menus, comboboxes and dialogs.

concepts.name: Manual screen reader testing
concepts.summary: Test flows with screen readers and keyboard, and interpret what announcements reveal about the accessibility tree.

concepts.name: Automated testing limits
concepts.summary: Evaluate what automated checkers can and cannot detect and combine them with manual review.

concepts.name: Accessibility tree inspection
concepts.summary: Use devtools to inspect roles, names and states and diagnose mismatches with the DOM.

concepts.name: Defect severity prioritisation
concepts.summary: Judge defects by user impact, affected journeys and WCAG level to prioritise remediation.

concepts.name: Accessible single-page apps
concepts.summary: Analyse how client-side routing and dynamic rendering break focus, titles and announcements, and fix them.

concepts.name: Cognitive accessibility patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs for consistency, clear instructions, timeouts and error prevention that reduce cognitive load.

misconceptions.text: Passing an automated scan means a page is accessible.
If it works in one screen reader, it works in all of them.
Custom widgets are accessible once they have the right ARIA role.

concepts.name: Accessibility in design systems
concepts.summary: Design reusable components and tokens with built-in accessibility contracts, documentation and tests.

concepts.name: Accessibility process integration
concepts.summary: Build workflows that embed accessibility into requirements, design review, CI checks and release criteria.

concepts.name: Interpreting WCAG ambiguity
concepts.summary: Evaluate borderline cases against the intent of success criteria and justify conformance decisions.

concepts.name: Legal and conformance reporting
concepts.summary: Evaluate conformance evidence and produce accurate reports and statements referencing regulations such as the ADA, Section 508 and the EN 301 549 standard.

concepts.name: Usability testing with disabled users
concepts.summary: Plan and run research with disabled participants and turn findings into design change.

concepts.name: Assistive tech compatibility strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs and define a supported browser and assistive technology matrix, handling inconsistencies and workarounds.

concepts.name: Accessible complex data visualisation
concepts.summary: Create accessible alternatives for charts, maps and canvas content, such as data tables and descriptions.

misconceptions.text: Accessibility is a one-off audit done before launch.
A VPAT or conformance claim proves real-world usability.
A design system's accessible components guarantee accessible pages.

concepts.name: Functions of several variables
concepts.summary: Recognise and evaluate functions of two or three inputs and describe their domain and range.

concepts.name: Graphs and level curves
concepts.summary: Interpret a surface z=f(x,y) and its level curves to read how the function changes.

concepts.name: Vectors in 2D and 3D
concepts.summary: Represent points and displacements as vectors and compute their sums, scalar multiples and lengths.

concepts.name: Dot and cross products
concepts.summary: Explain what the dot product (angle, projection) and cross product (perpendicular vector, area) measure.

concepts.name: Partial derivative meaning
concepts.summary: Explain a partial derivative as the rate of change in one variable while the others are held fixed.

concepts.name: Lines and planes in space
concepts.summary: Describe lines and planes in 3D using parametric and normal-vector equations.

misconceptions.text: A partial derivative with respect to x measures the total change of the function as all variables change.
The cross product of two vectors is a number, like the dot product.
Level curves of a function are the same as its cross-sections by vertical planes.

concepts.name: Computing partial derivatives
concepts.summary: Calculate first and second partial derivatives, including mixed partials, by treating other variables as constants.

concepts.name: Tangent planes and linearisation
concepts.summary: Find the tangent plane to a surface at a point and use it to approximate function values.

concepts.name: Gradient vector
concepts.summary: Compute the gradient and state that it points in the direction of steepest increase and is normal to level curves.

concepts.name: Directional derivatives
aliases: rate of change along a vector
concepts.summary: Compute the rate of change in any unit direction as the dot product of the gradient with that direction.

concepts.name: Multivariable chain rule
concepts.summary: Apply the chain rule to composite functions using tree diagrams to find derivatives with respect to underlying variables.

concepts.name: Iterated double integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate double integrals over rectangles and simple regions as iterated single integrals.

concepts.name: Parametric curves in space
concepts.summary: Describe curves by vector functions r(t) and compute their tangent vectors and arc length.

misconceptions.text: The gradient is a scalar giving the slope of the function.
The directional derivative does not depend on whether the direction vector is a unit vector.
The order of integration in an iterated integral never matters, even over non-rectangular regions, without adjusting the limits.

concepts.name: Optimisation with second-derivative test
concepts.summary: Find critical points and classify them as maxima, minima or saddles using the second-derivative test.

concepts.name: Lagrange multipliers
concepts.summary: Solve constrained extremum problems by setting the gradient of the objective parallel to the gradient of the constraint.

concepts.name: Double integrals over general regions
concepts.summary: Set up limits for non-rectangular regions and choose or reverse the order of integration.

concepts.name: Polar coordinate integration
concepts.summary: Convert a double integral to polar form including the factor r in dA.

concepts.name: Triple integrals
concepts.summary: Set up and evaluate triple integrals for volumes and masses over 3D regions.

concepts.name: Cylindrical and spherical coordinates
concepts.summary: Choose a suitable coordinate system for a region and convert integrals with the correct volume element.

concepts.name: Vector fields and divergence-curl
concepts.summary: Sketch vector fields and compute their divergence and curl.

misconceptions.text: A point where all partial derivatives are zero is always a local maximum or minimum.
Converting to polar coordinates only requires substituting x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ, with dA becoming dr dθ.
In spherical coordinates the volume element is simply dρ dφ dθ.

concepts.name: Change of variables with Jacobians
concepts.summary: Analyse a transformation, compute its Jacobian determinant and use it to rewrite integrals over a simpler region.

concepts.name: Line integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate line integrals of scalar and vector fields along parametrised curves and interpret them as mass or work.

concepts.name: Conservative fields and potentials
concepts.summary: Decide whether a field is conservative, find a potential function and use it to evaluate line integrals.

concepts.name: Green's theorem
concepts.summary: Relate a line integral around a closed plane curve to a double integral and apply it in either direction.

concepts.name: Parametric surfaces and surface area
concepts.summary: Parametrise surfaces and compute normal vectors and area through the cross product of tangent vectors.

concepts.name: Surface integrals and flux
concepts.summary: Evaluate scalar surface integrals and flux of a vector field through oriented surfaces.

concepts.name: Stokes' and divergence theorems
concepts.summary: Apply Stokes' and the divergence theorem, judging when each simplifies a computation and checking orientation and hypotheses.

misconceptions.text: The Jacobian is just the product of the partial derivatives and can be negative in the integral without taking absolute value.
Any vector field with zero curl is conservative on any domain.
Green's theorem applies to any closed curve regardless of orientation or singularities inside the region.

concepts.name: Unifying integral theorems
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the fundamental theorem, Green's, Stokes' and divergence theorems are instances of one boundary-integral principle.

concepts.name: Topology and conservative fields
concepts.summary: Judge how holes in a domain make curl-free fields non-conservative, as with the circulation of the angular field around the origin.

concepts.name: Curvilinear coordinates and scale factors
concepts.summary: Derive gradient, divergence, curl and Laplacian in arbitrary orthogonal coordinates using scale factors.

concepts.name: Conservation laws from theorems
concepts.summary: Derive integral and differential forms of physical laws such as continuity, Gauss's and Faraday's laws from the integral theorems.

concepts.name: Constrained optimisation analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate second-order conditions and inequality constraints for multivariable optimisation and interpret multipliers as sensitivities.

concepts.name: Validity and regularity conditions
concepts.summary: Critique when interchanging integrals, differentiating under the integral, or applying theorems fails due to singularities or lack of smoothness.

concepts.name: Modelling with fields and integrals
concepts.summary: Construct a multivariable model, choose coordinates and theorems, and design an efficient solution for a physical problem.

misconceptions.text: Zero curl on a domain is always enough for path independence, whatever the domain's shape.
The Laplacian and divergence in curvilinear coordinates are found by just replacing x,y,z with the new coordinates in the Cartesian formulas.
Iterated integrals can always be swapped in order if the integrand is defined everywhere.

issues: prf-3 and exp-2 overlap: both cover curl-free versus conservative fields, and the misconception 'zero curl on any domain is conservative' appears at both stages.
Several novice concepts are prerequisite topics, not multivariable calculus: vectors, dot and cross products, lines and planes.
nov-5 depends on nov-2, which is not a real dependency.
Advanced_beginner has 7 concepts, which is fine, but adb-5 depends on adb-7 and the chain rule dependency list lacks nov-3 links. This is minor.
adb-7 (parametric curves) has Bloom C2 and sits inside the band, but nov-4 -> nov-6 is weak: planes need the cross product but lines do not.
cmp-7 divergence and curl is not needed for adb-3 alone; it also needs adb-1. cmp-6 lacks a direct link from cmp-5 and cmp-4, which is present, so no change.

prf-7 needs prf-5 as well as prf-6 and a link to prf-3, since curl-free fields tie to Stokes. exp-5 duplicates cmp-2 and cmp-1 in part (bordered Hessian, multipliers) but is acceptable as deeper analysis.
Misconception in prf-1 is muddled: it merges 'product of partials' with absolute value.
Misconception in adb-6 is garbled ('never matters ... without adjusting the limits').

concepts.name: Functions of several variables
concepts.summary: Recognise and evaluate functions of two or three inputs and describe their domain and range.

concepts.name: Graphs and level curves
concepts.summary: Interpret a surface z=f(x,y) and its level curves to read how the function changes.

concepts.name: Vectors in 2D and 3D
concepts.summary: Represent points and displacements as vectors and compute their sums, scalar multiples and lengths.

concepts.name: Dot and cross products
concepts.summary: Explain what the dot product (angle, projection) and cross product (perpendicular vector, area) measure.

concepts.name: Partial derivative meaning
concepts.summary: Explain a partial derivative as the rate of change in one variable while the others are held fixed.

concepts.name: Lines and planes in space
concepts.summary: Describe lines and planes in 3D using parametric and normal-vector equations.

misconceptions.text: A partial derivative with respect to x measures the total change of the function as all variables change.
The cross product of two vectors is a number, like the dot product.
Level curves of a function are the same as its cross-sections by vertical planes.

concepts.name: Computing partial derivatives
concepts.summary: Calculate first and second partial derivatives, including mixed partials, by treating other variables as constants.

concepts.name: Tangent planes and linearisation
concepts.summary: Find the tangent plane to a surface at a point and use it to approximate function values.

concepts.name: Gradient vector
concepts.summary: Compute the gradient and state that it points in the direction of steepest increase and is normal to level curves.

concepts.name: Directional derivatives
aliases: rate of change along a vector
concepts.summary: Compute the rate of change in any unit direction as the dot product of the gradient with that direction.

concepts.name: Multivariable chain rule
concepts.summary: Apply the chain rule to composite functions using tree diagrams to find derivatives with respect to underlying variables.

concepts.name: Iterated double integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate double integrals over rectangles and simple regions as iterated single integrals.

concepts.name: Parametric curves in space
concepts.summary: Describe curves by vector functions r(t) and compute their tangent vectors and arc length.

misconceptions.text: The gradient is a scalar giving the slope of the function.
The directional derivative does not depend on whether the direction vector is a unit vector.
A double integral can be computed with the order of integration swapped without changing the limits, even over non-rectangular regions.

concepts.name: Optimisation with second-derivative test
concepts.summary: Find critical points and classify them as maxima, minima or saddles using the second-derivative test.

concepts.name: Lagrange multipliers
concepts.summary: Solve constrained extremum problems by setting the gradient of the objective parallel to the gradient of the constraint.

concepts.name: Double integrals over general regions
concepts.summary: Set up limits for non-rectangular regions and choose or reverse the order of integration.

concepts.name: Polar coordinate integration
concepts.summary: Convert a double integral to polar form including the factor r in dA.

concepts.name: Triple integrals
concepts.summary: Set up and evaluate triple integrals for volumes and masses over 3D regions.

concepts.name: Cylindrical and spherical coordinates
concepts.summary: Choose a suitable coordinate system for a region and convert integrals with the correct volume element.

concepts.name: Vector fields and divergence-curl
concepts.summary: Sketch vector fields and compute their divergence and curl.

misconceptions.text: A point where all partial derivatives are zero is always a local maximum or minimum.
Converting to polar coordinates only requires substituting x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ, with dA becoming dr dθ.
In spherical coordinates the volume element is simply dρ dφ dθ.

concepts.name: Change of variables with Jacobians
concepts.summary: Analyse a transformation, compute its Jacobian determinant and use it to rewrite integrals over a simpler region.

concepts.name: Line integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate line integrals of scalar and vector fields along parametrised curves and interpret them as mass or work.

concepts.name: Conservative fields and potentials
concepts.summary: Test whether a field is conservative, find a potential function and use it to evaluate line integrals.

concepts.name: Green's theorem
concepts.summary: Relate a line integral around a closed plane curve to a double integral and apply it in either direction.

concepts.name: Parametric surfaces and surface area
concepts.summary: Parametrise surfaces and compute normal vectors and area through the cross product of tangent vectors.

concepts.name: Surface integrals and flux
concepts.summary: Evaluate scalar surface integrals and flux of a vector field through oriented surfaces.

concepts.name: Stokes' and divergence theorems
concepts.summary: Apply Stokes' and the divergence theorem, judging when each simplifies a computation and checking orientation and hypotheses.

misconceptions.text: The Jacobian factor is just the product of the partial derivatives, with no determinant needed.
A field is conservative whenever the line integral is zero around one particular closed curve.
Green's theorem applies to any closed curve regardless of orientation or singularities inside the region.

concepts.name: Unifying integral theorems
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the fundamental theorem, Green's, Stokes' and divergence theorems are instances of one boundary-integral principle.

concepts.name: Domain topology and closed versus exact fields
concepts.summary: Judge how holes in a domain make curl-free fields non-conservative, as with the circulation of the angular field around the origin.

concepts.name: Curvilinear coordinates and scale factors
concepts.summary: Derive gradient, divergence, curl and Laplacian in arbitrary orthogonal coordinates using scale factors.

concepts.name: Conservation laws from theorems
concepts.summary: Derive integral and differential forms of physical laws such as continuity, Gauss's and Faraday's laws from the integral theorems.

concepts.name: Constrained optimisation analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate second-order conditions and inequality constraints for multivariable optimisation and interpret multipliers as sensitivities.

concepts.name: Validity and regularity conditions
concepts.summary: Critique when interchanging integrals, differentiating under the integral, or applying theorems fails due to singularities or lack of smoothness.

concepts.name: Modelling with fields and integrals
concepts.summary: Construct a multivariable model, choose coordinates and theorems, and design an efficient solution for a physical problem.

misconceptions.text: Zero curl on a domain is always enough for path independence, whatever the domain's shape.
The Laplacian and divergence in curvilinear coordinates are found by just replacing x,y,z with the new coordinates in the Cartesian formulas.
Iterated integrals can always be swapped in order if the integrand is defined everywhere.

concepts.name: Drawing tools and mark types
concepts.summary: Name common drawing tools such as graphite grades, charcoal and erasers, and recall the kinds of marks each makes.

concepts.name: Grip and arm movement
concepts.summary: Explain how holding the pencil in different grips and moving from the shoulder, elbow or wrist changes line quality.

concepts.name: Line quality and pressure
concepts.summary: Understand how pressure and speed create light, dark, thick, thin, smooth or hesitant lines.

concepts.name: Basic shapes as building blocks
concepts.summary: Recognise circles, squares and triangles, and their 3D counterparts of spheres, cubes and cylinders, within everyday objects.

concepts.name: Contour and outline
concepts.summary: Understand that a contour line describes the edge of a shape and where forms turn or overlap.

concepts.name: Light and dark value
concepts.summary: Understand that value is how light or dark an area is, independent of colour, and that it makes forms read.

concepts.name: Seeing versus knowing
concepts.summary: Understand that drawing from observation means recording the actual shapes seen rather than remembered symbols.

misconceptions.text: Drawing is an innate talent that you either have or lack, not a learnable skill.
Erasing every imperfect line is the right way to draw accurately.
Shading means only pressing harder with the pencil.

concepts.name: Gesture and light construction lines
concepts.summary: Use quick, light lines to capture movement and overall placement before committing to final lines.

concepts.name: Measuring proportion by sighting
concepts.summary: Apply a pencil held at arm's length to compare relative lengths and angles of parts of a subject.

concepts.name: Negative space
concepts.summary: Draw the shapes between and around objects to check and correct the positive shapes.

concepts.name: One-point perspective
concepts.summary: Construct simple boxes and interiors with a horizon line and a single vanishing point, so receding lines converge.

concepts.name: Value scale and basic shading
concepts.summary: Produce a smooth range of values and use it to shade a sphere or cube with a light source.

concepts.name: Shading techniques
concepts.summary: Apply hatching, cross-hatching, stippling and smudging to build value for different effects.

concepts.name: Overlap and scale for depth
concepts.summary: Explain and use overlapping, relative size and placement on the page to suggest depth.

misconceptions.text: Measuring with a pencil is cheating and real artists draw purely by eye.
Parallel edges in a box always stay parallel in a drawing regardless of perspective.
Blending with a finger is the best way to make shading look smooth and realistic.

concepts.name: Two-point perspective construction
concepts.summary: Construct objects and buildings seen at an angle using two vanishing points on the horizon.

concepts.name: Ellipses and cylindrical forms
concepts.summary: Draw ellipses with correct minor axes to represent circles on receding planes and build cylindrical objects.

concepts.name: Light logic and cast shadows
concepts.summary: Analyse a light source to place highlight, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow consistently.

concepts.name: Compositional layout and framing
concepts.summary: Plan placement, cropping and focal points using thumbnails so the arrangement supports the subject.

concepts.name: Figure proportion and structure
concepts.summary: Use head-based proportions and simplified skeletal and volumetric forms to construct a standing figure.

concepts.name: Analysing observed relationships
concepts.summary: Analyse a subject for key angles, alignments and relative sizes to find and fix errors in a drawing.

concepts.name: Edge control and texture
concepts.summary: Vary hard, soft and lost edges and marks to describe surfaces such as metal, cloth or hair.

misconceptions.text: Circles viewed in perspective become ellipses with pointed ends.
Shadows can be placed wherever looks good without a consistent light source.
Placing the subject in the centre of the page is always the best composition.

concepts.name: Three-point and curvilinear perspective
concepts.summary: Analyse when vertical convergence or wide-angle distortion applies and construct scenes accordingly.

concepts.name: Atmospheric perspective and value hierarchy
concepts.summary: Analyse how contrast, detail and value range recede with distance and group values to unify a scene.

concepts.name: Complex form and anatomy
concepts.summary: Analyse underlying anatomy, planes and foreshortened forms to draw figures in varied poses convincingly.

concepts.name: Critique of drawing accuracy
concepts.summary: Evaluate a drawing against its reference, diagnosing proportional, tonal and structural errors and prioritising corrections.

concepts.name: Edge hierarchy for focus
concepts.summary: Judge and apply varied edge sharpness and contrast to direct attention to the focal point.

concepts.name: Efficient drawing process
concepts.summary: Evaluate and choose a workflow from large masses to details suited to the subject and time available.

concepts.name: Drawing from complex scenes
concepts.summary: Analyse busy subjects to select, simplify and restructure what to include while keeping believable space.

misconceptions.text: More detail everywhere makes a drawing more realistic.
Anatomy knowledge replaces the need to observe the actual pose.
Distant objects should have the same contrast as near ones as long as they are smaller.

concepts.name: Personal visual language
concepts.summary: Create a consistent approach to line, value and abstraction that expresses an individual intent.

concepts.name: Deliberate departure from realism
concepts.summary: Evaluate when bending proportion, perspective or value serves expression better than accuracy.

concepts.name: Drawing from imagination
concepts.summary: Create believable imagined subjects by combining stored knowledge of structure, light and perspective.

concepts.name: Narrative and mood in drawing
concepts.summary: Design compositions, lighting and gesture that convey a story or atmosphere.

concepts.name: Critical evaluation of drawings
concepts.summary: Evaluate drawings, including one's own and masters', against intent, technique and tradition with reasoned arguments.

concepts.name: Mixed media and surface choice
concepts.summary: Judge how materials and paper interact and combine media to realise an intended result.

concepts.name: Developing and teaching a practice
concepts.summary: Design a sustainable practice of studies, projects and feedback that drives continued growth and can guide others.

misconceptions.text: Developing a style means avoiding fundamentals and copying nothing.
Drawing from imagination can be done well without ever studying from life.
A technically accurate drawing is automatically a successful or expressive one.

concepts.name: Cluster, nodes and control plane
concepts.summary: Explain that a cluster is made of worker nodes running workloads and a control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler, controllers) that manages desired state, with a kubelet on each node.

concepts.name: Pods as smallest unit
concepts.summary: Understand that a pod wraps one or more containers sharing network and storage, and is the unit Kubernetes schedules.

concepts.name: Declarative desired state
concepts.summary: Understand that you declare what you want and controllers continually work to make actual state match it.

concepts.name: YAML manifest structure
concepts.summary: Recognise and read the apiVersion, kind, metadata and spec fields of a Kubernetes manifest.

concepts.name: Basic kubectl commands
concepts.summary: Recall the commands to create, list, inspect and delete objects with kubectl (apply, get, describe, delete).

concepts.name: Labels and selectors
concepts.summary: Understand that labels are key-value tags on objects and selectors use them to group and target objects.

concepts.name: Namespaces for grouping
concepts.summary: Understand that namespaces partition resources within one cluster and that names are unique per namespace.

misconceptions.text: A pod is the same thing as a container and always holds exactly one container.
Kubernetes runs on the nodes only, and the control plane is just an optional dashboard.
Namespaces give strong security isolation between workloads by default.

concepts.name: ReplicaSets and replica counts
concepts.summary: Explain how a ReplicaSet keeps a specified number of matching pods running and replaces failed ones.

concepts.name: Deployments managing pods
concepts.summary: Write and apply a Deployment manifest and scale it, understanding it manages ReplicaSets that manage pods.

concepts.name: Services and ClusterIP
concepts.summary: Create a Service that selects pods by label to give a stable virtual IP and DNS name for reaching them.

concepts.name: Service types NodePort LoadBalancer
concepts.summary: Distinguish ClusterIP, NodePort and LoadBalancer Services and when each exposes a workload.

concepts.name: ConfigMaps for configuration
concepts.summary: Inject non-sensitive configuration into pods as environment variables or mounted files using ConfigMaps.

concepts.name: Secrets for sensitive data
concepts.summary: Create Secrets and consume them in pods via environment variables or volumes.

concepts.name: Logs and exec debugging
concepts.summary: Use kubectl logs, exec, describe and events to diagnose why a pod is failing or pending.

misconceptions.text: Secrets are encrypted, so base64 values in a Secret are safe from anyone who can read them.
You should create bare pods directly for production because Deployments add unnecessary overhead.
A Service's ClusterIP is reachable from outside the cluster.

concepts.name: Rolling update strategy
concepts.summary: Configure and perform rolling updates of a Deployment, tuning maxSurge and maxUnavailable.

concepts.name: Rollout history and rollback
concepts.summary: Monitor rollouts, inspect revision history and roll back a failed release.

concepts.name: Liveness readiness startup probes
concepts.summary: Analyse what each probe type does and choose probes so that restarts and traffic routing behave correctly.

concepts.name: Resource requests and limits
concepts.summary: Set requests and limits and analyse their effect on scheduling, throttling, OOM kills and QoS classes.

concepts.name: Ingress routing
concepts.summary: Define Ingress rules for host and path HTTP routing to Services, requiring an Ingress controller.

concepts.name: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
concepts.summary: Configure an HPA to scale replicas on metrics such as CPU utilisation relative to requests.

concepts.name: Persistent volumes and claims
concepts.summary: Provide durable storage to pods using PersistentVolumeClaims and StorageClasses.

concepts.name: Helm charts and releases
concepts.summary: Install, upgrade and roll back Helm releases and override chart values.

misconceptions.text: A failing readiness probe restarts the container.
HPA scales on actual CPU usage alone, regardless of whether requests are set.
Creating an Ingress resource alone makes traffic flow, with no controller needed.

concepts.name: StatefulSet identity and storage
concepts.summary: Analyse how StatefulSets give pods stable names, ordered rollout and per-pod volumes, and when to choose them over Deployments.

concepts.name: Headless services for stateful apps
concepts.summary: Use headless Services to provide per-pod DNS records for peer discovery in stateful workloads.

concepts.name: Scheduling constraints and affinity
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply selectors, affinity, taints and spread constraints to place pods for availability and isolation.

concepts.name: RBAC and service accounts
concepts.summary: Analyse and design least-privilege access with Roles, bindings and service accounts.

concepts.name: Network policies
concepts.summary: Restrict pod-to-pod traffic with NetworkPolicies, understanding they need a supporting network plugin.

concepts.name: Pod disruption budgets
concepts.summary: Evaluate how PodDisruptionBudgets protect availability during drains and upgrades.

concepts.name: Helm chart templating
concepts.summary: Author and review charts with templates, helpers and values that stay reusable and safe to upgrade.

concepts.name: Systematic troubleshooting workflow
concepts.summary: Diagnose failures such as CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending and failing Services by tracing events, logs, selectors and endpoints.

misconceptions.text: A PodDisruptionBudget prevents involuntary failures such as node crashes.
NetworkPolicies work on any cluster regardless of the network plugin.
StatefulSets make a database highly available and consistent automatically.

concepts.name: Control plane internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how API server, etcd, scheduler and controller manager interact and how their failure modes affect the cluster.

concepts.name: Custom resources and operators
concepts.summary: Design CustomResourceDefinitions and controllers that encode operational knowledge for an application.

concepts.name: Admission control and policy
concepts.summary: Evaluate admission controllers and policy engines to enforce security and governance rules.

concepts.name: Multi-tenancy and cluster design
concepts.summary: Design cluster and namespace topology balancing isolation, quotas, cost and blast radius.

concepts.name: Autoscaling at cluster level
concepts.summary: Evaluate how HPA, VPA and node autoscaling interact and design capacity strategies.

concepts.name: Progressive delivery and GitOps
concepts.summary: Design release pipelines using canary, blue-green and Git-driven reconciliation beyond basic rolling updates.

concepts.name: Upgrades and disaster recovery
concepts.summary: Plan and evaluate cluster upgrade, version skew and backup and restore strategies.

concepts.name: Observability and reliability engineering
concepts.summary: Design monitoring, alerting and capacity practices that make workloads and the platform reliable.

misconceptions.text: Running more replicas always guarantees high availability regardless of scheduling and dependencies.
HPA and VPA can safely scale the same pods on the same metric at the same time.
Operators are only needed for databases and replace the need to understand Kubernetes primitives.

concepts.name: Six tones and tone marks
concepts.summary: Recognise the six tones (ngang, huyền, sắc, hỏi, ngã, nặng), match each to its mark, and understand that tone changes word meaning, as in ma, má, mà, mả, mã, mạ.

concepts.name: Quốc ngữ vowels and đ
concepts.summary: Remember the special letters ă, â, ê, ô, ơ, ư and đ and the sounds they represent, distinct from a, e, o, u, d.

concepts.name: Syllable structure and spelling
concepts.summary: Understand that each written syllable is separated by spaces, is built from an initial, vowel, final and tone, and is pronounced largely as written.

concepts.name: Basic greetings and politeness
concepts.summary: Recall core phrases such as xin chào, cảm ơn, xin lỗi, vâng and không, and use them in simple exchanges.

concepts.name: Core personal pronouns
concepts.summary: Understand that tôi and bạn are neutral, while anh, chị and em signal relative age and gender.

concepts.name: Subject-verb-object word order
concepts.summary: Understand that simple sentences follow subject-verb-object order and that verbs never change form.

concepts.name: Copula là and negation không
concepts.summary: Understand that là links nouns (Tôi là sinh viên) and that không before a verb or adjective negates it.

misconceptions.text: Tone marks are optional accents that can be dropped without changing the meaning.
Vietnamese letters like đ, ơ and ư are just stylistic variants of d, o and u.
Each Vietnamese word is one syllable and there are no multi-syllable words.

concepts.name: Kinship pronouns by age and rank
concepts.summary: Choose anh, chị, em, cô, chú, bác, ông, bà for self and addressee according to relative age, gender and relationship.

concepts.name: Classifiers cái and con
concepts.summary: Use cái for inanimate objects, con for animals and some others, and other classifiers such as người, quyển, chiếc, with numbers and demonstratives.

concepts.name: Tense and aspect particles
concepts.summary: Use đã, đang, sẽ and vừa to express past, ongoing and future events, dropping them when time words make the time clear.

concepts.name: Question words and particles
concepts.summary: Form yes-no questions with có...không and wh-questions with gì, ai, đâu, khi nào, bao nhiêu in the right position.

concepts.name: Numbers and noun phrase order
concepts.summary: Build noun phrases in the order number, classifier, noun, adjective, demonstrative, such as hai con mèo đen này.

concepts.name: Adjectives as predicates
concepts.summary: Understand that adjectives act as verbs without là, as in Cô ấy rất đẹp, and use degree words like rất and quá.

concepts.name: Northern and southern accent differences
concepts.summary: Recognise main differences such as the Hanoi merging of d/gi/r and the southern merging of hỏi and ngã tones and distinct vocabulary.

misconceptions.text: Verbs must take đã, đang or sẽ to show tense, as with English tense endings.
Classifiers are optional decoration and can be left out of counting phrases.
Adjectives need là in front of them, as in Cô ấy là đẹp.

concepts.name: Compound and reduplicative words
concepts.summary: Analyse how compound words and reduplicatives (đẹp đẽ, xinh xắn) are formed and use them to vary tone and register.

concepts.name: Sentence-final and discourse particles
concepts.summary: Distinguish the pragmatic effect of particles like nhé, nhỉ, à, ạ, đâu and mà, and choose them to soften, confirm or emphasise.

concepts.name: Complex sentences and connectors
concepts.summary: Link clauses with vì...nên, nếu...thì, mặc dù...nhưng, để and khi to express cause, condition, concession and purpose.

concepts.name: Passive and adversity constructions
concepts.summary: Contrast bị for adverse and được for beneficial events and recognise when each marks a passive meaning.

concepts.name: Directional and resultative verbs
concepts.summary: Combine main verbs with ra, vào, lên, xuống, về, đi, lại, and with resultative complements like xong and được.

concepts.name: Topic-comment structure and ellipsis
concepts.summary: Analyse how topics are fronted and subjects or pronouns omitted when context makes them clear.

concepts.name: Comparison and degree structures
concepts.summary: Express comparison with hơn, bằng, như, nhất and không bằng, and with degree words such as hơi, khá and quá.

misconceptions.text: Bị and được are interchangeable ways of saying passive with no difference in nuance.
Sentence-final particles carry no meaning and can be freely omitted or swapped.
Every sentence must have an explicit subject, so dropping pronouns is incorrect.

concepts.name: Register and honorific selection
concepts.summary: Judge and adjust pronouns, particles and vocabulary for formality, relationship and situation, and repair mismatches.

concepts.name: Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary
concepts.summary: Analyse how Sino-Vietnamese roots form formal, academic and abstract terms, contrasted with native Vietnamese equivalents.

concepts.name: Dialect vocabulary and tone variation
concepts.summary: Compare northern, central and southern lexicon, tone inventories and final consonant pronunciation and decode them in listening.

concepts.name: Idioms and proverbs
concepts.summary: Interpret common thành ngữ and tục ngữ with their cultural imagery and use them appropriately.

concepts.name: Text cohesion and argumentation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how connectors, pronoun reference and parallelism build coherent essays, reports and arguments.

concepts.name: Pragmatics of indirectness and face
concepts.summary: Evaluate how indirect refusals, hedging and humility reflect social hierarchy and face in conversation.

concepts.name: Loanwords and borrowed terms
concepts.summary: Analyse the sources and adaptation of French and English loanwords and when native or borrowed terms are preferred.

misconceptions.text: Sino-Vietnamese words are Chinese and not really part of Vietnamese.
Using a single polite pronoun pair is enough for formality in every context.
A direct translation of idioms from English keeps the same meaning and tone.

concepts.name: Stylistic choice in literary Vietnamese
concepts.summary: Craft prose or verse that deliberately uses Hán Việt, reduplication, rhythm and parallelism for effect.

concepts.name: Translation and equivalence judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate translations for handling of pronouns, classifiers, tense, register and cultural references and justify alternatives.

concepts.name: Pronoun strategy in narrative voice
concepts.summary: Design address-term systems that convey character relationships, shifts in intimacy and power in narrative or subtitling.

concepts.name: Poetic forms and tonal prosody
concepts.summary: Compose in forms such as lục bát using the bằng-trắc tone patterns and rhyme rules.

concepts.name: Language change and standardisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate the history of quốc ngữ, debates on standard pronunciation and spelling, and emerging usage such as online slang.

concepts.name: Adapting speech across dialect audiences
concepts.summary: Create or adapt spoken and written material for northern, central and southern audiences, choosing lexicon and pronunciation intentionally.

misconceptions.text: A good translation maps each English pronoun to a single fixed Vietnamese pronoun.
Hanoi speech is the only correct Vietnamese and other accents are errors.
Lục bát only requires counting syllables, not tone patterns.

concepts.name: Material classes and their traits
concepts.summary: Recall the four main material classes and the typical properties that distinguish each, such as ductility in metals, hardness and brittleness in ceramics, and low density in polymers.

concepts.name: Bonding types in solids
concepts.summary: Explain how metallic, ionic, covalent and secondary bonds arise and how bond type relates to general properties like conductivity and melting point.

concepts.name: Crystalline versus amorphous structure
concepts.summary: Distinguish ordered crystalline arrangements from amorphous ones and describe how this affects behaviour.

concepts.name: Unit cells and common lattices
concepts.summary: Identify the FCC, BCC and HCP unit cells and state their coordination and atomic packing.

concepts.name: Stress and strain definitions
concepts.summary: Define engineering stress and strain and explain why normalising force and length makes results comparable between specimens.

concepts.name: Elastic versus plastic deformation
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between recoverable and permanent deformation and relate it to atomic bonds stretching versus atoms slipping.

concepts.name: Basic property vocabulary
concepts.summary: Define strength, stiffness, hardness, ductility, toughness and brittleness as distinct properties.

misconceptions.text: Strong materials are automatically tough.
Glass is a slow-flowing liquid at room temperature, which is why old windows are thicker at the bottom.
Stiffness and strength mean the same thing.

concepts.name: Reading stress-strain curves
concepts.summary: Extract Young's modulus, yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation and fracture point from a tensile curve.

concepts.name: Hooke's law and elastic modulus
concepts.summary: Apply E to compute elastic deflection or strain under a given load, including Poisson's ratio effects.

concepts.name: Point defects and dislocations
concepts.summary: Describe vacancies, interstitials, substitutional atoms and dislocations as imperfections that govern properties.

concepts.name: Slip and plastic deformation in metals
concepts.summary: Explain how dislocation motion on slip systems allows metals to deform plastically at stresses far below the theoretical value.

concepts.name: Grain structure and grain boundaries
concepts.summary: Describe polycrystalline microstructure and how grain boundaries impede dislocation motion.

concepts.name: Reading binary phase diagrams
concepts.summary: Identify phases present and their compositions at a given temperature and apply the lever rule to find phase fractions.

concepts.name: Thermal and electrical property basics
concepts.summary: Relate conductivity, thermal expansion and specific heat to bonding and structure across material classes.

misconceptions.text: Yield strength is the stress at which a material breaks.
Metals are strong because their crystals are perfect.
In a phase diagram, the lever rule gives the composition of the phases rather than their relative amounts.

concepts.name: Strengthening mechanisms in metals
concepts.summary: Apply grain refinement, solid solution, strain hardening and precipitation strengthening to raise strength and predict the ductility trade-off.

concepts.name: Eutectic and eutectoid reactions
concepts.summary: Analyse the iron-carbon diagram to predict equilibrium microstructures such as ferrite, pearlite and cementite.

concepts.name: Diffusion and Arrhenius kinetics
concepts.summary: Use Fick's laws and the temperature dependence of diffusion to estimate rates of processes such as carburising.

concepts.name: Heat treatment of steels
concepts.summary: Use TTT and CCT diagrams to analyse how cooling rate yields pearlite, bainite or martensite and how tempering adjusts properties.

concepts.name: Polymer structure and thermal behaviour
concepts.summary: Relate chain length, crosslinking, crystallinity and the glass transition temperature to polymer stiffness and processing.

concepts.name: Ceramic fracture and flaw statistics
concepts.summary: Analyse why ceramics fail in tension from flaws and why strength varies between nominally identical specimens.

concepts.name: Fracture toughness and stress concentration
concepts.summary: Apply stress concentration factors and fracture toughness to judge whether a cracked component will fracture.

concepts.name: Fatigue and creep failure
concepts.summary: Interpret S-N curves and creep curves to analyse failure under cyclic loads and sustained high-temperature loads.

misconceptions.text: Increasing strength always improves a material's performance, with no cost to ductility or toughness.
Quenched steel is simply harder because it is cooled colder, rather than because of the phase formed.
A component loaded below its yield strength will never fail.

concepts.name: Property-based material selection
concepts.summary: Derive performance indices for a function, objective and constraints and use property charts to rank candidates.

concepts.name: Composite micromechanics
concepts.summary: Predict composite stiffness and strength with iso-strain and iso-stress bounds and analyse the roles of fibre length, orientation and interface.

concepts.name: Viscoelasticity in polymers
concepts.summary: Analyse stress relaxation, creep and temperature dependence of polymer response using viscoelastic models.

concepts.name: Corrosion mechanisms and control
concepts.summary: Analyse electrochemical corrosion types and evaluate protection via coatings, cathodic protection, alloying or design.

concepts.name: Electronic and band properties
concepts.summary: Explain conductor, semiconductor and insulator behaviour via band structure and doping and how temperature and impurities change conductivity.

concepts.name: Fatigue life and damage tolerance
concepts.summary: Evaluate fatigue life using crack growth laws and decide inspection intervals or design changes.

concepts.name: Process-structure-property links
concepts.summary: Evaluate how casting, forming, powder processing and additive manufacturing alter microstructure and resulting properties.

misconceptions.text: The best material is the one with the highest value of a single property such as strength.
Composite properties are simply the average of fibre and matrix properties regardless of loading direction.
Corrosion resistant metals such as stainless steel are immune to corrosion in all environments.

concepts.name: Multi-objective material trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing objectives such as cost, mass, sustainability and risk to justify a material choice under uncertainty.

concepts.name: Hybrid and architected materials
concepts.summary: Design hybrids that fill empty regions of property space by combining materials and geometry.

concepts.name: Microstructure design for target properties
concepts.summary: Specify composition, processing route and heat treatment to produce a microstructure that meets a property set.

concepts.name: Failure analysis and forensics
concepts.summary: Diagnose a service failure from fracture surfaces, microstructure and loading history and judge the root cause.

concepts.name: Life-cycle and sustainability assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate materials by embodied energy, emissions, recyclability and end-of-life across the product life cycle.

concepts.name: Extreme environment materials
concepts.summary: Design or select materials for extreme temperature, radiation or aggressive chemical conditions, integrating creep, oxidation and degradation.

concepts.name: Computational and data-driven methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate the reliability of modelling and machine learning predictions of properties and decide how to validate them experimentally.

misconceptions.text: Failure analysis can usually identify one single cause, so design and processing need not be considered together.
Recyclable or bio-based materials are always the more sustainable choice.
Computational predictions can replace experimental validation once a model is calibrated.

concepts.name: Five pure vowel sounds
concepts.summary: Recall and pronounce the five Spanish vowels a, e, i, o, u as consistent, short, unreduced sounds.

concepts.name: Core greetings and farewells
concepts.summary: Recall and use common greetings, farewells and polite formulas such as hola, buenos días, por favor and gracias.

concepts.name: Noun gender and articles
concepts.summary: Understand that nouns are masculine or feminine and match el/la and un/una, using endings -o and -a as a guide.

concepts.name: Plural formation and agreement
concepts.summary: Form plurals with -s or -es and understand that adjectives agree with nouns in gender and number.

concepts.name: Subject pronouns and tú/usted
concepts.summary: Recognise subject pronouns and explain when to use informal tú versus formal usted.

concepts.name: Present tense of ser
concepts.summary: Understand and use present forms of ser to state identity, origin and basic characteristics.

concepts.name: Basic food ordering phrases
concepts.summary: Understand and produce simple phrases for ordering food and drink, such as quisiera, me gustaría and la cuenta, por favor.

misconceptions.text: Spanish vowels change quality depending on stress or position, as in English.
All nouns ending in -a are feminine and all ending in -o are masculine.
Subject pronouns must always be used in every sentence, as in English.

concepts.name: Estar for location and state
concepts.summary: Use estar for location and temporary conditions such as feelings and states.

concepts.name: Ser versus estar contrast
concepts.summary: Choose between ser and estar in common sentences by applying the rules of identity and characteristics versus location and state.

concepts.name: Regular present tense conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the present tense for all persons.

concepts.name: Tener idioms
concepts.summary: Use tener expressions such as tener hambre, sed, frío, miedo and years of age where English uses to be.

concepts.name: Hacer weather expressions
concepts.summary: Use hacer in weather expressions such as hace calor and hace viento and in the verb's basic meaning to do or make.

concepts.name: Rolled r and single r
concepts.summary: Distinguish and produce the single tap r and the trilled rr, noting how it changes meaning in pairs like pero and perro.

concepts.name: Travel and direction phrases
concepts.summary: Apply phrases to ask for directions, buy tickets and book accommodation.

concepts.name: Stem-changing present verbs
concepts.summary: Conjugate common stem-changing verbs such as querer, poder and dormir in the present tense.

misconceptions.text: Ser is for permanent things and estar for temporary ones, with no exceptions.
Tener expressions translate literally as to be, so I am hungry becomes soy hambre.
Stem changes apply to every verb form, including nosotros and vosotros.

concepts.name: Regular preterite formation
concepts.summary: Form and use the preterite of regular verbs to narrate completed past actions.

concepts.name: Irregular preterite verbs
concepts.summary: Apply irregular preterite forms of common verbs such as ir, ser, hacer, tener and estar.

concepts.name: Imperfect tense formation
concepts.summary: Form the imperfect, including the irregular ser, ir and ver, for habitual and ongoing past actions.

concepts.name: Preterite versus imperfect
concepts.summary: Analyse a narrative to decide between completed events and background, habitual or ongoing states.

concepts.name: Object and reflexive pronouns
concepts.summary: Place direct, indirect and reflexive pronouns correctly, including se lo and pronoun attachment.

concepts.name: Gustar-type verbs
concepts.summary: Use gustar-type verbs with indirect objects and agreement with the thing liked.

concepts.name: Por versus para
concepts.summary: Distinguish uses of por and para by analysing purpose, cause, duration and destination.

concepts.name: Latin American and Castilian differences
concepts.summary: Compare major regional features such as vosotros versus ustedes, seseo versus distinción, and vocabulary differences like coche and carro.

misconceptions.text: The preterite is just the simple past and the imperfect is just used to say used to.
Gustar agrees with the person who likes something, so I like apples is me gusto manzanas.
Spanish in Latin America is a simplified or incorrect version of Castilian Spanish.

concepts.name: Present subjunctive formation
concepts.summary: Form the present subjunctive of regular, stem-changing and irregular verbs by analysing the yo-form stem.

concepts.name: Subjunctive with wishes and emotion
concepts.summary: Analyse triggers of volition, emotion, doubt and denial that require subjunctive in subordinate clauses with a change of subject.

concepts.name: Subjunctive in adverbial clauses
concepts.summary: Distinguish when conjunctions like cuando, aunque and antes de que take indicative or subjunctive.

concepts.name: Imperfect subjunctive and si-clauses
concepts.summary: Form the imperfect subjunctive and use it in contrary-to-fact si-clauses with the conditional.

concepts.name: Perfect and compound tenses
concepts.summary: Analyse the use of haber with participles, including regional preference for present perfect versus preterite.

concepts.name: Commands and formal register
concepts.summary: Form affirmative and negative commands for tú, usted and ustedes and choose appropriate register.

concepts.name: Voseo and regional pronoun systems
concepts.summary: Evaluate how voseo, ustedes-for-vosotros and leísmo shape appropriate usage across regions.

misconceptions.text: The subjunctive is a tense that refers to uncertain future time.
Aunque always takes the subjunctive.
Voseo is substandard slang used only by uneducated speakers.

concepts.name: Mood choice as speaker stance
concepts.summary: Evaluate how indicative and subjunctive choices express speaker stance, assertion and presupposition beyond rules.

concepts.name: Register and dialect adaptation
concepts.summary: Adapt vocabulary, pronouns, pronunciation and idioms to suit audience and region in speech and writing.

concepts.name: Pragmatics of politeness and indirection
concepts.summary: Evaluate conditional, imperfect and diminutive strategies for politeness and tone across cultures.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and figurative expression
concepts.summary: Create natural idiomatic phrasing using expressions with tener, hacer, dar and echar, and recognise regional variants.

concepts.name: Discourse cohesion in extended text
concepts.summary: Compose coherent extended texts using connectors, tense sequencing, and clitic and ellipsis choices.

concepts.name: Critiquing usage norms
concepts.summary: Evaluate prescriptive norms from the RAE and ASALE against actual usage and justify choices in context.

misconceptions.text: Native-like Spanish means following one standard variety, usually Castilian.
Mood choice is a mechanical rule following triggers, not a meaningful choice.
Translating English idioms word for word yields natural Spanish.

concepts.name: Goleman's five components
concepts.summary: Recall the five components of Goleman's model: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skills.

concepts.name: Naming basic emotions
concepts.summary: Identify and label core emotions such as anger, fear, sadness, joy and disgust in oneself using accurate words.

concepts.name: Emotions versus thoughts
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between a feeling, a thought about it and a behaviour that follows from it.

concepts.name: Body signals of emotion
concepts.summary: Describe how emotions show up physically, such as a racing heart, tight chest or clenched jaw.

concepts.name: Emotional triggers
concepts.summary: Explain that specific events, words or situations can set off strong emotional reactions.

concepts.name: Basic facial expression cues
concepts.summary: Recognise common facial expressions of emotion in others, such as a smile, frown or wide eyes of fear.

concepts.name: Why emotional awareness matters
concepts.summary: Explain how recognising emotions influences decisions, relationships and wellbeing.

misconceptions.text: Emotional intelligence means being nice or never showing negative emotions.
Emotions are irrational and should be ignored when making decisions.
Other people or events directly make me feel a certain way, so I have no say in it.

concepts.name: Granular emotion vocabulary
concepts.summary: Distinguish related feelings such as frustrated, disappointed and resentful and pick the word that fits a situation.

concepts.name: Mood versus emotion
concepts.summary: Tell short, cause-linked emotions apart from longer, diffuse moods and notice how each colours behaviour.

concepts.name: Tracking triggers and patterns
concepts.summary: Keep a log of situations, feelings and reactions to spot recurring triggers and patterns.

concepts.name: Pause-and-breathe regulation
concepts.summary: Apply simple techniques such as slow breathing, counting or stepping away to calm a strong reaction before acting.

concepts.name: Reading tone and body language
concepts.summary: Use voice tone, posture, gestures and eye contact together with words to guess how someone feels.

concepts.name: Basic empathic listening
concepts.summary: Listen without interrupting and reflect back what another person seems to feel.

concepts.name: Goals and intrinsic motivation
concepts.summary: Distinguish internal motives like interest and purpose from external rewards and set a personal goal around them.

misconceptions.text: Regulating emotions means suppressing them so nobody can tell how I feel.
One facial expression or gesture reliably reveals exactly what a person feels.
Empathy means agreeing with the other person or fixing their problem.

concepts.name: Analysing trigger-response chains
concepts.summary: Break an emotional episode into trigger, interpretation, feeling and action to find where intervention is possible.

concepts.name: Cognitive reappraisal
concepts.summary: Change the meaning given to a situation to alter the emotion it produces.

concepts.name: Choosing regulation strategies
concepts.summary: Match strategies such as reappraisal, distraction, venting or problem solving to the situation and its intensity.

concepts.name: Delaying gratification and persistence
concepts.summary: Sustain effort toward goals through setbacks by managing impulses and discouragement.

concepts.name: Cognitive versus emotional empathy
concepts.summary: Distinguish understanding another's perspective, feeling with them and caring concern, and know when each helps.

concepts.name: Reading group dynamics
concepts.summary: Detect the emotional climate, power relations and unspoken tensions in a group or organisation.

concepts.name: Checking inferences about feelings
concepts.summary: Test guesses about others' emotions by asking open questions instead of assuming.

misconceptions.text: Venting anger fully is always the healthiest way to release it.
Being empathic means taking on other people's emotions and feeling exactly what they feel.
Reframing a situation is just positive thinking or denying the problem.

concepts.name: Emotional blind spots
concepts.summary: Compare self-perception with feedback and behaviour to find gaps between how one thinks one feels and acts and how it appears.

concepts.name: Emotional hijack analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse how intense threat responses override reasoning and design early-warning and recovery plans.

concepts.name: Evaluating motivation sources
concepts.summary: Judge whether a person's drive rests on values and purpose or on fear, status or reward, and the effects on resilience.

concepts.name: Cultural variation in expression
concepts.summary: Evaluate how cultural display rules and context change the meaning of expressions and tone, limiting universal readings.

concepts.name: Detecting mixed and masked emotions
concepts.summary: Interpret conflicts between words, face, voice and context and judge how confident an inference can be.

concepts.name: Emotionally intelligent feedback
concepts.summary: Assess and adapt how to deliver hard messages given the other person's emotional state and the relationship.

concepts.name: Limits and misuse of EI
concepts.summary: Evaluate criticisms of EI measurement and the risk of using emotional insight to manipulate.

misconceptions.text: Microexpressions or body language can reliably reveal when someone is lying.
Facial expressions of emotion are read identically in every culture and context.
High emotional intelligence guarantees success and ethical behaviour.

concepts.name: Critiquing EI models and measures
concepts.summary: Compare Goleman's mixed model with ability models and trait measures and judge their validity and predictive value.

concepts.name: Designing personal EI development plans
concepts.summary: Create a tailored plan with baselines, practice, feedback and measures to build specific EI competencies over time.

concepts.name: Coaching others' emotional skills
concepts.summary: Design coaching approaches that help others build awareness and regulation without dependence or judgement.

concepts.name: Shaping team emotional climate
concepts.summary: Create norms, rituals and structures that build psychological safety and healthy emotional expression in a team.

concepts.name: Integrating EI in leadership decisions
concepts.summary: Evaluate leadership styles and choices by their emotional effects on performance and trust, and adjust to context.

concepts.name: Ethics of emotional influence
concepts.summary: Judge where legitimate emotional influence ends and manipulation or emotional labour harms begin, and set principles for practice.

concepts.name: Synthesising EI with evidence
concepts.summary: Combine findings from psychology and neuroscience with practice to build and test new training or assessment methods.

misconceptions.text: EI is a fixed trait that training cannot meaningfully change.
Goleman's model is settled science with strong, uniform evidence behind every claim about EI and performance.
Leaders should always display warmth and positive emotion, since suppressing or managing display is inauthentic.

concepts.name: Static versus runtime typing
