concepts.summary: Explain that TypeScript checks types at compile time and then erases them, so the emitted JavaScript contains no type information.

concepts.name: Primitive type annotations
concepts.summary: Recall and write annotations for string, number, boolean, null, undefined and arrays on variables and parameters.

concepts.name: Type inference
concepts.summary: Understand how the compiler infers types from initial values so that annotations are not needed everywhere.

concepts.name: Function parameter and return types
concepts.summary: Annotate function parameters and return values and understand the errors raised when calls do not match.

concepts.name: Object type literals
concepts.summary: Describe the shape of an object with property names and types, including optional properties.

concepts.name: Compiling with tsc
concepts.summary: Recall that tsc type-checks .ts files and emits .js files, and read basic compiler error messages.

concepts.name: The any type
concepts.summary: Understand that any switches off type checking for a value and why it undermines safety.

misconceptions.text: TypeScript types are checked while the program runs and protect against bad data at runtime.
Every variable must have an explicit type annotation.
Using any is a harmless way to make errors go away.

concepts.name: Interfaces and type aliases
concepts.summary: Define named object shapes with interface and type, and apply them to parameters and variables.

concepts.name: Union types
concepts.summary: Combine types with | to accept several possible values and handle each case.

concepts.name: Type narrowing
concepts.summary: Use typeof, instanceof, equality and truthiness checks to narrow a union to a specific type within a branch.

concepts.name: Literal types and enums
concepts.summary: Restrict values to specific constants using literal unions or enums and choose between them.

concepts.name: Typed arrays and tuples
concepts.summary: Type arrays and fixed-length tuples and apply them to function arguments and return values.

concepts.name: Optional and readonly properties
concepts.summary: Mark properties optional or readonly and handle possibly undefined values safely.

concepts.name: Typing classes
concepts.summary: Annotate class properties and methods, use public, private and readonly modifiers, and implement interfaces.

concepts.name: Strict null checking
concepts.summary: Handle null and undefined explicitly when strict null checks are enabled.

misconceptions.text: Interfaces and type aliases are completely interchangeable in every situation.
A union type value lets you use any member of any of its types without checks.
The private modifier makes a class member inaccessible at runtime.

concepts.name: Generic functions and constraints
concepts.summary: Write functions with type parameters and constrain them with extends so types flow from input to output.

concepts.name: Generic interfaces and classes
concepts.summary: Define reusable containers and APIs parameterised by type, with defaults where useful.

concepts.name: Discriminated unions
concepts.summary: Model variants with a shared literal tag and use it for exhaustive narrowing, including a never check.

concepts.name: Built-in utility types
concepts.summary: Apply Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record and ReturnType to derive types from existing ones.

concepts.name: keyof and indexed access
concepts.summary: Use keyof, typeof and T[K] to tie property names and value types together safely.

concepts.name: tsconfig compiler options
concepts.summary: Configure target, module, strict and include settings and analyse how each changes checking and output.

concepts.name: Unknown versus any
concepts.summary: Contrast unknown with any and narrow unknown values before use, such as parsed JSON.

concepts.name: Declaration files and modules
concepts.summary: Use .d.ts files and @types packages to type JavaScript libraries and organise code with typed imports and exports.

misconceptions.text: Type assertions with as convert values and make them safe at runtime.
Generics are only needed for collections like arrays.
Turning on strict mode changes the generated JavaScript.

concepts.name: Conditional types and infer
concepts.summary: Write types that branch on type relationships and extract parts of types with infer.

concepts.name: Mapped types
concepts.summary: Transform every property of a type with mapped types, modifiers and key remapping.

concepts.name: Template literal types
concepts.summary: Build string types from unions and patterns to model keys, routes and event names.

concepts.name: Distributive conditional behaviour
concepts.summary: Predict how conditional types distribute over unions and when to prevent it.

concepts.name: Structural typing and variance
concepts.summary: Evaluate assignability using structural rules, and reason about covariance and contravariance in function parameters.

concepts.name: Overloads and type predicates
concepts.summary: Choose between overloads, generics and custom guards to give call sites precise types.

concepts.name: Type-safe API design
concepts.summary: Judge and design function and library signatures that infer well and prevent invalid states.

concepts.name: Project references and build performance
concepts.summary: Structure multi-package repositories with project references and diagnose slow type checking.

misconceptions.text: TypeScript uses nominal typing, so two types with the same shape are incompatible unless one declares the other.
Conditional types always evaluate a union as a whole rather than per member.
More complex types always make code safer and better.

concepts.name: Type-level programming limits
concepts.summary: Evaluate when recursive and computed types are justified given depth limits, compile cost and readability.

concepts.name: Soundness trade-offs
concepts.summary: Assess where TypeScript is deliberately unsound, such as bivariance, array covariance and assertions, and mitigate the risks.

concepts.name: Runtime validation bridging
concepts.summary: Design boundaries that link runtime validation of external data with static types, using schemas and branded types.

concepts.name: Library typing and declaration authoring
concepts.summary: Create declaration files and public type surfaces for libraries, using merging and augmentation and keeping them compatible across releases.

concepts.name: Compiler API and tooling
concepts.summary: Build tools such as analysers or code generators on the compiler and language service APIs.

concepts.name: Migration strategy for codebases
concepts.summary: Plan staged migration of large JavaScript codebases using allowJs, checkJs and tightening strictness over time.

concepts.name: Type design standards and review
concepts.summary: Establish and critique team conventions for type design, strictness and lint rules that balance safety with productivity.

misconceptions.text: If the code compiles with no errors, it is guaranteed free of type-related runtime errors.
The most precise possible type is always the best design for a public API.
A JavaScript codebase must be fully converted in one pass to benefit from TypeScript.

concepts.name: Parts of speech
concepts.summary: Recognise and name nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions and conjunctions and say what job each does.

concepts.name: Subject and predicate
concepts.summary: Explain that a basic sentence has a subject that names who or what and a predicate that says what it does or is.

concepts.name: Complete sentences
concepts.summary: Tell a complete sentence from a fragment by checking for a subject, a finite verb and a complete thought.

concepts.name: Singular and plural nouns
concepts.summary: Form regular and common irregular plurals and understand that number changes the noun's form.

concepts.name: Basic verb tenses
concepts.summary: Understand how simple present, past and future tenses place an action in time.

concepts.name: Capitalisation and end punctuation
aliases: capital letters, full stops, question marks
concepts.summary: Remember to capitalise sentence starts and proper nouns and to end sentences with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.

concepts.name: Subject pronouns and object pronouns
concepts.summary: Understand that pronouns change form depending on whether they act as subject or object.

misconceptions.text: A sentence is complete whenever it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
Every word ending in -s is a plural noun.
A verb is always a word that shows physical action.

concepts.name: Subject-verb agreement
concepts.summary: Make the verb match its subject in number, including with simple compound subjects and words placed between subject and verb.

concepts.name: Commas in lists and clauses
concepts.summary: Use commas in series, after introductory elements and before coordinating conjunctions joining independent clauses.

concepts.name: Apostrophes for possession and contraction
concepts.summary: Apply apostrophes correctly to form possessives and contractions and avoid using them in plurals.

concepts.name: Perfect and progressive tenses
concepts.summary: Choose and form perfect and progressive tenses to show completed, ongoing or repeated actions.

concepts.name: Coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
concepts.summary: Combine simple sentences into compound and complex ones using suitable conjunctions.

concepts.name: Irregular verb forms
concepts.summary: Use the correct past tense and past participle of common irregular verbs.

concepts.name: Adjective and adverb forms
concepts.summary: Choose between adjective and adverb and form comparatives and superlatives correctly.

misconceptions.text: Use an apostrophe whenever a noun is made plural.
A comma can join two independent clauses on its own.
Put a comma wherever you would pause when speaking.

concepts.name: Independent and dependent clauses
concepts.summary: Analyse sentences to identify clause types and how they build simple, compound, complex and compound-complex sentences.

concepts.name: Run-ons and comma splices
concepts.summary: Diagnose run-ons and comma splices and repair them with punctuation, conjunctions or restructuring.

concepts.name: Relative clauses and restrictiveness
concepts.summary: Use relative pronouns and punctuate restrictive and non-restrictive clauses correctly.

concepts.name: Pronoun reference and case
concepts.summary: Analyse pronoun antecedents for clarity and agreement and select correct case, including who and whom.

concepts.name: Parallel structure
concepts.summary: Spot and correct faulty parallelism in lists, comparisons and paired constructions.

concepts.name: Modifier placement
concepts.summary: Identify misplaced and dangling modifiers and revise so the modifier attaches to the intended word.

concepts.name: Semicolons, colons and dashes
concepts.summary: Apply semicolons, colons and dashes according to the grammatical structure they connect.

concepts.name: Active and passive voice
concepts.summary: Analyse when active or passive voice fits the purpose and convert between them.

misconceptions.text: Which and that are always interchangeable in relative clauses.
Whom is just a more formal version of who and can be used anywhere.
The passive voice is always wrong and should be avoided.

concepts.name: Mood and subjunctive
concepts.summary: Analyse how verb mood expresses fact, command or hypothetical and use the subjunctive where standard usage requires it.

concepts.name: Nonfinite verb phrases
concepts.summary: Distinguish infinitives, gerunds and participial phrases and judge their correct use, such as with possessives and verb patterns.

concepts.name: Formal and informal register
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a grammatical form or usage choice suits an audience, medium and purpose.

concepts.name: Contested usage rules
concepts.summary: Evaluate rules such as split infinitives, stranded prepositions and singular they against evidence of actual usage and authority.

concepts.name: Concord with collective and notional subjects
concepts.summary: Resolve agreement with collective nouns, quantifiers, either/or and notional plurals by analysing meaning and form.

concepts.name: Information structure and emphasis
concepts.summary: Judge how word order, clefting and sentence position affect emphasis and clarity.

concepts.name: Variety of English
concepts.summary: Distinguish major differences in grammar, spelling and punctuation between English varieties and keep a consistent choice.

misconceptions.text: Grammar rules are fixed laws, so any usage that breaks a textbook rule is an error.
The subjunctive has disappeared and never applies in modern English.
Formal writing is always more correct than informal writing.

concepts.name: Editing for style and grammar
concepts.summary: Evaluate a text for grammar, usage and clarity and decide which edits improve it without altering the author's voice.

concepts.name: Applying style guides
concepts.summary: Judge between style guides and apply or reconcile their rulings on punctuation and usage for a given publication.

concepts.name: Grammar rule design
concepts.summary: Create clear, evidence-based usage guidance and rules for a defined audience, with justified exceptions.

concepts.name: Diagnosing learner errors
concepts.summary: Evaluate patterns of error to find underlying causes and design targeted explanations or exercises.

concepts.name: Crafting stylistic effect
concepts.summary: Create sentences that use syntax, fragments or rule-bending deliberately for rhythm, tone or rhetorical effect.

concepts.name: Language change and corpus evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate disputed usage using corpus data and the history of how forms change.

misconceptions.text: A single authoritative style guide settles every grammar and usage question.
Skilled writers never break grammar rules.
Editing means correcting every deviation from the rules, whatever the context.

concepts.name: Synchronous versus asynchronous execution
concepts.summary: Explain that synchronous code runs line by line and blocks, while asynchronous work is started now and finishes later without halting other code.

concepts.name: Single-threaded execution model
concepts.summary: Understand that JavaScript runs one piece of code at a time on a single main thread, so long tasks freeze the page.

concepts.name: Callback functions
concepts.summary: Describe a callback as a function passed to another function to be called later, when work completes.

concepts.name: Timers with setTimeout
concepts.summary: Recall how setTimeout and setInterval schedule a function to run after a delay and how clearTimeout cancels it.

concepts.name: Common asynchronous sources
concepts.summary: Recognise typical asynchronous operations such as network requests, timers, file access and user events.

concepts.name: Promise states and meaning
concepts.summary: Explain that a promise represents a future value and is pending, then either fulfilled with a value or rejected with a reason.

misconceptions.text: setTimeout with a delay of 0 runs the function immediately, before the next line of code.
Asynchronous code runs at the same time as other JavaScript code on separate threads.
A line of code after an asynchronous call will wait until that call has finished.

concepts.name: Consuming promises with then and catch
concepts.summary: Use then, catch and finally to handle the result, error and cleanup of a promise.

concepts.name: Promise chaining
concepts.summary: Chain then calls, returning values or promises, so that each step receives the previous step's result.

concepts.name: Async and await syntax
concepts.summary: Write async functions that use await to pause until a promise settles and always return a promise.

concepts.name: Fetching data with fetch
concepts.summary: Request data using fetch and parse the response body with json(), handling its promise-based steps.

concepts.name: Error handling with try/catch
concepts.summary: Wrap awaited calls in try/catch to handle rejections and failed requests.

concepts.name: Callback error-first convention
concepts.summary: Read and write callbacks whose first argument carries an error, and handle it before using the result.

concepts.name: Creating promises with constructor
concepts.summary: Wrap a callback-based operation in new Promise, calling resolve or reject appropriately.

misconceptions.text: fetch rejects its promise when the server responds with an HTTP error such as 404 or 500.
Using await makes the whole program stop and wait, blocking the main thread.
A then handler's return value is ignored, so there is no need to return a promise inside a chain.

concepts.name: Event loop, call stack and queues
concepts.summary: Analyse how the call stack, Web APIs and task queue interact to decide when callbacks run.

concepts.name: Microtasks versus macrotasks
concepts.summary: Predict the output order of code mixing promise callbacks, timers and synchronous statements.

concepts.name: Parallel execution with Promise.all
concepts.summary: Start independent tasks together and await them with Promise.all, understanding its fail-fast behaviour.

concepts.name: Promise combinators
concepts.summary: Choose among all, allSettled, race and any based on how results and failures should be combined.

concepts.name: Sequential versus parallel awaiting
concepts.summary: Analyse when awaiting in a loop serialises work needlessly and restructure it for appropriate concurrency.

concepts.name: Error propagation through chains
concepts.summary: Trace how errors and rejections travel through chains and async functions and where they must be caught.

concepts.name: Cancellation with AbortController
concepts.summary: Cancel fetch requests and implement timeouts using an AbortController signal.

misconceptions.text: Promise.all runs the promises in parallel on multiple threads.
A setTimeout callback with zero delay runs before an already resolved promise's then callback.
Promise.all waits for every promise and returns partial results even if one rejects.

concepts.name: Concurrency limiting and pooling
concepts.summary: Evaluate and implement limits on simultaneous asynchronous tasks to avoid overloading servers or resources.

concepts.name: Retry with backoff
concepts.summary: Judge which failures merit retries and design retry strategies with delays and caps.

concepts.name: Race conditions in async code
concepts.summary: Identify how interleaved async operations produce out-of-order results or shared-state bugs and guard against them.

concepts.name: Async iteration and generators
concepts.summary: Consume and produce sequences of asynchronous values using for await...of and async generators.

concepts.name: Unhandled rejection diagnosis
concepts.summary: Find forgotten awaits and uncaught rejections and decide on global handling and logging.

concepts.name: Blocking the event loop
concepts.summary: Evaluate CPU-heavy work that starves the loop and choose chunking or Web Workers to offload it.

concepts.name: Debounce and async caching
concepts.summary: Choose debouncing, caching of in-flight promises and deduplication to reduce redundant async work.

misconceptions.text: Web Workers share variables with the main thread, so offloaded work needs no message passing.
Since JavaScript is single-threaded, race conditions cannot occur.
Retrying every failed request immediately is always the safest way to be resilient.

concepts.name: Designing async architecture
concepts.summary: Design module and API boundaries that expose cancellation, errors, progress and concurrency control consistently.

concepts.name: Evaluating async abstractions
concepts.summary: Compare promises, callbacks, event emitters, observables and streams and justify the right fit for a problem.

concepts.name: Building promise utilities
concepts.summary: Implement utilities such as a promise polyfill, task queue or limiter that obey the Promises/A+ semantics.

concepts.name: Structured concurrency patterns
concepts.summary: Create patterns where child async tasks are scoped, cancelled and cleaned up together with their parent.

concepts.name: Runtime differences in scheduling
concepts.summary: Evaluate how browser and Node.js scheduling differ and how that affects ordering and performance.

concepts.name: Testing and observability of async code
concepts.summary: Assess strategies for deterministic async tests, fake timers, tracing and diagnosing flaky timing issues.

concepts.name: Streaming and backpressure
concepts.summary: Evaluate how streaming data with backpressure controls memory and throughput compared with buffering whole results.

misconceptions.text: Promises are always the best abstraction, so streams and observables add nothing for repeated or large data.
Event loop ordering is identical in browsers and Node.js, so scheduling code is portable.
Adding timeouts and retries at every layer of a system makes it more reliable.

concepts.name: Variables and algebraic expressions
concepts.summary: Understand that a letter stands for a number and that an expression combines numbers, variables and operations.

concepts.name: Order of operations
concepts.summary: Evaluate expressions by applying operations in the agreed order, including parentheses and exponents.

concepts.name: Evaluating expressions by substitution
concepts.summary: Replace variables with given numbers and compute the value correctly.

concepts.name: Like terms
concepts.summary: Recognise which terms share the same variable part and can be combined.

concepts.name: Equation as balance
concepts.summary: Understand that an equation states two quantities are equal and that a solution is a value making it true.

concepts.name: Inverse operations
concepts.summary: Know that addition undoes subtraction and multiplication undoes division, and use this to isolate a variable.

misconceptions.text: The equals sign means 'compute the answer' rather than 'both sides have the same value'.
A variable such as x always stands for one fixed number, or a letter's value depends on its position in the alphabet.
Terms like 3x and 3x² are like terms and can be added to give 6x².

concepts.name: Simplifying by combining like terms
concepts.summary: Simplify expressions with several terms, handling signs correctly.

concepts.name: Distributive property
concepts.summary: Multiply a factor across a sum or difference, including negative factors, and simplify the result.

concepts.name: Solving one-variable linear equations
concepts.summary: Solve linear equations with variables on one or both sides, using distribution and inverse operations.

concepts.name: Laws of exponents
concepts.summary: Apply product, quotient, power rules and zero and negative exponents to simplify expressions.

concepts.name: Linear inequalities
concepts.summary: Solve and graph inequalities, reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

concepts.name: Translating words to equations
concepts.summary: Define a variable and write and solve an equation for a simple verbal situation.

concepts.name: Solving formulas for a variable
concepts.summary: Rearrange a formula to isolate a chosen variable.

misconceptions.text: In 3(x + 4) only the first term is multiplied, giving 3x + 4.
The inequality sign never changes direction when dividing by a negative number.
Powers multiply when multiplying like bases, so x² · x³ = x⁶.

concepts.name: Factoring polynomials
concepts.summary: Factor out common factors, difference of squares and quadratic trinomials.

concepts.name: Multiplying polynomials
concepts.summary: Expand products of binomials and polynomials and recognise special products.

concepts.name: Solving quadratics by factoring
concepts.summary: Use the zero product property to find roots of quadratics written in factorable form.

concepts.name: Radicals and rational exponents
concepts.summary: Simplify radicals, rationalise denominators and convert between radical and fractional exponent forms.

concepts.name: Systems of linear equations
concepts.summary: Solve two-variable systems by substitution and elimination and interpret the result graphically.

concepts.name: Absolute value equations and inequalities
concepts.summary: Split absolute value statements into cases and express solutions correctly.

concepts.name: Modelling multi-step word problems
concepts.summary: Choose variables and set up equations or systems for rate, mixture and geometry situations, then check answers.

misconceptions.text: (x + 3)² equals x² + 9.
If (x − 2)(x − 3) = 6, then x − 2 = 6 or x − 3 = 6 can be set separately.
√(a + b) equals √a + √b.

concepts.name: Completing the square
concepts.summary: Rewrite a quadratic as a perfect square plus a constant and use it to solve and to find the vertex.

concepts.name: Quadratic formula derivation and use
concepts.summary: Understand how the formula follows from completing the square and apply it to any quadratic.

concepts.name: Discriminant and nature of roots
concepts.summary: Analyse the number and type of real or complex roots from the discriminant.

concepts.name: Choosing a solution method
concepts.summary: Judge whether factoring, square roots, completing the square or the formula is most efficient for a given quadratic.

concepts.name: Extraneous solutions
concepts.summary: Detect and justify rejecting invalid solutions in radical, rational and absolute value equations.

concepts.name: Rational expressions and equations
concepts.summary: Simplify, combine and solve equations with polynomial fractions, noting excluded values.

concepts.name: Systems with nonlinear equations
concepts.summary: Solve systems mixing linear and quadratic equations and interpret solutions as intersections.

misconceptions.text: Every solution found by algebraic manipulation is automatically valid in the original equation.
Cancelling any matching terms in the numerator and denominator of a fraction is allowed, such as (x + 2)/2 = x.
A negative discriminant means the quadratic has no solutions at all.

concepts.name: Structure and equivalence of expressions
concepts.summary: Judge which equivalent form of an expression best reveals a property such as roots, extrema or growth.

concepts.name: Proof by algebraic argument
concepts.summary: Construct algebraic proofs of general claims, such as properties of integers or identities.

concepts.name: Evaluating solution validity and generality
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether each manipulation is reversible and whether a solution set is complete, with no lost or added solutions.

concepts.name: Parametric and symbolic families
concepts.summary: Analyse equations with parameters and judge how solutions change across cases.

concepts.name: Designing models from context
concepts.summary: Create algebraic models for unfamiliar situations, justifying assumptions and variables and critiquing the model.

concepts.name: Relationships between roots and coefficients
concepts.summary: Use sum and product of roots to evaluate and construct quadratics without solving them.

concepts.name: Constructing problems and teaching methods
concepts.summary: Create original problems and counterexamples that target specific algebraic ideas and reveal errors.

misconceptions.text: Showing that an identity works for several numerical examples proves it holds in general.
Squaring both sides or dividing by an expression is always a safe, reversible step.
An equation with a parameter has the same solution structure for all parameter values.

issues: Flagged thin misconceptions are real, common errors stated as wrong beliefs and tied to the right concepts; the flags are harmless.
Minor: nov-4 'Like terms' is C1 and adb-1 repeats it only at the application level, which is acceptable.
Stages, Bloom levels, prerequisites and concept names are sound; no cycles or forward references.

concepts.name: Concurrency versus parallelism
concepts.summary: Explain that concurrency is structuring work as overlapping tasks while parallelism is literally executing tasks at the same instant on multiple cores.

concepts.name: Threads and processes
concepts.summary: Describe a process as an isolated program instance with its own memory and a thread as an execution path sharing its process's memory.

concepts.name: Shared mutable state
concepts.summary: Recognise that data accessible and modifiable by several threads is the root of most concurrency bugs.

concepts.name: Nondeterministic interleaving
concepts.summary: Understand that the scheduler may interleave instructions of different threads in varying orders, so results can differ between runs.

concepts.name: Race condition
concepts.summary: Explain that a race condition occurs when the outcome depends on the timing of unsynchronised accesses to shared data.

concepts.name: Starting and joining threads
concepts.summary: Recall that threads are started to run a function and joined to wait for their completion.

misconceptions.text: Concurrent programs always run faster than sequential ones.
If a program gave the right answer once, it has no race condition.
Threads in the same program each have their own separate copy of all variables.

concepts.name: Critical sections and mutual exclusion
concepts.summary: Identify code that touches shared data and protect it so only one thread executes it at a time.

concepts.name: Locks and mutexes
concepts.summary: Use a lock to guard shared data, acquiring before access and always releasing afterwards, including on error paths.

concepts.name: Atomic operations
concepts.summary: Understand that an atomic operation completes indivisibly and why a plain increment is not atomic.

concepts.name: Deadlock
concepts.summary: Describe how threads each holding a lock the other needs wait forever.

concepts.name: Thread-safe code
concepts.summary: Judge and make simple functions and data structures safe to call from multiple threads.

concepts.name: Thread pools and tasks
concepts.summary: Submit units of work to a fixed pool of workers instead of creating a thread per task.

concepts.name: Producer-consumer queues
concepts.summary: Pass work between threads through a thread-safe queue rather than sharing raw variables.

misconceptions.text: Locking every method of a class automatically makes any use of it correct.
A single statement like counter++ is atomic.
Deadlock only happens when many threads are involved.

concepts.name: Coffman deadlock conditions
concepts.summary: Analyse a deadlock by identifying mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait.

concepts.name: Lock ordering and avoidance
concepts.summary: Prevent deadlocks by imposing a global lock order, shrinking lock scope or using try-lock with timeouts.

concepts.name: Condition variables and signalling
concepts.summary: Coordinate threads waiting for a state change using condition variables, rechecking predicates in a loop.

concepts.name: Semaphores and barriers
concepts.summary: Choose semaphores, latches or barriers to limit access or synchronise phases of work.

concepts.name: Memory visibility and ordering
concepts.summary: Analyse why one thread may not see another's writes without synchronisation and how happens-before guarantees fix this.

concepts.name: Starvation and livelock
concepts.summary: Distinguish deadlock from starvation and livelock and diagnose each from symptoms.

concepts.name: Immutability and confinement
concepts.summary: Avoid locking by sharing only immutable data or keeping mutable data owned by one thread.

concepts.name: Futures and async results
concepts.summary: Represent a pending result with a future and compose or await it without blocking unnecessarily.

misconceptions.text: A condition variable wait can use an if check because wakeups always mean the condition holds.
Without a lock, a write by one thread becomes visible to others immediately.
Using volatile or similar flags makes compound operations thread-safe.

concepts.name: Event loops and async/await
concepts.summary: Analyse how an event loop interleaves non-blocking tasks on one thread and where blocking calls stall it.

concepts.name: Actor and message-passing models
concepts.summary: Evaluate message passing with actors or channels against shared-memory locking for a given problem.

concepts.name: Lock-free and wait-free techniques
concepts.summary: Analyse compare-and-swap based structures, including the ABA problem and the trade-offs against locks.

concepts.name: Lock contention and granularity
concepts.summary: Evaluate coarse, fine-grained and read-write locking choices by their contention and complexity costs.

concepts.name: Scalability limits
concepts.summary: Use Amdahl's law and overhead analysis to judge how much parallelism will actually speed a workload.

concepts.name: Backpressure and cancellation
concepts.summary: Design pipelines that bound queues, propagate cancellation and clean up resources when tasks fail.

concepts.name: CPU-bound versus I/O-bound workloads
concepts.summary: Classify workloads and match them to threads, processes or async I/O accordingly.

concepts.name: Cache effects and false sharing
concepts.summary: Analyse how cache-line sharing between cores degrades parallel performance.

misconceptions.text: Async/await code runs in parallel on multiple cores by default.
Lock-free algorithms are always faster than lock-based ones.
Adding more threads always improves throughput until cores run out.

concepts.name: Formal concurrency correctness
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs against safety and liveness properties and linearizability using invariants and formal reasoning.

concepts.name: Hardware memory models
concepts.summary: Judge when acquire-release or relaxed atomics are valid given language and hardware reordering rules.

concepts.name: Concurrent data structure design
concepts.summary: Create concurrent data structures balancing correctness, progress guarantees and scalability, including safe memory reclamation.

concepts.name: Systematic concurrency testing
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply race detectors, stress tests, deterministic schedulers and model checking to find rare interleavings.

concepts.name: Concurrency architecture selection
concepts.summary: Design a system-level concurrency architecture combining threads, async, actors and processes to meet latency and throughput goals.

concepts.name: Distributed concurrency hazards
concepts.summary: Assess how partial failure, unreliable clocks and message reordering change local concurrency assumptions across machines.

concepts.name: Production concurrency diagnosis
concepts.summary: Diagnose live hangs, tail latency and contention using thread dumps, profilers and tracing, and judge the fix.

misconceptions.text: Passing a large number of stress-test runs proves a concurrent program is correct.
On modern hardware, sequential consistency can be assumed for ordinary memory accesses.
Distributed locks behave like local mutexes and give the same guarantees.

concepts.name: Vectors as arrows and lists
concepts.summary: Recognise a vector as both a geometric arrow and an ordered list of numbers, and read its components.

concepts.name: Vector addition and scaling
concepts.summary: Add vectors componentwise and multiply by scalars, and explain what each does geometrically.

concepts.name: Linear combinations
concepts.summary: Form and interpret sums of scaled vectors as new vectors reachable from given ones.

concepts.name: Matrices as rectangular arrays
concepts.summary: Identify matrix size, rows, columns and entries, and recognise special forms such as identity, zero and diagonal.

concepts.name: Systems of linear equations
concepts.summary: Write a system of equations in matrix form Ax = b and explain what a solution means.

concepts.name: Matrix-vector product
concepts.summary: Compute Ax as a linear combination of the columns of A and as row-wise dot products.

misconceptions.text: A vector is only an arrow and cannot be described by a list of numbers, or vice versa.
A matrix times a vector is computed by multiplying corresponding entries one by one.
A system of linear equations always has exactly one solution.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.summary: Apply elementary row operations to reduce an augmented matrix to echelon or reduced echelon form and solve the system.

concepts.name: Solution set types
concepts.summary: Use pivots and free variables to decide whether a system has no, one or infinitely many solutions and describe them parametrically.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.summary: Multiply compatible matrices, check dimensions, and know that the product is generally not commutative.

concepts.name: Transpose and special matrices
concepts.summary: Compute transposes and recognise symmetric, triangular and diagonal matrices and the rule (AB)^T = B^T A^T.

concepts.name: Matrix inverse
concepts.summary: Find the inverse of a square matrix by row reducing [A | I] and use it to solve Ax = b.

concepts.name: Dot product and length
concepts.summary: Compute dot products, vector lengths and angles, and test whether two vectors are perpendicular.

concepts.name: Linear transformations as matrices
concepts.summary: Describe how a matrix rotates, scales, reflects or shears the plane and read the matrix from the images of basis vectors.

misconceptions.text: Matrix multiplication is commutative, so AB = BA.
Every square matrix has an inverse.
The inverse of a matrix is found by taking the reciprocal of each entry.

concepts.name: Linear independence
concepts.summary: Test whether vectors are independent by checking whether Ax = 0 has only the trivial solution.

concepts.name: Span and subspaces
concepts.summary: Determine the span of a set of vectors and verify whether a set is a subspace by closure under addition and scaling.

concepts.name: Basis and dimension
concepts.summary: Identify a basis of a subspace, find its dimension and express vectors in coordinates relative to it.

concepts.name: Null space and column space
concepts.summary: Compute bases for the null space and column space of a matrix and interpret them in terms of solutions and outputs.

concepts.name: Rank and rank-nullity
concepts.summary: Use rank + nullity = number of columns to analyse solvability and invertibility of a matrix.

concepts.name: Determinants
concepts.summary: Compute determinants by cofactor expansion or row reduction and interpret them as signed volume scaling and an invertibility test.

concepts.name: Orthogonality and projections
concepts.summary: Project a vector onto a line or subspace and relate orthogonal complements to row space and null space.

misconceptions.text: Any set of vectors that spans a space is a basis for it.
The column space of the row-reduced matrix is the same as the column space of the original matrix.
The determinant of A + B equals det A + det B.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
concepts.summary: Find eigenvalues from det(A - λI) = 0, compute eigenspaces, and interpret them as directions preserved by a transformation.

concepts.name: Diagonalization
concepts.summary: Decide when a matrix is diagonalizable and use A = PDP^-1 to compute powers and understand dynamics.

concepts.name: Algebraic versus geometric multiplicity
concepts.summary: Compare multiplicities of an eigenvalue to diagnose defective matrices that cannot be diagonalized.

concepts.name: Gram-Schmidt and QR
concepts.summary: Build an orthonormal basis from independent vectors and use QR factorization to organise the result.

concepts.name: Least squares
concepts.summary: Solve inconsistent systems by projecting b onto the column space via A^T A x = A^T b and judge the fit.

concepts.name: Spectral theorem for symmetric matrices
concepts.summary: Explain why symmetric real matrices have real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors and use A = QΛQ^T.

concepts.name: Change of basis
concepts.summary: Represent a linear map in different bases and recognise that similar matrices share eigenvalues, trace and determinant.

misconceptions.text: Every square matrix is diagonalizable.
Matrices with the same eigenvalues are always similar.
Eigenvalues of a real matrix are always real numbers.

concepts.name: Singular value decomposition
concepts.summary: Derive and interpret A = UΣV^T for any matrix, linking singular values to A^T A and to the geometry of the map.

concepts.name: Low-rank approximation
concepts.summary: Evaluate truncated SVD as the optimal rank-k approximation and judge truncation levels for compression or denoising.

concepts.name: Pseudoinverse
concepts.summary: Construct the pseudoinverse from the SVD and use it to give minimum-norm least-squares solutions for any system.

concepts.name: Conditioning and numerical stability
concepts.summary: Assess how the condition number governs error amplification and choose stable algorithms such as QR or SVD over normal equations.

concepts.name: Jordan form and generalized eigenvectors
concepts.summary: Analyse defective matrices through Jordan blocks and explain their effect on matrix powers and exponentials.

concepts.name: Positive definite matrices
concepts.summary: Characterise definiteness through eigenvalues, pivots and quadratic forms, and connect it to optimisation and Cholesky factorization.

concepts.name: Modelling with spectral methods
concepts.summary: Design spectral models such as PCA or Markov steady states, choosing the decomposition that suits the problem.

misconceptions.text: Singular values are just the absolute values of the eigenvalues of A.
A small determinant means a matrix is ill-conditioned.
Solving least squares through the normal equations is always as accurate as using QR or SVD.

concepts.name: Response and predictor variables
concepts.summary: Identify which variable is being explained (response) and which are used to explain it (predictors) in a given question.

concepts.name: Scatterplot and association
concepts.summary: Read a scatterplot to describe direction, form and strength of the relationship between two quantitative variables.

concepts.name: Correlation coefficient
concepts.summary: Explain what r measures, its range from -1 to 1, and that it captures only linear association.

concepts.name: Line of best fit
concepts.summary: Understand that a straight line summarises how the response changes on average with the predictor.

concepts.name: Slope and intercept meaning
concepts.summary: Interpret the slope as the average change in response per one-unit increase in predictor and the intercept as the predicted value at zero.

concepts.name: Predicted values and residuals
concepts.summary: Describe a prediction as a point on the line and a residual as the observed value minus the predicted value.

misconceptions.text: A strong correlation proves that changes in the predictor cause changes in the response.
A correlation near zero means the two variables are unrelated.
The intercept always has a meaningful real-world interpretation.

concepts.name: Least squares estimation
concepts.summary: Explain that the fitted line minimises the sum of squared residuals and compute slope and intercept from summary statistics.

concepts.name: Making predictions from a fit
concepts.summary: Use a fitted equation to predict the response for new predictor values and avoid extrapolating beyond the data range.

concepts.name: Coefficient of determination
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret R² as the proportion of response variability explained by the model.

concepts.name: Residual plots
concepts.summary: Plot residuals against fitted values and spot curvature or changing spread that signals a poor linear fit.

concepts.name: Multiple regression with categorical predictors
concepts.summary: Encode a categorical predictor as indicator variables and interpret its coefficient relative to the reference group.

concepts.name: Outliers and influential points
concepts.summary: Recognise how an extreme point can pull the fitted line and check its effect by refitting without it.

misconceptions.text: A high R² means the model is correct and its predictions are reliable.
The regression line can safely be used to predict at any predictor value.
Outliers should always be deleted because they are errors.

concepts.name: Multiple linear regression model
concepts.summary: Fit a model with several predictors and interpret each coefficient as the effect holding the other predictors fixed.

concepts.name: Inference on coefficients
concepts.summary: Use standard errors, t-tests and confidence intervals to judge whether a coefficient differs from zero and how precisely it is estimated.

concepts.name: Overall F-test and adjusted R²
concepts.summary: Test whether the predictors jointly explain the response and compare models of different size using adjusted R².

concepts.name: Linear model assumptions diagnostics
concepts.summary: Assess linearity, independence, constant variance and normality of errors using residual plots and Q-Q plots.

concepts.name: Interaction terms
concepts.summary: Include and interpret an interaction so that the effect of one predictor depends on the level of another.

concepts.name: Multicollinearity
concepts.summary: Detect correlated predictors with VIF and explain how they inflate standard errors and destabilise coefficients.

concepts.name: Logistic regression and odds
concepts.summary: Model a binary outcome with the logit link and interpret exponentiated coefficients as odds ratios.

concepts.name: Transforming variables
concepts.summary: Apply log or polynomial transformations to fix nonlinearity or skew and interpret the resulting coefficients.

misconceptions.text: The response variable itself must be normally distributed for linear regression to be valid.
A non-significant coefficient proves that the predictor has no effect.
An odds ratio of 2 means the probability of the outcome doubles.

concepts.name: Model selection criteria
concepts.summary: Compare candidate models using AIC, BIC and subject knowledge and justify the choice while recognising selection bias.

concepts.name: Cross-validation for prediction
concepts.summary: Estimate predictive error on held-out data to judge generalisation and detect overfitting.

concepts.name: Regularisation methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how ridge and lasso penalties trade bias for variance and when each helps with many or correlated predictors.

concepts.name: Influence diagnostics
concepts.summary: Use leverage, studentised residuals and Cook's distance to separate outliers from points that change conclusions.

concepts.name: Heteroscedasticity and robust errors
concepts.summary: Diagnose non-constant variance and choose between transformation, weighting or robust standard errors.

concepts.name: Logistic model evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a logistic model through discrimination, calibration and threshold-dependent metrics suited to the problem.

concepts.name: Generalised linear models
concepts.summary: Relate response distribution, link function and linear predictor to select models for counts, proportions and binary data.

concepts.name: Confounding and causal interpretation
concepts.summary: Judge when adjusted coefficients can be read causally and how omitted variables or colliders bias estimates.

misconceptions.text: Stepwise selection reliably finds the true set of predictors and its p-values remain valid.
Accuracy on the training data shows how well the model will predict new data.
Controlling for more variables always moves the estimate closer to the causal effect.

concepts.name: Bias-variance trade-off in modelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate how model complexity, sample size and regularisation shape error, and choose a strategy accordingly.

concepts.name: Hierarchical and mixed models
concepts.summary: Design models with random effects for clustered or repeated data and justify partial pooling over ignoring the structure.

concepts.name: Bayesian regression
concepts.summary: Specify priors, interpret posterior and predictive distributions and assess sensitivity to prior choices.

concepts.name: Flexible nonlinear regression
concepts.summary: Build models with splines or additive terms to capture nonlinear effects while controlling smoothness.

concepts.name: Causal inference with regression
concepts.summary: Design analyses using DAGs, instruments or quasi-experimental designs and defend the identifying assumptions.

concepts.name: Missing data and measurement error
concepts.summary: Assess how missingness mechanisms and noisy predictors bias estimates and select appropriate corrections.

concepts.name: Time series and dependent errors
concepts.summary: Detect serial or spatial correlation in residuals and apply generalised least squares or other models that handle it.

concepts.name: Reproducible modelling workflow
concepts.summary: Create an end-to-end analysis plan covering pre-specification, validation, uncertainty reporting and communication of limitations.

misconceptions.text: Mixed models are only a fancier way to get smaller p-values and can be replaced by adding group dummies without consequence.
Multiple imputation or complete-case analysis gives unbiased results regardless of why data are missing.
A flexible model with enough terms to fit the data closely is the best choice for inference.

concepts.name: Nucleotide and DNA structure
concepts.summary: Recall that DNA is an antiparallel double helix of nucleotides (sugar, phosphate, base) paired A-T and G-C by hydrogen bonds.

concepts.name: Central dogma flow
concepts.summary: Explain that genetic information is copied from DNA to RNA by transcription and read by ribosomes to make protein by translation.

concepts.name: Semiconservative replication
concepts.summary: Describe how each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one newly made strand, each parental strand serving as a template.

concepts.name: RNA types and differences
concepts.summary: Distinguish RNA from DNA (ribose, uracil, usually single-stranded) and name the roles of mRNA, tRNA and rRNA.

concepts.name: Codons and genetic code
concepts.summary: Explain that three-base codons specify amino acids, that the code is redundant and nearly universal, and that AUG starts and stop codons end translation.

concepts.name: Purpose of molecular techniques
concepts.summary: Recall what PCR, gel electrophoresis, restriction enzymes and sequencing are used for in general terms.

misconceptions.text: Each new DNA double helix is made entirely of new strands, or the old DNA is kept intact and a fully new copy is made.
Proteins are made directly from DNA in the nucleus without an RNA intermediate.
Each amino acid is specified by exactly one codon.

concepts.name: Replication enzymes and roles
concepts.summary: Explain what helicase, primase, DNA polymerase, topoisomerase and ligase each do at the replication fork.

concepts.name: Leading and lagging strands
concepts.summary: Apply the 5'→3' synthesis rule to predict which strand is made continuously and which as Okazaki fragments.

concepts.name: Transcription stages
concepts.summary: Describe how RNA polymerase binds a promoter, synthesizes RNA from the template strand and terminates.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic mRNA processing
concepts.summary: Describe capping, polyadenylation and removal of introns by splicing to produce mature mRNA.

concepts.name: Translation steps with tRNA
concepts.summary: Use codon-anticodon pairing to trace how a ribosome builds a polypeptide from an mRNA.

concepts.name: Using the codon table
concepts.summary: Transcribe a template strand and translate the mRNA into an amino acid sequence, predicting effects of point mutations.

concepts.name: Gel electrophoresis and restriction digest
concepts.summary: Predict fragment patterns when DNA is cut by restriction enzymes and separated by size on a gel.

concepts.name: PCR cycle steps
concepts.summary: Apply the denaturation, primer annealing and extension cycle to predict the amount of product after n cycles.

misconceptions.text: DNA polymerase can start a new strand from scratch without a primer and can synthesize in either direction.
Introns are the parts of mRNA that are translated and exons are removed.
In gel electrophoresis, larger DNA fragments travel farther than smaller ones.

concepts.name: Replication initiation and origins
concepts.summary: Analyse how origins are recognized and forks assembled, and why bacteria use a single origin while eukaryotes use many.

concepts.name: Proofreading and DNA repair
concepts.summary: Analyse how polymerase proofreading and mismatch repair keep replication error rates low.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic operon regulation
concepts.summary: Predict operon expression under different conditions and mutations using repressors, operators, inducers and activators like CAP.

concepts.name: Eukaryotic transcription factors
concepts.summary: Analyse how general and specific transcription factors, enhancers and chromatin state control gene expression.

concepts.name: Alternative splicing and spliceosome
concepts.summary: Analyse how the spliceosome recognizes splice sites and how alternative splicing yields multiple proteins from one gene.

concepts.name: Plasmid cloning design
concepts.summary: Design a cloning workflow with compatible restriction sites, ligation, transformation and selection using antibiotic resistance and reporters.

concepts.name: PCR primer design and optimization
concepts.summary: Design primers with suitable length, melting temperature and specificity and troubleshoot failed or nonspecific amplification.

concepts.name: Sanger sequencing principle
concepts.summary: Analyse how dideoxynucleotides terminate chains to produce fragments read as a sequence.

misconceptions.text: The lac operon is switched on whenever lactose is present, regardless of glucose levels.
Proofreading eliminates all replication errors so no mutations arise from replication.
Any primer that matches the target will work in PCR regardless of its melting temperature or self-complementarity.

concepts.name: CRISPR-Cas9 mechanism and editing
concepts.summary: Analyse how guide RNA and PAM direct Cas9 cuts and how NHEJ versus HDR determine editing outcomes.

concepts.name: Quantitative PCR and RT-PCR
concepts.summary: Evaluate qPCR designs, controls and Ct data to judge gene expression or template quantity.

concepts.name: Next-generation sequencing workflows
concepts.summary: Analyse library preparation, read alignment and coverage and the trade-offs between short- and long-read methods.

concepts.name: Post-transcriptional regulation
concepts.summary: Analyse how miRNAs, siRNAs and mRNA decay pathways tune gene expression after transcription.

concepts.name: Epigenetic and chromatin control
concepts.summary: Analyse how histone modifications and DNA methylation alter accessibility and transcription.

concepts.name: Expression vectors and protein production
concepts.summary: Evaluate vector, promoter, tag and host choices to express functional recombinant protein.

concepts.name: Experimental controls and troubleshooting
concepts.summary: Judge results from cloning, PCR and gel experiments and diagnose failures using appropriate controls.

misconceptions.text: CRISPR-Cas9 edits are always precise and only happen at the intended target site.
A lower Ct value in qPCR means less starting template.
Epigenetic marks change the DNA sequence itself.

concepts.name: Designing genome editing strategies
concepts.summary: Design editing strategies choosing among nuclease, base and prime editing and plan validation of on- and off-target outcomes.

concepts.name: Evaluating sequencing approaches
concepts.summary: Evaluate which sequencing assay and depth best answers a question about expression, binding or variation, accounting for bias and error.

concepts.name: Synthetic gene circuit design
concepts.summary: Create regulatory circuits from promoters, repressors and RNA elements and predict their dynamics and failure modes.

concepts.name: Mechanistic models of gene regulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate quantitative models of transcription, translation fidelity and noise against experimental data.

concepts.name: Replication-transcription conflicts and genome stability
concepts.summary: Evaluate how collisions, R-loops and stalled forks cause instability and how cells resolve them.

concepts.name: Designing rigorous molecular experiments
concepts.summary: Create experimental plans with orthogonal assays, controls and statistics that distinguish causal mechanisms from artefacts.

concepts.name: Therapeutic nucleic acid strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate the benefits and risks of ASOs, siRNA, mRNA and gene-editing therapies for a given disease mechanism.

misconceptions.text: Sequencing with high coverage removes all errors and biases from the result.
Engineered gene circuits behave in cells exactly as designed on paper, independent of host context.
Gene expression is a smooth, deterministic process, so average measurements capture cell behaviour.

concepts.name: Population versus sample
concepts.summary: Distinguish the whole group of interest from the subset actually measured, and recognise why we sample.

concepts.name: Types of variables
concepts.summary: Classify variables as categorical or numerical and explain which summaries suit each.

concepts.name: Mean, median and mode
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret the three measures of centre and say what each tells about a data set.

concepts.name: Range and spread
concepts.summary: Explain spread as how far values vary and compute the range as a simple measure of it.

concepts.name: Reading histograms
concepts.summary: Read a histogram to describe the shape, centre and spread of a numerical data set.

concepts.name: Five-number summary and boxplots
concepts.summary: Identify the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum and read them from a boxplot.

misconceptions.text: The mean is always the best description of the typical value.
A taller bar in a histogram means the value is larger rather than more frequent.
The median line in a boxplot sits at the centre of the box, and each quarter of the box holds the same number of values only by width.

concepts.name: Variance and standard deviation
concepts.summary: Calculate the standard deviation of a sample and interpret it as typical distance from the mean.

concepts.name: Skewness and outliers
concepts.summary: Identify skew and outliers in plots and predict their effect on the mean and median.

concepts.name: Interquartile range and outlier rule
concepts.summary: Compute the IQR and use the 1.5×IQR fences to flag outliers on a boxplot.

concepts.name: Random sampling methods
concepts.summary: Describe simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling and when each is used.

concepts.name: Sampling bias
concepts.summary: Spot how a sampling procedure can systematically distort results, such as voluntary response or convenience samples.

concepts.name: Comparing distributions
concepts.summary: Compare two groups using centre, spread and shape from histograms or parallel boxplots.

misconceptions.text: A large sample automatically removes bias from a poorly designed sampling method.
Outliers should always be deleted from the data.
Standard deviation can be negative or measures the total distance of values from the mean.

concepts.name: Normal distribution and z-scores
concepts.summary: Use z-scores and the empirical rule to find proportions and percentiles under a normal model.

concepts.name: Sampling distribution of the mean
concepts.summary: Explain how sample means vary across repeated samples and how that distribution differs from the data distribution.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.summary: Analyse why sample means become approximately normal for large samples regardless of population shape.

concepts.name: Standard error
concepts.summary: Compute the standard error and show how it shrinks with sample size.

concepts.name: Confidence intervals for a mean
concepts.summary: Construct and interpret an interval estimate using the estimate, critical value and standard error.

concepts.name: Null and alternative hypotheses
concepts.summary: State null and alternative hypotheses, one- or two-sided, for a research question.

concepts.name: p-values and significance level
concepts.summary: Interpret a p-value as the probability of data this extreme under the null and compare it with alpha.

misconceptions.text: A 95% confidence interval contains 95% of the individual data values.
The p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
The central limit theorem says the data themselves become normal as the sample grows.

concepts.name: One-sample and two-sample t-tests
concepts.summary: Choose and carry out the right t-test for one mean or two independent means and interpret the t statistic.

concepts.name: Paired t-test
concepts.summary: Recognise paired designs and test the mean of the within-pair differences.

concepts.name: Chi-square test of independence
concepts.summary: Compute expected counts and the chi-square statistic to test association between two categorical variables.

concepts.name: Chi-square goodness of fit
concepts.summary: Test whether observed category counts match a hypothesised distribution.

concepts.name: Test assumptions and checks
concepts.summary: Evaluate independence, normality, equal variance and expected-count conditions and judge whether a test is valid.

concepts.name: Type I and Type II errors
concepts.summary: Distinguish the two error types and how significance level and sample size affect them.

concepts.name: Statistical power
concepts.summary: Judge how effect size, variability, alpha and sample size determine power and what that means for study design.

concepts.name: Statistical versus practical significance
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a statistically significant result is large enough to matter, using effect sizes and intervals.

misconceptions.text: A non-significant result proves there is no effect.
A smaller p-value means a larger or more important effect.
A chi-square test shows that one variable causes the other.

concepts.name: Multiple comparisons problem
concepts.summary: Evaluate how running many tests inflates false positives and choose corrections such as Bonferroni or false discovery rate.

concepts.name: p-hacking and researcher degrees of freedom
concepts.summary: Critique analyses whose flexibility in choices invalidates reported p-values.

concepts.name: Bootstrap and permutation methods
concepts.summary: Design resampling procedures to estimate uncertainty or test hypotheses when parametric assumptions fail.

concepts.name: Interpretation of confidence intervals
concepts.summary: Evaluate the frequentist meaning of coverage and contrast it with Bayesian credible intervals.

concepts.name: Nonparametric alternatives
concepts.summary: Judge when rank-based tests are preferable to t-tests and what they actually test.

concepts.name: Study design and confounding
concepts.summary: Design studies with randomisation, control and blinding to support causal claims and handle confounders.

concepts.name: Replication and reporting
concepts.summary: Plan analyses and reports, including pre-registration, effect sizes and intervals, that hold up under replication.

misconceptions.text: If the test is run once on the final chosen analysis, earlier exploratory tests do not affect the p-value.
Bootstrapping can fix a biased or unrepresentative sample.
A particular computed 95% interval has a 95% probability of containing the true parameter.

concepts.name: Functional versus non-functional requirements
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a system must do from qualities like latency, availability and scale, and clarify both before designing.

concepts.name: Client-server request flow
concepts.summary: Explain how a user request travels from client through DNS, load balancer, application servers and data store and back.

concepts.name: Vertical versus horizontal scaling
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between adding power to one machine and adding more machines, and the limits of each.

concepts.name: Latency, throughput and availability
concepts.summary: Define latency, throughput and availability and state the units used to express each.

concepts.name: Stateless application servers
concepts.summary: Explain why keeping session state out of app servers makes them easy to replicate and replace.

concepts.name: Load balancer role
concepts.summary: Describe how a load balancer spreads requests over servers and removes unhealthy ones.

concepts.name: Cache purpose
concepts.summary: Explain that a cache stores frequently read data in fast storage to cut latency and database load.

misconceptions.text: Scaling a system just means buying a bigger server.
Adding more servers automatically makes a system faster and more available.
A design can start immediately without asking clarifying questions about requirements.

concepts.name: Back-of-envelope capacity estimation
concepts.summary: Estimate QPS, storage and bandwidth from user counts, usage rates and object sizes using powers of ten.

concepts.name: Read-heavy versus write-heavy workloads
concepts.summary: Use the read-to-write ratio of a product to decide where to focus optimisation.

concepts.name: Load balancing algorithms
concepts.summary: Choose between round robin, least connections and hashing for a given traffic pattern.

concepts.name: Cache-aside and write strategies
concepts.summary: Apply cache-aside, write-through and write-back patterns and describe what each does on reads and writes.

concepts.name: Cache eviction policies
concepts.summary: Explain how LRU, LFU and TTL decide what to remove from a full cache.

concepts.name: CDN for static content
concepts.summary: Decide which assets to serve from edge locations to cut latency for distant users.

concepts.name: SQL versus NoSQL selection
concepts.summary: Pick a relational or NoSQL store based on data model, query patterns and scale needs.

concepts.name: API design for services
concepts.summary: Define simple endpoints, parameters and responses for a product's core operations.

misconceptions.text: Estimation must be exact to be useful.
A cache always returns correct, current data.
NoSQL is always faster and more scalable than a relational database.

concepts.name: Database replication topologies
concepts.summary: Set up leader-follower and multi-leader replication and explain read scaling and failover behaviour.

concepts.name: Sharding strategies
concepts.summary: Compare range, hash and directory-based partitioning and their effects on hotspots and queries.

concepts.name: Consistent hashing
concepts.summary: Use a hash ring with virtual nodes to add or remove nodes while moving little data.

concepts.name: Message queues and async processing
concepts.summary: Decouple producers from consumers with queues to absorb bursts and handle slow work asynchronously.

concepts.name: CAP theorem trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse how a system must trade consistency against availability when a network partition occurs.

concepts.name: Consistency models
concepts.summary: Distinguish strong and eventual consistency and judge which a feature can tolerate.

concepts.name: Unique ID generation
concepts.summary: Generate unique, roughly sortable IDs across many servers without a single bottleneck.

concepts.name: Indexing and denormalisation trade-offs
concepts.summary: Analyse when indexes or duplicated data speed up reads at the cost of write complexity.

misconceptions.text: CAP means you pick any two of three properties at all times.
Replicas make a database both faster for writes and fully consistent.
Hashing keys with modulo N is fine when nodes are added or removed.

concepts.name: Hotspot and skew mitigation
concepts.summary: Diagnose uneven load from popular keys and mitigate it with key splitting, caching or fan-out changes.

concepts.name: Fan-out on write versus read
concepts.summary: Evaluate push, pull and hybrid feed generation against follower counts and freshness needs.

concepts.name: Delivery semantics and idempotency
concepts.summary: Judge at-most-once, at-least-once and effectively-once processing and design idempotent consumers.

concepts.name: Cache stampede and invalidation
concepts.summary: Analyse cache invalidation risks and prevent stampedes with locking, request coalescing or jittered TTLs.

concepts.name: Failure handling patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and load shedding to stop cascading failures.

concepts.name: Real-time communication design
concepts.summary: Compare polling, long polling and persistent connections for chat or notifications, including presence and ordering.

concepts.name: Quorum reads and writes
concepts.summary: Evaluate quorum settings to balance consistency, latency and availability in replicated stores.

concepts.name: Capacity and bottleneck analysis
concepts.summary: Use estimates to find the first component to saturate and justify the next scaling step.

misconceptions.text: Retrying failed requests always improves reliability.
Exactly-once delivery is achievable by the broker alone without idempotent consumers.
Fan-out on write is always better for news feeds.

concepts.name: Multi-region architecture design
concepts.summary: Design active-active or active-passive multi-region systems with explicit latency, conflict and failover plans.

concepts.name: Conflict resolution strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate last-write-wins, vector clocks and CRDTs for reconciling concurrent writes.

concepts.name: Trade-off justification under constraints
concepts.summary: Weigh alternatives against stated requirements, cost and team capacity, and defend the choice with numbers.

concepts.name: Evolutionary scaling roadmap
concepts.summary: Create a staged path from a simple single-region design to a large-scale one with triggers for each step.

concepts.name: SLO-driven reliability design
concepts.summary: Derive SLOs and error budgets from user needs and design redundancy, observability and degradation to meet them.

concepts.name: Distributed transactions and sagas
concepts.summary: Evaluate two-phase commit, sagas and the outbox pattern for cross-service data integrity.

concepts.name: Cost and efficiency optimisation
concepts.summary: Assess storage tiering, compression and compute choices to reduce cost without breaking requirements.

concepts.name: Novel system composition
concepts.summary: Combine known building blocks to design a system for an unfamiliar problem and test it against failure scenarios.

misconceptions.text: Two-phase commit is a cheap way to get cross-service consistency at any scale.
Last-write-wins is safe because it never loses data.
A good design should include every scaling technique from the start.

concepts.name: Assets, liabilities, and equity
concepts.summary: Define and recognise assets, liabilities and owner's equity and give examples of each.

concepts.name: The accounting equation
concepts.summary: Explain why assets always equal liabilities plus equity and how a transaction keeps it in balance.

concepts.name: Revenues and expenses
concepts.summary: Distinguish revenues and expenses from assets and liabilities and explain how they change equity.

concepts.name: Business transactions
concepts.summary: Identify which events are recorded as transactions and which are not.

concepts.name: Debits and credits
concepts.summary: State that debit means left and credit means right and know which account types increase with each.

concepts.name: Double-entry principle
concepts.summary: Explain that every transaction affects at least two accounts with total debits equal to total credits.

misconceptions.text: Debit always means an increase and credit always means a decrease.
Equity is the same thing as cash the business holds.
Any event involving the business, such as signing a job offer, must be recorded as a transaction.

concepts.name: Chart of accounts
concepts.summary: Use a chart of accounts to choose the correct account for each part of a transaction.

concepts.name: Journal entries
concepts.summary: Analyse a transaction and record it as a dated, balanced journal entry with a description.

concepts.name: Posting to the ledger
concepts.summary: Transfer journal entries into ledger accounts and calculate running account balances.

concepts.name: Trial balance preparation
concepts.summary: List all ledger balances and check that total debits equal total credits.

concepts.name: Simple income statement
concepts.summary: Prepare an income statement by subtracting expenses from revenues to find net income.

concepts.name: Simple balance sheet
concepts.summary: Prepare a balance sheet listing assets, liabilities and equity at a date, including retained net income.

concepts.name: Owner investments and drawings
concepts.summary: Record owner contributions and withdrawals and show their effect on equity separate from revenue and expense.

misconceptions.text: A balanced trial balance proves that all transactions were recorded correctly.
Owner drawings are an expense that appears on the income statement.
Posting to the ledger is where a transaction is first recorded.

concepts.name: Accrual basis accounting
concepts.summary: Apply the accrual basis so revenue and expenses are recognised when earned or incurred rather than when cash moves.

concepts.name: Revenue recognition and matching
concepts.summary: Analyse when revenue is earned and match expenses to the periods they help generate.

concepts.name: Adjusting entries
concepts.summary: Prepare entries for prepaid expenses, unearned revenue, accrued items and depreciation at period end.

concepts.name: Depreciation of fixed assets
concepts.summary: Calculate and record depreciation and show assets at carrying amount.

concepts.name: Inventory and cost of goods sold
concepts.summary: Record purchases and sales of inventory and calculate cost of goods sold and gross profit.

concepts.name: Closing entries and the cycle
concepts.summary: Analyse how closing entries reset temporary accounts and carry results into retained earnings within the full accounting cycle.

concepts.name: Bank reconciliation and receivables
concepts.summary: Reconcile cash records to bank statements and account for credit sales and uncollectible receivables.

misconceptions.text: Revenue is earned when cash is received.
Depreciation sets aside cash to replace the asset or measures its market value.
Closing entries apply to all accounts including assets and liabilities.

concepts.name: Cash flow statement
concepts.summary: Derive operating, investing and financing cash flows and explain why they differ from net income.

concepts.name: Financial ratio analysis
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret liquidity, profitability and leverage ratios from the statements.

concepts.name: Inventory costing methods
concepts.summary: Compare cost-flow assumptions and judge their effects on profit, assets and taxes.

concepts.name: Accounting estimates and judgment
concepts.summary: Evaluate how estimates for depreciation, bad debts and provisions affect reported results.

concepts.name: Error detection and correction
concepts.summary: Find errors that a trial balance does not reveal and correct them with appropriate entries.

concepts.name: Accounting for equity structures
concepts.summary: Analyse how partnership and corporate equity, dividends and retained earnings are recorded and presented.

concepts.name: Internal controls
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether controls adequately protect assets and the reliability of records.

misconceptions.text: Profitable companies cannot run out of cash.
A ratio is meaningful on its own without comparison to peers or trends.
Accounting figures are objective facts with no judgment involved.

concepts.name: Conceptual framework evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate accounting treatments against relevance, faithful representation and recognition criteria.

concepts.name: Earnings quality assessment
concepts.summary: Judge whether reported earnings reflect sustainable performance or aggressive choices.

concepts.name: Complex transaction treatment
concepts.summary: Determine the appropriate recognition and measurement for transactions such as leases and deferred tax.

concepts.name: Accounting system design
concepts.summary: Design charts of accounts, journals and workflows that fit a business and support reporting and control.

concepts.name: Consolidated reporting concepts
concepts.summary: Assess how group structures determine which entities are combined and how intra-group items are eliminated.

concepts.name: Management reporting frameworks
concepts.summary: Create reporting packs that translate ledger data into decision-useful management information.

misconceptions.text: Following the standards mechanically guarantees a fair presentation.
Legal compliance is the same as high-quality earnings.
Consolidation simply adds together every subsidiary's figures.

concepts.name: Purpose of testing
concepts.summary: Explain that testing gathers evidence about whether software meets expectations and finds defects, but cannot prove the absence of bugs.

concepts.name: Expected versus actual result
concepts.summary: Describe a test as running code with a given input and comparing the actual output to an expected output.

concepts.name: Test case anatomy
concepts.summary: Identify the setup, action and assertion parts of a simple test and what each does.

concepts.name: Pass, fail and error
concepts.summary: Recall the difference between a test passing, failing an assertion, and erroring due to an unexpected exception.

concepts.name: Manual versus automated testing
concepts.summary: Distinguish manual checks from automated tests and explain why automated tests are repeatable and fast to rerun.

concepts.name: Bugs, defects and failures
concepts.summary: Recall the terms for a mistake in code, the faulty state it causes, and the visible failure.

concepts.name: Test levels overview
concepts.summary: Name unit, integration and end-to-end tests and describe in one line what scope each one covers.

misconceptions.text: If all tests pass, the software has no bugs.
Testing is only something done by a separate QA person after the code is finished.
A test that fails always means the code under test is wrong.

concepts.name: Writing unit tests with a framework
concepts.summary: Write and run unit tests using a testing framework, with assertions, test discovery and readable failure messages.

concepts.name: Test fixtures and setup
concepts.summary: Use setup and teardown to create a known starting state and clean up after each test.

concepts.name: Boundary and edge cases
concepts.summary: Choose inputs at limits such as empty, zero, maximum and off-by-one values to expose common defects.

concepts.name: Testing error handling
concepts.summary: Write tests asserting that invalid input or failing operations raise the expected errors.

concepts.name: Test independence and determinism
concepts.summary: Explain why each test should run alone, in any order, and give the same result every time.

concepts.name: Descriptive test naming
concepts.summary: Name tests so a failure report states the scenario and the expected behaviour.

concepts.name: Basic test-driven development cycle
concepts.summary: Apply the red-green-refactor loop to implement a small function by writing a failing test first.
