misconceptions.text: Tests can safely share and modify global state as long as they all pass when run together.
Testing a few typical inputs is enough to show a function works.
In TDD you write all the tests for the whole program before writing any code.

concepts.name: Test doubles taxonomy
concepts.summary: Choose among dummies, stubs, fakes, spies and mocks according to what a test needs to control or observe.

concepts.name: Isolating dependencies by injection
concepts.summary: Analyse code for hard-wired dependencies and restructure it with injection so collaborators can be substituted in tests.

concepts.name: Integration test design
concepts.summary: Design tests that exercise real interactions between modules, databases or services and decide which parts to keep real.

concepts.name: Equivalence partitioning and boundaries
concepts.summary: Divide an input space into classes that behave alike and pick representative and boundary values from each.

concepts.name: Code coverage metrics
concepts.summary: Interpret statement, branch and condition coverage and analyse what a coverage figure does and does not reveal.

concepts.name: Behaviour versus implementation testing
concepts.summary: Distinguish tests that assert observable behaviour from tests coupled to internals and explain why the latter break on refactoring.

concepts.name: Diagnosing flaky tests
concepts.summary: Identify causes of flakiness such as timing, shared state, ordering and randomness and isolate them.

concepts.name: Continuous integration test runs
concepts.summary: Run the automated suite on every change in a CI pipeline and act on failures promptly.

misconceptions.text: 100% code coverage means the code is fully tested and correct.
Every dependency should be mocked in every test.
A flaky test can just be rerun until it passes, since it is not a real problem.

concepts.name: Test pyramid trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate the balance of unit, integration and end-to-end tests for a system by cost, speed, confidence and fragility.

concepts.name: End-to-end test strategy
concepts.summary: Judge which user journeys deserve end-to-end tests and design them to be stable, using controlled data and waits on conditions.

concepts.name: Contract testing
concepts.summary: Analyse how contract tests verify agreements between services without full integrated environments.

concepts.name: Property-based testing
concepts.summary: Express invariants of code as properties checked against many generated inputs, and interpret shrunk counterexamples.

concepts.name: Mutation testing
concepts.summary: Evaluate test suite strength by whether it detects injected faults, and compare this with coverage.

concepts.name: Risk-based test prioritisation
concepts.summary: Decide where to focus testing effort by weighing failure impact, likelihood and change frequency.

concepts.name: Testing legacy code
concepts.summary: Add characterization tests and create seams so untested code can be changed safely.

concepts.name: Test data management
concepts.summary: Analyse approaches to building, seeding and isolating test data so tests stay readable and independent.

misconceptions.text: The more end-to-end tests a suite has, the better, because they are the most realistic.
A high mutation score or coverage figure should be maximised everywhere as the goal of testing.
Property-based testing replaces example-based tests.

concepts.name: Designing a test strategy
concepts.summary: Create a coherent strategy across teams that sets test levels, ownership, quality gates and feedback speed for an architecture.

concepts.name: Architecting for testability
concepts.summary: Design system structure, such as ports and adapters and observability hooks, so behaviour can be verified cheaply.

concepts.name: Evaluating test suite economics
concepts.summary: Assess the cost of writing, running and maintaining tests against the defects they prevent, and retire low-value tests.

concepts.name: Testing distributed and concurrent systems
concepts.summary: Evaluate techniques such as deterministic scheduling, fault injection and simulation for finding races and partial-failure bugs.

concepts.name: Testing in production
concepts.summary: Judge when monitoring, canaries and staged rollouts complement pre-release tests and what risks they carry.

concepts.name: Building test infrastructure
concepts.summary: Create fast, parallel, hermetic test infrastructure and custom harnesses, including flaky test quarantine and selection of affected tests.

concepts.name: Testing non-functional qualities
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches for verifying performance, reliability and security properties and their limits as evidence.

misconceptions.text: Good testing before release removes the need for monitoring and production verification.
Testability is something that can be added afterwards by writing more tests, not through design.
A single organisation-wide test ratio or coverage target suits every system.

concepts.name: Intuitive limit of a function
concepts.summary: Explain that a limit describes the value a function approaches as the input nears a point, regardless of the value at that point.

concepts.name: One-sided limits
concepts.summary: Distinguish left and right approach and state that a two-sided limit exists only when both agree.

concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.summary: State the three conditions for continuity (defined, limit exists, equal) and recognise breaks in a graph.

concepts.name: Average rate of change
concepts.summary: Interpret the slope of a secant line as average rate of change over an interval.

concepts.name: Instantaneous rate and tangent
concepts.summary: Describe the derivative as the slope of the tangent line, obtained as secant slopes approach a limit.

concepts.name: Derivative notation
concepts.summary: Recognise and read f'(x), dy/dx and d/dx as notations for the derivative.

misconceptions.text: The limit of a function at a point is always just the function's value at that point.
If a limit exists at a point, the function must be defined there.
The derivative is the slope between two separate points on the graph, not a limiting value.

concepts.name: Evaluating limits algebraically
concepts.summary: Compute limits using limit laws, substitution, factoring, and conjugates to remove indeterminate 0/0 forms.

concepts.name: Limits at infinity
concepts.summary: Find limits as x grows without bound and identify horizontal asymptotes of rational functions.

concepts.name: Limit definition of derivative
concepts.summary: Compute f'(x) as the limit of (f(x+h)-f(x))/h for simple polynomial and rational functions.

concepts.name: Power and constant rules
concepts.summary: Differentiate polynomials and power functions term by term using the power, constant multiple and sum rules.

concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
concepts.summary: Apply the product and quotient rules correctly to differentiate products and ratios of functions.

concepts.name: Tangent line equations
concepts.summary: Write the equation of the tangent line at a point using the derivative as slope.

concepts.name: Differentiability and continuity
concepts.summary: Explain that differentiability implies continuity but not conversely, recognising corners, cusps and vertical tangents.

misconceptions.text: A 0/0 form means the limit does not exist.
The derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.
A continuous function is always differentiable.

concepts.name: Chain rule
concepts.summary: Differentiate composite functions by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

concepts.name: Trigonometric derivatives
concepts.summary: Differentiate all six trig functions and combine them with product, quotient and chain rules.

concepts.name: Exponential and logarithmic derivatives
concepts.summary: Differentiate e^x, a^x, ln x and log_a x, including composite forms.

concepts.name: Implicit differentiation
concepts.summary: Differentiate relations in x and y by treating y as a function of x and solving for dy/dx.

concepts.name: Logarithmic differentiation
concepts.summary: Use logarithms to differentiate products, quotients and variable exponents like x^x.

concepts.name: Related rates
concepts.summary: Model a situation with a relation between changing quantities and differentiate in time to link their rates.

concepts.name: Higher-order derivatives
concepts.summary: Compute second and higher derivatives and interpret the second derivative as rate of change of slope.

misconceptions.text: In the chain rule you can skip the inner derivative, e.g. d/dx sin(3x) = cos(3x).
The derivative of a^x is x·a^(x-1), as with the power rule.
In related rates you should substitute the specific numerical values before differentiating with respect to time.

concepts.name: L'Hôpital's rule
concepts.summary: Decide when 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms permit differentiating numerator and denominator, and convert other indeterminate forms to those.

concepts.name: Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.summary: Use continuity on a closed interval to justify the existence of roots and intermediate values.

concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem
concepts.summary: Verify hypotheses and use the theorem to guarantee a point where the tangent slope equals the average slope.

concepts.name: Critical points and first-derivative test
concepts.summary: Find critical points and use sign changes of f' to classify local maxima and minima.

concepts.name: Concavity and second-derivative test
concepts.summary: Use the sign of f'' to determine concavity, locate inflection points and classify critical points.

concepts.name: Absolute extrema on intervals
concepts.summary: Find global extrema on a closed interval by comparing critical-point and endpoint values.

concepts.name: Optimisation modelling
concepts.summary: Build an objective function with constraints, find the optimum, and justify that it is a maximum or minimum.

concepts.name: Curve sketching synthesis
concepts.summary: Combine domain, intercepts, asymptotes, monotonicity and concavity to sketch and justify a function's graph.

misconceptions.text: L'Hôpital's rule can be applied to any limit, and it means differentiating the quotient with the quotient rule.
Wherever f'(c)=0 there must be a local maximum or minimum.
Wherever f''(c)=0 there is an inflection point.

concepts.name: Formal epsilon-delta limits
concepts.summary: Construct and evaluate epsilon-delta arguments to prove limits and judge their correctness.

concepts.name: Proofs of differentiation rules
concepts.summary: Derive the product, quotient and chain rules from the limit definition and critique flawed proofs.

concepts.name: Consequences of the MVT
concepts.summary: Use the MVT to prove that functions with zero derivative are constant and that sign of f' determines monotonicity.

concepts.name: Linearisation and differentials
concepts.summary: Evaluate the accuracy of tangent-line approximations and propagate small errors using differentials.

concepts.name: Taylor polynomial approximation
concepts.summary: Construct Taylor polynomials and use the remainder to bound approximation error and to evaluate limits.

concepts.name: Pathological functions and counterexamples
concepts.summary: Assess how counterexamples show the limits of theorems, such as differentiable functions with discontinuous derivatives.

concepts.name: Inverse function differentiation
concepts.summary: Derive derivatives of inverse functions and inverse trig functions from the inverse derivative relation.

misconceptions.text: If f is differentiable, then f' must be continuous.
A Taylor series of a smooth function always converges to the function.
Tangent-line approximation error is the same size regardless of distance from the base point or curvature.

concepts.name: Claims versus opinions
concepts.summary: Recognise that a claim is a statement that can be true or false, and distinguish factual claims from value judgments and preferences.

concepts.name: Premises and conclusions
concepts.summary: Identify which statements in a short argument are the reasons offered and which is the point they are meant to support.

concepts.name: Indicator words
concepts.summary: Recall words such as 'because', 'since', 'therefore' and 'thus' that signal reasons or conclusions.

concepts.name: Arguments versus explanations
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between giving reasons to persuade someone a claim is true and explaining why something is the case.

concepts.name: Asking for evidence
concepts.summary: Understand that a claim needs support and that the person making it is expected to provide evidence.

concepts.name: Strong versus weak reasons
concepts.summary: Explain why a reason is stronger when it is relevant to the conclusion and backed by evidence rather than just repeated assertion.

misconceptions.text: Critical thinking means criticising or finding fault with everything.
If many people believe a claim or it is stated confidently, it counts as good evidence.
Every statement in an argument is a premise.

concepts.name: Extracting arguments from text
concepts.summary: Pick out premises and conclusion from a short everyday passage, ignoring rhetoric and filler, and lay them out in order.

concepts.name: Hidden assumptions
concepts.summary: Spot and state the unspoken premise that an everyday argument needs in order to get from its reasons to its conclusion.

concepts.name: Strawman fallacy
concepts.summary: Recognise when someone attacks a distorted or weakened version of an opponent's position instead of the real one.

concepts.name: Ad hominem fallacy
concepts.summary: Recognise when a claim is dismissed because of who said it rather than because of the reasons given.

concepts.name: Slippery slope fallacy
concepts.summary: Recognise arguments that claim one step will inevitably lead to extreme consequences without evidence for each link.

concepts.name: False dilemma
concepts.summary: Recognise when an argument presents only two options although others exist.

concepts.name: Correlation versus causation
concepts.summary: Explain that two things occurring together does not show that one causes the other.

misconceptions.text: If an argument commits a fallacy, its conclusion must be false.
Any personal remark about an opponent is an ad hominem fallacy.
Any argument that predicts bad consequences is a slippery slope fallacy.

concepts.name: Deductive versus inductive arguments
concepts.summary: Analyse whether an argument aims at guaranteeing its conclusion or only making it probable, and judge it by the matching standard.

concepts.name: Validity versus soundness
concepts.summary: Separate whether the conclusion follows from the premises from whether the premises are actually true.

concepts.name: Confirmation bias
concepts.summary: Apply the idea that people favour evidence supporting existing beliefs to explain how a person's reasoning or information diet is skewed.

concepts.name: Common cognitive biases
concepts.summary: Identify biases such as anchoring, availability, and sunk cost in everyday judgments and decisions.

concepts.name: Source credibility assessment
concepts.summary: Weigh a source's expertise, evidence, incentives, and track record to judge how far to trust its claims.

concepts.name: Confounders and reverse causation
concepts.summary: Analyse a claimed causal link by looking for common causes, reversed direction, and coincidence.

concepts.name: Relevance and appeal fallacies
concepts.summary: Distinguish legitimate appeals to authority or popularity from fallacious ones, and spot red herrings that shift the topic.

concepts.name: Circular reasoning
concepts.summary: Detect arguments whose conclusion is already assumed in a premise and explain why that gives no real support.

misconceptions.text: A valid argument must have a true conclusion.
Being aware of biases means I am no longer affected by them.
Citing an authority is always a fallacy.

concepts.name: Evaluating evidence quality
concepts.summary: Judge how much a piece of evidence supports a claim by considering sample size, selection, controls, replication, and anecdote versus systematic data.

concepts.name: Base rates and statistical reasoning
concepts.summary: Analyse claims using base rates, proportions, and conditional probabilities rather than vivid cases.

concepts.name: Charitable argument reconstruction
concepts.summary: Rebuild an opponent's argument in its strongest plausible form before evaluating it.

concepts.name: Burden of proof allocation
concepts.summary: Judge who should carry the burden of proof in a dispute and detect attempts to shift it improperly.

concepts.name: Inference to the best explanation
concepts.summary: Compare rival explanations of the same evidence by fit, simplicity, scope, and testability and justify the preferred one.

concepts.name: Motivated reasoning and rhetoric
concepts.summary: Analyse how framing, emotional appeals, and identity-protective thinking shape both arguments and one's own judgment.

concepts.name: Judging fallacy accusations
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a suspected fallacy really undermines an argument in context, as slippery slope and authority appeals can sometimes be reasonable.

misconceptions.text: A large sample guarantees reliable evidence regardless of how it was collected.
Pointing out a fallacy settles the debate and proves the conclusion false.
Whoever doubts a claim never has to justify that doubt, so the burden always falls on the claimant.

concepts.name: Designing argument evaluation frameworks
concepts.summary: Create a reusable method for assessing arguments that weighs premise acceptability, relevance, sufficiency, and rebuttal across varied domains.

concepts.name: Calibrated belief updating
concepts.summary: Judge how strongly evidence should shift one's confidence and keep stated confidence matched to actual accuracy.

concepts.name: Debiasing strategies
concepts.summary: Design practical procedures, such as pre-mortems, devil's advocates, and outside-view checks, that reduce bias in individual and group decisions.

concepts.name: Limits of critical thinking
concepts.summary: Evaluate where critical analysis fails or misleads, including intellectual overconfidence, cynicism, expertise deference, and domain knowledge gaps.

concepts.name: Adversarial and disinformation analysis
concepts.summary: Assess deliberate manipulation tactics such as selective statistics, astroturfing, and coordinated misleading narratives and judge their likely effect.

concepts.name: Teaching and facilitating reasoning
concepts.summary: Create exercises and discussion formats that help others examine their own reasoning without triggering defensiveness.

misconceptions.text: Expert critical thinkers are immune to bias and manipulation.
Good critical thinking means distrusting all experts and institutions.
Being more confident in a conclusion shows better reasoning.

concepts.name: Temperature and thermal equilibrium
concepts.summary: Explain that temperature determines the direction of heat flow and that objects in thermal equilibrium share the same temperature, as stated by the zeroth law.

concepts.name: Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin
concepts.summary: Recall the three temperature scales, convert between them, and identify absolute zero as the zero of the Kelvin scale.

concepts.name: Heat versus temperature
concepts.summary: Distinguish heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference from temperature as a measure of thermal state.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.summary: Explain that different materials need different amounts of heat per unit mass to change temperature, and relate this to Q = mcΔT.

concepts.name: Latent heat and phase change
concepts.summary: Describe how heat absorbed or released during melting, boiling or freezing changes the phase without changing the temperature.

concepts.name: Heat transfer modes
concepts.summary: Name and describe conduction, convection and radiation as ways thermal energy moves.

concepts.name: Pressure, volume and temperature of gases
concepts.summary: Describe a gas by its pressure, volume, temperature and amount, and explain qualitatively how they change together.

misconceptions.text: Heat and temperature are the same thing.
Adding heat to a substance always raises its temperature.
Cold is a substance that flows from one object to another, instead of heat flowing from hot to cold.

concepts.name: Ideal gas law
concepts.summary: Apply PV = nRT with absolute temperature to find an unknown state variable for a gas sample.

concepts.name: Calorimetry problems
concepts.summary: Use energy conservation with specific and latent heats to find final temperatures or masses when bodies exchange heat.

concepts.name: First law of thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Apply ΔU = Q − W with consistent sign conventions to track heat, work and internal energy of a system.

concepts.name: Work done by expanding gas
concepts.summary: Compute work for constant-pressure changes as PΔV and interpret it as area under a pV diagram.

concepts.name: Internal energy of ideal gas
concepts.summary: Explain that internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature and relates to molecular kinetic energy.

concepts.name: Molar heat capacities Cv and Cp
concepts.summary: Use Cv and Cp to compute heat for constant-volume and constant-pressure processes and explain why Cp exceeds Cv.

concepts.name: Reading pV diagrams
concepts.summary: Identify isobaric, isochoric and other processes on a pV diagram and read off work and state changes.

misconceptions.text: The ideal gas law can be used with temperature in Celsius.
Work done by a gas is always positive regardless of the sign convention or whether it expands or compresses.
Heat and work are properties stored in a system, like internal energy.

concepts.name: Isothermal process analysis
concepts.summary: Compute work W = nRT ln(V2/V1) and show that heat in equals work out for an ideal gas isotherm.

concepts.name: Adiabatic process analysis
concepts.summary: Use PV^γ = constant and TV^(γ−1) = constant to find states and work when no heat is exchanged.

concepts.name: Heat engine and efficiency
concepts.summary: Compute efficiency as net work over heat input for a cycle and account for heat rejected to a cold reservoir.

concepts.name: Refrigerators and heat pumps
concepts.summary: Calculate coefficients of performance for refrigerators and heat pumps from heat and work flows.

concepts.name: Second law statements
concepts.summary: Analyse the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements and show their equivalence and what they forbid.

concepts.name: Reversible and irreversible processes
concepts.summary: Distinguish reversible idealisations from real irreversible processes and identify sources of irreversibility such as friction and finite temperature differences.

concepts.name: Entropy change calculation
concepts.summary: Compute entropy changes for heating, phase changes and ideal gas processes using dS = dQ_rev/T.

concepts.name: Carnot cycle
concepts.summary: Analyse the four steps of the Carnot cycle and derive its efficiency 1 − Tc/Th.

misconceptions.text: In an isothermal ideal gas process, no heat flows because the temperature is constant.
A heat engine can reach 100% efficiency if friction is eliminated.
Adiabatic means isothermal, so temperature stays constant.

concepts.name: Entropy increase principle
concepts.summary: Use total entropy change of system plus surroundings to decide whether a process is reversible, irreversible or impossible.

concepts.name: Carnot theorem and bounds
concepts.summary: Evaluate real engines and refrigerators against the Carnot limit and justify why no engine between two reservoirs can beat it.

concepts.name: Boltzmann microstate entropy
concepts.summary: Relate entropy to the number of microstates via S = k ln W and explain macrostates as collections of microstates.

concepts.name: Real engine cycles
concepts.summary: Analyse Otto-type and similar cycles on pV or TS diagrams to derive efficiencies and locate losses.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic potentials
concepts.summary: Choose among internal energy, enthalpy, Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies to predict spontaneity under given constraints.

concepts.name: Free expansion and mixing entropy
concepts.summary: Calculate entropy generated in irreversible free expansion and mixing by constructing a reversible path between the same states.

concepts.name: Third law and absolute entropy
concepts.summary: Explain that entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero at absolute zero and that absolute zero cannot be reached in finitely many steps.

concepts.name: Temperature-entropy diagrams
concepts.summary: Use TS diagrams to read heat as area and compare cycles, identifying isentropic and isothermal segments.

misconceptions.text: Entropy can never decrease anywhere, even within a subsystem.
Entropy is simply a measure of visible messiness rather than a count of accessible microstates.
Entropy does not change in a free expansion because no heat is exchanged.

concepts.name: Statistical ensembles and partition function
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the partition function generates thermodynamic quantities such as energy, entropy and free energy from microscopic spectra.

concepts.name: Gibbs entropy and information
concepts.summary: Assess the equivalence between Gibbs entropy −kΣp ln p and information-theoretic entropy and its role in resolving Maxwell's demon.

concepts.name: Second law and arrow of time
concepts.summary: Critically evaluate how time-reversible microscopic laws coexist with the statistical, probabilistic irreversibility of the second law.

concepts.name: Maxwell relations and response functions
concepts.summary: Derive relations among response functions such as Cp − Cv and compressibilities from potentials via Legendre transformation and Maxwell relations.

concepts.name: Finite-time and nonequilibrium engines
concepts.summary: Evaluate efficiency at maximum power for engines with finite heat transfer rates and contrast it with Carnot efficiency.

concepts.name: Phase transition thermodynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate phase coexistence and transitions using Gibbs free energy, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and critical behaviour.

concepts.name: Design of thermodynamic systems
concepts.summary: Design or optimise a thermal system using exergy and entropy generation analysis to justify trade-offs between efficiency, cost and irreversibility.

concepts.name: Fluctuation theorems
concepts.summary: Construct arguments for how fluctuation theorems extend the second law to small systems far from equilibrium.

misconceptions.text: The second law is an absolute dynamical law that forbids any entropy-decreasing fluctuation in any system.
Carnot efficiency is the practical target for engines operating at maximum power.
Information entropy and thermodynamic entropy are unrelated, merely sharing a name.

concepts.name: Sales funnel stages
concepts.summary: Recall the main stages a prospect moves through from awareness to closed deal and what happens at each.

concepts.name: Prospects versus leads
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between a raw contact, a lead, a qualified prospect and a customer.

concepts.name: Value proposition
concepts.summary: Explain in a sentence what problem the product solves for a buyer and the benefit they gain.

concepts.name: Features versus benefits
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a product does from what that does for the buyer and translate one into the other.

concepts.name: Outreach channels
concepts.summary: Name the common outreach channels such as phone, email, social and referrals and when each is typically used.

concepts.name: Sales roles and quota
concepts.summary: Describe common sales roles and what a quota measures.

concepts.name: Ideal customer profile
concepts.summary: Explain how an ideal customer profile defines which companies and people are worth pursuing.

misconceptions.text: Selling is mainly about persuading people to buy something they do not need.
Anyone who could possibly use the product is a good lead.
Listing every product feature is the best way to show value.

concepts.name: Writing cold outreach messages
concepts.summary: Write a short, personalised cold email or message with a relevant hook and a single clear ask.

concepts.name: Cold call opening
concepts.summary: Open a cold call with a brief introduction, a reason for calling and a request for permission to continue.

concepts.name: Lead sourcing and research
concepts.summary: Build a list of leads matching the ICP and research each for a relevant trigger or context.

concepts.name: Basic lead qualification
concepts.summary: Use criteria such as budget, authority, need and timing to decide whether a lead is worth pursuing.

concepts.name: Open and probing questions
concepts.summary: Use open and follow-up questions to draw out a buyer's situation rather than closed yes/no questions.

concepts.name: CRM record keeping
concepts.summary: Log contacts, activities, notes and deal stages in a CRM so the record is accurate and usable by others.

concepts.name: Scripted objection responses
concepts.summary: Respond to common objections such as price or timing using acknowledge, question and respond patterns.

misconceptions.text: A cold email works best when it is long and explains everything about the product.
Most objections mean the buyer is saying no for good.
CRM updates are admin that can wait until the deal closes.

concepts.name: Discovery call structure
concepts.summary: Plan and run a discovery call that covers current situation, pain, impact, decision process and next steps.

concepts.name: Pain and impact quantification
concepts.summary: Analyse a buyer's problem to estimate its business cost and tie it to the value of solving it.

concepts.name: Tailored pitch and demo
concepts.summary: Shape a pitch or demo around the pains uncovered in discovery rather than a generic feature tour.

concepts.name: Stakeholder and buying committee mapping
concepts.summary: Identify the champion, economic buyer, users and blockers and how each influences the decision.

concepts.name: Diagnosing objections
concepts.summary: Separate stated objections from underlying concerns and choose a response that addresses the real cause.

concepts.name: Closing techniques and next steps
concepts.summary: Ask for commitment at the right moment and secure a dated, specific next step after every interaction.

concepts.name: Pipeline stage criteria
concepts.summary: Judge whether a deal truly meets the criteria for its stage and keep close dates and amounts realistic.

concepts.name: Follow-up cadence
concepts.summary: Plan follow-up touches across channels that add new value rather than just checking in.

misconceptions.text: A discovery call is a chance to talk through the product and pitch early.
Talking to one enthusiastic contact is enough to win the deal.
Moving a deal to a later stage shows progress even if the buyer has not met the stage criteria.

concepts.name: Sales forecasting
concepts.summary: Analyse pipeline coverage, stage conversion rates and deal age to produce a defensible forecast against quota.

concepts.name: Deal qualification frameworks
concepts.summary: Evaluate a complex deal against frameworks such as MEDDICC and decide whether to invest, adjust or disqualify.

concepts.name: Negotiation and concessions
concepts.summary: Judge when and how to trade concessions for commitments while protecting value and margin.

concepts.name: Competitive positioning
concepts.summary: Assess a competitor's strengths and weaknesses and position against them without disparaging.

concepts.name: Territory and account planning
concepts.summary: Analyse accounts and territory to prioritise effort and plan multi-stage campaigns toward target accounts.

concepts.name: Win-loss analysis
concepts.summary: Examine won and lost deals to find patterns in qualification, process and positioning.

concepts.name: Funnel metrics diagnosis
concepts.summary: Diagnose where the funnel leaks using conversion rates, cycle length and average deal size and choose a fix.

misconceptions.text: A large pipeline guarantees hitting quota regardless of deal quality.
Discounting is the quickest way to close and costs little.
Criticising competitors is the strongest way to differentiate.

concepts.name: Designing a sales process
concepts.summary: Create a repeatable sales process with stages, exit criteria and playbooks fitted to a market and deal type.

concepts.name: Go-to-market and segmentation strategy
concepts.summary: Design which segments, channels and motions such as inbound, outbound or partner a company should pursue.

concepts.name: Quota and compensation design
concepts.summary: Evaluate how quotas and incentives shape seller behaviour and set them to be achievable and aligned with strategy.

concepts.name: Coaching and enablement systems
concepts.summary: Build coaching, call review and training programs that raise team performance measurably.

concepts.name: Strategic enterprise deal leadership
concepts.summary: Judge and steer large multi-party deals including executive sponsorship, procurement and risk.

concepts.name: Revenue operations and tooling
concepts.summary: Design CRM data models, handoffs and reporting that align sales, marketing and customer success.

concepts.name: Pricing and packaging strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate pricing and packaging models against buyer value, competition and sales motion.

misconceptions.text: Top individual sellers make the best managers and coaches without further training.
Higher quotas and bigger commissions always drive better performance.
A single sales process works for every segment and deal size.

concepts.name: Features, labels and examples
concepts.summary: Identify rows as examples, columns as features, and the target column as the label in a tabular dataset.

concepts.name: Supervised versus unsupervised learning
concepts.summary: Explain how learning from labelled data (prediction) differs from finding structure in unlabelled data.

concepts.name: Classification versus regression
concepts.summary: Decide whether a problem predicts a category or a numeric value based on the target.

concepts.name: Train and test split
concepts.summary: Explain why a model is fitted on one part of the data and evaluated on held-out data.

concepts.name: Model fitting and prediction
concepts.summary: Describe training as learning parameters from data and prediction as applying the fitted model to new examples.

concepts.name: Accuracy as a basic metric
concepts.summary: Define accuracy as the fraction of correct predictions and compute it from predictions and true labels.

concepts.name: Overfitting intuition
concepts.summary: Describe how a model can do well on training data yet poorly on new data because it memorized noise.

misconceptions.text: A model with high training accuracy is necessarily a good model.
Machine learning always needs labelled data.
Any problem with numbers in the target column is a regression problem, even when the numbers are class codes.

concepts.name: Decision tree splitting
concepts.summary: Explain how a tree chooses feature thresholds that reduce impurity such as Gini or entropy, and read a fitted tree.

concepts.name: k-nearest neighbours prediction
concepts.summary: Apply kNN by finding the k closest examples under a distance and voting or averaging their labels.

concepts.name: Feature scaling
concepts.summary: Apply standardization or min-max scaling and know which methods depend on feature scale.

concepts.name: Confusion matrix metrics
concepts.summary: Build a confusion matrix and compute precision, recall and F1 from true/false positives and negatives.

concepts.name: Encoding categorical features
concepts.summary: Convert categorical columns to numeric form using one-hot or ordinal encoding as appropriate.

concepts.name: Hyperparameters versus parameters
concepts.summary: Distinguish values learned from data from settings such as tree depth or k that are chosen beforehand.

concepts.name: Missing value handling
concepts.summary: Apply simple imputation strategies such as median or most frequent and recognise their effect.

concepts.name: k-means clustering procedure
concepts.summary: Run k-means by alternating assignment to nearest centroid and centroid updates until convergence.

misconceptions.text: Decision trees and kNN need feature scaling in the same way.
Accuracy is a reliable metric on any dataset, including heavily imbalanced ones.
Encoding categories as integers 1, 2, 3 is always harmless for distance-based models.

concepts.name: Cross-validation
concepts.summary: Use k-fold and stratified cross-validation to estimate generalization and compare models.

concepts.name: Bias-variance tradeoff
concepts.summary: Analyse errors as bias and variance and use learning curves to diagnose underfitting or overfitting.

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.summary: Apply penalties or complexity limits such as L1, L2, pruning and depth limits to reduce variance.

concepts.name: Random forests and bagging
concepts.summary: Explain and apply bagging with random feature subsets to reduce the variance of trees.

concepts.name: Data leakage
concepts.summary: Identify how information from test data or the target leaks into training and prevent it with pipelines.

concepts.name: ROC curve and AUC
concepts.summary: Interpret ROC curves and AUC and relate decision thresholds to the precision-recall trade-off.

concepts.name: Hyperparameter search
concepts.summary: Tune hyperparameters with grid or random search inside cross-validation.

concepts.name: Feature engineering
concepts.summary: Construct and select features such as ratios, interactions and aggregates, and judge their usefulness.

misconceptions.text: Scaling or imputing on the full dataset before splitting is fine because it uses no labels.
A higher ROC AUC means the model is better at every threshold and for any class balance.
Adding more trees to a random forest causes it to overfit more.

concepts.name: Gradient boosting mechanics
concepts.summary: Analyse how boosting fits trees sequentially to the gradient of the loss and how learning rate, depth and rounds interact.

concepts.name: SVM margins and kernels
concepts.summary: Explain maximum margin, the role of C and support vectors, and how kernels such as RBF enable nonlinear boundaries.

concepts.name: PCA and variance explained
concepts.summary: Interpret principal components as directions of maximal variance and choose the number of components.

concepts.name: Handling class imbalance
concepts.summary: Evaluate class weights, resampling and threshold moving against the cost of errors.

concepts.name: Model comparison and selection
concepts.summary: Judge models using nested cross-validation, variance across folds and metrics suited to the problem.

concepts.name: Choosing k and cluster validity
concepts.summary: Evaluate cluster quality and the choice of k using silhouette, inertia and stability.

concepts.name: Feature importance and interpretation
concepts.summary: Compare impurity-based and permutation importance and interpret model behaviour while recognising correlated-feature pitfalls.

concepts.name: Probability calibration
concepts.summary: Assess whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies and choose a calibration method.

misconceptions.text: Oversampling before the train-test split is a valid way to balance classes.
Impurity-based feature importance reliably shows which features truly drive predictions.
PCA components are always the most predictive directions for the target.

concepts.name: Designing evaluation protocols

concepts.name: Refs and DOM access
concepts.summary: Use refs for DOM nodes and mutable values that do not affect rendering, and know when not to.

concepts.name: Deciding where state lives
concepts.summary: Decide what is state versus derived data and structure state to avoid duplication and contradiction.

misconceptions.text: The virtual DOM makes React faster than direct DOM manipulation in every case.
A re-render means the browser DOM is fully rebuilt.
An effect with an empty dependency array is the right place for any logic, and omitting dependencies is harmless.

concepts.name: Context for shared data
concepts.summary: Evaluate when context avoids prop drilling and analyse how its updates re-render consumers.

concepts.name: Reducer-based state management
concepts.summary: Model complex state transitions as actions and a pure reducer and choose it over multiple useState calls.

concepts.name: Render performance optimisation
concepts.summary: Judge when memoisation pays off, diagnose needless re-renders with profiling and avoid premature optimisation.

concepts.name: Data fetching in effects
concepts.summary: Handle loading, error and race conditions when fetching data, with cancellation or ignore flags.

concepts.name: Component API design
concepts.summary: Evaluate and shape component interfaces using compound components, render props and controlled versus uncontrolled patterns.

concepts.name: Error boundaries and Suspense
concepts.summary: Contain rendering failures with error boundaries and split code with lazy and Suspense fallbacks.

concepts.name: Testing components by behaviour
concepts.summary: Evaluate tests that exercise components through user-visible behaviour rather than implementation details.

misconceptions.text: Wrapping every component in memo and every function in useCallback always improves performance.
Context is a full state management replacement that never causes extra re-renders.
Error boundaries catch errors thrown in event handlers and async code.

concepts.name: Architecture of large React apps
concepts.summary: Design the structure of a large single-page app, including module boundaries, routing and state ownership.

concepts.name: State management strategy selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs between local state, context, external stores and server-state caching for a given application.

concepts.name: Concurrent rendering model
concepts.summary: Assess how interruptible rendering, transitions and deferred values affect responsiveness and component purity requirements.

concepts.name: Server rendering and hydration
concepts.summary: Evaluate client, server and hybrid rendering strategies and their effects on hydration, performance and complexity.

concepts.name: Design system component libraries
concepts.summary: Create a reusable, accessible, well-typed component library with stable APIs and versioning.

concepts.name: Performance and accessibility auditing
concepts.summary: Judge an app's rendering performance and accessibility with profiling data and audits and prioritise fixes.

concepts.name: Migration and refactoring strategy
concepts.summary: Plan incremental migration of class-based or legacy codebases to modern patterns with controlled risk.

misconceptions.text: A single global store is the best place for all application state.
Server rendering always improves performance and removes the need for client-side work.
Concurrent features make rendering faster by running code on parallel threads.

concepts.name: Major groups of microbes
concepts.summary: Name and distinguish bacteria, archaea, viruses, fungi, protozoa and algae by basic features such as size, cellular organisation and examples.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic cell structure
concepts.summary: Describe the bacterial cell envelope, nucleoid, ribosomes, flagella and pili and explain what each does.

concepts.name: Gram stain differences
concepts.summary: Explain how Gram-positive and Gram-negative walls differ and why this produces different staining results.

concepts.name: Bacterial binary fission
concepts.summary: Explain how bacteria divide by binary fission and why populations can grow exponentially.

concepts.name: Virus structure and nature
concepts.summary: Describe a virion as a nucleic acid genome in a protein capsid, sometimes enveloped, and explain why viruses need host cells to replicate.

concepts.name: Microscopy and staining basics
concepts.summary: Explain how light microscopy, simple staining and magnification reveal microbes.

concepts.name: Beneficial and harmful microbes
concepts.summary: Give examples of microbes that cause disease and others that aid digestion, food production and nutrient cycling.

concepts.name: Sterile technique principles
concepts.summary: Explain why contamination matters and how aseptic handling prevents it.

misconceptions.text: All bacteria are harmful germs that cause disease.
Viruses are just very small bacteria.
Gram-positive bacteria are those that cause disease, and Gram-negative ones are harmless.

concepts.name: Bacterial growth curve phases
concepts.summary: Interpret a growth curve and identify lag, exponential, stationary and death phases and what drives each.

concepts.name: Culture media types
concepts.summary: Choose among defined, complex, selective, differential and enriched media to grow or identify an organism.

concepts.name: Isolation by streak plating
concepts.summary: Use streaking and dilution to obtain isolated colonies and count them as colony forming units.

concepts.name: Environmental growth requirements
concepts.summary: Classify microbes by oxygen, temperature, pH and salt needs and predict where they can grow.

concepts.name: Energy and carbon nutritional types
concepts.summary: Classify organisms by energy and carbon source.

concepts.name: Fermentation versus respiration
concepts.summary: Compare aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration and fermentation in ATP yield and end products.

concepts.name: Viral replication cycle
concepts.summary: Apply the steps of attachment, entry, synthesis, assembly and release and contrast lytic with lysogenic cycles.

concepts.name: Physical and chemical microbial control
concepts.summary: Select heat, filtration, radiation, disinfectants or antiseptics for a given situation and distinguish sterilisation from disinfection.

misconceptions.text: Counting colonies on a plate gives the total number of cells, living and dead, in the sample.
Anaerobes are killed by any trace of oxygen and all non-aerobes behave the same way.
Disinfection and sterilisation mean the same thing.

concepts.name: Bacterial genome organisation
concepts.summary: Describe circular chromosomes, plasmids, operons and how they differ from eukaryotic genomes.

concepts.name: Operon gene regulation
concepts.summary: Analyse how repressors, inducers and catabolite repression control lac and trp operon expression under different conditions.

concepts.name: Horizontal gene transfer
concepts.summary: Distinguish the three mechanisms and analyse how each spreads traits like resistance.

concepts.name: Antimicrobial mechanisms of action
concepts.summary: Match antibiotic classes to targets such as cell wall, ribosome, folate synthesis and DNA replication, and explain selective toxicity.

concepts.name: Antibiotic resistance mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse how enzymatic inactivation, target modification, efflux and reduced uptake produce resistance and how selection spreads it.

concepts.name: Pathogenesis and virulence factors
concepts.summary: Analyse how adhesins, toxins, capsules and invasion factors contribute to infection, including exotoxin versus endotoxin.

concepts.name: Innate and adaptive host defence
concepts.summary: Apply knowledge of barriers, phagocytes, antibodies and T cells to explain responses to bacterial and viral infection.

concepts.name: Susceptibility testing
concepts.summary: Interpret minimum inhibitory concentration and zone of inhibition results.

misconceptions.text: Antibiotics create resistance in individual bacteria that then adapt in response to the drug.
Antibiotics are effective against viral infections such as colds.
A larger zone of inhibition always means a drug is better, regardless of the drug or organism.

concepts.name: Biofilm formation and tolerance
concepts.summary: Analyse how biofilm development, quorum sensing and matrix protection raise tolerance to antimicrobials and host defences.

concepts.name: Epidemiology of infectious disease
concepts.summary: Analyse transmission routes, reservoirs, R0 and herd immunity to interpret outbreak data.

concepts.name: Molecular diagnostic methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate culture, PCR, antigen, serological and sequencing methods for sensitivity, specificity and speed in a clinical scenario.

concepts.name: Vaccine design strategies
concepts.summary: Evaluate live attenuated, inactivated, subunit, conjugate and nucleic acid vaccines for safety and immune response.

concepts.name: Viral evolution and immune escape
concepts.summary: Analyse how mutation, reassortment and recombination drive variants and affect vaccine and drug strategies.

concepts.name: Microbiome and host interaction
concepts.summary: Analyse how commensals provide colonisation resistance and how dysbiosis or antibiotics contribute to disease.

concepts.name: Microbial ecology and biogeochemical cycles
concepts.summary: Analyse the microbial roles in nitrogen, carbon and sulfur cycles and in wastewater treatment.

concepts.name: Antimicrobial stewardship evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate treatment choices and policies to balance cure against selection of resistance.

misconceptions.text: A positive PCR result always means a viable, infectious organism is present.
Herd immunity requires everyone to be immune to protect the population.
Antibiotic courses should always be extended to prevent resistance, regardless of the infection.

concepts.name: Comparative genomics and phylogeny
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence from genome comparison, pan-genomes and phylogenies to infer evolution, outbreak linkage and gene transfer.

concepts.name: Metagenomic study design
concepts.summary: Design metagenomic or amplicon studies, controlling for bias and contamination, to characterise uncultured communities.

concepts.name: Genetic engineering of microbes
concepts.summary: Design engineered strains or pathways using plasmids and genome editing, including biocontainment considerations.

concepts.name: Novel antimicrobial strategy design
concepts.summary: Create approaches such as phage therapy, anti-virulence agents or combination regimens, justified by mechanism and resistance risk.

concepts.name: Evaluating causation in infection
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a microbe causes a disease using Koch's postulates and their molecular and metagenomic extensions.

concepts.name: Host-pathogen coevolution
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-off models of virulence and transmission and how host and pathogen adapt to each other.

concepts.name: Biosafety and risk assessment
concepts.summary: Judge biosafety levels, containment and dual-use risk for work with specific agents.

concepts.name: Experimental design in microbiology
concepts.summary: Design controlled, reproducible experiments and critique published microbiological evidence.

misconceptions.text: Virulent pathogens inevitably evolve to become harmless over time.
Detecting a microbe's DNA in diseased tissue proves it caused the disease.
Relative abundance from sequencing reflects the true absolute abundance of organisms in a sample.

concepts.name: File-based routing with app directory
concepts.summary: Understand that folders under app define URL segments and that a page file makes a segment publicly reachable.

concepts.name: Page and layout files
concepts.summary: Explain how page files render route UI and layout files wrap pages and persist across navigation.

concepts.name: Server Components by default
concepts.summary: Understand that components in the App Router render on the server by default and send no component JavaScript to the client.

concepts.name: Client Components and use client
concepts.summary: Recognise when the use client directive is needed, such as for state, effects and event handlers.

concepts.name: Navigation with next/link
concepts.summary: Use the Link component to navigate between routes without a full page reload.

concepts.name: Dynamic route segments
concepts.summary: Understand that a folder named in square brackets captures a URL part as a parameter.

concepts.name: Optimised images with next/image
concepts.summary: Remember that the Image component resizes, lazy-loads and serves modern formats and requires dimensions or fill to avoid layout shift.

misconceptions.text: Next.js is a separate language or replacement for React rather than a framework built on top of it.
Any file inside the app folder automatically becomes a route.
Every component needs use client to be interactive or to work at all.

concepts.name: Reading dynamic route params
concepts.summary: Access path params and search params in pages and use them to load the right data.

concepts.name: Async data fetching in server components
concepts.summary: Write async server components that await fetch calls or database queries directly.

concepts.name: Nested layouts and route groups
concepts.summary: Compose nested layouts and use route groups to organise routes or split layouts without changing URLs.

concepts.name: Loading and error UI files
concepts.summary: Apply special files to show loading states, handle errors and render not-found pages per segment.

concepts.name: Passing server data to client components
concepts.summary: Pass serialisable props from server to client components and compose them using children.

concepts.name: Metadata API
concepts.summary: Set static and dynamic page titles and descriptions using metadata exports.

concepts.name: Programmatic navigation hooks
concepts.summary: Use navigation hooks in client components and redirect in server code to change routes.

misconceptions.text: You must use useEffect to fetch data in the App Router.
Route groups in parentheses add a segment to the URL.
Any value, including functions, can be passed as props from a server to a client component.

concepts.name: Rendering strategies SSG SSR ISR
concepts.summary: Analyse a route's data needs to choose between static, dynamic and revalidated rendering.

concepts.name: Fetch caching and revalidation
concepts.summary: Control cache behaviour of data fetches with time-based and on-demand revalidation and reason about staleness.

concepts.name: Server Actions for mutations
concepts.summary: Implement mutations and form handling with server actions, including validation and revalidating affected data.

concepts.name: Route handlers
concepts.summary: Build HTTP endpoints with route files exporting method handlers and decide when they are preferable to server actions.

concepts.name: Streaming with Suspense
concepts.summary: Split slow data into Suspense boundaries so the page streams progressively.

concepts.name: Pages Router data functions
concepts.summary: Compare getServerSideProps and getStaticProps in the Pages Router with App Router equivalents to read and migrate legacy code.

concepts.name: Static params generation
concepts.summary: Prerender dynamic routes at build time and control behaviour for unlisted params.

concepts.name: Environment variables and exposure
concepts.summary: Keep secrets server-only and expose only NEXT_PUBLIC variables to the browser bundle.

misconceptions.text: getServerSideProps works inside app directory pages.
Server actions are only a convenience and do not create public endpoints needing authorisation checks.
ISR re-renders the page on every request so content is always fresh.

concepts.name: Middleware request interception
concepts.summary: Use middleware matchers to redirect, rewrite or modify headers and judge what belongs there versus in route code.

concepts.name: Authentication and authorisation placement
concepts.summary: Evaluate where to verify sessions so that data access is protected at the data layer rather than only in layouts or middleware.

concepts.name: Caching layers interplay
concepts.summary: Diagnose stale or unexpectedly dynamic output by tracing request memoisation, data cache, full route cache and client router cache.

concepts.name: Server and client boundary design
concepts.summary: Evaluate where to place client boundaries to minimise bundle size while preserving interactivity.

concepts.name: Performance optimisation
concepts.summary: Assess and improve LCP, CLS and INP using image, font and script optimisation and code splitting.

concepts.name: Runtimes Node and Edge
concepts.summary: Analyse the constraints of Edge versus Node runtimes for each route and choose accordingly.

concepts.name: Parallel and intercepting routes
concepts.summary: Model advanced UI patterns such as modals and dashboards using parallel slots and intercepting routes.

concepts.name: Vercel deployment and previews
concepts.summary: Analyse how a Next.js app maps onto Vercel serverless functions, static assets, preview deployments and environment scopes.

misconceptions.text: Checking authentication in a layout is enough to protect all data beneath it.
Middleware can run any Node API and is the right place for heavy logic like database queries.
Putting use client at the top of a page is harmless for performance.

concepts.name: Rendering architecture trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge static, dynamic and partially prerendered designs for a product by cost, freshness, latency and complexity.

concepts.name: Cache strategy design
concepts.summary: Design tag and path invalidation schemes across data sources, CDN and client so freshness guarantees are explicit.

concepts.name: Self-hosting and portability
concepts.summary: Evaluate running Next.js outside Vercel, including standalone output, shared caches across instances and platform feature gaps.

concepts.name: Monorepo and large-app structure
concepts.summary: Design project structure, shared packages and build pipelines that scale across teams.

concepts.name: Observability and failure handling
concepts.summary: Evaluate instrumentation, tracing and error boundaries to detect and diagnose production issues in server and client code.

concepts.name: Security hardening
concepts.summary: Assess threats such as data leakage across the server-client boundary, CSRF on actions and missing headers, and apply mitigations.

concepts.name: Migration strategy Pages to App
concepts.summary: Plan an incremental migration from Pages Router to App Router with coexistence, risk control and verification.

misconceptions.text: Next.js apps only run well on Vercel and cannot be self-hosted with full features.
Maximising static generation is always the best architecture regardless of data freshness needs.
A migration to the App Router must be done all at once because the two routers cannot coexist.

concepts.name: Pattern as reusable solution
concepts.summary: Recall that a design pattern is a named, proven solution template to a recurring design problem, not finished code or a library.

concepts.name: Problem, solution, consequences structure
concepts.summary: Explain that a pattern is described by the problem it addresses, the solution's structure and the trade-offs it brings.

concepts.name: Creational, structural, behavioural categories
concepts.summary: Recall the three classic categories and what kind of concern each groups: object creation, composition, and interaction.

concepts.name: Shared pattern vocabulary
concepts.summary: Explain how pattern names let developers communicate design intent concisely.

concepts.name: Coupling and flexibility motivation
concepts.summary: Understand that many patterns exist to reduce coupling between classes so that code is easier to change.

concepts.name: Interfaces and polymorphism in patterns
concepts.summary: Understand that most patterns rely on abstract types and polymorphism so callers depend on interfaces rather than concrete classes.

misconceptions.text: A design pattern is a ready-made piece of code or library you can copy in unchanged.
Using more patterns always makes a design better.
Patterns are specific to one programming language.

concepts.name: Factory Method and simple factory
concepts.summary: Implement a factory that hides which concrete class is created so client code depends only on an interface.

concepts.name: Observer subscription and notification
concepts.summary: Implement a subject that notifies registered observers of state changes without knowing their concrete types.

concepts.name: Strategy as interchangeable algorithms
concepts.summary: Encapsulate a family of algorithms behind one interface and swap them at runtime via composition.

concepts.name: Decorator wrapping behaviour
concepts.summary: Add responsibilities to an object dynamically by wrapping it in objects that share its interface.

concepts.name: Singleton and its drawbacks
concepts.summary: Explain how a singleton restricts a class to one instance and why global state makes it hard to test.

concepts.name: Composition over inheritance
concepts.summary: Apply object composition instead of subclassing to vary behaviour flexibly.

concepts.name: Reading UML class diagrams of patterns
concepts.summary: Interpret a class diagram of a pattern and map its roles to concrete classes.

misconceptions.text: Strategy and inheritance with overridden methods are the same thing.
Singleton is a harmless way to share data across the program.
A decorator must change the interface of the object it wraps.

concepts.name: Abstract Factory and Builder
concepts.summary: Choose between Abstract Factory for related product families and Builder for stepwise construction of complex objects.

concepts.name: Adapter versus Facade versus Proxy
concepts.summary: Distinguish wrapper patterns by intent: converting interfaces, simplifying subsystems, or controlling access.

concepts.name: Command and undo
concepts.summary: Encapsulate requests as objects to support queuing, logging and undoable operations.

concepts.name: State versus Strategy
concepts.summary: Analyse how State changes behaviour with internal transitions while Strategy is chosen externally despite similar structure.

concepts.name: Composite for tree structures
concepts.summary: Treat individual objects and groups uniformly through a shared component interface.

concepts.name: Template Method and hooks
concepts.summary: Define an algorithm skeleton in a base class while subclasses override specific steps.

concepts.name: Matching patterns to design problems
concepts.summary: Identify the force or smell in code, such as large conditionals or tight coupling, and select the pattern that addresses it.

concepts.name: Dependency injection and factories
concepts.summary: Pass dependencies in from outside, and decide when injection replaces a factory or singleton.

misconceptions.text: Adapter, Facade and Proxy are interchangeable because they all wrap another object.
State and Strategy are identical because their class diagrams look the same.
Dependency injection is just another name for the factory pattern.

concepts.name: Evaluating pattern trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge whether a pattern's added indirection and classes are justified by the actual variation and change expected.

concepts.name: Recognising overengineering
concepts.summary: Detect premature or unnecessary pattern use and decide to keep the simpler design.

concepts.name: Refactoring toward patterns
concepts.summary: Evolve existing code toward a pattern in small safe steps once duplication or rigidity appears.

concepts.name: Combining patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse how patterns cooperate, such as Composite with Visitor or Command with Memento, and where the combination adds complexity.

concepts.name: Patterns and language features
concepts.summary: Evaluate when first-class functions, closures, enums or generics make a classic pattern unnecessary.

concepts.name: Visitor and double dispatch
concepts.summary: Analyse how Visitor adds operations to a stable class hierarchy and the cost when the hierarchy changes.

concepts.name: Patterns and testability
concepts.summary: Assess how patterns affect isolation, mocking and test seams in a design.

misconceptions.text: A good design should apply a pattern wherever one could fit.
Visitor is always the right way to add new operations to a class hierarchy.
Patterns must be implemented exactly as the textbook class diagram shows.

concepts.name: Designing domain-specific patterns
concepts.summary: Distil a recurring problem in a domain into a new documented pattern with context, forces, solution and consequences.

concepts.name: Pattern languages and architecture
concepts.summary: Compose related patterns into a coherent language that guides design decisions across a system.

concepts.name: Critiquing pattern-heavy codebases
concepts.summary: Evaluate an existing codebase for misapplied, missing or accidental patterns and recommend changes.

concepts.name: Patterns across paradigms
concepts.summary: Judge how pattern intents translate to functional, concurrent and distributed contexts and where object-oriented forms fail.

concepts.name: Evolving designs under change
concepts.summary: Create designs that anticipate likely axes of change and decide which flexibility to build now versus defer.

concepts.name: Teaching and governing pattern use
concepts.summary: Establish team conventions, documentation and review practices that foster sound pattern use.

misconceptions.text: Patterns are a complete catalogue, so every design problem already has a named pattern.
Object-oriented patterns apply unchanged in functional and distributed systems.
Building maximum flexibility up front is the safest way to handle future change.

concepts.name: Regions and Availability Zones
concepts.summary: Explain that a region is a geographic area made of multiple isolated availability zones and why resources are placed in a specific region.

concepts.name: Console and account root user
concepts.summary: Recognise how to sign in to the console, find services, and know that the root user is a special all-powerful identity to be protected.

concepts.name: EC2 instances and AMIs
concepts.summary: Describe an EC2 instance as a virtual server launched from an AMI with a chosen instance type.

concepts.name: S3 buckets and objects
concepts.summary: Explain that S3 stores objects identified by keys inside globally uniquely named buckets rather than files in a filesystem.

concepts.name: IAM users and permissions
concepts.summary: Understand that IAM controls who can do what in an account and that new users start with no permissions.

concepts.name: Managed service categories
concepts.summary: Name which AWS service fits each broad role: RDS and DynamoDB for databases, Lambda for serverless code, CloudFront for content delivery, Route 53 for DNS, CloudWatch for monitoring.

concepts.name: Pay-as-you-go billing and Free Tier
concepts.summary: Understand that resources incur charges while running or stored and that the Free Tier has limits.

misconceptions.text: Resources created in one region automatically appear and work in every other region.
Stopping or ignoring a resource means AWS charges nothing for it.
The root user should be used for everyday administration.

concepts.name: AWS CLI configuration and use
concepts.summary: Configure credentials and a default region with profiles and run commands such as listing buckets or describing instances.

concepts.name: Launching and connecting to EC2
concepts.summary: Launch an instance with a key pair and security group, connect over SSH, and stop, start or terminate it.

concepts.name: Security groups
concepts.summary: Write inbound and outbound rules that allow only needed ports and sources, knowing groups are stateful allow-lists.

concepts.name: S3 access and storage classes
concepts.summary: Upload and retrieve objects, keep buckets private by default, enable versioning, and choose a storage class by access pattern.

concepts.name: IAM policies and groups
concepts.summary: Attach policies with Effect, Action and Resource to groups and users to grant least privilege for simple tasks.

concepts.name: Basic RDS and DynamoDB use
concepts.summary: Create a managed relational database or a DynamoDB table and connect an application to it.

concepts.name: CloudWatch metrics and alarms
concepts.summary: View built-in metrics and logs and set an alarm on a threshold such as CPU utilisation.

concepts.name: Simple Lambda functions
concepts.summary: Write and invoke a small function triggered by an event such as an S3 upload.

misconceptions.text: Opening a security group to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports is an acceptable way to get things working.
Putting access keys in code or on an instance is a normal way to authenticate.
Data on an EC2 instance's instance store or terminated root volume is always preserved.

concepts.name: VPC design with subnets and routing
concepts.summary: Build a VPC with public and private subnets across AZs, route tables, an internet gateway and NAT gateway.

concepts.name: IAM roles and temporary credentials
concepts.summary: Analyse when to use roles with trust policies so services and applications get temporary credentials instead of long-lived keys.

concepts.name: Load balancing and Auto Scaling
concepts.summary: Distribute traffic across instances in multiple AZs and scale capacity by policy using health checks.

concepts.name: Route 53 routing and DNS records
concepts.summary: Configure hosted zones and records with alias targets and choose simple, weighted, latency or failover routing.

concepts.name: CloudFront distribution with S3 origin
concepts.summary: Serve content through CloudFront with caching behaviours, origin access control and HTTPS.

concepts.name: RDS high availability and backups
concepts.summary: Distinguish Multi-AZ failover from read replicas and plan automated backups and restores.

concepts.name: DynamoDB key and access design
concepts.summary: Choose partition and sort keys from access patterns and pick on-demand or provisioned capacity.

concepts.name: Logs-based troubleshooting with CloudWatch
concepts.summary: Use logs, metrics and alarms together to diagnose failures in deployed applications.

misconceptions.text: A subnet is public simply because it is named public, regardless of its route table.
A Multi-AZ RDS standby can be used to serve read traffic and improve read performance.
DynamoDB can be modelled like a relational database and queried flexibly on any attribute efficiently.

concepts.name: Least-privilege policy evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how identity policies, resource policies, boundaries and organisation SCPs combine, with explicit deny winning, and tighten policies accordingly.

concepts.name: Multi-AZ resilient architecture
concepts.summary: Assess an architecture for single points of failure and choose redundancy across AZs and regions to meet availability goals.

concepts.name: Infrastructure as code with CloudFormation
concepts.summary: Define environments as templates, review change sets, and reason about stack updates and drift.

concepts.name: Serverless event-driven design
aliases: Lambda with SQS SNS API Gateway
concepts.summary: Judge when to use Lambda with queues, topics and APIs, accounting for concurrency, timeouts and cold starts.

concepts.name: Encryption and key management
aliases: encryption at rest and in transit
concepts.summary: Evaluate use of KMS keys, key policies and TLS to protect data in S3, RDS and DynamoDB.

concepts.name: Cost analysis and optimisation
concepts.summary: Compare on-demand, Savings Plans and Spot options, right-size resources, and use cost tools to find waste.

concepts.name: Private connectivity and VPC endpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse ways to connect VPCs and reach AWS services privately without traversing the internet.

concepts.name: Observability and audit trails
concepts.summary: Combine metrics, logs, traces and CloudTrail records to detect problems and investigate changes.

misconceptions.text: An Allow in any attached policy is enough to grant access even if another policy explicitly denies it.
Spreading instances across multiple AZs alone makes an application fully highly available.
Serverless functions scale without limit and cost less than other options in every workload.

concepts.name: Multi-account governance strategy
concepts.summary: Design an account structure with organisational units, SCP guardrails, centralised logging and identity federation.

concepts.name: Disaster recovery strategy selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate backup-restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active designs against RPO, RTO and cost.

concepts.name: Well-Architected trade-off review
concepts.summary: Critique a workload across the pillars and justify trade-offs between reliability, security, performance, cost and operations.

concepts.name: Global architecture design
concepts.summary: Create multi-region designs combining Route 53, CloudFront and replicated data stores, accounting for consistency and failover.

concepts.name: Secure CI/CD and deployment pipelines
concepts.summary: Design automated pipelines with safe rollout strategies, scoped deployment roles and rollback.

concepts.name: Threat detection and incident response
concepts.summary: Evaluate detective controls and construct response runbooks for compromised credentials or exposed resources.

concepts.name: Scaling limits and performance tuning
concepts.summary: Diagnose bottlenecks from quotas, throttling and data distribution and redesign to remove them.

misconceptions.text: Having Multi-AZ resources removes the need for a cross-region disaster recovery plan.
Active-active multi-region is always the best design regardless of cost and complexity.
Tight perimeter controls make detective monitoring and incident runbooks unnecessary.

concepts.name: Differential equation and its order
concepts.summary: Recognise an equation containing an unknown function and its derivatives and state its order and whether it is ordinary.

concepts.name: Solutions as functions
concepts.summary: Understand that a solution is a function that satisfies the equation, and check a candidate by substituting it and its derivatives.

concepts.name: General versus particular solution
concepts.summary: Explain that integration introduces arbitrary constants giving a family of solutions, and that a particular solution picks one member.

concepts.name: Initial value problem
concepts.summary: Describe how an initial condition fixes the constant and selects a single solution curve.

concepts.name: Direction field reading
concepts.summary: Interpret a slope field as showing the slope y' at each point and sketch how solution curves follow the arrows.

concepts.name: Rate-of-change modelling statements
concepts.summary: Understand that a statement like 'rate proportional to amount' translates into an equation such as dy/dt = ky.

misconceptions.text: A differential equation has one single answer number rather than a function or family of functions.
The order of a differential equation is the highest power of the unknown function or derivative rather than the highest derivative.
The arbitrary constant can be dropped because it does not affect the solution.

concepts.name: Separation of variables
concepts.summary: Solve dy/dx = f(x)g(y) by moving each variable to one side and integrating both sides.

concepts.name: Exponential growth and decay
concepts.summary: Apply y = y0 e^{kt} to population, radioactive decay and similar problems, determining k from data.

concepts.name: First-order linear form
concepts.summary: Rewrite a first-order equation into standard linear form and identify p(x) and q(x).

concepts.name: Integrating factor method
concepts.summary: Multiply by e^{∫p dx} so the left side becomes a product-rule derivative, then integrate to solve.

concepts.name: Equilibrium solutions
concepts.summary: Find constant solutions of an autonomous equation by setting y' = 0 and recognise those lost when dividing during separation.

concepts.name: Solving initial value problems
concepts.summary: Use the initial condition to find the constant in the general solution of a first-order equation.

concepts.name: Mixing tank models
concepts.summary: Set up and solve dQ/dt = rate in − rate out for a well-stirred tank with constant flows.

misconceptions.text: After separating variables you can integrate only one side and put the constant anywhere without consequence.
The integrating factor method works without first putting the equation in standard form with y' having coefficient 1.
In a mixing problem the outflow concentration equals the inflow concentration.

concepts.name: Exact equations and potential functions
concepts.summary: Test exactness with M_y = N_x and construct the potential function F whose level curves are the solutions.

concepts.name: Existence and uniqueness theorem
concepts.summary: Analyse when an IVP has a unique solution using continuity of f and ∂f/∂y, and find the interval on which it exists.

concepts.name: Characteristic equation method
concepts.summary: Solve ay'' + by' + cy = 0 using roots of the characteristic polynomial: real distinct, repeated or complex.

concepts.name: Superposition and linear independence
concepts.summary: Use the Wronskian to decide whether two solutions form a fundamental set and build the general solution from them.

concepts.name: Undetermined coefficients
concepts.summary: Find a particular solution of a nonhomogeneous equation by guessing a form based on the forcing term, adjusting for resonance with the homogeneous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative analysis of autonomous equations
concepts.summary: Use a phase line to classify equilibria as stable, unstable or semi-stable and predict long-term behaviour.

concepts.name: Spring-mass oscillator model
concepts.summary: Relate the roots of the characteristic equation to undamped, underdamped, critically damped and overdamped motion.

misconceptions.text: Any equation M dx + N dy = 0 can be solved by integrating M with respect to x and N with respect to y and adding the results.
Every IVP has a solution defined for all x.
A repeated root of the characteristic equation gives only one solution, so the general solution has a single constant.

concepts.name: Laplace transform definition and properties
concepts.summary: Compute transforms from the integral definition and using linearity, the first shifting theorem and transforms of derivatives.

concepts.name: Solving IVPs by Laplace transform
concepts.summary: Transform an IVP into an algebraic equation in s, solve it, and invert using partial fractions and tables.

concepts.name: Discontinuous and impulsive forcing
concepts.summary: Model switched and impulsive inputs with unit step and delta functions and solve the resulting problems with transforms.

concepts.name: Convolution and transfer function
concepts.summary: Express the response of a linear system to arbitrary forcing as a convolution with the impulse response and interpret the transfer function.

concepts.name: Variation of parameters
aliases: particular solution by variation of parameters
concepts.summary: Construct a particular solution for general forcing using the Wronskian when undetermined coefficients does not apply.

concepts.name: Resonance and forced oscillation analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate how forcing frequency and damping determine amplitude, beats, resonance and transient versus steady-state behaviour.
