concepts.name: Choosing a solution method
concepts.summary: Judge which technique (separable, linear, exact, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Laplace) is most efficient for a given equation and justify it.

misconceptions.text: The Laplace transform of a product of functions is the product of their transforms.
Laplace transforms only work for homogeneous equations or only for zero initial conditions.
Resonance occurs for any forcing frequency whenever damping is present, giving unbounded growth.

concepts.name: Systems of linear ODEs
concepts.summary: Evaluate solution structure of x' = Ax through eigenvalues and eigenvectors and relate it to higher-order equations.

concepts.name: Phase plane classification
concepts.summary: Judge stability and equilibrium type from trace and determinant of the system matrix.

concepts.name: Linearisation of nonlinear systems
concepts.summary: Assess local behaviour near equilibria of nonlinear systems via the Jacobian and recognise when linearisation is inconclusive.

concepts.name: Power series solutions
concepts.summary: Derive series solutions about ordinary points via recurrence relations and evaluate their radius of convergence.

concepts.name: Numerical method error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate the accuracy, order and stability of Euler and Runge–Kutta schemes and diagnose stiff problems.

concepts.name: Constructing models from phenomena
concepts.summary: Design ODE models such as logistic growth with harvesting or predator-prey, justify assumptions and analyse their predictions.

concepts.name: Bifurcation analysis
concepts.summary: Create bifurcation diagrams showing how equilibria and their stability change with a parameter.

misconceptions.text: Linearisation always determines the stability of a nonlinear equilibrium, including centres.
A smaller step size always makes a numerical ODE solver more accurate and stable regardless of the method.
A fitted ODE model that matches observed data is therefore a correct description of the underlying mechanism.

concepts.name: Floating-point representation
concepts.summary: Explain that computers store reals as finite-precision binary floating-point numbers with limited range and spacing, so most reals are only approximated.

concepts.name: Absolute and relative error
concepts.summary: Define and compute absolute and relative error between an exact and an approximate value.

concepts.name: Round-off versus truncation error
concepts.summary: Distinguish errors from finite-precision arithmetic from errors caused by approximating a process with a finite one.

concepts.name: Iterative approximation idea
concepts.summary: Understand that many problems are solved by generating a sequence of improving approximations until a stopping tolerance is met.

concepts.name: Bisection method
concepts.summary: Explain how bisection brackets a root of a continuous function with a sign change and halves the interval each step.

concepts.name: Machine epsilon
concepts.summary: Recall that machine epsilon gives the relative spacing of floating-point numbers near 1 and bounds relative rounding error.

misconceptions.text: Computers represent decimal numbers like 0.1 exactly.
A smaller absolute error always means a more accurate answer regardless of the size of the true value.
Round-off and truncation error are the same thing and both vanish with a better algorithm.

concepts.name: Newton's method for roots
concepts.summary: Implement Newton's iteration using the derivative and recognise when it converges quickly or fails.

concepts.name: Secant method
concepts.summary: Apply the secant iteration to find roots without computing derivatives.

concepts.name: Convergence tolerance and stopping criteria
concepts.summary: Choose and implement stopping tests based on step size, residual and iteration limits.

concepts.name: Polynomial interpolation
concepts.summary: Construct the polynomial through given data points using Lagrange or Newton form.

concepts.name: Trapezoidal and Simpson rules
concepts.summary: Approximate definite integrals with the composite trapezoidal and Simpson rules.

concepts.name: Finite difference derivatives
concepts.summary: Approximate derivatives with forward, backward and central difference formulas.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.summary: Solve a linear system by forward elimination and back substitution.

misconceptions.text: Newton's method converges to a root from any starting guess.
Making the step size h in a finite difference as small as possible always gives the best derivative estimate.
A small difference between successive iterates guarantees a small error in the root.

concepts.name: Order of convergence analysis
concepts.summary: Determine and compare linear, superlinear and quadratic convergence of iterative methods from error sequences.

concepts.name: Truncation error via Taylor series
concepts.summary: Derive error orders of difference and quadrature formulas using Taylor expansions.

concepts.name: LU factorization with pivoting
concepts.summary: Factor a matrix as PA=LU and reuse the factors to solve multiple right-hand sides while avoiding unstable pivots.

concepts.name: Condition number
concepts.summary: Analyse how sensitive a problem's output is to input perturbations, including matrix condition number.

concepts.name: Numerical stability of algorithms
concepts.summary: Distinguish ill-conditioned problems from unstable algorithms and identify causes such as cancellation.

concepts.name: Splines and interpolation error
concepts.summary: Explain why high-degree equispaced polynomial interpolation oscillates and when piecewise splines are preferable.

concepts.name: Gaussian quadrature
concepts.summary: Apply Gauss-Legendre rules and explain why optimally placed nodes give higher exactness degree.

concepts.name: Iterative linear solvers
concepts.summary: Implement Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterations and check convergence via diagonal dominance.

misconceptions.text: A tiny residual guarantees an accurate solution of a linear system.
Using higher-degree interpolating polynomials always improves accuracy.
Gaussian elimination without pivoting is safe whenever the matrix is nonsingular.

concepts.name: Error budgeting and method selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing methods against accuracy, cost, robustness and problem structure and justify a choice.

concepts.name: Adaptive quadrature
concepts.summary: Analyse how error estimates drive adaptive subdivision for integrands with local difficulty.

concepts.name: Hybrid root finders
concepts.summary: Evaluate combinations of bracketing and fast methods that retain guaranteed convergence.

concepts.name: Krylov and conjugate gradient methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how Krylov subspace methods solve large sparse systems and how convergence depends on spectrum.

concepts.name: Preconditioning
concepts.summary: Evaluate preconditioners that reduce effective condition number to speed iterative convergence.

concepts.name: Least squares via QR and SVD
concepts.summary: Compare normal equations, QR and SVD for least squares in terms of stability and rank deficiency.

concepts.name: Sparse matrix computation
concepts.summary: Analyse storage formats and fill-in effects on cost of direct solvers for sparse systems.

concepts.name: Richardson extrapolation
concepts.summary: Use error expansions to combine coarse and fine results into higher-order estimates and diagnose convergence.

misconceptions.text: Solving least squares through the normal equations is as accurate as QR.
Conjugate gradient works for any square matrix.
Adaptive methods always beat fixed-step methods regardless of integrand smoothness or cost.

concepts.name: Backward error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate algorithms by proving or assessing that computed results are exact for slightly perturbed inputs.

concepts.name: Verification and validation of numerics
concepts.summary: Design convergence studies and tests with known solutions to verify implementations and error claims.

concepts.name: Designing custom numerical algorithms
concepts.summary: Create tailored schemes that exploit problem structure such as symmetry, singularities or oscillation.

concepts.name: Mixed-precision strategies
concepts.summary: Design workflows combining low- and high-precision arithmetic, such as iterative refinement, balancing speed and accuracy.

concepts.name: Eigenvalue algorithms
concepts.summary: Evaluate power, inverse and QR-based eigenvalue methods for accuracy, cost and structure.

concepts.name: Interval and rigorous error bounds
concepts.summary: Assess when guaranteed enclosures are needed and what they cost compared to heuristic error estimates.

concepts.name: Performance-aware numerical software
concepts.summary: Create implementations that balance accuracy with memory access, parallelism and library use such as BLAS and LAPACK.

misconceptions.text: Double precision is always enough, so numerical error can be ignored in production code.
If a convergence plot shows the expected order, the implementation is proven correct.
Hand-written algorithms are generally preferable to established libraries for performance.

concepts.name: Neuron structure and parts
concepts.summary: Name and describe the roles of the soma, dendrites, axon, myelin sheath and axon terminals.

concepts.name: Glial cell roles
concepts.summary: Recall that glia support neurons through insulation, metabolic support, immune defence and homeostasis.

concepts.name: Resting membrane potential
concepts.summary: Explain that neurons maintain a negative voltage across the membrane through ion gradients and the sodium-potassium pump.

concepts.name: Action potential sequence
concepts.summary: Describe the all-or-none spike as depolarisation, repolarisation and refractory recovery driven by ion flow.

concepts.name: Chemical synapse transmission
concepts.summary: Explain how an impulse triggers neurotransmitter release, receptor binding and a postsynaptic response.

concepts.name: Major neurotransmitters and roles
concepts.summary: Match glutamate, GABA, dopamine, serotonin and acetylcholine to their typical functions.

concepts.name: Central and peripheral nervous systems
concepts.summary: Distinguish the brain and spinal cord from peripheral nerves and the somatic and autonomic divisions.

concepts.name: Main brain regions and functions
concepts.summary: Link the cortex lobes, cerebellum, hippocampus, amygdala and brainstem to their broad functions.

misconceptions.text: Humans use only 10% of their brains.
Neurons physically touch each other and pass electrical current directly at every connection.
Glial cells are just passive filler with no role in brain function.

concepts.name: Ion channels and the Nernst potential
concepts.summary: Use ion concentration gradients to predict the direction of ion flow and equilibrium potentials for Na+ and K+.

concepts.name: Voltage-gated channel dynamics
concepts.summary: Apply channel opening and inactivation to explain the phases of the action potential and the refractory period.

concepts.name: Saltatory conduction
concepts.summary: Explain how myelin and nodes of Ranvier speed conduction and what happens in demyelination.

concepts.name: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials
concepts.summary: Predict whether a given neurotransmitter-receptor pair moves the membrane toward or away from threshold.

concepts.name: Ionotropic versus metabotropic receptors
concepts.summary: Contrast fast channel receptors with slower G-protein-coupled receptors in terms of speed and effect.

concepts.name: Sensory transduction and pathways
concepts.summary: Trace how a stimulus is converted to neural signals and relayed via the thalamus to primary sensory cortex.

concepts.name: Reflex arc and motor pathway
concepts.summary: Trace the path of a simple spinal reflex and distinguish upper from lower motor neurons.

concepts.name: Autonomic sympathetic and parasympathetic
concepts.summary: Predict bodily effects of sympathetic versus parasympathetic activation.

misconceptions.text: A stronger stimulus produces a bigger action potential.
Glutamate is always excitatory and GABA always inhibitory regardless of receptor type.
Sensory information from the body always goes to the cortex on the same side without crossing.

concepts.name: Synaptic integration
concepts.summary: Work out whether a neuron fires by combining spatial and temporal summation of inputs at the axon hillock.

concepts.name: Cable properties and length constant
concepts.summary: Analyse how membrane resistance, capacitance and axon diameter shape signal spread and conduction velocity.

concepts.name: Long-term potentiation and depression
concepts.summary: Analyse how NMDA receptor coincidence detection and AMPA receptor changes strengthen or weaken synapses.

concepts.name: Hebbian and spike-timing plasticity
concepts.summary: Apply the rule that correlated activity strengthens connections to predict synaptic changes.

concepts.name: Hippocampus and memory systems
concepts.summary: Distinguish memory types and match them to hippocampal, striatal, cerebellar and amygdala involvement using patient evidence such as H.M.

concepts.name: Basal ganglia and cerebellar motor control
concepts.summary: Contrast basal ganglia action selection with cerebellar error correction and relate them to Parkinson's disease and ataxia.

concepts.name: Cortical organisation and maps
concepts.summary: Use receptive fields, topographic maps and hierarchical visual processing to explain perception.

concepts.name: EEG and fMRI signal basis
concepts.summary: Analyse what EEG and fMRI BOLD actually measure and their trade-offs in temporal and spatial resolution.

misconceptions.text: fMRI directly measures neuronal firing.
Memories are stored in the hippocampus permanently.
The cerebellum is involved only in movement and the basal ganglia only in initiating movement.

concepts.name: Neural circuit motifs
concepts.summary: Analyse how feedforward, feedback and lateral inhibition and recurrent excitation shape circuit computation.

concepts.name: Systems consolidation and reconsolidation
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for hippocampal-neocortical transfer, replay during sleep and memory reconsolidation.

concepts.name: Neural coding schemes
concepts.summary: Compare rate, temporal and population codes and tuning curves as accounts of how information is represented.

concepts.name: Reward prediction error in dopamine
concepts.summary: Evaluate the claim that dopamine neurons encode reward prediction error and its role in basal ganglia learning.

concepts.name: Amygdala and emotional learning
concepts.summary: Analyse amygdala circuits in fear conditioning and extinction and their interaction with prefrontal cortex.

concepts.name: Experimental design in neuroimaging
concepts.summary: Evaluate the validity of neuroimaging claims, including reverse inference, multiple comparisons and confounds.

concepts.name: Causal tools: lesions, stimulation, optogenetics
concepts.summary: Evaluate which manipulation or recording method best supports a causal claim about a circuit.

concepts.name: Perceptual inference and attention
concepts.summary: Analyse how top-down signals and attention modulate sensory processing and perceptual illusions.

misconceptions.text: Dopamine is simply the brain's pleasure chemical.
If a brain region activates during a task, it must be the region for that mental process.
Perception is a passive bottom-up readout of sensory input.

concepts.name: Computational models of neurons
concepts.summary: Build and fit conductance-based or simplified spiking models to explain or predict neural dynamics.

concepts.name: Network models of memory
concepts.summary: Design network models such as attractors or complementary learning systems that capture plasticity and memory phenomena.

concepts.name: Critique of neuroscience evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate claims for statistical power, circularity, small samples and generalisation from animal models to humans.

concepts.name: Neural population dynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate analyses that infer computation from low-dimensional population activity.

concepts.name: Experiment design for circuits
concepts.summary: Design experiments combining recording, perturbation and behaviour to test competing circuit hypotheses.

concepts.name: Homeostatic and structural plasticity
concepts.summary: Evaluate how homeostatic mechanisms, critical periods and adult neurogenesis stabilise or reshape circuits.

concepts.name: Integrating theories of cognition
concepts.summary: Compare theoretical frameworks such as predictive coding and Bayesian inference against empirical evidence.

concepts.name: Translational neurotherapeutics
concepts.summary: Propose mechanism-based interventions for disorders using knowledge of circuits, receptors and neuromodulation.

misconceptions.text: A model that fits the data well proves the brain implements that mechanism.
Findings in rodents transfer directly to human brain function and treatment.
Low-dimensional population structure shows the brain computes in that space rather than reflecting analysis choices.

concepts.name: Weather versus climate
concepts.summary: Explain that weather is short-term atmospheric conditions while climate is the long-term statistical pattern over decades.

concepts.name: Components of climate system
concepts.summary: Name the atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, lithosphere and biosphere and state that they interact to shape climate.

concepts.name: Natural greenhouse effect
concepts.summary: Describe how greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, keeping Earth's surface warmer than it would otherwise be.

concepts.name: Major greenhouse gases
concepts.summary: Identify water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and their main natural and human sources.

concepts.name: Solar radiation as energy source
concepts.summary: Explain that the Sun supplies nearly all of Earth's climate energy and that latitude causes uneven heating.

concepts.name: Observed global warming
concepts.summary: State that global average surface temperature has risen by roughly 1.1 °C since the late 1800s.

concepts.name: Fossil fuel emissions
concepts.summary: Explain that burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide and is the main driver of recent warming.

misconceptions.text: A single cold winter or snowstorm disproves global warming.
The greenhouse effect is itself harmful and would not exist without human activity.
The ozone hole is the main cause of global warming.

concepts.name: Earth's energy balance
concepts.summary: Apply the idea that incoming absorbed sunlight equals outgoing infrared at equilibrium to reason about warming or cooling.

concepts.name: Albedo and reflectivity
concepts.summary: Use albedo values of ice, ocean, forest and clouds to predict how surface changes alter absorbed sunlight.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle reservoirs and fluxes
concepts.summary: Trace carbon among atmosphere, oceans, biosphere, soils and rocks and distinguish fast from slow exchanges.

concepts.name: Ocean heat and circulation
concepts.summary: Explain how oceans absorb most excess heat and redistribute it through currents.

concepts.name: Instrumental temperature record
concepts.summary: Read a temperature anomaly graph relative to a baseline and describe the long-term trend despite year-to-year variability.

concepts.name: Ice cores and proxy records
concepts.summary: Explain how ice cores, tree rings and sediments record past temperature and atmospheric composition.

concepts.name: Ocean acidification
concepts.summary: Apply carbonate chemistry to explain how dissolved CO2 lowers ocean pH and harms shell-forming organisms.

concepts.name: Sea level rise drivers
concepts.summary: Distinguish thermal expansion, land-ice melt and sea-ice melt as contributors to sea level change.

misconceptions.text: Melting sea ice raises sea level in the same way as melting land ice.
Ocean acidification means the ocean has become acidic with pH below 7.
Plants and oceans will absorb all the extra CO2 so atmospheric levels cannot keep rising.

concepts.name: Radiative forcing
concepts.summary: Quantify and compare forcings in W/m² from greenhouse gases, aerosols and solar changes.

concepts.name: Climate feedback mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse water vapour, ice-albedo, cloud and lapse-rate feedbacks and whether each amplifies or damps warming.

concepts.name: Climate sensitivity
concepts.summary: Interpret equilibrium and transient sensitivity as the warming response to doubled CO2 and its uncertainty range.

concepts.name: Attribution of recent warming
concepts.summary: Use fingerprints such as stratospheric cooling and hemispheric patterns to show that human activity, not natural causes, drives warming.

concepts.name: Milankovitch orbital cycles
concepts.summary: Explain how orbital variations pace glacial and interglacial cycles and why they cannot explain current warming.

concepts.name: Aerosols and volcanic effects
concepts.summary: Analyse how sulfate aerosols reflect sunlight and mask part of greenhouse warming.

concepts.name: Climate modelling basics
concepts.summary: Describe how models discretise physics on grids, are validated by hindcasts, and project scenarios.

concepts.name: Emissions scenarios and pathways
concepts.summary: Relate scenarios of emissions and socioeconomic development to projected concentration and temperature outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Past natural climate change shows that current warming must also be natural.
Climate models are just extrapolations of past trends rather than physics-based simulations.
Water vapour is the main cause of warming, so CO2 does not matter.

concepts.name: Carbon budget and cumulative emissions
concepts.summary: Analyse the near-linear relationship between cumulative CO2 emissions and warming to derive budgets for temperature targets.

concepts.name: Tipping points and abrupt change
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence and thresholds for ice sheet collapse, AMOC weakening, permafrost and Amazon dieback.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle feedbacks
concepts.summary: Analyse how warming alters natural sinks and releases carbon, changing airborne fraction.

concepts.name: Extreme event attribution
concepts.summary: Evaluate how studies estimate changes in the likelihood and intensity of heatwaves, floods and storms due to warming.

concepts.name: Regional climate projections and downscaling
concepts.summary: Analyse how precipitation, monsoon and drought changes differ regionally and the uncertainty in regional projections.

concepts.name: Paleoclimate analogues
concepts.summary: Evaluate how past warm and cold periods constrain sensitivity and show rates and impacts of change.

concepts.name: Uncertainty and model ensembles
concepts.summary: Evaluate sources of projection uncertainty (scenario, model, internal variability) and how ensembles represent them.

concepts.name: Mitigation and carbon removal pathways
concepts.summary: Evaluate how emission pathways, net zero and carbon dioxide removal relate to temperature outcomes.

misconceptions.text: Warming will stop soon after emissions fall to zero-growth levels, so cutting emission growth is enough.
Uncertainty in projections means scientists do not know whether serious impacts will occur.
Attribution studies claim a single extreme event was caused solely by climate change.

concepts.name: Constraining sensitivity with multiple evidence
concepts.summary: Critically combine process understanding, historical and paleo evidence and emergent constraints to judge sensitivity estimates.

concepts.name: Cloud feedback uncertainty
concepts.summary: Evaluate why cloud responses dominate sensitivity spread and which observations and process studies could reduce it.

concepts.name: Design of climate experiments
concepts.summary: Design model or observational experiments that isolate forcings, feedbacks or variability to test a specific hypothesis.

concepts.name: Pattern effects and ocean variability
concepts.summary: Assess how evolving ocean warming patterns and decadal variability influence feedbacks and the interpretation of trends.

concepts.name: Solar and aerosol geoengineering assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate the physical effects, risks and termination hazards of proposed climate interventions.

concepts.name: Integrated climate risk assessment
concepts.summary: Synthesise hazard, exposure, vulnerability and uncertainty to build a risk assessment for a region or sector.

concepts.name: Evaluation of climate evidence claims
concepts.summary: Appraise datasets, methods and claims, including homogenisation and contrarian arguments, against the weight of evidence.

misconceptions.text: Cloud feedbacks are so uncertain that sensitivity is essentially unconstrained.
Geoengineering by reflecting sunlight would fully offset the effects of CO2 including ocean acidification.
A pause or slowdown in surface warming over a decade disproves the long-term forced trend.

concepts.name: Authentication versus authorization
concepts.summary: Explain that authentication verifies who a user is while authorization decides what that verified user may do.

concepts.name: Credentials and authentication factors
concepts.summary: Recall that credentials such as passwords, devices and biometrics are grouped into knowledge, possession and inherence factors.

concepts.name: Why passwords are hashed
concepts.summary: Explain why a server stores a one-way hash of a password rather than the password itself.

concepts.name: Session as login memory
concepts.summary: Understand that because HTTP is stateless, a server issues an identifier after login so later requests are recognised as the same user.

concepts.name: Cookies carrying session identifiers
concepts.summary: Recall that a browser stores a session identifier in a cookie and sends it automatically with each request to that site.

concepts.name: Least privilege principle
concepts.summary: Explain why users and processes should receive only the permissions they need.

concepts.name: Multi-factor authentication purpose
concepts.summary: Understand that requiring a second independent factor limits damage when a password is stolen.

misconceptions.text: Authentication and authorization are two names for the same thing.
Encrypting passwords and hashing them are the same, and a site should be able to show you your original password.
Once a user is logged in, the server automatically knows who they are on every request without any identifier being sent.

concepts.name: Salted password hashing
concepts.summary: Apply a unique random salt per password so identical passwords produce different hashes and precomputed tables fail.

concepts.name: Slow adaptive hash functions
concepts.summary: Choose a deliberately slow, tunable password hashing function instead of a fast general-purpose hash.

concepts.name: Login flow implementation
concepts.summary: Implement a login endpoint that verifies a hash, creates a session and returns uniform error messages.

concepts.name: Secure cookie attributes
concepts.summary: Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite on session cookies and explain the threat each one reduces.

concepts.name: Session lifecycle management
concepts.summary: Create, expire and destroy sessions on the server so logout and timeouts truly end access.

concepts.name: Server-side permission checks
concepts.summary: Apply an authorization check on the server for every protected request rather than relying on hidden interface elements.

concepts.name: Role-based access control basics
concepts.summary: Understand how assigning users to roles that bundle permissions simplifies access decisions.

misconceptions.text: Hashing passwords with SHA-256 is as good as bcrypt because both are secure hashes.
A salt must be kept secret to be effective.
Hiding a button or menu link from unauthorised users is enough to protect a feature.

concepts.name: Session fixation and hijacking defenses
concepts.summary: Analyse how session identifiers are stolen or imposed and apply regeneration on login, entropy and transport protection.

concepts.name: CSRF protection mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse why cookie-based authentication enables cross-site request forgery and choose tokens or SameSite policies to counter it.

concepts.name: Token-based authentication with JWT
concepts.summary: Apply signed tokens carrying claims, validating signature, algorithm, expiry and audience on each request.

concepts.name: Access and refresh token tradeoffs
concepts.summary: Compare stateless tokens with server sessions, including revocation difficulty and the use of short-lived access with refresh tokens.

concepts.name: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
concepts.summary: Apply the authorization code flow with PKCE, identifying the resource owner, client, authorization server and resource server.

concepts.name: OpenID Connect for login
concepts.summary: Distinguish OAuth authorization from OpenID Connect authentication and validate an ID token for sign-in.

concepts.name: Broken access control analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse code for missing ownership and role checks that allow users to reach other users' resources.

concepts.name: Brute force and credential stuffing defense
concepts.summary: Analyse automated guessing attacks and weigh rate limiting, lockout and breached-password checks as defenses.

misconceptions.text: A JWT is encrypted, so its contents are hidden from anyone who holds it.
OAuth 2.0 is an authentication protocol that proves who the user is.
Storing a JWT in local storage is safer than a cookie because CSRF no longer applies, with no other risk.

concepts.name: Attribute-based and policy-based access
concepts.summary: Analyse when role models become too coarse and policies using user, resource and context attributes fit better.

concepts.name: Centralised authorization architecture
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs that separate policy decision from enforcement and keep checks consistent across services.

concepts.name: Token validation and key management
concepts.summary: Evaluate token verification practices, including key rotation, algorithm pinning and defenses against forged tokens.

concepts.name: Token revocation and lifetime strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate revocation approaches such as introspection, denylists and short lifetimes against latency and risk requirements.

concepts.name: Passwordless and phishing-resistant authentication
concepts.summary: Analyse how public-key credentials bound to an origin resist phishing compared with passwords and one-time codes.

concepts.name: Federated identity and SSO design
concepts.summary: Evaluate single sign-on designs, trust relationships and account-linking risks across identity providers.

concepts.name: Account recovery threat modelling
concepts.summary: Analyse reset and recovery flows as alternate authentication paths and identify weaknesses such as guessable or reusable links.

concepts.name: Service-to-service authentication
concepts.summary: Evaluate mechanisms for authenticating workloads, such as client credentials and mutual TLS, with scoped permissions.

misconceptions.text: Adding more roles always scales access control cleanly as an application grows.
Any valid signature on a token means the token is acceptable for this service.
SMS one-time codes are as phishing-resistant as WebAuthn.

concepts.name: Zero trust access architecture
concepts.summary: Evaluate architectures that authenticate and authorize every request using identity, device and context rather than network position.

concepts.name: Authorization model design
concepts.summary: Design a scalable authorization model, choosing between role, attribute and relationship-based approaches for a product's sharing needs.

concepts.name: Identity protocol vulnerability assessment
concepts.summary: Assess an OAuth, OIDC or SAML deployment for flaws such as open redirects, missing state checks and token replay.

concepts.name: Sender-constrained tokens
concepts.summary: Evaluate binding tokens to a client key so that a stolen token cannot be replayed by another party.

concepts.name: Adaptive and risk-based authentication
concepts.summary: Design policies that raise authentication requirements based on risk signals while managing friction and false positives.

concepts.name: Multi-tenant identity architecture
concepts.summary: Design identity and authorization for multi-tenant systems that isolate tenants, delegate administration and support enterprise federation.

concepts.name: Authentication migration and incident response
concepts.summary: Plan migrations such as password hash upgrades or IdP changes and responses to credential or signing key compromise.

concepts.name: Authorization testing and auditing
concepts.summary: Evaluate test strategies, audit logs and policy analysis that verify access rules hold across a system.

misconceptions.text: Placing services in a private network removes the need for per-request authentication and authorization.
One authorization model such as RBAC fits every product without modification.
Using a standard protocol like OAuth makes a deployment secure regardless of how it is configured.

concepts.name: Customer needs and expectations
concepts.summary: Explain that customers contact you with a goal and expectations such as speed, accuracy, courtesy and a clear outcome.

concepts.name: Courteous greeting and tone
concepts.summary: Recall how to open and close contacts politely, using a warm, respectful tone and the customer's name.

concepts.name: Active listening
concepts.summary: Describe how to give full attention, avoid interrupting and confirm what the customer said by paraphrasing.

concepts.name: Clear simple language
concepts.summary: Explain why short, jargon-free wording makes answers easier for customers to understand and act on.

concepts.name: Channel characteristics
concepts.summary: Describe how phone, email and chat differ in speed, tone cues and written record.

concepts.name: Knowing your limits
concepts.summary: Recall that you should not guess or promise beyond your authority and should know who to ask or hand over to.

misconceptions.text: Good customer service just means being friendly and smiling.
Listening means waiting for the customer to stop talking so you can give the answer.
Using technical terms makes you sound professional and reassures the customer.

concepts.name: Clarifying questions
concepts.summary: Use open and closed questions to uncover the real issue and gather the details needed to help.

concepts.name: Empathy statements
concepts.summary: Apply short, sincere statements that acknowledge the customer's feelings and situation before moving to solutions.

concepts.name: Structured call or chat flow
concepts.summary: Run a contact through opening, diagnosis, resolution and closing, including checking the customer is satisfied.

concepts.name: Setting realistic expectations
concepts.summary: Give honest timeframes and next steps and avoid promises you cannot be sure of keeping.

concepts.name: Writing clear customer emails
concepts.summary: Write replies that answer the question first, are well organised and use an appropriate, courteous tone.

concepts.name: Accurate case notes
concepts.summary: Record each contact factually and completely so a colleague can continue without asking the customer to repeat themselves.

concepts.name: Handling a basic complaint
concepts.summary: Handle a straightforward complaint by listening, apologising, fixing it or offering options, and confirming the outcome.

misconceptions.text: Apologising means admitting the company is at fault and should be avoided.
Promising a fast fix, even if unsure, keeps the customer happy.
Case notes are only for managers, so brief or vague notes are fine.

concepts.name: De-escalating angry customers
concepts.summary: Use calm tone, acknowledgement and focus on solutions to reduce a customer's anger without taking it personally.

concepts.name: Root-cause diagnosis
concepts.summary: Analyse symptoms and customer information to separate the real cause from the stated complaint.

concepts.name: Service recovery
concepts.summary: Analyse a service failure and choose an apology, fix and fair compensation that restores trust.

concepts.name: Escalation and handover
concepts.summary: Decide when to escalate and hand over with full context so the customer does not repeat their story.

concepts.name: Prioritising and managing workload
concepts.summary: Order competing contacts and follow-ups by urgency, impact and promised deadlines.

concepts.name: Policy and the customer's interest
concepts.summary: Weigh policy rules against the customer's situation to explain limits clearly or request justified exceptions.

concepts.name: Saying no constructively
concepts.summary: Decline a request while explaining why and offering workable alternatives.

misconceptions.text: The customer's stated complaint is always the real problem.
The way to calm an angry customer is to quickly explain why they are wrong or cite policy.
Escalating a case means you have failed and should be avoided.

concepts.name: Customer effort and journey analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse a customer's end-to-end journey to find points of friction, repeat contacts and effort that can be removed.

concepts.name: Service metrics interpretation
concepts.summary: Evaluate what measures such as satisfaction, first-contact resolution and handling time do and do not tell you, and their trade-offs.

concepts.name: Complaint pattern analysis
concepts.summary: Categorise contacts and feedback to find recurring causes and prioritise those worth fixing at source.

concepts.name: Tailoring approach to customer type
concepts.summary: Judge and adapt communication style and solution to vulnerable, expert, repeat or high-value customers.

concepts.name: Proactive service
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to contact customers before they complain, such as about delays, to prevent contacts and build trust.

concepts.name: Coaching colleagues on service quality
concepts.summary: Review interactions against quality criteria and give specific, constructive feedback that improves a colleague's practice.

concepts.name: Legal and fairness obligations
concepts.summary: Analyse how consumer rights, privacy and fair-treatment duties constrain what you can say, share and offer.

misconceptions.text: A high satisfaction score means service is good, so no further analysis is needed.
Shorter handling time always indicates better service.
Handling each complaint well makes analysing patterns unnecessary.

concepts.name: Designing a service strategy
concepts.summary: Create a service model that sets standards, channels, staffing and promises aligned with the organisation's strategy and customers' needs.

concepts.name: Cost-to-serve versus value trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate how investment in service levels, automation and self-service balances cost against loyalty and retention.

concepts.name: Building a service culture
concepts.summary: Create hiring, training, empowerment and recognition practices that make good service the norm rather than individual heroics.

concepts.name: Human and automated service blend
concepts.summary: Design how self-service, bots and human agents work together, with consistent context and smooth handoffs across channels.

concepts.name: Crisis and mass-failure response
concepts.summary: Judge and lead communication and remediation when a widespread failure hits many customers at once.

concepts.name: Closing the feedback loop
concepts.summary: Create a system that turns customer insight into prioritised product and process changes and tells customers what changed.

concepts.name: Evaluating service quality frameworks
concepts.summary: Critique and refine quality scorecards and measures so they reward real outcomes and avoid gaming.

misconceptions.text: Automating as much service as possible always lowers cost and keeps customers satisfied.
Service quality is the responsibility of the service team alone.
A strict scorecard guarantees good service because staff will follow it.

concepts.name: Fluid versus solid behaviour
concepts.summary: Recall that a fluid continuously deforms under shear stress and that liquids and gases differ mainly in compressibility and in filling their container.

concepts.name: Density and specific gravity
concepts.summary: Explain density as mass per unit volume and compare fluids using specific gravity.

concepts.name: Pressure as force per area
concepts.summary: Understand pressure as normal force per unit area acting equally in all directions at a point in a static fluid.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic pressure variation
concepts.summary: Explain why pressure increases linearly with depth in a static fluid of constant density.

concepts.name: Gauge and absolute pressure
concepts.summary: Distinguish gauge pressure from absolute pressure and recognise atmospheric pressure as the reference.

concepts.name: Buoyancy and Archimedes' principle
concepts.summary: Understand that a submerged object feels an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

concepts.name: Streamlines and steady flow
concepts.summary: Recall what streamlines show and what steady flow means.

misconceptions.text: Pressure at a point in a fluid acts only downward.
Pressure at depth depends on the container's shape or the total amount of water.
Buoyant force depends on the object's weight rather than the displaced fluid's weight.

concepts.name: Pascal's law and hydraulic systems
concepts.summary: Apply the transmission of pressure changes in an enclosed fluid to calculate forces in hydraulic devices.

concepts.name: Manometer and barometer readings
concepts.summary: Calculate pressure differences from fluid column heights in manometers and barometers.

concepts.name: Flotation and floating equilibrium
concepts.summary: Use buoyancy and density ratios to find the submerged fraction of a floating body.

concepts.name: Continuity equation
concepts.summary: Apply conservation of mass to relate speed and cross-sectional area in incompressible pipe flow.

concepts.name: Volume and mass flow rate
concepts.summary: Compute volumetric and mass flow rates from velocity, area and density.

concepts.name: Bernoulli's equation
concepts.summary: Apply the relation between pressure, speed and height along a streamline for steady, inviscid, incompressible flow.

concepts.name: Viscosity as internal friction
concepts.summary: Explain viscosity as resistance to shear and how it differs between fluids and with temperature.

concepts.name: Laminar versus turbulent flow
concepts.summary: Describe the qualitative difference between smooth layered flow and chaotic mixing flow.

misconceptions.text: Fluid speeds up in a narrowing pipe because pressure must always rise there.
Bernoulli's equation holds between any two points in a fluid regardless of friction or flow type.
Thicker-looking or denser fluids are always more viscous.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic force on surfaces
concepts.summary: Calculate the resultant hydrostatic force and its line of action on plane submerged surfaces.

concepts.name: Extended Bernoulli with pumps and losses
concepts.summary: Analyse a system using the energy equation in head form including pump head, turbine head and losses.

concepts.name: Reynolds number
concepts.summary: Compute Reynolds number and use it to predict laminar, transitional or turbulent flow in pipes.

concepts.name: Hagen-Poiseuille laminar pipe flow
concepts.summary: Apply the parabolic velocity profile and flow-rate-pressure-drop relation for laminar pipe flow.

concepts.name: Major head loss in pipes
concepts.summary: Calculate frictional head loss using the Darcy-Weisbach equation and friction factor from Moody chart or correlations.

concepts.name: Minor losses in fittings
concepts.summary: Include losses from valves, bends and area changes using loss coefficients.

concepts.name: Momentum equation for control volumes
concepts.summary: Analyse forces on bends, nozzles and jets by applying momentum balance to a control volume.

concepts.name: Drag and boundary layer concepts
concepts.summary: Use drag coefficients and distinguish friction drag from pressure drag with the boundary layer idea.

misconceptions.text: Head loss in a pipe is caused by the fluid losing mass or speed rather than by viscous dissipation.
Reynolds number transition at about 2000 is a sharp universal threshold.
The friction factor is a constant of the fluid independent of flow and roughness.

concepts.name: Dimensional analysis and similarity
concepts.summary: Derive dimensionless groups and judge whether model tests are dynamically similar to a prototype.

concepts.name: Pipe network analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse systems of series and parallel pipes and match pump curves to system curves.

concepts.name: Compressible flow fundamentals
concepts.summary: Analyse flows where density changes matter using Mach number, stagnation properties and choking.

concepts.name: Boundary layer separation and stall
concepts.summary: Explain how adverse pressure gradients cause separation and its effect on drag and lift.

concepts.name: Lift and circulation
concepts.summary: Analyse lift on airfoils through circulation and pressure distribution, not simplistic explanations.

concepts.name: Differential continuity and momentum
concepts.summary: Derive and interpret the differential forms of mass and momentum conservation.

concepts.name: Potential flow models
concepts.summary: Evaluate when irrotational ideal-flow solutions using stream function and velocity potential are valid approximations.

concepts.name: Turbulence modelling choices
concepts.summary: Evaluate the suitability of time-averaged turbulence models and wall treatments for a given problem.

misconceptions.text: Lift is explained solely by air needing to travel faster over the longer upper surface to meet at the trailing edge.
Matching geometry alone makes a scale model behave like the prototype.
Potential flow predicts drag on bodies accurately.

concepts.name: Navier-Stokes equations
concepts.summary: Evaluate the terms, assumptions and well-posedness issues of the incompressible and compressible Navier-Stokes equations.

concepts.name: Exact and similarity solutions
concepts.summary: Judge and construct analytical solutions by reducing the Navier-Stokes equations under symmetry assumptions.

concepts.name: Vorticity dynamics
concepts.summary: Evaluate flows through vorticity transport, stretching and circulation conservation.

concepts.name: Turbulence energy cascade
concepts.summary: Assess turbulence through energy transfer across scales and the resolution demands it implies.

concepts.name: Choosing simulation fidelity
concepts.summary: Design a simulation strategy balancing DNS, LES and RANS with mesh, numerics and validation.

concepts.name: Stability and transition theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate how perturbations grow and lead to transition in shear flows and boundary layers.

concepts.name: Asymptotic and perturbation methods
concepts.summary: Construct reduced models such as boundary-layer, lubrication and Stokes approximations through scaling arguments.

concepts.name: Flow experiment and model design
concepts.summary: Design experiments or validation campaigns, choosing similarity, instrumentation and uncertainty treatment.

misconceptions.text: Turbulence is random noise unrelated to the deterministic Navier-Stokes equations.
A finer mesh and more computing power always make a CFD result more accurate.
Vorticity is created within the bulk of an inviscid fluid by pressure forces.

concepts.name: Stages of hiring pipeline
concepts.summary: Recall the main steps from defining a role through sourcing, screening, interviewing, offer and onboarding.

concepts.name: Job description components
concepts.summary: Identify the parts of a job description such as responsibilities, required skills, level and location, and what each tells candidates.

concepts.name: Role requirements versus preferences
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between essential and desirable requirements and why mixing them narrows the candidate pool.

concepts.name: Common interview formats
concepts.summary: Name the common interview formats and what each is typically used to assess.

concepts.name: Purpose of interviews
concepts.summary: Explain that interviews gather evidence about job-relevant skills and fit for both sides, not just a gut impression.

concepts.name: Basic candidate preparation
concepts.summary: Understand why candidates research the company, review the role and prepare examples of past work.

concepts.name: Fair and lawful hiring basics
concepts.summary: Understand that decisions must rest on job-relevant criteria and that questions about protected characteristics are inappropriate.

misconceptions.text: A good interviewer can reliably judge a candidate from a gut feeling in the first few minutes.
Job descriptions should list every skill the team might ever want so candidates see the full picture.
Hiring starts when the first interview is scheduled.

concepts.name: Role scorecard drafting
concepts.summary: Turn a role into a short list of outcomes and competencies that can be assessed.

concepts.name: Sourcing channels
concepts.summary: Describe channels such as referrals, job boards and direct outreach and the trade-offs in reach and quality of each.

concepts.name: Resume screening against criteria
concepts.summary: Screen applications against written criteria rather than impressions like school or past employer prestige.

concepts.name: Behavioural question construction
concepts.summary: Write questions that ask for specific past situations tied to a competency.

concepts.name: STAR answer structuring
concepts.summary: Structure candidate answers as situation, task, action and result, with concrete outcomes.

concepts.name: Structured note-taking
concepts.summary: Record what the candidate said and did separately from your interpretation.

concepts.name: Candidate experience basics
concepts.summary: Explain how clear timelines, prompt feedback and respectful conduct affect acceptance and employer reputation.

misconceptions.text: Candidates from well-known companies or universities are automatically stronger.
Any question asked in an interview counts as a behavioural question.
A STAR answer is simply a story, and polish matters more than the specifics of the action taken.

concepts.name: Structured interview design
concepts.summary: Design an interview loop where each stage covers specific competencies with the same questions for every candidate.

concepts.name: Scoring rubrics with anchors
concepts.summary: Build rubrics with defined behavioural anchors so ratings are comparable across interviewers.

concepts.name: Bias mitigation in hiring
concepts.summary: Analyse where halo effect, similarity bias and anchoring enter the process and apply controls such as blind screening and independent scoring.

concepts.name: Work sample assessments
concepts.summary: Design realistic, time-bounded tasks that mirror the job and evaluate them against the rubric.

concepts.name: Debrief and decision meeting
concepts.summary: Run a debrief where interviewers submit written ratings first and then compare evidence on each competency.

concepts.name: Interviewer probing technique
concepts.summary: Use follow-ups to separate personal contribution from team outcomes and to test depth.

concepts.name: Pipeline metrics analysis
concepts.summary: Interpret stage conversion, time-to-hire and drop-off to locate bottlenecks or inequities.

misconceptions.text: Structured interviews are rigid and less predictive than free-flowing conversations.
Being aware of your biases is enough to prevent them affecting your ratings.
The debrief should start with the most senior person's opinion to save time.

concepts.name: Predictive validity of methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate selection methods by evidence on how well they predict job performance and decide how to combine them.

concepts.name: Interviewer calibration
concepts.summary: Analyse rating differences across interviewers and correct them with training, shadowing and feedback.

concepts.name: Adverse impact analysis
concepts.summary: Assess whether stages screen out groups disproportionately and judge whether the criterion is job-related.

concepts.name: Offer and negotiation strategy
concepts.summary: Judge offer structure, leveling and negotiation approach balancing internal equity, budget and candidate motivations.

concepts.name: Level and role calibration
concepts.summary: Distinguish scope, autonomy and impact across levels so candidates are assessed and placed consistently.

concepts.name: Evaluating borderline candidates
concepts.summary: Weigh conflicting evidence, decide whether to gather more data and justify a hire or no-hire.

concepts.name: Strategic candidate positioning
concepts.summary: As a candidate, analyse the interviewers' criteria and tailor evidence, questions and negotiation to them.

misconceptions.text: Unstructured conversation about culture fit is the best predictor of success.
If no protected-group differences were intended, the process cannot have adverse impact.
Hiring a borderline candidate is fine because they can grow into the role.

concepts.name: Hiring system design
concepts.summary: Design a hiring system aligned with workforce planning, covering roles, methods, tooling and governance.

concepts.name: Selection process validation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a company's own process by linking assessment scores to later performance and retention.

concepts.name: Trade-off assessment of speed and rigour
concepts.summary: Judge how much assessment is justified by role risk and market conditions.

concepts.name: Interview question bank creation
concepts.summary: Create validated question sets, exercises and rubrics for new roles.

concepts.name: Hiring culture and governance
concepts.summary: Build norms, accountability and incentives that sustain a consistent hiring bar and fair practice across teams.

concepts.name: Impact of AI in screening
concepts.summary: Evaluate automated screening and assessment tools for validity, bias and transparency before adopting them.

concepts.name: Executive and rare-skill hiring
concepts.summary: Create tailored approaches for senior or scarce-talent roles, including references, search partners and stakeholder alignment.

misconceptions.text: A vendor's claim that a screening algorithm is bias-free removes the need to audit it.
A rigorous process is always worth its cost, whatever the role and market.
A strong hiring bar comes from hiring only exceptional people, not from consistent process and accountability.

concepts.name: Open-loop versus closed-loop control
concepts.summary: Explain how feedback from a measured output corrects errors, in contrast to open-loop control that applies inputs without measuring the result.

concepts.name: Plant, controller, sensor, actuator
concepts.summary: Identify the roles of each element in a feedback loop and name the reference, error, control and output signals.

concepts.name: Block diagram elements
concepts.summary: Read block diagrams with blocks, summing junctions and pickoff points and describe the signal flow they represent.

concepts.name: Transfer function of a plant
concepts.summary: Understand a transfer function as the ratio of output to input Laplace transforms with zero initial conditions.

concepts.name: Poles and zeros meaning
concepts.summary: Define poles and zeros as roots of the denominator and numerator and locate them on the s-plane.

concepts.name: Step response features
concepts.summary: Describe rise time, peak overshoot, settling time and steady-state value on a step response plot.

concepts.name: Stability as bounded response
concepts.summary: Explain that a stable system's response to bounded inputs stays bounded and decays to equilibrium when disturbed.

misconceptions.text: Feedback control always makes a system faster and more stable.
A transfer function describes the system's response to one specific input such as a step.
Overshoot and rise time are the same thing, both describing how quickly the output reaches the target.

concepts.name: Block diagram reduction
concepts.summary: Simplify block diagrams with series, parallel and feedback rules to obtain closed-loop transfer functions such as G/(1+GH).

concepts.name: First-order response parameters
concepts.summary: Compute time constant and DC gain from a first-order transfer function and predict its step response.

concepts.name: Second-order response parameters
concepts.summary: Use damping ratio and natural frequency to classify underdamped, critically damped and overdamped responses and estimate overshoot and settling time.

concepts.name: Pole location and response
concepts.summary: Relate pole positions in the s-plane to decay rate, oscillation frequency and stability of the time response.

concepts.name: Routh-Hurwitz stability test
concepts.summary: Build a Routh array from a characteristic polynomial to count right-half-plane roots and find gain ranges for stability.

concepts.name: Steady-state error and system type
concepts.summary: Apply the final value theorem and error constants to compute steady-state error for step, ramp and parabolic inputs by system type.

concepts.name: Proportional control effects
concepts.summary: Predict how raising proportional gain changes speed, overshoot and steady-state error of a simple loop.

misconceptions.text: Increasing proportional gain indefinitely improves performance without any downside.
Steady-state error can be found only by simulating the response, not analytically.
A system with all poles in the left half-plane has no overshoot.

concepts.name: Root locus construction rules
concepts.summary: Sketch a root locus using branches, real-axis segments, asymptotes, breakaway points and angles of departure.

concepts.name: Root locus gain selection
concepts.summary: Analyse the locus to choose a gain that meets damping and settling targets and recognise when no gain can.

concepts.name: PID controller terms
concepts.summary: Apply P, I and D actions and predict how each affects rise time, overshoot, settling and steady-state error.

concepts.name: Frequency response and Bode plots
concepts.summary: Construct and read asymptotic Bode magnitude and phase plots from a transfer function.

concepts.name: Gain and phase margins
concepts.summary: Determine gain and phase margins from Bode plots and relate them to closed-loop stability and damping.

concepts.name: Nyquist stability criterion
concepts.summary: Use encirclements of -1 by the Nyquist plot and open-loop RHP poles to determine closed-loop stability.

concepts.name: PID tuning heuristics
concepts.summary: Tune PID gains using Ziegler-Nichols rules or manual iteration and judge the resulting response.

concepts.name: Sensitivity and disturbance rejection
concepts.summary: Analyse sensitivity and complementary sensitivity to explain disturbance rejection and noise tradeoffs.

misconceptions.text: Derivative action improves any loop and is safe with noisy measurements.
Positive gain and phase margins computed from the Bode plot guarantee stability for any plant.
Ziegler-Nichols tuning yields optimal, well-damped responses.

concepts.name: Lead compensator design
concepts.summary: Design a lead compensator to add phase near crossover and improve transient response and margins.

concepts.name: Lag compensator design
concepts.summary: Design a lag compensator to raise low-frequency gain and reduce steady-state error without disturbing crossover phase.

concepts.name: Loop shaping
concepts.summary: Shape the open-loop frequency response to meet bandwidth, margin, tracking and noise specifications together.

concepts.name: Fundamental performance limitations
concepts.summary: Evaluate how right-half-plane zeros, delays and the waterfall effect limit achievable bandwidth and sensitivity.

concepts.name: Integrator windup and anti-windup
concepts.summary: Diagnose windup under actuator saturation and select anti-windup schemes such as clamping or back-calculation.

concepts.name: Practical PID implementation
concepts.summary: Implement PID with derivative filtering, setpoint weighting and discretisation while analysing their effects on the loop.

concepts.name: Time delay in feedback loops
concepts.summary: Analyse the phase penalty of delay and apply Pade approximation or Smith-predictor ideas to loop design.

concepts.name: Two-degree-of-freedom control
concepts.summary: Separate tracking from disturbance rejection using prefilters or feedforward and justify the structure chosen.

misconceptions.text: A lead compensator can be made arbitrarily strong to gain unlimited phase and bandwidth.
Anti-windup is only needed if the integral gain is too high.
Right-half-plane zeros can be cancelled by placing a pole at the same location in the controller.

concepts.name: Robust stability and uncertainty
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a design remains stable under modelled plant uncertainty using the small gain theorem and sensitivity bounds.

concepts.name: Specification trade-off judgement
concepts.summary: Critique conflicting requirements on speed, robustness, noise, actuator effort and cost, and justify prioritisation.

concepts.name: Design of full compensation architectures
concepts.summary: Create cascade, feedforward and gain-scheduled architectures suited to a plant's structure and operating range.

concepts.name: Nonlinear plant linearisation validity
concepts.summary: Assess when linearised models are valid and design schedules or alternatives when nonlinearity breaks the assumptions.

concepts.name: Model identification for design
concepts.summary: Develop plant models from experimental frequency or step data and quantify uncertainty for controller design.

concepts.name: Digital implementation effects
concepts.summary: Evaluate how sampling, quantisation and computation delay erode margins and choose discretisation methods and rates.

concepts.name: Controller validation and commissioning
concepts.summary: Create simulation and hardware test plans, including margin measurement and worst-case cases, to verify and tune a deployed loop.

misconceptions.text: A controller that works well in simulation will work on the real plant if the nominal margins are good.
Sampling at just above twice the bandwidth is enough for digital control.
A single linear model identified at one operating point suffices across the whole range.

adb-7 sits at C2 and is a thin duplicate of cmp-3, which covers the effects of P, I and D
Poles and zeros meaning (nov-5) is C1 but is a prerequisite topic restated and overlaps adb-4

Missing dependency: adb-6 depends on adb-1 and system type, but also adb-5 is wrongly not required for cmp-6 or cmp-4 context; cmp-6 should depend on cmp-5 or Bode only loosely

cmp-1 depends on root locus rules requiring adb-1 (closed-loop characteristic equation), missing
exp-2 is a vague trade-off judgement and overlaps prf-3 loop shaping
exp-3 name 'Design of full compensation architectures' is vague and overlaps prf-8 and exp-4 (gain scheduling appears in both)
exp-1 depends on exp-5 in prerequisites, which is questionable; identification and uncertainty belong together but exp-5 is listed after
Misconception in adb stage: 'all poles in LHP has no overshoot' is fine, but misconception on prf-5 and exp-6 are ok
Expert stage repeats lower content (digital implementation effects overlaps prf-6 discretisation)
