concepts.name: Root locus gain selection
concepts.summary: Analyse the locus to choose a gain that meets damping and settling targets and recognise when no gain can.

concepts.name: PID controller terms
concepts.summary: Apply P, I and D actions and predict how each affects rise time, overshoot, settling and steady-state error.

concepts.name: Frequency response and Bode plots
concepts.summary: Construct and read asymptotic Bode magnitude and phase plots from a transfer function.

concepts.name: Gain and phase margins
concepts.summary: Determine gain and phase margins from Bode plots and relate them to closed-loop stability and damping.

concepts.name: Nyquist stability criterion
concepts.summary: Use encirclements of -1 by the Nyquist plot and open-loop RHP poles to determine closed-loop stability.

concepts.name: PID tuning heuristics
concepts.summary: Tune PID gains using Ziegler-Nichols rules or manual iteration and judge the resulting response.

concepts.name: Sensitivity and disturbance rejection
concepts.summary: Analyse sensitivity and complementary sensitivity to explain disturbance rejection and noise tradeoffs.

misconceptions.text: Derivative action improves any loop and is safe with noisy measurements.
Positive gain and phase margins computed from the Bode plot guarantee stability for any plant.
Ziegler-Nichols tuning yields optimal, well-damped responses.

concepts.name: Lead compensator design
concepts.summary: Design a lead compensator to add phase near crossover and improve transient response and margins.

concepts.name: Lag compensator design
concepts.summary: Design a lag compensator to raise low-frequency gain and reduce steady-state error without disturbing crossover phase.

concepts.name: Loop shaping
concepts.summary: Shape the open-loop frequency response to meet bandwidth, margin, tracking and noise specifications together.

concepts.name: Fundamental performance limitations
concepts.summary: Evaluate how right-half-plane zeros, delays and the waterfall effect limit achievable bandwidth and sensitivity.

concepts.name: Integrator windup and anti-windup
concepts.summary: Diagnose windup under actuator saturation and select anti-windup schemes such as clamping or back-calculation.

concepts.name: PID derivative filtering and setpoint weighting
concepts.summary: Implement PID with derivative filtering and setpoint weighting while analysing their effects on noise amplification and setpoint response.

concepts.name: Time delay in feedback loops
concepts.summary: Analyse the phase penalty of delay and apply Pade approximation or Smith-predictor ideas to loop design.

concepts.name: Two-degree-of-freedom control
concepts.summary: Separate tracking from disturbance rejection using prefilters or feedforward and justify the structure chosen.

misconceptions.text: A lead compensator can be made arbitrarily strong to gain unlimited phase and bandwidth.
Anti-windup is only needed if the integral gain is too high.
Right-half-plane zeros can be cancelled by placing a pole at the same location in the controller.

concepts.name: Robust stability and uncertainty
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a design remains stable under modelled plant uncertainty using the small gain theorem and sensitivity bounds.

concepts.name: Conflicting specification prioritisation
concepts.summary: Critique conflicting requirements on speed, robustness, noise, actuator effort and cost, and justify prioritisation.

concepts.name: Cascade and multi-loop architecture design
concepts.summary: Create cascade and multi-loop architectures with inner and outer loops suited to a plant's structure and time-scale separation.

concepts.name: Linearisation validity and gain scheduling
concepts.summary: Assess when linearised models are valid and design schedules or alternatives when nonlinearity breaks the assumptions.

concepts.name: Model identification for design
concepts.summary: Develop plant models from experimental frequency or step data and quantify uncertainty for controller design.

concepts.name: Sampling and computation delay effects on margins
concepts.summary: Evaluate how sampling, quantisation and computation delay erode margins and choose discretisation methods and rates.

concepts.name: Controller validation and commissioning
concepts.summary: Create simulation and hardware test plans, including margin measurement and worst-case cases, to verify and tune a deployed loop.

misconceptions.text: A controller that works well in simulation will work on the real plant if the nominal margins are good.
Sampling at just above twice the bandwidth is enough for digital control.
A single linear model identified at one operating point suffices across the whole range.

concepts.name: Cell theory
concepts.summary: State that all living things are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and cells arise from pre-existing cells.

concepts.name: Prokaryotic versus eukaryotic cells
concepts.summary: Explain how cells lacking a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles differ from cells that have them.

concepts.name: Plasma membrane structure
concepts.summary: Describe the phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins as a selectively permeable boundary of the cell.

concepts.name: Major organelles and functions
concepts.summary: Name the nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, lysosomes and ribosomes and state the main function of each.

concepts.name: Plant versus animal cells
concepts.summary: Explain why plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole while animal cells do not.

concepts.name: Passive and active transport
concepts.summary: Distinguish movement down a gradient without energy from movement against a gradient that requires energy.

concepts.name: Osmosis and tonicity
concepts.summary: Predict whether a cell swells or shrinks in hypotonic, isotonic and hypertonic solutions.

misconceptions.text: Only plant cells have mitochondria because animal cells get energy from food directly.
Osmosis is the movement of solutes from high to low concentration.
The cell membrane is a solid wall that nothing can pass through except via pores.

concepts.name: Facilitated diffusion and channels
concepts.summary: Explain how channel and carrier proteins let specific polar molecules and ions cross the membrane down their gradients.

concepts.name: Primary and secondary active transport
concepts.summary: Apply the idea that ATP-driven pumps build gradients that then power cotransport of other solutes.

concepts.name: Secretory pathway
concepts.summary: Trace a secreted protein from ribosome on rough ER through the Golgi and vesicles to the cell exterior.

concepts.name: Endocytosis and exocytosis
concepts.summary: Describe how cells import and export material using membrane-bound vesicles.

concepts.name: Cytoskeleton filament types
concepts.summary: Match actin filaments, microtubules and intermediate filaments to their structures and roles in shape and movement.

concepts.name: Cell cycle phases
concepts.summary: Place events such as DNA replication and chromosome segregation in the correct phase of the cell cycle.

concepts.name: Stages of mitosis
concepts.summary: Identify prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase from chromosome behaviour and spindle position.

concepts.name: Light microscope use
concepts.summary: Calculate magnification and distinguish it from resolution when viewing stained cells.

misconceptions.text: Higher magnification always gives a clearer image with more detail.
Chromosomes are duplicated at the start of mitosis in prophase.
Active transport and facilitated diffusion both need ATP.

concepts.name: Membrane potential and ion gradients
concepts.summary: Explain how unequal ion distribution and selective permeability generate a voltage across the membrane.

concepts.name: Protein targeting and sorting
concepts.summary: Analyse how signal sequences direct proteins to the ER, mitochondria, nucleus or secretion.

concepts.name: Mitochondrial and chloroplast bioenergetics
concepts.summary: Compare how proton gradients across inner mitochondrial and thylakoid membranes drive ATP synthesis, and relate this to endosymbiotic origin.

concepts.name: Receptor-ligand signaling
concepts.summary: Describe how ligand binding to receptors triggers intracellular responses and distinguish receptor classes.

concepts.name: Second messengers and cascades
concepts.summary: Analyse how signals are amplified and relayed through second messengers and kinase cascades.

concepts.name: Cell cycle checkpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse how checkpoints detect DNA damage or misattachment and halt progression.

concepts.name: Meiosis and genetic variation
concepts.summary: Contrast meiosis with mitosis and explain how recombination and assortment generate diversity.

concepts.name: Fluorescence microscopy and culture
concepts.summary: Choose fluorescent labelling and sterile culture methods to visualise and maintain cells for a given question.

misconceptions.text: Meiosis is just two rounds of mitosis producing identical cells.
Mitochondria make ATP directly in the matrix using only substrate-level reactions, with no role for the membrane.
A signaling molecule must enter the cell to trigger a response.

concepts.name: Regulation of cyclin-CDK activity
concepts.summary: Analyse how cyclin synthesis, degradation and inhibitors control CDK activity to drive cell cycle transitions.

concepts.name: Signal pathway crosstalk and feedback
concepts.summary: Analyse how feedback, scaffolding and crosstalk shape signal strength, duration and specificity.

concepts.name: Cancer and signaling dysregulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how mutations in growth signaling and checkpoint genes such as Ras and p53 lead to uncontrolled division.

concepts.name: Apoptosis and cell death
concepts.summary: Analyse intrinsic and extrinsic apoptosis pathways and contrast apoptosis with necrosis.

concepts.name: Cytoskeletal dynamics and motors
concepts.summary: Analyse how filament polymerisation and motor proteins drive transport, division and migration.

concepts.name: Membrane trafficking machinery
concepts.summary: Analyse how coat proteins, Rabs and SNAREs ensure specific vesicle budding, targeting and fusion.

concepts.name: Experimental design in cell biology
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether imaging, fractionation, RNAi or CRISPR experiments support a causal claim, including controls and artefacts.

concepts.name: Confocal and live-cell imaging
concepts.summary: Evaluate imaging modalities for resolution, phototoxicity and dynamics when studying live cells.

misconceptions.text: Signaling pathways are linear chains where each receptor activates only one fixed outcome.
Cancer arises from a single mutation in one gene.
Apoptosis is just passive cell breakdown like necrosis and causes inflammation.

concepts.name: Evaluating mechanistic models
concepts.summary: Judge competing mechanistic explanations of cellular processes against quantitative and perturbation data.

concepts.name: Super-resolution and cryo-EM methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate when super-resolution or cryo-electron methods can resolve structures that conventional microscopy cannot.

concepts.name: Organelle contact sites and phase separation
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for condensates and inter-organelle contacts as organising principles of the cell.

concepts.name: Designing a cell biology study
concepts.summary: Design a multi-method study with orthogonal approaches, controls and statistics to test a hypothesis about cell function.

concepts.name: Engineering cells and synthetic circuits
concepts.summary: Create genetic or optogenetic tools to perturb or reprogram cell behaviour with spatial and temporal control.

concepts.name: Organoid and 3D culture systems
concepts.summary: Design culture systems that better recapitulate tissue context and judge their limits against in vivo behaviour.

concepts.name: Cell fate and stem cell regulation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how signaling, cell cycle and asymmetry decisions determine self-renewal versus differentiation.

misconceptions.text: A protein seen colocalised with an organelle by fluorescence is proven to function there.
Cell lines in a dish behave the same as cells in intact tissue.
Organelles are always membrane-bound compartments with fixed boundaries.

concepts.name: Prior, likelihood, posterior
concepts.summary: Name and describe the prior, likelihood and posterior as the three parts of a Bayesian update.

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem for events
concepts.summary: Explain how Bayes' theorem reverses a conditional probability by combining P(B|A), P(A) and P(B).

concepts.name: Probability as degree of belief
concepts.summary: Explain that Bayesians use probability to express uncertainty about unknown quantities, not only long-run frequencies.

concepts.name: Parameters as random quantities
concepts.summary: Understand that an unknown parameter is described by a probability distribution that reflects what is currently known.

concepts.name: Updating beliefs with data
concepts.summary: Describe how a posterior after one batch of data can serve as the prior for the next.

concepts.name: Base rate and diagnostic reasoning
concepts.summary: Explain why a positive test result depends on the prevalence as well as sensitivity and specificity.

misconceptions.text: P(hypothesis | data) is the same as P(data | hypothesis).
A positive result from an accurate test means the condition is almost certainly present, regardless of how rare it is.
The prior is just a guess that the data will simply overwrite, so it does not matter.

concepts.name: Posterior proportional to prior times likelihood
concepts.summary: Compute a posterior on a grid or discrete set by multiplying prior and likelihood and normalising.

concepts.name: Beta-binomial conjugate update
concepts.summary: Update a Beta prior with binomial data to obtain a Beta posterior by adding successes and failures.

concepts.name: Choosing a simple prior
concepts.summary: Pick a flat, weakly informative or informative prior for a proportion and justify the choice from context.

concepts.name: Credible interval
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret an interval that contains the parameter with stated posterior probability.

concepts.name: Posterior summaries
concepts.summary: Report posterior mean, median and mode (MAP) and say when they differ.

concepts.name: Prior strength as pseudo-observations
concepts.summary: Interpret prior parameters as equivalent prior data and see how sample size shifts weight toward the likelihood.

concepts.name: Posterior predictive for next observation
concepts.summary: Calculate the probability of a future outcome by averaging over the posterior in a simple model.

misconceptions.text: A 95% credible interval means that in 95% of repeated experiments the interval would cover the true value.
A flat prior is completely objective and adds no assumptions.
The posterior mean and the most likely value are always the same.

concepts.name: Conjugate families beyond beta-binomial
concepts.summary: Derive and apply conjugate updates for Poisson rates and normal means with known variance.

concepts.name: Prior sensitivity analysis
concepts.summary: Compare posteriors under different reasonable priors to judge how much conclusions depend on them.

concepts.name: Highest density intervals
concepts.summary: Distinguish equal-tailed from highest density intervals and choose between them for skewed posteriors.

concepts.name: Bayesian hypothesis comparison
concepts.summary: Compare two hypotheses using Bayes factors and posterior odds and analyse their sensitivity to priors.

concepts.name: Bayesian linear regression
concepts.summary: Specify priors on coefficients and noise, and interpret the resulting posterior over regression parameters.

concepts.name: Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling
concepts.summary: Explain and apply sampling from an unnormalised posterior with Metropolis-style algorithms.

concepts.name: MCMC convergence diagnostics
concepts.summary: Assess chains using trace plots, multiple chains, R-hat and effective sample size.

concepts.name: Posterior predictive checking
concepts.summary: Simulate data from the fitted model and compare to observed data to find misfit.

misconceptions.text: A Bayes factor is the probability that the hypothesis is true.
If the MCMC trace looks noisy and the run finished, the posterior samples are reliable.
With enough data prior sensitivity is irrelevant in every model.

concepts.name: Hierarchical models and partial pooling
concepts.summary: Analyse how group-level priors shrink group estimates and trade off between complete and no pooling.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo behaviour
concepts.summary: Analyse why gradient-based samplers scale better and diagnose divergences and poor geometry.

concepts.name: Model comparison with predictive criteria
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing models using cross-validated predictive performance and justify the selection.

concepts.name: Weakly informative prior design
concepts.summary: Evaluate priors by simulating from the prior predictive distribution and judging plausibility.

concepts.name: Generalised linear models in Bayesian form
concepts.summary: Analyse Bayesian logistic and count models, including link functions and coefficient interpretation.

concepts.name: Decision-theoretic use of posteriors
concepts.summary: Evaluate actions by minimising posterior expected loss and justify the choice of loss.

concepts.name: Reparameterisation for sampling
concepts.summary: Analyse when reparameterising a model removes funnel-shaped posteriors and improves sampling.

misconceptions.text: Hierarchical models just average groups together and hide real differences between them.
The model with the best in-sample fit is the best model.
Divergent transitions in HMC can be ignored if R-hat looks fine.

concepts.name: Bayesian workflow design
concepts.summary: Design an iterative workflow of model building, fitting, checking and revision for a new problem.

concepts.name: Approximate inference trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate when variational or Laplace approximations are acceptable versus exact MCMC, and their known biases.

concepts.name: Nonparametric Bayesian models
concepts.summary: Construct flexible models with priors over functions or distributions for problems where parametric forms fail.

concepts.name: Simulation-based calibration
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether an inference procedure is correct by recovering parameters from simulated data.

concepts.name: Identifiability and prior influence
concepts.summary: Judge when parameters are only weakly identified and how much the prior drives the posterior.

concepts.name: Causal and missing-data Bayesian models
concepts.summary: Build models that jointly handle missingness, measurement error or causal structure using latent variables.

concepts.name: Communicating Bayesian results
concepts.summary: Critique and craft reports of posterior uncertainty, assumptions and decisions for non-specialist stakeholders.

misconceptions.text: Variational inference gives the same posterior as MCMC, only faster.
If the sampler converges, the model must be a good description of reality.
Nonparametric Bayesian models have no assumptions because they have no fixed parameters.

issues: nov-1 (prior, likelihood, posterior) and adb-1 (posterior proportional to prior times likelihood) overlap, and the flag is justified: adb-1 restates the same three-part update, so it needs a more distinct, specific framing.
nov-5 (updating beliefs) overlaps with nov-1 and with the sequential-update idea; the prerequisite nov-1 -> nov-5 is fine but the concept is thin.
adb-4 (credible interval) is C2 and sits at the low edge of the band, but it is described as 'compute and interpret', so it should be C3.
adb-5 and adb-6 depend on adb-2 correctly, but adb-4's prerequisite on adb-2 skips the more fundamental dependency on posterior summaries; this is minor.
The first adb-4 misconception is a real confusion of credible and confidence intervals, so it is retained.

cmp-5 (Bayesian linear regression) has prerequisite cmp-6 (MCMC) listed, which is acceptable, but cmp-5 at C3 is fine; cmp-4 depends on adb-1 only when it should depend on adb-3 (priors affect Bayes factors).
cmp-7 misconception text cites cmp-6 and cmp-7, which is fine.
cmp-2 (prior sensitivity) and prf-4 (weakly informative prior design) are distinct enough, but prf-4 is named by its method (prior predictive checks) and the name should say so.

exp-5 depends on prf-4 but identifiability really depends on cmp-2 and prf-1; acceptable, but exp-5 is near-duplicate with cmp-2 in the 'prior influence' part, so the name should focus on identifiability.
exp-6 bundles three different topics (causal, missing data, measurement error) in one concept, making it too broad; narrow it to latent-variable models for missing data and measurement error.
